topic: onboarding-activation: time-to-value before sign-up, carrying pre-signup state across devices and email verification, first-week setup asks and checklists, progressive disclosure versus tours, empty and warming states, notification-permission timing, and acknowledging the saved-to-claimed (T1 to T3) promotion

principles.principle: Show the fact before asking for an account. The account wall goes at the moment the person wants to keep something (save, remind me), never in front of the preview.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG (Managing accounts) says to delay sign-in as long as possible, because people often abandon apps that make them sign in before they can do anything useful. It says to ask for an account only if core functionality needs one, and to explain in the sign-in view why an account is needed and what it gives. App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(v): an app without significant account-based features must be usable without a login. Baymard's current cart-abandonment list: 18% of US shoppers abandoned a checkout because the site wanted them to create an account. Older Baymard editions are cited elsewhere at 19% and 26%, so the figure moves between survey waves. Duolingo's VP of Growth said that moving the sign-up screen back a few steps raised DAU by about 20% (self-reported, First Round Review). Hacker News users say a site that makes them create an account before they can see anything turns them away (anecdote).
principles.implication: The /start preview, the seasonal aha card, the compare reveal and every Band-A section must be fully readable signed out. The first account ask is the WallBar or save CTA, and it names what the person gets in one line ('Keep this address handy — Today and a night-before pickup reminder run on it'). No other surface that comes before the preview may require an account, a location permission or a notification permission.

principles.principle: Hold the address the person typed before signing up on the server, and never make them type it again. Where it cannot be recovered, offer the held value as a one-tap choice instead of an empty field.
principles.evidence: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (Level A): information the user already entered in the same process must be auto-populated or available to select. The W3C Understanding document says the criterion does not require keeping data between sessions, so register → verify → save is covered only while it counts as one process. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.6 Timeouts (AAA): warn users how much inactivity will lose their data unless the data is kept for more than 20 hours. Firebase Auth documents linking an anonymous account to a permanent credential, so data created before sign-up stays with the new account. This is the standard engineering pattern for deferred accounts.
principles.implication: The held-address chip on the verify interstitial is correct. Add to it: (a) if the server still holds the address, the save-confirmation 'recovery' frame shows it as a selectable suggestion row ('1402 NE 3rd Ave, Camas — Save it'), not a blank field; (b) any hold that expires lasts at least 20 hours, and the interstitial states the length ('We'll hold it for 7 days'); (c) the add-place duplicate state is also a select-not-retype pattern. A blank re-entry field is reserved for 'nothing was ever held'.

principles.principle: Don't make email verification a wall that forces a switch to another app or device. Let the save take effect first, and offer a typed or pasted code next to the link.
principles.evidence: NN/g's mobile registration checklist advises against asking users to confirm registration by email: switching apps disorients people and can stop them reaching their goal. It suggests codes, which are easier to enter without switching context. NN/g's passwordless article names the costs of email links: the person has to switch apps to reach the email, and the message may be filtered as spam. WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.8 accepts email-link authentication (technique G218), and codes must be pasteable. The pilot's most common signup path is register on a laptop and open the mail on a phone, which is exactly the device-switch case.
principles.implication: The 'Check your email' interstitial gets a 6-digit code field ('Or enter the code from the email') that accepts paste, so a laptop signup can finish on the laptop. The link stays as the alternative. Add a one-line spam hint next to 'Resend the link'. If the auth provider allows it, the pending place becomes a real saved place at registration, and verification only protects the account, so the copy says 'Saved privately. Confirm your email to keep your account' rather than 'Verify your email to save it'.

principles.principle: No upfront tour or welcome carousel. Teach each capability inside the section it fills, when the person first meets that section.
principles.evidence: NN/g (Mobile-App Onboarding): avoid onboarding when possible. In its study, deck-of-cards tutorials did not improve task performance, and people who skipped them did as well as people who watched. Instructional overlays work better when shown at the first encounter with a feature. Apple HIG Onboarding: keep it fast, fun and optional; prefer interactive learning; put off nonessential setup and use sensible defaults so people can start right away. NN/g Progressive Disclosure: show up front only what people often need, and make the path to the rest obvious with labels that set clear expectations.
principles.implication: After save, the first screen is Today itself: no intro slides, no coach-mark overlay. Each first-week ask is an inline row in the section it completes. The pickup card's 'That's my day' completes pickup_day, the 14-day strip's '+ Add a date' completes important_date, and the household block completes household. The keeper sheet and the widget how-to open only from a tap. Nothing presents itself on first launch.

principles.principle: Ask for notification permission only right after the person does something that makes the purpose obvious, and show them the exact notification they will get.
principles.evidence: Apple's UserNotifications docs: make the request in a context that shows why. Their example is asking after a person schedules a first task rather than at first launch. Android developer guidance for POST_NOTIFICATIONS (API 33+): let users get familiar with the app first, ask in response to an action that makes the purpose clear, and show an educational screen only when shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale() returns true. NN/g (Permission Requests): users were 12% more likely to grant when given a reason, and the most compelling reason got an 81% lift over the least compelling one. Asks fired by the system at launch surprise people. Airship 2025 benchmarks recommend a soft prompt rather than a generic launch prompt, and report that in-app messages raise opt-in among opted-out users by 14% on average (vendor data).
principles.implication: Remove the cold-launch request on iOS (the v1 primer already plans this). The natural trigger is the first 'That's my day' tap, because the purpose ('the night before pickup') is then concrete. The ask copy follows 'so that you can…': the person learns they will hear the night before their confirmed day. After a denial, the surface names what is unavailable and links to Settings (NN/g decision reversal), and the widget row is promoted.

principles.principle: A custom screen shown before a system permission prompt should not become a second decision, and should never look like the system dialog.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Privacy: a custom screen before a privacy-related permission alert should have exactly one button, titled with a word like 'Continue' or 'Next' that makes clear it opens the system alert. It should have no close or cancel, and should not use 'Allow'-style wording that suggests permission is granted inside the custom screen. The HIG also says that ideally the context already explains the request, so no extra screen is needed. Caveat: this passage is written for private-data permissions. The HIG Notifications page does not restate it, so how it applies to notification primers is an inference. App Store Guideline 5.1.1(iv) forbids manipulating or tricking people into consenting.
principles.implication: When the person has just tapped an explicit 'Yes' on the briefing opt-in card, go straight to the OS dialog: that card is the context. Keep the primer only for entries where the purpose is implicit (first 'That's my day', household activity from Mail). There, the action that opens the OS dialog is labelled 'Continue' or 'Turn on reminders', not 'Yes'/'Allow'. The tray-card preview is drawn as a clearly in-app illustration and never styled as an iOS or Android system alert.

principles.principle: On iOS, consider provisional (quiet) authorization so the person can try the night-before notice without using up the one-time prompt.
principles.evidence: Apple's UserNotifications docs: provisional authorization lets an app send notifications on a trial basis without prompting. They arrive quietly (no sound, no banner, not on the lock screen) and appear only in Notification Center history, with Keep and Turn Off controls. Keep then asks whether to deliver immediately or in the scheduled summary.
principles.implication: For a T1 user who confirms a pickup day but has not answered the primer, a provisional night-before notice is an option: it arrives quietly, and the person decides with Keep/Turn Off. The design must still treat the in-app pickup card and the widget as the dependable trigger, because provisional notices never reach the lock screen. Settings shows the state as 'Quiet delivery — Notification Center only'. This is a product decision to test, not a mandate.

principles.principle: Limit the first-week asks to three or four, and count only steps the person can actually complete at their current tier.
principles.evidence: Chameleon's analysis of 550M+ in-app interactions (vendor data; its two pages disagree slightly): 3- and 4-step tours complete best (72% and 74% in the blog), 7+ step tours only 16%, and completion drops sharply beyond 5 steps. Apple HIG says to put off nonessential setup. GOV.UK's Complete multiple tasks pattern says to simplify the transaction before using a task list. It shows tasks that depend on another task as 'Cannot start yet' in grey text, not as incomplete. The Pantopus design doc (F2) already says the banner must never show a step the user cannot complete at their tier, and its activation definition is: save + (briefing or widget) + one household fact.
principles.implication: The first-week set follows the activation definition: Save your address (already done) · Set your pickup day · Turn on a reminder or add the widget · Add one date or one person. Verify, profile and photo are not in the first-week count. At T1 the household step is shown in grey as 'Claim this address first', with no CTA, and is not counted in the denominator.

principles.principle: If you show progress, show a set that has already started and can be finished. Otherwise show an open-ended count with no denominator.
principles.evidence: Nunes & Drèze (J. Consumer Research 32(4), 2006): a task framed as already started (10 steps with 2 done, versus 8 steps with none done) is more likely to be finished, and finished faster. The widely cited car-wash figures, 34% versus 19% redemption, come from secondary sources; the abstract confirms only the direction. Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng (JMR 2006): effort speeds up as people near a reward, including when the progress is partly illusory. Villar, Callegaro & Yang (2013), a meta-analysis of 32 experiments: a constant progress indicator did not significantly reduce drop-off, fast-to-slow indicators reduced it, and slow-to-fast indicators increased it.
principles.implication: The Today row may read '1 of 4 done — next: set your pickup day →', where the done step is the save. A fraction must never include steps that cannot be completed at the current tier, because that is a slow or stalled indicator, the kind that increased drop-off. The place file's '14 things on file' has no denominator and is fine. A segmented ring that can never fill at T1 is not.

principles.principle: Checklist rows: start each with a verb, make the whole row tappable, quiet the finished ones, sync them across devices, and give every item a permanent decline with undo.
principles.evidence: GOV.UK Task list component research: uppercase status tags were harder to read; some users tried to tap the status as if it were a button, so the whole row became the link. Completed items are shown as plain black text so attention goes to what is left, and task names start with verbs. Hacker News users complain about setup nags that come back after updates and offer only 'Yes' and 'Not now', with no 'never' (anecdote). The design doc records that the mover checklist's ticks and dismissals are device-local today (F6).
principles.implication: Row copy is 'Set your pickup day', 'Add one date that matters', 'Add the people you live with'. The whole row is the hit target. Done rows disappear or go to text.secondary with a tick. Each ask pairs 'Not now' (which does not re-present by itself) with a terminal decline ('Just me', 'Skip', 'No thanks') that persists server-side, can be undone, and can be reopened from the place file or settings.

principles.principle: Every empty or warming surface must say which state it is in (loading, genuinely empty, or failed) and offer the one action that fills it.
principles.evidence: NN/g (Designing Empty States in Complex Applications) gives three guidelines: communicate system status, give in-context learning cues, and give direct paths to the key task. It warns that showing 'no records' and then replacing it with real content moments later damages trust. NN/g Skeleton Screens 101: use them for full-page loads of roughly 2–10 s, not under ~1 s; use a progress bar beyond 10 s; avoid frame-only skeletons, which make people think the page is broken. NN/g response-time limits: 0.1 s feels instant, 1 s keeps flow, 10 s is the limit of attention.
principles.implication: Today's warming state draws content-shaped skeletons in the final slots and never shows 'Nothing needs your attention today' until every provider has returned. The place file and the 14-day strip draw 'Checked — nothing…' only after a successful check, and draw nothing on error. Every empty list (Your places, the strip, the widget preview) carries its filling action inline ('+ Add a place', '+ Add a date', 'Sample' preview). Skip skeletons for loads under about a second.

principles.principle: Show what was checked. A visible record of the work makes a quiet result believable.
principles.evidence: Buell & Norton (Management Science 57(9), 2011), five experiments on simulated travel and dating sites: when a site showed the work it was doing (operational transparency), people valued the service more and sometimes preferred a slower site to an instant one with identical results. Perceived effort drove the effect through reciprocity.
principles.implication: The quiet-day receipt line (weather · air · alerts · your calendar, each ticked, with times or sources) is the right design, and warming can show each provider landing. Do not add artificial delay to create this effect. Show the real checks and their timestamps.

principles.principle: Acknowledge a tier promotion with a receipt the person can check: what changed, what happens next, and a way to find it again later.
principles.evidence: GOV.UK Confirmation pages pattern: say what happens next and when, link to what the user is likely to need next, and give a way to keep a record. Some users treat confirmation pages as receipts and bookmark them, so a service must respond helpfully when someone returns through that link. WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages: a save or sync confirmation injected into the page must be announced by assistive technology without taking focus.
principles.implication: The save confirmation states in one sentence what the save changed and hands off to Today. The claim receipt lists each item that moved. Both need a stable, revisitable form: a 'What moved when you claimed' entry in the place file, and a receipt URL that still renders later instead of a one-time banner. 'Synced 3 items from your other device', 'Removed … Undo' and 'Saved to your calendar. Only you.' are role=status live regions.

principles.principle: When a promotion changes who can see data, nothing becomes shared until the person makes an explicit choice, and the choice is as easy to reverse as to make.
principles.evidence: ICO guidance on valid consent: silence, pre-ticked boxes or inactivity are not consent. Requests should be granular, prominent and separate, and withdrawing should be as easy as consenting. This is UK regulator guidance, not binding on a WA pilot, but it is the clearest authoritative statement of the norm.
principles.implication: On the claim receipt, the dates stay private until 'Share with the household' is tapped. Leaving the screen without choosing keeps them private. Every date later carries its own visibility control in the date sheet and the place file ('Only you' / 'Household').

principles.principle: A call to action must predict where it goes.
principles.evidence: NN/g Progressive Disclosure: make the progression mechanics obvious and use labels that set clear expectations for what users will find. NN/g empty-state guidance: give a direct path to the task that fills the empty state.
principles.implication: A button that opens the compact Save sheet (no preview, no grade) is labelled 'Add a place' or 'Save an address', not 'Preview an address'. If the design wants a preview, the button goes to the preview.

patterns.name: Gradual engagement (lazy registration)
patterns.exemplars: Duolingo lets people finish a lesson before asking for an account; its growth lead said moving sign-up later raised DAU by about 20%. Apple's HIG example is a shopping app that allows unlimited browsing and asks for sign-in only at purchase. Firebase anonymous-to-permanent account linking keeps data created before sign-up.
patterns.howToApply: The /start preview and the compare reveal are the full value. The account ask comes only at 'Keep this address handy', names the benefit, and whatever was typed carries into the new account on the server.
patterns.pitfalls: Hiding 'why an account' behind the wall; losing the held address when the person switches device; letting the wall cover the sources or the honesty marks.

patterns.name: Visible held-state chip across the verification gap
patterns.exemplars: Cart persistence in e-commerce (Baymard shows account walls cost conversions). WCAG 3.3.7's model: re-show the earlier value as the default rather than asking again.
patterns.howToApply: Pinned address chip under 'Check your email' with 'Only you will see this'. If held state exists on the recovery frame, show it as a selectable row. State how long the hold lasts if it expires, at 20 hours or more.
patterns.pitfalls: A chip that promises holding while the data is really device-local; an expiry that nobody was told about; a blank retype field when the server has the value.

patterns.name: Code-or-link verification
patterns.exemplars: NN/g recommends codes, which are easier to enter without switching context, and names device-switching and spam as the costs of email links. WCAG G218 accepts email links, and pasted codes must be allowed.
patterns.howToApply: The interstitial offers a 6-digit code field (paste enabled) above 'Resend the link'. The link still works on any device and lands on the same saved state.
patterns.pitfalls: Blocking paste; a code that expires faster than email arrives; sending the person to a login screen after they tap the link on a second device.

patterns.name: In-context permission ask with a preview of the real artefact
patterns.exemplars: Apple's example is a task app that asks after the first task is scheduled. Android's examples are a bell tap, following an account, or placing an order. Airship's soft-prompt advice; Hawaiian Airlines raised opt-ins 23% with in-app education about 'Ready to Board' alerts (vendor case study).
patterns.howToApply: Trigger on the first 'That's my day'. Show the actual night-before notification for this address, then the OS dialog. After a denial, show 'Notifications are off' with Open Settings and promote the widget.
patterns.pitfalls: A second 'Yes' after the person already said yes; a primer styled like a system alert; benefit bullet lists; asking at cold launch.

patterns.name: Provisional (quiet) notification trial on iOS
patterns.exemplars: Apple's UNAuthorizationOptions.provisional: delivered only to Notification Center, with Keep / Turn Off controls on the notification itself.
patterns.howToApply: Optional path for T1 users who confirmed a pickup day but haven't answered the primer: the first night-before notice arrives quietly, and the person decides from the notification itself.
patterns.pitfalls: Provisional notices never reach the lock screen, so they are a weak return trigger. The in-app card and the widget must still carry the loop.

patterns.name: Status-based task list (GOV.UK)
patterns.exemplars: GOV.UK Complete multiple tasks and Task list: sentence-case statuses, completed items in plain text, 'Cannot start yet' in grey for dependent tasks, whole row clickable, task names starting with verbs, and 'simplify first'.
patterns.howToApply: Place file rows and the Today first-week row: verb-first asks, whole-row targets, done rows quiet, tier-locked rows grey with the reason ('Claim this address first') instead of a CTA.
patterns.pitfalls: Status tags that look like buttons; red for 'missing'; counting locked steps in the total.

patterns.name: Endowed first step
patterns.exemplars: Nunes & Drèze car-wash card with pre-stamped progress; Kivetz et al. coffee card (goal-gradient).
patterns.howToApply: If the first-week row uses a fraction, the save is already counted as step 1, the total is 4 or fewer, and the row names the next step.
patterns.pitfalls: Artificial progress that isn't real work (the save genuinely is); denominators that grow over time; fractions that cannot reach full at T1.

patterns.name: Empty state as the doorway
patterns.exemplars: NN/g cites DataDog ('Star your favorites to list them here'), Power BI's explanation of an empty recent-items list, and Loggly offering 'add a source' or 'explore demo data'.
patterns.howToApply: Your places empty state gets '+ Add a place'. The 14-day strip empty state shows drawn cells reading 'Checked — nothing…' with '+ Add a date'. The widget how-to with no snapshot shows a 'Sample' preview.
patterns.pitfalls: Illustration-only empty states; showing 'empty' before loading has finished; CTA labels that don't match their destination.

patterns.name: Final-slot skeleton plus receipt of checks
patterns.exemplars: NN/g skeleton screens (content-shaped, 2–10 s); Buell & Norton's operational transparency.
patterns.howToApply: Today warming fills each section as its provider returns. The quiet day shows four ticked checks with times. The place file year band reserves its height while loading.
patterns.pitfalls: Frame-only skeletons; a full-page spinner; an all-clear before every check succeeds; fake delays.

patterns.name: Asks placed inline in the sections they complete, instead of a separate checklist or modal
patterns.exemplars: Chameleon: click-triggered tours 67% completion versus 31% for timed ones; modals dismissed nearly 50% of the time; embedded asks get higher click-through (vendor data). NN/g recommends showing guidance when the person first meets a feature.
patterns.howToApply: pickup_day is done by 'That's my day' on the pickup card; important_date by '+ Add a date' in the strip; household by the household block; the return trigger by the briefing opt-in card or the widget row. The Today summary row only points at the next one.
patterns.pitfalls: Showing the same ask twice (summary row plus inline) with different dismissals; asks that present themselves automatically.

patterns.name: Promotion receipt with a per-item scope change and an explicit share choice
patterns.exemplars: GOV.UK confirmation pages (what happens next; receipts get bookmarked); ICO granular consent.
patterns.howToApply: Each carried row shows private → household glyphs. Dates stay 'Only you' until 'Share with the household' is tapped. The receipt stays reachable from the place file afterwards.
patterns.pitfalls: Past-tense copy that announces sharing before consent; a one-time banner as the only record; counts in the summary sentence that don't match the rows.

patterns.name: Permanent decline alongside 'Not now'
patterns.exemplars: Hacker News users object to prompts that offer only 'Yes' and 'Not now'. The v1 household block's 'Just me' and the keeper sheet's equal-weight 'Skip' already follow this.
patterns.howToApply: Every first-week ask has a decline that persists server-side and can be undone, plus a way back in (place file row, settings). 'Not now' never re-presents automatically.
patterns.pitfalls: 'Not now' that silently re-asks every session; declines stored only on the device.

antipatterns: Requesting notification permission at cold launch or before a place exists. Apple and Android guidance both say to ask in context, and NN/g reports that launch-time asks surprise and frustrate people.
A welcome carousel or deck-of-cards tutorial before Today. NN/g found these did not improve task performance and made the interface seem more complicated.
A second 'Yes' in a primer after the person already tapped 'Yes' on the opt-in card. It is a redundant decision, and Apple says context should make extra explanation unnecessary.
A pre-permission screen styled like the iOS or Android system alert, or a primer button labelled 'Allow' or 'Yes' when the grant happens in the OS dialog. Apple HIG says to use 'Continue' or 'Next'.
Blocking the save behind email verification with a link-only path. NN/g advises against email confirmation walls because of app and device switching and spam filtering.
Asking the person to retype an address the system already holds (WCAG 3.3.7 Redundant Entry), or letting a hold expire without saying how long it lasts (WCAG 2.2.6: 20 hours).
A progress fraction or ring whose total includes steps the person cannot complete at their tier. It is a stalled indicator, and slow-to-fast indicators increased drop-off in Villar et al.
Percent-complete bars or 'you are 60% done' framing for a list that has no natural end. Constant progress indicators did not reduce drop-off in the 32-experiment meta-analysis.
More than about four simultaneous first-week asks. Tour completion in Chameleon's data falls sharply beyond five steps, and Apple says to put off nonessential setup.
Onboarding asks as auto-presented modals. Chameleon reports nearly 50% dismissal for modals, versus higher engagement for embedded and click-triggered asks.
'Not now' as the only decline, with automatic re-asking. Users call this out as nagging, so pair it with a persistent decline and a way back in.
Setup-checklist ticks and dismissals stored only on the device. They come back on another device, which reads as nagging and undermines trust.
Flashing 'Nothing needs your attention' or 'No records' before every check has returned. NN/g says inaccurate status messages damage trust.
Full-page spinners or frame-only skeletons during warming. NN/g says to use content-shaped skeletons for 2–10 s loads.
Empty states with an illustration and no action, or a CTA whose label promises something the destination doesn't do ('Preview an address' opening a no-preview save sheet).
Sharing previously private dates at claim before the person chooses, or copy in the past tense ('are now visible') above the choice. ICO says inactivity is not consent.
Treating a toast as the only record of a consequential change (claim, sync merge, removal). Receipts get revisited, and status text must be announced (WCAG 4.1.3).
Confetti, badges or 'Congratulations' on save or claim. The product's receipts must be checkable facts, not celebration.
Offering a button that cannot work (for example 'Add widget for me'). No public API places widgets, so the only honest path is preview plus steps.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Entry points include 'tapping Yes on the briefing opt-in card on Today'. The primer then asks again with two equal-weight actions, 'Yes' / 'Not now', before the OS dialog.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG Privacy: if context already explains a permission request, no extra screen is needed. A custom pre-alert screen should have one action labelled like 'Continue'/'Next' that opens the system alert, with no way to leave and no 'Allow'-style wording. That passage is written for private-data permissions, so applying it to notifications is an inference. Android: show an educational screen only when shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale() is true. Apple's notification docs say to ask in context, as the opt-in card already does.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: When the entry is the opt-in card's 'Yes', skip the primer and fire the OS dialog directly. The card can carry the tray preview in its expanded state. Keep the primer for the first 'That's my day' and the Mail entry, relabel its forward action 'Continue' (or 'Turn on reminders'), and make clear the OS asks next. If 'Not now' stays, define it as never re-presenting on its own, and note the App Review risk. Evaluate iOS provisional authorization as the no-prompt alternative for the pickup entry.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The interstitial line is 'We're holding 1402 NE 3rd Ave for you. Verify your email to save it.' Verification is by emailed link only, with 'Resend the link'. The save depends on verification.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g's registration checklist advises against confirming registration through email, because switching apps and devices can stop users reaching their goal, and recommends codes. NN/g's passwordless article names app switching and spam filtering as costs of email links. Apple HIG says to delay sign-in and not block useful work. WCAG 3.3.8 accepts email links, but codes must be pasteable.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add a paste-enabled 6-digit code field to the interstitial so the laptop user can finish on the laptop, and keep the link as an alternative. Where the auth provider allows it, make the save happen at registration (server-held pending place becomes the saved place), so the copy reads 'Saved privately — confirm your email to keep your account'. If a hold can expire, state the length on the interstitial and keep it at least 20 hours (WCAG 2.2.6). Add a spam-folder hint next to Resend.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The 'Preview lost / expired / different device' frame is an empty focused 'Street address' field that the user retypes ('the value the user retypes'), on the premise that the address is device-local with a 24-hour life. The companion prompt, f1-email-verify-handoff, says the server now holds the pending place.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 Redundant Entry (Level A): information already entered in the same process must be auto-populated or selectable. The W3C note says it does not force storage across sessions, so the obligation is strongest while the server still holds the value. Firebase's anonymous-account linking shows the standard way to keep data created before sign-up.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Split the recovery frame into two. (1) Server holds the address: show it as a one-tap selectable row ('1402 NE 3rd Ave, Camas — Save it') with the field as a secondary 'Different address'. (2) Nothing held at all: the blank field as drawn. Update the WHY paragraph so it no longer describes the device-local draft as the normal cross-device case.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The consent block copy is 'The 2 dates you entered are now visible to everyone in this household.', placed above the two peer buttons 'Share with the household' / 'Keep them private to me'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: ICO valid-consent guidance says silence, pre-ticked options or inactivity are not consent, and consent must be an affirmative, granular choice. The prompt's own WHY says it should never be a silent migration. Past-tense copy tells the person the sharing has already happened before they choose.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Make the copy conditional and the default private: 'Share the 2 dates you entered with Sam and Dana?' The dates stay 'Only you' until 'Share with the household' is tapped, and leaving the screen without choosing keeps them private. Draw the per-row glyph pair as private → (household, pending) until the choice is made.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Besides the post-claim landing, the receipt appears 'once, as a dismissible banner at the top of the place file the first time it is opened after a claim'. No persistent place is specified for reviewing what moved or changing the sharing choice later.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: GOV.UK Confirmation pages: users treat confirmations as receipts, bookmark them, and should get a helpful response when they return. ICO: withdrawing consent should be as easy as giving it.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the one-time banner, and add a persistent route: a 'What moved when you claimed' entry in the place file (Place section or history) that renders the same manifest. Give each date a visibility control ('Only you' / 'Household') in the date sheet, so 'Keep them private' and 'Share' can be reversed at any time.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The count is 'a five-segment ring, one segment per category, a segment filled if anything is known in that category'. In the T1 saved-place frame, Money, People and Proof each render 'Not here — this is a saved place'. The ring's appearance at T1 is not specified, so by the stated rule it sits permanently at 2 of 5 segments.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Villar et al. (32 experiments): progress indicators that move slowly increased drop-off, and constant ones did not help. The endowed-progress and goal-gradient work shows motivation depends on a goal that is reachable and already under way. GOV.UK shows dependent tasks as 'Cannot start yet' in grey, not as incomplete. A ring that can never fill reads as a stalled completion meter, which the prompt itself forbids.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: At T1, draw only the segments reachable at that tier (Place and Dates), or draw the out-of-tier segments in a distinct 'not at this tier' treatment (dashed or absent) that cannot be read as unfilled. Add a T1 ring spec to frame 3, and keep the integer count as the primary reading.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The dense Today frame (a T1 'Saved place · Only you') ends with 'Progress row: "3 of 6 things on file →"'. x-place-file defines this as the Today entry for the first 14 days, while forbidding anything that reads as 'you are 60% complete'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: A fraction is a completion meter, and '3 of 6' reads as 50% complete. The design doc's F2 defines a three-question first week and says the banner must never show a step the person cannot complete at their tier. At T1, household requires a claim and verify requires a home. Villar et al.: stalled or slow indicators increase drop-off. Nunes & Drèze: a bounded set that has already started increases completion. Chameleon: 3–4 steps complete best.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Either drop the fraction ('Next: set your pickup day →', naming the one next ask), or use a bounded first-week set that follows the activation definition (Save ✓ · Pickup day · Reminder or widget · One date or person), with a denominator of 4 or fewer that counts only tier-reachable steps. Exclude verify, profile and photo. Make x-place-file and f1-today-tab use the same wording.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The dense T3 frame renders every missing fact as an ask with a CTA: insurance date, electricity, gas, water and sewer, ownership, plus three mover rows, a widget row and an invite Resend. That is about ten simultaneous calls to action on first open.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Chameleon (vendor, 550M+ interactions): completion drops sharply beyond about five steps, with 3–4 step flows completing best. Apple HIG says to put off nonessential setup. NN/g Progressive Disclosure says to show up front only what is frequently needed and put the rest behind a clear control. GOV.UK says to simplify before listing tasks.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Promote at most three asks at a time as real CTAs, chosen by the activation order (pickup day, return trigger, one date or person), with mover rows only inside their 60-day window. Render other missing facts as quiet rows with a text 'Add' affordance, or behind a 'More you can add (5)' disclosure inside each category. Keep missing facts as invitations, as the prompt says, but cap how many compete for attention.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The sheet is reached from 'Today's empty state CTA "Preview an address"', and the sheet explicitly has no preview ('no map… no grade… this sheet's only claim is "bookmark it"'). The design doc's F1 routes the same label to /start, which this sheet forbids.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g Progressive Disclosure: use labels that set clear expectations for what users will find. NN/g empty states: give a direct path to the task that fills the empty state. A button that promises a preview and opens a save-only sheet breaks that expectation.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Rename the Today empty-state CTA (and the 'Save an address to see today here' landings) to 'Add a place' or 'Save an address' when it opens this sheet. Keep 'Preview an address' only for an entry that actually goes to the /start preview. Update f1-today-tab's frame 1 copy to match.

numbers: Response-time limits (NN/g): 0.1 s feels instant; 1 s keeps flow; 10 s is the limit of attention, and beyond it show a percent-done indicator.
Skeleton screens (NN/g): use for full-page loads of about 2–10 s; not for loads under about 1 s; use a progress bar over 10 s; never frame-only skeletons.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.6 Timeouts (AAA): keep user-entered data for more than 20 hours, or warn about the inactivity length that loses it. Use this as the floor for how long a held pre-signup address lasts.
WCAG 2.2 SC 3.3.7 Redundant Entry is Level A (the minimum conformance level); SC 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication (Minimum) is AA, and email links satisfy it (G218); codes must be pasteable.

Baymard (current list page): 18% of US online shoppers abandoned a checkout because the site wanted them to create an account. Other Baymard editions are quoted at 19% and 26%, so the number varies by survey wave.
Duolingo (Gina Gotthilf, First Round Review): moving the sign-up screen back a few steps gave about a 20% increase in DAU. Self-reported, not peer-reviewed.
NN/g permission requests: +12% grant rate when a reason is given; the most compelling reason got an 81% lift over the least compelling.

Chameleon (vendor, 550M+ interactions): 3-step tours 72% completion, 4-step 74%, 7+ step 16%; click-triggered 67% vs set-delay 31%; tours launched from checklists 67%; modals dismissed nearly 50%; 23% of users click inside checklists (27% after a welcome state). The two Chameleon pages disagree slightly on the best step count (3 vs 4).
Userpilot onboarding-checklist completion: average 19.2%, median 10.1%, across 188 companies. UNVERIFIED: the primary page returned 403 and the figures come only from a search snippet.

Nunes & Drèze 2006 (JCR 32(4):504–512): endowed progress (10 steps with 2 done vs 8 steps with none) raises completion and speed. The commonly quoted 34% vs 19% car-wash redemption comes from secondary sources; the abstract confirms only the direction.

Villar, Callegaro & Yang 2013 (Social Science Computer Review 31(6)): meta-analysis of 32 randomized experiments. A constant progress indicator did not significantly reduce drop-off; fast-to-slow reduced it; slow-to-fast increased it; with small incentives, a constant indicator increased drop-off.

Airship 2025 push benchmarks (vendor): in-app messages raise opt-in among opted-out users by 14% on average; onboarding campaigns reach up to 40% above category-average opt-in; Hawaiian Airlines +23% opt-ins with in-app education. Third-party summaries quote medians of 44.5% for iOS and about 71% for Android; UNVERIFIED, because the PDF chart text could not be reliably mapped.
Android POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission applies from API 33 (Android 13); show educational UI only when shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale() returns true.
iOS provisional authorization: delivered quietly to Notification Center history only (no sound, banner or lock screen), with Keep / Turn Off controls.

First-week ask budget: 3–4 bounded asks, one already done (the save); count only tier-reachable steps. The design doc's activation window is 7 days, while x-place-file shows the Today progress row for 14 days. Align the two.
Minimum hold for a server-held pre-signup address: at least 20 hours (WCAG 2.2.6); if it expires, state the length in visible text on the interstitial.

topic: glanceable-today-widgets: home-screen widgets (iOS WidgetKit, Android app widgets), daily summary screens, stale and partial data, deep-link landings, and teaching people that a widget exists

principles.principle: Each widget size uses a different form, not the smaller widget's content stretched to fill more space. If a size cannot be done well, leave it out rather than pad it.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG, Widgets: 'Avoid expanding a smaller widget's content to simply fill a larger area. It's more important to create one widget in the size that best represents the content than providing the widget in all sizes.' It also says to keep every size centred on one purpose while widening the range of information (the Calendar example). WWDC20 'Design great widgets': 'make sure not to scale up your smaller widget into your larger widget.' Android's app-widget overview gives a weather example: 3x2 shows location, temperature and symbol; 5x2 adds a label and an hourly forecast; 5x4 adds a multi-day forecast.
principles.implication: Keep v1's plan: small sells one fact, medium sells the 14-day strip, large sells the year. Keep each size about 'what is due at this address' and only widen the time range (today, then 14 days, then 12 months). If the large year strip cannot be made legible at 338x354pt (see the size principle), ship small and medium first, as the design doc already plans for iOS, and leave large out instead of filling it with extra text rows.

principles.principle: A small widget holds at most four pieces of information and has exactly one tap target, which opens the fact it shows.
principles.evidence: WWDC20 'Design great widgets': 'We recommend only including a max of four pieces of information in the small widget size' and 'The small widget supports a single tap target. Tapping it should deep link to the content that's on the widget.' HIG: 'Small widgets use their limited space to typically show a single piece of information.'
principles.implication: v1's small widget (kind glyph, line, provenance mark, place label) is exactly four pieces. Add nothing to it: no AQI chip, no date, no logo. Its one widgetURL should open the surface of whichever fact the urgency ladder chose. A pickup hero opens the pickup lead card; an AQI hero opens Today scrolled to the air band. It should not always open the top of Today.

principles.principle: Draw widgets at the real point sizes for the device in the frame, and design Android widgets as responsive layouts that are checked at their minimum cell sizes.
principles.evidence: HIG specification table: on a 393x852 screen (iPhone 15/16 Pro) small is 158x158pt, medium 338x158pt and large 338x354pt. Lock Screen sizes are circular 72x72, rectangular 160x72 and inline 234x26. The sizes 170x170 / 364x170 / 364x382 belong to 430x932 and 428x926 screens (Pro Max). Android handheld defaults: 2x2 is 109–306dp wide by 115–276dp tall; 4x2 is 245–624dp wide by 115–276dp tall. The widths depend on the launcher, so Android requires breakpoints and responsive containers.
principles.implication: Redraw every iOS widget frame and the how-to preview at 158 / 338x158 / 338x354pt on the 393x852 canvas. The v1 sizes are about 8% too wide and 7% too tall, so a layout that fits there will clip on a real device. For Android, draw the 4x2 at its minimum of 245x115dp as well as the roughly 330x150dp comfortable case. The 14-cell strip and the band-bar must survive the minimum size.

principles.principle: Widget text is never smaller than 11pt, is never rasterised, and must work across Dynamic Type sizes Large through AX5. Layout geometry comes from that text floor, not the other way round.
principles.evidence: HIG: 'In general, display text using fonts at 11 points or larger. Text in a font that's smaller than 11 points can be too hard for many people to read.' 'Avoid rasterizing text.' Widgets support Dynamic Type from Large to AX5. HIG margins: a standard 16pt, or 11pt for grouped graphics.
principles.implication: At 11pt, one weekday initial needs about 10–11pt of width, so 14 initials need a cell pitch of at least about 20pt. That means the strip needs about 290pt or more, which is the full content width of a medium widget (338 − 2×16 = 306pt). The alternative is to label only 'Today' and the first day of each week. A 120pt strip with an initial under every 6pt cell cannot be built at legal type sizes. Draw one AX-size frame to show what gets dropped first (the band-bar row goes before the place label).

principles.principle: Meaning must survive tinted, clear, vibrant (Lock Screen / StandBy at night) and monochrome rendering, where hue is removed and only shape, position, opacity and text remain.
principles.evidence: Apple, 'Optimizing your widget for accented rendering mode and Liquid Glass': in tinted or clear appearance the system 'Tints opaque images with a single white color', 'Maintains opacity for transparent content and gradients, and tints them white', and 'Removes the background'. HIG: 'Convey meaning without relying on specific colors… Use text and iconography in addition to color.' In vibrant mode (Lock Screen, and StandBy in low light with a red tint), brightness sets contrast, and the guidance is to 'use opaque grayscale values, rather than opacities of white'.
principles.implication: In tinted mode the six EPA hues all become white, the class colours (pickup, civic, money, yours) disappear, and the weekend tint survives only if it is drawn as reduced opacity. So: (a) keep provenance as filled / hollow / filled-with-tick; (b) separate band segments with visible gaps and print the category name next to the number; (c) draw weekend cells as a lower-opacity fill, not a hue; (d) mark the hero glyph and the marker `widgetAccentable` so they carry the accent group. The tinted frames (18–19) should also show the band-bar and the strip, not only the marks.

principles.principle: When data is old, show the last known values with their age. Never hide them behind a placeholder or a blank. Judge staleness per fact, not for the whole widget.
principles.evidence: HIG: 'show content quickly without hiding stale data behind placeholder content' and 'If people are likely to check your widget more frequently than you can update it, consider displaying text that describes when the data was last updated.' Android widget quality puts 'Content consistently stale or untimely' (WT-3) in the low-quality tier. Apple Community users complained when the Weather widget replaced good data with 'No weather data available'. (WWDC20 advised against 'last updated' wording; the 2025 HIG text above is newer and says the opposite.)
principles.implication: Pickup cadence and the user's dates are rules that stay valid for weeks. Render them normally from the stored ISO dates, with day words computed at render time, until the snapshot's horizon runs out. AQI is the perishable fact: show its observation time ('7:00 am') and grey only that row once it is old. When the whole snapshot is past its horizon, grey everything and state the snapshot time ('As of Mon 7:40 am'); 'Open to refresh' can be the second line. Never swap any value for a blank.

principles.principle: Plan widget refreshes within the WidgetKit budget. Schedule timeline entries at the moments the content actually changes, and write the snapshot whenever the app is in the foreground, because those reloads cost nothing.
principles.evidence: Apple, 'Keeping a widget up to date': a frequently viewed widget typically gets '40 to 70 refreshes' a day, 'roughly… every 15 to 60 minutes'. Entries should be 'at least about 5 minutes apart'. Reloads while 'The widget's containing app is in the foreground' do not count against the budget. Rarely viewed Home Screen pages get fewer reloads. The same page recommends generating 'a timeline for as many future dates as possible'. 'Displaying dynamic dates' shows that Text(date, style:) views keep updating without a reload.
principles.implication: Emit timeline entries at each local midnight for the next 14 days, and at the evening boundary where 'Bins out tonight' becomes true, instead of a blanket 30-minute `.after` policy. Write the snapshot and call reloadTimelines on every Today load, which the widget-tap landing's forced refresh already does. Render any 'as of' age with system relative-date text so it stays current for free.

principles.principle: A tap opens the exact thing that was tapped. Medium and large widgets may have several link regions, and the landing must show the tapped fact without the user scrolling for it.
principles.evidence: HIG: 'Ensure that a widget interaction opens your app at the right location… don't make people navigate to the relevant area.' Its example is the medium Stocks widget opening the tapped symbol. Apple 'Linking to specific app scenes': systemSmall and larger can use one widgetURL plus Link controls; a tap on a Link uses that link's URL. HIG also warns: 'avoid creating app-like layouts… make sure people can tap… with confidence'. Android quality WS-5 asks for the system launch transition when entering the app from a widget; Android 12+ enables it with @android:id/background.
principles.implication: Medium widget: two regions at most, each at least 44pt tall on iOS and 48dp on Android. The hero opens its own surface (pickup card, or the air band scrolled into view); the strip and band row open Today's 14-day strip. Large widget: the year strip opens the place file's year band. The landing (f7-widget-tap-landing) gets a `section` parameter alongside `src=widget`, scrolls to that section and briefly highlights it, as the reminder push already does for the 14-day strip.

principles.principle: A quiet or empty result has to be visibly finished. Say what was checked, and never show 'nothing' until every check has returned.
principles.evidence: NN/g, 'Designing Empty States in Complex Applications': 'Totally empty states cause confusion about how and whether the system is working.' It also warns that showing 'No records' and then filling in content moments later damages trust. HIG, Loading: 'If you make people wait for loading to complete before displaying anything, they can interpret the lack of content as a problem.'
principles.implication: Keep three states that look different on every surface. Loading uses skeleton shapes in their final slots. Checked-and-empty uses drawn cells and a receipt of ticks ('weather · air · alerts · your calendar'). Failed shows no strip, or a greyed bar with no marker, plus a named retry. The widget's 'nothing due' (cells drawn, no dots) must never look like 'stale' (greyed dots) or like 'no snapshot' (the placeholder).

principles.principle: Report partial failure per component: name the source that failed and keep everything else live. An overall 'all clear' needs every component to be healthy.
principles.evidence: Atlassian Statuspage gives each component its own status ('Operational', 'Degraded performance', 'Partial outage', 'Major outage', 'Under maintenance'), so an outage is attributed to one component instead of taking down the whole page. NN/g, 'Visibility of system status': 'Systems should always keep users informed about what is going on, through appropriate feedback within reasonable time.'
principles.implication: Each tick in Today's receipt line has its own state (ticked, 'couldn't reach AirNow', or pending), and the heading 'Nothing needs your attention today' appears only when all four are ticked. In the widget, a missing air reading removes that row and rebalances the layout (v1 frame 7). It never marks the whole widget as failed.

principles.principle: Refresh a screen that already has content in place. Use skeletons only for a cold, full-page load, and skip indicators for waits under a second.
principles.evidence: NN/g, 'Skeleton Screens 101': no indicator below 1 second, skeletons or spinners for 2–10 seconds, progress bars above 10 seconds. Skeletons suit full-page loads, and frame-only skeletons 'function as a spinner'. HIG, Loading: 'Show something as soon as possible… Let people do other things… while they wait.'
principles.implication: This supports v1's widget-tap landing: a 2pt hairline plus a persistent 'Updating… / Updated just now' line, no dimming, and a skeleton only on cold start. Add one rule: if the forced refresh finishes in under about 1 second, skip the hairline and only update the freshness line, so the landing does not flicker.

principles.principle: Put the most important fact first and keep the widget's priority and the landing's priority consistent.
principles.evidence: NN/g, 'Inverted pyramid': lead with the most important information, because users scan and stop early, so they can 'stop reading at any point… and still come away with the main point.' Blascheck et al. cite prior work showing 'a vast majority of smartwatch interactions last under 5s', which is the attention budget of a glance.
principles.implication: The widget's urgency ladder (pickup within 1 day > AQI ≥ 101 > nearest date) is the right way to choose a hero. Today's fixed section order puts air and alerts sixth and seventh. When a threshold is crossed, that fact must appear above the fold on Today for every arrival (widget, organic, push), not only for push arrivals. The simplest way is to reuse the pinned-briefing slot.

principles.principle: Use simple linear marks for data meant to be read at a glance; radial forms read slowly.
principles.evidence: Blascheck et al. (IEEE TVCG 2019), two perception studies on smartwatches with 7, 12 and 24 values: a comparison task took on average under 300 ms for bar charts, under 220 ms for donut charts and under 1780 ms for radial bar charts. The authors recommend bars and donuts when quick comparison is needed. The studies were lab tasks on watches, so they indicate direction, not a spec.
principles.implication: This supports v1's choices of a 14-cell linear strip, a linear AQI band-bar and 12 month columns, and its ban on completion rings. The strip holds 14 values, which falls between the tested 12 and 24, so keep its encoding minimal: one dot shape per event, a cap of three dots, and no second colour channel in the widget.

principles.principle: The AQI display uses EPA's category name together with its colour, and its segments need a non-colour boundary because several EPA hues fail 3:1 contrast against the card.
principles.evidence: EPA AQI Technical Assistance Document (May 2026): reports must give the AQI value, the 'category descriptor and color (if your report uses color)'. It fixes the standard RGB values (Green 0,228,0; Yellow 255,255,0; Orange 255,126,0; Red 255,0,0; Purple 143,63,151; Maroon 126,0,35) and allows 'ColorVision Assist' colours for colour-vision deficiency. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for graphics needed to understand content, unless visible text conveys the same information. My own calculation from those RGB values: against white, Yellow is 1.07:1, Green 1.74:1 and Orange 2.55:1. Against the dark raised surface #1E293B, Maroon is 1.33:1 and Purple 2.32:1. Adjacent bands are 1.57–2.37:1 against each other.
principles.implication: Always print the category name next to the number (in the widget too, where short forms like 'Sensitive groups' are acceptable). Give the bar a border-token outline and 1pt gaps between segments. Give the marker 3:1 contrast against both the segment under it and the card. Consider EPA's ColorVision Assist set as the sanctioned variant; it keeps the same hue families.

principles.principle: The widget gallery preview must be realistic, fully populated and the correct size. Its description begins with a verb and never mentions 'this widget'.
principles.evidence: HIG: 'Design a realistic preview… You can display real data in your widget preview, but if the data takes too long to generate or load, display realistic simulated data instead.' 'Begin a description with an action verb — for example, "See the current weather conditions…"' and 'Avoid… phrases that reference the widget itself.' Group all sizes under one description. Android discovery guidance: previews must be 'accurate to the widget size', must use dynamic colours if the widget does, and a missing preview shows only the app icon. Android quality tier 1 (WD-1): 'Preview includes user content and/or applies system theme.' Android 15 adds generated previews through setWidgetPreview, rate-limited to about two calls per hour.
principles.implication: Keep the baked sample as the default and the no-place preview. Once a real snapshot exists, allow the user's own data: on iOS the snapshot is a fast local App Group read, and on Android 15+ it can be a generated preview pushed after the first Today load. Draw the Android picker frames in dynamic colour. Rewrite the description to start with a verb, for example 'See pickup day, air quality and your next date at your address.'

principles.principle: Promote the widget inside the app at a moment of success, without getting in the way. On Android, place it with the pin API. On iOS, teach the current gestures with pictures.
principles.evidence: Android: from API 26, `requestPinAppWidget()` shows a system dialog, with a preview on Glance, and the app is told only if the pin succeeded. Guidance: present the option 'After a user successfully completes a task that has a corresponding widget', use 'subtle visual hints', and 'should never block or hinder the user's primary actions.' Duolingo reports that widget installs 'skyrocketed' after adding in-app prompts and animated installation guides after a lesson. iOS has no pin API. Apple Support gives the current steps as: 'touch and hold… until the apps jiggle. Tap the Edit button in the upper-left corner. Tap Add Widget.' HIG, Offering help: prefer 'animation or graphics to educate', 'If a feature requires more than three actions, it's probably too complicated for a tip', and show tips at a reasonable cadence, for example 'once every 24 hours'. NN/g, onboarding: 'tutorials didn't improve task performance'; help given in context at teachable moments works better.
principles.implication: Android how-to sheet: the main button is 'Add to home screen' when isRequestPinAppWidgetSupported() is true, and the gesture steps are the fallback. iOS how-to sheet: three illustrated steps using the current 'Edit → Add Widget' wording, drawn generically enough to survive OS changes. Triggers: right after 'That's my day' confirms a pickup, and after push is declined. Show at most one promotion in 24 hours, never as a blocking modal.

principles.principle: On iOS, feed Smart Stack relevance so the widget rises when something is due. This is the only system channel on iOS, besides the gallery, that surfaces a widget.
principles.evidence: Apple, 'Widget Suggestions in Smart Stacks': on iPhone and iPad, timeline entries carry a TimelineEntryRelevance score and duration; 'When the date of an entry arrives, and for the duration you specify, WidgetKit may rotate your widget to the top of the Smart Stack'. A score of 0 or below means not relevant. Donated PredictableIntents let the system 'automatically suggest your widget' when no matching widget is in a stack.
principles.implication: Give high relevance to the evening before pickup and to AQI ≥ 101 entries, and a score of 0 to quiet days, so a stacked widget comes up only when it has something to say. This matches the product's 'silence is a designed state' rule. Donate an intent when the user opens Today so the system can suggest the widget.

principles.principle: The small widget also has to work in StandBy and CarPlay (no background, scaled up, red-tinted at night). The Lock Screen rectangular accessory is the most glanceable place for a one-line fact.
principles.evidence: HIG: in StandBy, 'the system displays two small system family widgets side-by-side, scaled up'. The guidance is to 'Limit usage of rich images or color', and 'don't use background colors for your widget when it appears in StandBy'. In low light, widgets are drawn 'in a monochromatic look with a red tint'. Apple's StandBy/CarPlay page says to make the background removable and use larger type, or declare disfavoredLocations. Lock Screen widgets use vibrant rendering, and the guidance is to 'Provide useful information… don't treat it only as an additional way… to launch'.
principles.implication: Add a StandBy frame for the small widget with no background, larger type and the provenance shape in grayscale. Otherwise, explicitly declare StandBy and CarPlay as disfavoured. Consider a 160x72pt accessoryRectangular for 'Recycling tomorrow · Bins out tonight' as a later, low-cost addition. It reuses the small widget's content and needs no new permission.

principles.principle: Android widgets follow Material system coherence: dynamic colour, light and dark themes, the system corner radius, full grid bounds and 48dp touch targets.
principles.evidence: Android widget quality tier 1: WC-1 'Supports color theming based on device or app context', WC-2 light and dark, WS-2 system-provided corner radius, WL-1.1 rectangular widgets touch all four grid edges, WL-2 resizable to at least one of 2x2/4x1/4x2. Tier 2: WL-4.2 minimum size meets 48x48dp touch targets. 'Enhance' page: dynamic colour needs API 31 or higher (Theme.Material3.DynamicColors.DayNight), with a fallback theme below that; corner radius at most 28dp.
principles.implication: Android widget chrome (background, hero text, strip cells) uses Material dynamic roles (surface, primary, primaryContainer) on API 31 and above, with Pantopus tokens as the fallback theme. Provenance shapes and EPA hues stay fixed because they carry meaning. Draw one Android frame with a non-blue wallpaper theme.

principles.principle: Freshness labels use relative time for recency. Future deadlines show relative and absolute dates together.
principles.evidence: Cloudscape timestamps pattern: 'Since relative dates are easier to read, we recommend using them in most situations.' It gives granularities 'Now' (0–59 s), '# minutes ago', '# hours ago'. It recommends absolute human-readable dates when 'Users need a specific date and time for when an event occurred or will occur'.
principles.implication: 'Updated just now / 12m ago / 2h ago' is right for the Today header. Calendar rows further out than tomorrow should read 'in 11 days · Fri 30 Oct', because a lease notice or tax deadline is acted on by its date. Everything is computed at render and never stored as a string.

principles.principle: A widget that states one concrete daily fact can work as a return trigger that needs no permission, but only after people know the widget exists.
principles.evidence: Duolingo's widget shows streak length and whether today's lesson is done. Duolingo found 'simply reminding a learner of their current streak, and whether or not it's at risk, is hugely valuable', and that 'Half of the learners with the widget installed have a streak of at least 6 months'. Duolingo says widget learners retained better even after accounting for selection bias. Installs rose sharply only after in-app prompts were added. (A widely repeated '60% increase in commitment' figure comes from secondary blogs and could not be verified at the source.)
principles.implication: The widget's one fact should be binary and time-bound in the way Duolingo's streak is: 'Bins out tonight' or nothing due. The funnel event that matters is widget installs driven by the how-to sheet. Pilot metrics should measure `session_open{trigger:widget}` separately from snapshot writes.

patterns.name: Urgency-ladder hero (one fact wins)
patterns.exemplars: Duolingo's widget shows streak and whether it is at risk, and Duo's mood grows more desperate towards midnight (blog.duolingo.com/widget-feature). Google At a Glance always shows the date and adds events, severe-weather warnings, tickets or commute information only when they are relevant (support.google.com/pixelphone/answer/14884067). Apple's Weather widget puts current conditions and high/low first (HIG).
patterns.howToApply: Keep v1's single ordered ladder (pickup ≤1 day > AQI ≥101 > nearest date > any pickup > any AQI) and share it across the small widget hero, the medium hero, Smart Stack relevance scores, and Today's pinned slot, so the widget and the landing agree on what matters most.
patterns.pitfalls: A chore (pickup) must not fill the hero on a day when nothing is due; v1 already forbids this. The ladder must not reorder the in-app sections, which confuses people; use a pinned slot instead.

patterns.name: Pre-rendered timeline from a stored snapshot
patterns.exemplars: Apple's 'Keeping a widget up to date' shows a game-health widget planned as hourly entries, a stock widget with no reloads over the weekend, and system Text(date, style:) that updates without reloads.
patterns.howToApply: When the app writes the snapshot, the provider generates entries at every local midnight for 14 days, plus the evening-before-pickup boundary. Each entry recomputes 'Tomorrow / Tonight / Thu 1 Oct' from ISO dates, and only AQI ages. The widget stays truthful for days without the app being opened.
patterns.pitfalls: Storing `days_until` or preformatted strings. A blanket `.after(+30 min)` spends the 40–70/day budget without changing anything. Server stampedes if many devices reload at the same fixed time (Apple warns about this for after(_:) dates).

patterns.name: Receipt-style all-clear with per-component state
patterns.exemplars: Atlassian Statuspage lists each component with its own status (Operational, Degraded performance, Partial outage, Major outage); NN/g recommends messages that confirm the system finished and found nothing.
patterns.howToApply: Today's quiet day is a heading plus four small checks (weather · air · alerts · your calendar). Each check can be ticked, failed ('Couldn't reach AirNow · Retry') or pending. The heading appears only when all four are ticked. The 14-day strip's empty state follows the same logic with drawn cells and 'Checked — nothing in the next two weeks'.
patterns.pitfalls: Showing the all-clear while a provider is still loading, then replacing it (NN/g says this damages trust). Illustrations or cheerful 'all done!' tone, which read as a generic empty state, not a verified result.

patterns.name: Refresh in place with a persistent freshness line
patterns.exemplars: NN/g skeleton guidance limits skeletons to full-page loads; HIG Loading says to show something immediately; Cloudscape's relative-time granularity ('Now', '# minutes ago').
patterns.howToApply: On widget arrival, content already on screen stays. A 2pt hairline runs only if the refresh takes 1 second or longer. The header line reads 'Updating…', then 'Updated just now', then ages. A failure keeps the content and shows 'Couldn't refresh · Retry'.
patterns.pitfalls: A toast that disappears, leaving no proof the refresh ran. Dimming or reflowing cards. A skeleton on a warm screen.

patterns.name: Region deep links with a scroll-and-highlight landing
patterns.exemplars: The medium Stocks widget opens the tapped symbol (HIG). Apple's Emoji Rangers leaderboard widget gives each row its own Link (Apple, 'Linking to specific app scenes'). Android supports per-view click intents and the system launch transition (WS-5).
patterns.howToApply: Use `pantopus://today?src=widget&section=pickup|strip|air|year`. Today scrolls to the section and highlights it once, as the reminder push already does for strip rows. The small widget uses one widgetURL chosen by the hero's kind.
patterns.pitfalls: Too many small targets in a 158pt-tall medium widget (keep each at least 44pt / 48dp). Landing at the top of Today when the tapped fact sits below the fold. More than one widgetURL in the hierarchy, which Apple calls undefined behaviour.

patterns.name: Shape-first provenance that survives tinted and vibrant rendering
patterns.exemplars: Apple's accented mode keeps opacity and shape but flattens hue to white. HIG: 'Use text and iconography in addition to color.' WCAG 1.4.11 allows flat indicators if they contrast with adjacent colours.
patterns.howToApply: Use filled for official, hollow for unconfirmed and filled-with-tick for user-entered, at a size where the tick is still readable (see numbers). Weekend cells use opacity, not hue. Band segments are separated by gaps, and the category name is printed.
patterns.pitfalls: 6pt dots with an interior tick that turn into a smudge. Using class colour as the only difference between pickup and civic items in the widget.

patterns.name: In-app widget promotion at a teachable moment
patterns.exemplars: Duolingo shows an animated install guide after a lesson, and installs 'skyrocketed'. Android's requestPinAppWidget opens a system pin dialog with a preview (API 26+). Android guidance says to promote after a related task is completed, subtly and without blocking.
patterns.howToApply: After 'That's my day' confirms a pickup, or after push is declined, show a one-line inline hint that opens the how-to sheet. On Android, the sheet's main button calls the pin API. On iOS, the sheet shows the user's own preview and three illustrated gestures with the current 'Edit → Add Widget' wording.
patterns.pitfalls: On iOS, an 'Add it for me' button that cannot work. On Android, withholding the button the API supports. Screenshots of a specific OS menu. Repeating the prompt more than once per 24 hours. A modal that blocks the pickup confirmation.

patterns.name: Populated, correctly sized, placeholder-aware gallery preview
patterns.exemplars: HIG says a realistic preview may use real data and that placeholders are 'static interface components with semi-opaque shapes'. Android 15 generated previews can carry user content. Android warns that a missing preview falls back to the app icon.
patterns.howToApply: Use a baked sample (half-full strip, AQI 42 low in Good, nine year markers) as the default and the no-place preview. Switch to the real snapshot when one exists. The redacted placeholder keeps cells, segments and lane rules drawn. Android picker frames use dynamic colour.
patterns.pitfalls: An empty state as the advertisement ('Save an address…'). A size whose preview is emptier than the size below it. Device frames or marketing gloss.

patterns.name: Relevance-scored Smart Stack rotation
patterns.exemplars: Apple's TimelineEntryRelevance score and duration can rotate a widget to the top of a Smart Stack; a score of 0 or below means not relevant. Donated PredictableIntents enable system widget suggestions.
patterns.howToApply: High score from 5 pm on the evening before pickup until pickup morning, and while AQI ≥ 101. Medium score for a date within 3 days. Zero on quiet days. Donate an intent each time Today is opened.
patterns.pitfalls: A constant high score, which the system learns to ignore and which contradicts the 'silence is designed' rule. Relevance based on data the snapshot does not actually hold.

antipatterns: Replacing last-known widget content with a blank or 'No data' placeholder when a refresh is late. HIG says not to hide stale data behind placeholders, and Apple Community users reported the Weather widget doing exactly this.

Greying the whole widget after a fixed age when most of its facts are rule-based and still true. This turns the one permission-free return trigger into Android's low-quality tier (WT-3 'consistently stale').
Storing preformatted relative strings ('in 3 days', 'Tomorrow') in the snapshot. They become false at midnight; compute them at render from ISO dates with timeline entries at day boundaries.
A blanket 30-minute refresh policy. It spends the 40–70/day WidgetKit budget on reloads that change nothing and still misses the midnight flip.
Scaling the small widget's content up to fill the medium or large size (HIG, WWDC20).
Text under 11pt or rasterised text in any widget. It fails HIG and breaks Dynamic Type Large–AX5 and VoiceOver.
Using hue alone for meaning in a widget (class colours, EPA bands, weekend tint). Tinted and clear modes turn every opaque colour white.
Showing the AQI band-bar with no category name. EPA requires the category descriptor with the colour, and several EPA hues are below 3:1 against white or dark surfaces.

Radial or ring gauges, progress bars, percentages or letter grades for glance data. Radial bars took up to about 1.8 s to read against under 0.3 s for bars (Blascheck et al.), and grades imply a judgement the product does not make.
Sending every widget tap to the top of Today when the tapped fact (AQI, a date) sits below the fold (HIG: don't make people navigate).
More than one widgetURL in a widget view hierarchy (Apple: undefined behaviour), or tap regions under 44pt (iOS) or 48dp (Android).
Using the live layout, or an empty or sign-in state, as the widget gallery preview. It sells the empty state instead of the widget.
Gallery descriptions that start with a noun list or with 'This widget shows…' (HIG: begin with an action verb).
On iOS, an 'Install widget / Add it for me' button (no API exists). On Android, leaving out the pin button that requestPinAppWidget supports.
Version-specific OS menu wording or screenshots in how-to content. iOS has already changed from the '+' button to 'Edit → Add Widget', and a wrong label is worse than none.
Blocking modals or repeated widget promotions (Android: never block primary actions; HIG tips: roughly once per 24 hours at most).
Skeletons, dimming or spinners over a screen that already shows content on the widget path. Skeletons are for full-page cold loads (NN/g).
Showing 'Nothing needs your attention' before every provider has returned, then filling content in (NN/g: this damages trust).
Logos, app names or word marks inside the widget (WWDC20; HIG says brand elements should be subtle).
Background colours or full-colour imagery in StandBy (HIG: blend with the black background; night mode is red monochrome).
Mirroring the widget as an interactive-looking card elsewhere in the app (HIG: an element that looks like the widget but doesn't behave like it confuses people).

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Frame sizes for iOS drawn on a 393x852 home screen: systemSmall 170x170pt, systemMedium 364x170pt, systemLarge 364x382pt.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG specification table: on a 393x852 screen, small is 158x158, medium 338x158 and large 338x354. The 170/364/382 values apply to 430x932 and 428x926 (Pro Max) screens.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw at 158x158 / 338x158 / 338x354pt on the 393x852 canvas, or switch the canvas to 430x932 if the larger size is wanted. Check that the strip, band-bar and year lanes still fit at the smaller size.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: MEDIUM: a 14-day dot strip of '14 equal cells, ~6pt each, ~120pt wide… weekday initial under each cell'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG: display text at 11pt or larger, and support Dynamic Type from Large to AX5. At 11pt a weekday initial needs about 10–11pt of width, but a 120pt strip gives about 8.6pt per cell. Distinguishing filled, hollow and ticked marks also needs marks larger than 6pt (WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 for graphics needed to understand the content).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Run the strip across the full medium content width (about 306pt, a pitch of about 21pt) with dots of about 8–10pt, or keep it narrow and label only 'Today' and each week start. Add an AX Dynamic Type frame.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Staleness: after 6h the whole widget greys its marks with 'Open to refresh' (frames 11–12), matching the design doc's single 6h rule.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG: show content 'without hiding stale data behind placeholder content' and 'consider displaying text that describes when the data was last updated'. Pickup cadence and user dates are rules that stay valid for weeks and can be rendered truthfully from timeline entries. Android quality marks 'consistently stale' widgets as low quality.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Judge staleness per fact. Calendar and pickup render normally until the snapshot horizon (for example 14 days) runs out. AQI shows its observation time and greys on its own once it is more than a few hours old. Grey everything only past the horizon, and label that state with the snapshot time ('As of Mon 7:40 am') before 'Open to refresh'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: IA + ENTRY: 'A tap deep-links to the Today tab' for every size and every region.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG: interactions should open the app at the location related to the content, as in the Stocks medium widget. WidgetKit supports one widgetURL plus Link regions on systemSmall and larger.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Small: the widgetURL targets the hero's own section. Medium: two link regions, the hero and then the strip plus air, each at least 44pt / 48dp. Large: the year strip links to the place file year band. Pass `section=` to the landing.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: House style applied to the widget: every colour is a Pantopus semantic token, and Android frames use the same sky-blue tokens.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android widget quality tier 1 requires colour theming from the device (WC-1, dynamic colour on API 31+), and Android's discovery guidance asks for previews in dynamic colours if the widget supports them.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: On Android 12+, draw widget chrome with Material dynamic roles (surface, primary, primaryContainer) and keep Pantopus tokens as the fallback theme. Provenance shapes and EPA band hues stay fixed. Add one Android frame with a non-blue wallpaper palette.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: STATES TO DRAW cover full colour, dark, and tinted/accented for small and medium, but no StandBy/CarPlay or vibrant frame.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple: WidgetKit automatically uses the systemSmall widget in StandBy and CarPlay, with the background removed and scaled up, and in red monochrome in low light. The widget should either support that (removable background, larger type, no colour-dependent meaning) or be declared disfavored.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add a StandBy frame (black ground, no background, grayscale provenance shapes, larger type) plus a low-light red variant, or record an explicit decision to mark StandBy and CarPlay as disfavoredLocations.
