contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'No public API can place a widget for the user'. DO NOT add an 'Add it for me', 'Install widget' or 'Take me there' button. Android gets the same three gesture steps.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: On Android 8.0 (API 26) and higher, AppWidgetManager.requestPinAppWidget() asks the launcher to show a system pin dialog (with a preview in Glance), after checking isRequestPinAppWidgetSupported(). Android guidance recommends offering it after a related task. The statement is true only for iOS.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Android: the main footer action is 'Add to home screen', which calls the pin API when it is supported. The gesture steps show only when pinning is unsupported. Keep the no-button rule for iOS only.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: iOS step 2: 'Tap the plus in the corner, then look for Pantopus.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple Support's current steps: 'touch and hold a widget or an empty area until the apps jiggle. Tap the Edit button in the upper-left corner. Tap Add Widget.' The '+' wording is out of date, which is the exact failure the prompt's own rationale warns about.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Step 2 becomes 'Tap Edit, then Add Widget, and search for Pantopus.' Illustrate it without depending on the button's shape, and check the wording against Apple Support at each iOS release.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Android steps: 'Touch and hold an empty spot… Tap Widgets, then scroll to Pantopus… Touch and hold the size you want and drag it into place.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Pixel Help documents a shorter app-specific route: 'touch and hold the app' then 'tap Widgets', which opens straight to that app's widgets without scrolling the whole picker.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: In the fallback steps, teach the app-icon route: touch and hold the Pantopus icon, tap Widgets, then drag a size into place. It has fewer steps and needs no scrolling through other apps.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The top of the sheet is the user's own widget rendered at true size from the real snapshot, so it reads 'as a thing already on a home screen'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG: 'Avoid mirroring your widget's appearance within your app. Including an element in your app that looks like your widget but doesn't behave like it can confuse people.' Against that, Duolingo found that in-app animated install guides drove installs.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the preview, but make it clearly an illustration: non-interactive, on the home-screen ground patch, with a small caption such as 'Your widget'. Never reuse this widget-look card anywhere else in the app, such as on Today.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Build a DEDICATED preview composition with baked sample content — never the live layout bound to real state.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG: 'You can display real data in your widget preview, but if the data takes too long to generate or load, display realistic simulated data instead.' Android quality tier 1 (WD-1) wants a preview that 'includes user content and/or applies system theme'. Android 15 generated previews (setWidgetPreview, about 2 calls/hour) exist for this purpose.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep baked sample content as the default and for users with no place or snapshot, which fixes the real bug the prompt names. Once a snapshot exists, allow the user's own data in the preview: a local read on iOS, a generated preview pushed after the first Today load on Android 15+. Always apply dynamic colour on Android.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Description: 'Pickup, air and your next date — no notification needed.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG: 'Begin a description with an action verb — for example, "See the current weather conditions and forecast for a location"', and avoid phrases that refer to the widget itself.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use a verb-led line such as 'See pickup day, air quality and your next date at your address.' If the 'no notification' idea matters, carry it in the how-to sheet instead.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Every widget tap opens Today with its existing section order unchanged, and the landing is the top of Today (location row, then pickup card, and so on).
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: HIG: deep-link to the details that relate to the widget content and 'don't make people navigate to the relevant area in the app'. On an AQI-hero day the tapped fact (the air band, sixth section) is below the fold at 393x852. Android WS-5 also asks for the system launch transition.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the section order, but read a `section` parameter: scroll that section into view and highlight it once, the same treatment the 14-day strip gives reminder pushes. On Android, use @android:id/background for the launch transition. Add frames for an AQI-hero arrival.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Fixed order location → pinned briefing (push arrivals only) → pickup → 14-day strip → weather → air → alerts → signals, where surviving sections never move.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g's inverted pyramid puts the most important fact first, and the HIG deep-link rule applies too. The widget's own urgency ladder ranks AQI ≥ 101 above any date, yet on Today an AQI or NOAA crossing sits sixth or seventh for any arrival that is not a push.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the fixed order, since a stable layout is a sound goal. Make the pinned slot show any active threshold crossing (AQI ≥ 101, a NOAA alert) for every arrival type (widget, organic, push), with a link down to the full section.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: List rows show 'relative day ("Tomorrow", "in 4 days")' with no absolute date specified.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Cloudscape's timestamp guidance: relative time is easier to read, but use absolute human-readable dates when 'Users need a specific date and time for when an event occurred or will occur'. Lease-notice, tax-appeal and registration deadlines are acted on by their date.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Rows further out than tomorrow show both: 'in 11 days · Fri 30 Oct'. 'Tonight', 'Today' and 'Tomorrow' stand alone. Compute everything at render time.

numbers: iOS widget sizes on a 393x852 or 390x844 iPhone: small 158x158pt, medium 338x158pt, large 338x354pt; Lock Screen circular 72x72, rectangular 160x72, inline 234x26 (HIG).
iOS widget sizes on 430x932 / 428x926 (Pro Max): small 170x170, medium 364x170, large 364x382; circular 76x76, rectangular 172x76, inline 257x26 (HIG).
Widget margins: 16pt standard; 11pt for tighter grouping of graphics, buttons or background shapes (HIG).
Minimum widget text size 11pt; widgets support Dynamic Type from Large to AX5 (HIG).
Small widget: at most 4 pieces of information and exactly 1 tap target (WWDC20 'Design great widgets').
Update animations: up to 2 seconds (HIG).

WidgetKit refresh budget: typically 40–70 refreshes a day for a frequently viewed widget, about every 15–60 minutes; timeline entries at least about 5 minutes apart; reloads while the app is in the foreground, or triggered by an app intent, don't count (Apple, 'Keeping a widget up to date').
Smart Stack relevance: a TimelineEntryRelevance score of 0 or below means not relevant; scores are relative across your own entries (Apple).
StandBy shows 2 small widgets side by side, scaled up with backgrounds removed, and red monochrome in low light (HIG).
Android handheld widget sizes: 2x2 = 109–306dp wide × 115–276dp tall; 4x2 = 245–624dp × 115–276dp; 4x1 = 245–624dp × 56–130dp; 2x1 = 109–306dp × 56–130dp (Android sizing guide).
Android widget touch target minimum 48x48dp (quality WL-4.2); corner radius is the system value, at most 28dp; tier 1 requires resizing to at least one of 2x2, 4x1 or 4x2.

Android dynamic colour needs API 31 (Android 12) or higher; in-app pinning (requestPinAppWidget) needs API 26 (Android 8.0) or higher; generated picker previews need API 35 (Android 15), with setWidgetPreview limited to about 2 calls per hour.

Glance perception (Blascheck et al. 2019, smartwatch, 7/12/24 values): comparisons averaged under 300 ms for bar charts, under 220 ms for donut charts and under 1780 ms for radial bar charts; most smartwatch interactions last under 5 s.
Loading indicators (NN/g): none under 1 s; skeleton or spinner for 2–10 s; progress bar above 10 s.
WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11: at least 3:1 for graphical objects needed to understand content, treated as a hard threshold (2.999:1 fails).

EPA standard AQI RGB: Green 0,228,0 · Yellow 255,255,0 · Orange 255,126,0 · Red 255,0,0 · Purple 143,63,151 · Maroon 126,0,35. ColorVision Assist: Green 158,255,145 · Yellow 255,201,5 · Orange 255,130,5 · Red 240,34,0 · Purple 137,9,151 · Maroon 100,0,21 (EPA TAD, May 2026).
AQI bands: Good 0–50, Moderate 51–100, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 101–150, Unhealthy 151–200, Very Unhealthy 201–300, Hazardous 301+ (AirNow).

Computed with the WCAG formula from EPA's RGB: against white, Yellow is 1.07:1, Green 1.74:1, Orange 2.55:1, Red 4.00:1. Against the dark raised surface #1E293B, Maroon is 1.33:1 and Purple 2.32:1. Adjacent EPA bands are 1.57–2.37:1 against each other, so segments need an outline or gaps.
HIG tips: a feature needing more than 3 actions is too complex for a tip; show tips at a reasonable cadence, for example once every 24 hours.
Relative-time steps (Cloudscape): 'Now' for 0–59 s, then minutes, hours, days, weeks, months, years ago.

Duolingo: half of learners with the widget installed have a streak of at least 6 months (a correlation, which Duolingo says holds after accounting for selection bias). A widely cited '+60% commitment' figure could not be verified at the source.
Medium strip arithmetic: 338pt − 2×16pt margins = 306pt of content width, so 14 cells give about 21.9pt pitch, enough for 11pt initials. A 120pt strip gives about 8.6pt pitch, which is not enough.

topic: dates-reminders-pickup: entering dates, repeating schedules, reminder lead times, pickup schedules and holiday moves, bill reminders and "mark paid", and 14-day / 12-month timeline views

principles.principle: Let people type dates they are copying from a document (lease, policy, warranty). Use a calendar grid only for dates within about a year where the weekday matters, and never make the calendar the only way in.
principles.evidence: NN/g recommends calendar pickers for events within less than a year and says typing is faster for dates far ahead. It also finds mobile scroll pickers slow when they hold many dates, and recommends dropdowns only when there are fewer than 10 options. Material's DatePicker docs describe docked pickers as 'ideal for navigating dates in both the near future or past and the distant future or past' and describe modal date input as keyboard entry. A search snippet from m3.material.io (the page did not render when fetched) says not to use a modal date picker for dates in the distant past or future. Apple's HIG says date pickers also allow 'entering dates and times using a numeric keypad' and recommends the compact style when space is tight. GOV.UK says to use a calendar only when people benefit from seeing dates in relation to other dates, and never to make a JavaScript calendar the only input. USWDS says to 'Always allow a user to type in the date manually' and to use memorable-date fields for dates people already know. Smashing Magazine (2021) describes calendar-only native pickers as needing 'dozens and dozens of taps'.
principles.implication: The Date sheet should choose the control by kind. For Lease ends, Notice deadline, Insurance renews and Warranty ends: on Android, a docked M3 picker or a picker that opens in text-input mode; on iOS, the compact style with a visible month/year jump; on web, a typeable date field. For Pickup day, use a weekday chooser, not a date picker. For the first recycling date and dates in the next few weeks, a calendar grid is fine. Draw the Android frame with the keyboard-input toggle visible. Draw the 31 Mar 2027 entry reached in two or three taps, not by paging through six months.

principles.principle: Let people enter a date they are unsure of, and make that date look approximate.
principles.evidence: GOV.UK: 'Allow users to enter an approximate date when you are asking them for information they may not know or may struggle to remember.' Warranty end dates and insurance renewal dates are often not remembered. They sit in paperwork the user may not have to hand.
principles.implication: Add a 'Not sure of the day' option to the Date sheet that keeps only the month and year (e.g. 'about Dec 2026'). Show it everywhere with an 'about' label and without a day number. A reminder for an approximate date fires at the start of that month. On the place file, an approximate date counts as known but its row offers 'Add the exact day'. This fits the honesty rules: a guess never looks exact.

principles.principle: Anchor an every-other-week schedule to one explicit date, and show the next few dates it produces so the user can check them.
principles.evidence: RFC 5545 says DTSTART 'defines the first instance of the recurrence' and gives FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2 as the every-other-week example. The Google Calendar API anchors a series on its start and tracks moved instances with originalStartTime. Todoist reads 'every other Friday' as starting on 'the second Friday from now (and not the next upcoming Friday)'. That is a hidden anchoring rule a user cannot see.
principles.implication: Keep the explicit 'Next recycling' field in the Date sheet. Under it, add a read-only preview of the next three computed dates ('Tue 22 Sep · Tue 6 Oct · Tue 20 Oct') so the user can check them against the bin they actually saw collected. Store the rule as an RRULE with DTSTART. Never compute the anchor from 'next week'.

principles.principle: Pickup frequency is a per-household fact that official sources get wrong or contradict. Seed only what a source states, and cite the source for each claim.
principles.evidence: On the City of Camas site, the recycling page says 'Waste Connections will come by on your regular garbage day to pick up your recycling each week'. The garbage pages say garbage is collected 'either once a week, or every other week pick up, depending on individual need' and point to an 'every other week collection' calendar. Clark County and Vancouver pick up recycling 'on an every-other-week basis', and the pickup day is assigned when a household signs up. A Recycle Coach review reports the app had the wrong town and a schedule that contradicted three years of real pickups (from a search snippet of reviews).
principles.implication: A city default can give the weekday with a hollow mark. Frequency stays 'Not set' until the household confirms it, even inside Camas. The source caption should name which page said what ('City of Camas — recycling weekly'). 'Not my schedule' on the pickup card is essential, not an edge case, so give it equal weight as the prompt already does.

principles.principle: Holiday moves are the main job of a pickup product. Every surface that shows a pickup needs a 'moved for a holiday' state, and the night-before push must follow the moved day.
principles.evidence: The City of Camas 2026 garbage calendar lists 10 observed holidays, each moving that day's route to the next business day: MLK Mon Jan 19 → Tue Jan 20; Juneteenth Fri Jun 19 → Mon Jun 22; Labor Day Mon Sep 7 → Tue Sep 8; Veterans' Day Wed Nov 11 → Thu Nov 12; Thanksgiving Thu Nov 26 → Fri Nov 27; Christmas Fri Dec 25 → Mon Dec 28. The Routeware/ReCollect blog advises two channels: a 'campaign' that 'rides along with residents' regular collection reminders' in the weeks before, and a separate service alert on the day. Messages can be targeted, e.g. 'tell only the Tuesday zone that it is moving to Wednesday'. Recycle Coach promotes reminders 'around holidays when collection schedules may change'. RecycleRight reviewers praise how it handles date changes. A Recycle Coach review (search snippet) says the app showed a Presidents' Day pickup two weeks away when nothing had changed.
principles.implication: Design a holiday-moved state once and use it on the pickup card, 14-day strip, year band, household calendar, widget and push. The mark goes on the new day. The usual day gets a faint struck ghost. A caption names the holiday and source: 'Thanksgiving — moved to Fri 27 Nov · City of Camas 2026 calendar'. The push goes out the evening before the moved day and never on the usual evening. Any pickup marks after the last published city calendar (currently Dec 2026) are drawn as projected, not confirmed.

principles.principle: Send the pickup reminder the evening before, with the set-out time from the source. Date reminders can default to the morning.
principles.evidence: Camas requires carts at the curb by 6:30 AM on pickup day. A Recycle Coach reviewer liked getting 'a notification the evening prior early enough to put it out for the next morning pickup'. Apple Reminders sends all-day reminders at 9:00 AM by default, which would be too late for a 6:30 AM set-out. Google Calendar has a separate notification default for all-day events.
principles.implication: The instruction line on the pickup card should come from the source: 'Bins out tonight — curbside by 6:30 AM (City of Camas)'. The notification settings page should say plainly that pickup reminders come with the evening briefing (6:00 PM) and date reminders with the morning briefing (7:00 AM). Never default a pickup reminder to the morning.

principles.principle: For deadlines that matter, send a short series of reminders, not one, and name the specific action in each.
principles.evidence: Fishbane, Ouss and Shah (Science 2020) sent three texts, 7, 3 and 1 day before court. The two interventions studied (a redesigned summons form and the texts) cut failures to appear by 13 to 21%. A plan-making text that did not mention consequences cut them by 6 percentage points (15.8%). Karlan et al. (NBER w16205) found reminders raised total savings by 6%, and reminders that named the saver's specific goal were twice as effective. Google Calendar lets users add more than one notification per event. Chronicle advertises several reminder options per bill.
principles.implication: In the Date sheet, 'Remind me' should show the whole series that will fire: the chosen lead plus the day before and the day of, as the design doc specifies. Draw it as three ticks on the leader line with their real dates. Reminder copy names the action and the object: 'Tell your landlord in writing by Sun 31 Jan' rather than 'Lease notice deadline in 30 days'. Push titles on the household notifications surface follow the same pattern.

principles.principle: Count the reminder lead back from the date the user must act, not from the date the thing ends. For a lease, that means the notice deadline.
principles.evidence: Washington law requires a tenant to give written notice at least 20 days before the end of a rental period, and 'Some leases may require more than 20 days' notice' (WashingtonLawHelp, summarising RCW 59.18.200). The current prompts' own sample data shows the failure. x-date-sheet: lease ends Wed 31 Mar 2027, 60-day reminder falls on Sat 30 Jan 2027, notice deadline is Sun 31 Jan 2027. x-place-file: lease ends 31 May 2027, 60-day reminder falls on Thu 1 Apr 2027, which is the notice deadline itself.
principles.implication: Lease ends should ask 'How much notice does your lease require?' with options 20 days (WA minimum) / 30 / 60 / other. It then works out and saves the notice deadline as its own linked row, and the reminders attach to that deadline (for example 14 days before plus the day before). Always show the weekday on a deadline so a Sunday deadline is visible, and when it falls on a weekend suggest acting on the Friday before.

principles.principle: Some civic deadlines depend on a date specific to the household. Show them as a rule with an input, not as one seeded date.
principles.evidence: Clark County Board of Equalization: 'The deadline for filing an appeal is July 1 of the assessment year or within 60 CALENDAR DAYS of when your Notice of Value was mailed', and 'LATE APPEALS CANNOT BE ACCEPTED' (RCW 84.40.038). The page also mentions filing from January 1 through July 1.
principles.implication: The seeded tax-appeal row reads 'Closes July 1, or 60 days after your value notice was mailed' and asks 'When was your notice mailed?'. Only once that is answered does the row show a single computed date, drawn with the tick mark because the user supplied part of it. Until then the strip and year band show the July 1 marker with a 'may be later' caption.

principles.principle: Word statutory deadlines exactly: say whether the date is when something must arrive or when it must be sent.
principles.evidence: RCW 29A.08.140: online and mail registrations must be 'received by an election official no later than eight days before' the election. In-person registration is open until 8:00 p.m. on election day. For 2026 that means Mon 26 Oct and Tue 3 Nov. RCW 84.56.020: property tax is due on or before April 30 and October 31, with a three-business-day allowance for mail with no readable postmark. Oct 31 2026 is a Saturday. The fetched statute text says nothing about weekend due dates, so we could not confirm whether the date moves.
principles.implication: Voter-registration rows say 'Online or by mail — must arrive by Mon 26 Oct'. Property-tax rows say 'Due Sat 31 Oct (Clark County Treasurer)'. Pantopus never shifts a statutory date on its own. A weekend note appears only when the authority itself publishes one.

principles.principle: Validate dates by kind, and when a date is out of range, suggest a fix instead of blocking.
principles.evidence: NN/g: 'Report mistakes and suggest corrections rather than rejecting input.' f6-home-basics-rows already lets move-in dates be in the future or more than 60 days past and still saves them.
principles.implication: Each kind in the Date sheet gets its own valid range. Move-in date can be in the past or the near future. Warranty ends can be in the past ('already ended — keep it on file?'). Notice deadline and insurance renewal must be in the future. When a chosen lead has already passed, offer the nearest one that works: 'That's already passed — remind 7 days before (Thu 24 Sep)?'.

principles.principle: Make a dense strip of day cells non-interactive, and make the list rows the tap targets.
principles.evidence: Apple's HIG gives iOS controls a default size of 44x44 pt and a minimum of 28x28 pt. Android asks for 48x48dp targets with 8dp between them. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 requires 24x24 CSS px or equivalent spacing, with an exception when 'the function can be achieved through a different control on the same page'. On a 393 pt phone with a 16 pt page margin and 16 pt card padding, 14 cells get 329/14 ≈ 23.5 pt each.
principles.implication: Tapping the strip does nothing per cell, or the whole strip is one target that scrolls to and highlights the list. Tonight's pickup is reached through its list row (at least 44 pt tall) or the pickup card above. A per-cell tap is allowed only on desktop web, where cells are wide enough.

principles.principle: Provenance marks must be readable at the size they are drawn, and must not rely on colour alone.
principles.evidence: WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 contrast for 'parts of graphics required to understand the content', including chart markers and icons whose shape carries meaning. WCAG 1.4.1 forbids using colour as the only way to convey information. The widget prompt already asks that filled, hollow and tick marks stay distinguishable after iOS desaturation.
principles.implication: In a strip cell holding up to three dots in about 23 pt, use fill versus outline for provenance, plus a class shape or glyph rather than hue alone. Keep the full three-state mark, including the tick, for list rows and the Date sheet, where it can be drawn large enough to see. Check at 1x in light, dark and tinted rendering. We found no source that sets a minimum size for a tick mark, so test it.

principles.principle: For a 12-month view of a few scattered deadlines, use a month-grouped timeline or list, not a heatmap and not markers placed to the exact day on a phone.
principles.evidence: Calendar heatmaps (van Wijk & van Selow 1999) were built for periodic numeric time series such as weekday/weekend and holiday patterns. A 2025 review notes they work poorly for data without periodic patterns. EventLines (Wong & Elmqvist, arXiv 2507.17320) addresses 'cluttered regions during event bursts' on linear timelines of discrete events. Arithmetic: after about 72 pt of lane labels, 12 months on a phone get about 21 pt each, about 0.7 pt per day. The x-place-file markers on Oct 26, Oct 31 and Nov 3 would sit 3.5 pt and 2 pt apart.
principles.implication: On phones, the year band groups items by month within each lane (a stacked count or glyph cluster per month cell, with the count shown when there are two or more), or it scrolls sideways at a readable scale. Placing markers to the exact day is kept for desktop widths. The pickup lane can copy Camas's printed 12-month calendar, which shades service weeks, and that shading also shows holiday moves.

principles.principle: For sparse household dates, use an agenda with a clear upcoming window, and make any longer look-ahead a deliberate separate view.
principles.evidence: Rocket Money's Upcoming view shows 'the next two weeks' in calendar form. Chronicle has upcoming, overdue and paid lists plus a Pro 'Forecast' of the next year. Chronicle reviewers complained that the list 'only shows bills due within 30 days' and asked for a monthly total.
principles.implication: A 14-day strip on Today, a 12-month band on the place file, and an agenda for the household calendar is a split competitors also use. The household calendar should label each month with its item count, and a quiet month should read as finished. The bills list header should state the total for its window, e.g. '6 upcoming · $2,233.48 through Oct 31'.

principles.principle: Marking a bill paid should be quick, reversible, and move a repeating bill on to its next date.
principles.evidence: Chronicle lets users mark bills paid from the widget and 'confirm the payments the next time you launch the app'. A search snippet of Chronicle reviews describes the swipe-then-save flow as painful. A bill-reminder app on the App Store (search snippet) creates the next instance automatically once a recurring bill is marked paid. BillOut supports partial payment, skipping and rescheduling a single instance (search snippet from billout.app).
principles.implication: Keep 'Mark paid' out of the row itself, since it notifies the whole household. Once it is tapped, show an Undo toast and hold the 'Sam marked … paid' notification until the undo window closes. Bill detail then shows the next due date for a repeating bill. Offer 'Paid a different amount' and 'Skip this month' next to 'Mark paid'.

principles.principle: Send fewer reminders, combine the ones that coincide, open the exact item, and let users control reminders inside the app.
principles.evidence: NN/g: combine notifications when there are more than five to send at once, and let users edit notification preferences inside the app. It cites an average of 56 notifications per day (Telefonica 2016). The ReCollect blog: 'The key is not to overuse the loud channel, so it still carries weight when it matters.' A Recycle Coach review reports phone calls continuing after the user switched them off. RecycleRight reviewers praise alerts that are not excessive.
principles.implication: When a pickup, a bill and a date reminder fall on the same evening, send one briefing push with one headline and the others as lines inside it. Each push opens its exact item. The notification settings page must reflect what is actually delivered, and per-kind muting sits on the date row.

patterns.name: Hybrid date entry (typed field plus calendar)
patterns.exemplars: Material 3's docked date picker shows an input field with a calendar dropdown, either of which works, and its modal date input takes keyboard entry. iOS's compact date picker opens a calendar editor from a button. USWDS's date picker always allows typing and shows an mm/dd/yyyy hint.
patterns.howToApply: The Date sheet uses a typeable field plus a calendar for document dates. Android starts in input mode for Lease, Notice, Insurance and Warranty. Web uses a native typeable input. Dates are shown with the month spelled out ('31 Mar 2027').
patterns.pitfalls: A modal calendar inside a bottom sheet for dates months away, and scroll wheels, both cost many taps. Ambiguous numeric dates like 10/11/2026 cause misreads.

patterns.name: Recurrence with an explicit anchor and a preview
patterns.exemplars: The RFC 5545 DTSTART + INTERVAL=2 model underlies Google Calendar's 'Repeat every 2 weeks', where the start date decides which weeks are on. Todoist's 'starting' keyword pins the first date. Todoist's default 'every other Friday' (the second Friday from now) shows the surprise an implicit anchor causes.
patterns.howToApply: Frequency is a three-way choice: Not set / Weekly / Every other week. Every other week reveals 'Next recycling' plus a preview of the next three dates. Weekly garbage and every-other-week recycling are stored as separate rules.
patterns.pitfalls: Working out the recycling week from the garbage day. Hiding the anchor. Previewing without any holiday moves applied.

patterns.name: Holiday move: advance notice plus a day-of alert
patterns.exemplars: ReCollect (Routeware): a campaign rides along with regular reminders in the weeks before, a service alert fires on the day, both targeted by zone. The Camas 2026 brochure has a holiday table giving each holiday and its next collection day. Garbage Day Reminder offers holiday handling and skip/move for single days.
patterns.howToApply: The address calendar stores exceptions (EXDATE plus a moved instance, as Google does with originalStartTime). The pickup card and strip draw the moved mark with a struck ghost on the usual day. The evening briefing in the week before mentions the move in one line. The night-before push goes out for the moved day.
patterns.pitfalls: Showing an even rhythm through Thanksgiving week. Sending 'bins out tonight' on the usual evening. Presenting projected dates after the last published city calendar as confirmed.

patterns.name: Pickup reminder that separates trash-only and trash-plus-recycling days
patterns.exemplars: A RecycleRight Vancouver ClarkCo reviewer (4.8 stars, 1.4K ratings) valued notices that tell trash-only days apart from combined trash and recycling days. A Recycle Coach reviewer relies on reminders for alternating weekly pickups.
patterns.howToApply: The pickup card headline and push title name the bins due that night ('Garbage only tomorrow' vs 'Recycling and garbage tomorrow'), with a per-bin glyph. The strip uses a different glyph for combined days.
patterns.pitfalls: A generic 'Pickup tomorrow' makes the user work out which week it is, which is the confusion the product is meant to remove.

patterns.name: Reminder series with dates shown
patterns.exemplars: Fishbane et al.'s court reminders at 7, 3 and 1 day before. Apple Calendar's second alert. Google Calendar's multiple notifications per event.
patterns.howToApply: The Date sheet's 'Remind me' draws the chosen lead plus the day before and the day of as ticks on a mini timeline, each labelled with its real date. Copy states the action to take.
patterns.pitfalls: Drawing one lead when three pushes will fire. Using lead choices that land on or after the day the user must act.

patterns.name: Deadline derived from a lease term
patterns.exemplars: We found no verified product that does this. The pattern comes from RCW 59.18.200 (20-day minimum tenant notice) and WashingtonLawHelp's note that leases can require more.
patterns.howToApply: Lease ends asks for the required notice (20 / 30 / 60 / other days), creates a linked Notice deadline row, and reminds against that row.
patterns.pitfalls: Presenting 20 days as the notice the user owes when their lease may require more. Always say 'check your lease'.

patterns.name: Mark paid with undo, then roll a repeating bill forward
patterns.exemplars: Chronicle: mark paid from the widget, confirm on next launch, and repeating bills move forward automatically. Bill Reminder & Tracker creates the next instance once one is paid. BillOut: partial pay, skip, reschedule.
patterns.howToApply: The bills list keeps Mark paid in the overflow menu. After marking, show an Undo toast and hold the household notification until it expires. Bill detail shows 'Next: <date>' for repeating bills.
patterns.pitfalls: A one-tap write on a glanceable card that notifies the whole house. A flow long enough to push users back to their bank app.

patterns.name: Two look-ahead windows: 14 days and 12 months
patterns.exemplars: Rocket Money's Upcoming shows the next two weeks. Chronicle's Pro Forecast shows the next year, and its 30-day-only list drew complaints. Camas's printed 12-month garbage calendar shades service weeks and lists holidays.
patterns.howToApply: Today shows a 14-day strip plus list rows. The place file shows the year band, grouped by month on phones. The two share geometry and marks, and the 14-day window is shaded inside the year band.
patterns.pitfalls: Placing markers to the exact day on a phone, where they collide. A heatmap for sparse deadlines. A year band that can't show holiday moves.

antipatterns: Calendar-only or scroll-wheel date entry for dates months away (lease end, policy renewal). NN/g and Smashing both report it takes many taps and is slower than typing, and M3 advises against modal calendar pickers for distant dates.
Numeric-only dates such as 10/11/2026. NN/g flags the day/month ambiguity. Spell out the month and show the weekday.

Working out the every-other-week recycling date from the garbage day or from 'next week'. Todoist's hidden second-Friday rule shows how implicit anchors surprise users, and RFC 5545 requires an explicit DTSTART.

Drawing weekly pickup as a perfectly even rhythm through holiday weeks. Camas moves 10 holiday routes in 2026, e.g. Thanksgiving Thu Nov 26 → Fri Nov 27, so an even rhythm is wrong in exactly the weeks people most need the app.
Sending 'Bins out tonight' on the usual evening of a holiday week. That push is itself dishonest, whatever the confidence mark says.
Defaulting pickup reminders to the morning, as Apple Reminders does for all-day items (9:00 AM). Camas carts must be out by 6:30 AM.
Reminding against a lease END date. In the current sample data, the 60-day lead lands one day before, or on, the notice deadline.
Showing a single reminder lead when the backend sends the lead, the day before and the day of. The control then understates what will happen.
Showing a conditional civic deadline (tax appeal: July 1 or 60 days after the notice is mailed) as one seeded date. It is wrong for every household whose notice arrived late.
'By mail — by <date>' wording for a deadline defined as received-by (RCW 29A.08.140). People will read it as a postmark date.
Per-day tap targets in a 14-cell phone strip (about 23.5 pt each). This is below Apple's 28 pt minimum and Android's 48dp, and passes WCAG 2.5.8 only through the equivalent-control exception.
Encoding event class by hue alone, and a tick drawn too small to see, on tiny dots. This breaks WCAG 1.4.1 and 1.4.11, and the honesty rule requires provenance to be visible in the pixels.
Calendar heatmaps for sparse, one-off deadlines. They were built for periodic numeric series.
Placing markers to the exact day on a 12-month band at phone width (about 0.7 pt per day). Late-October civic deadlines merge into one blob.
A one-tap 'Mark paid' that notifies the household with no undo, or at the other extreme a multi-step save flow (a complaint in Chronicle reviews).
Blocking out-of-range dates without suggesting a fix, for example a blanket 'no past dates' rule that stops a real move-in date.
Notification toggles that do not match what is actually sent. A Recycle Coach reviewer kept getting phone calls after turning them off.
Stating 'Bulk pickup — curbside by 6am' on a Saturday for Camas. The city's brochure says it takes no large items and lists weekday service only.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: '60 days must exist in Remind me: it is the only lead anyone ever picks for a lease notice.' Sample: 'Lease ends — 31 Mar 2027, remind 60 days' next to 'Notice to vacate — 31 Jan 2027'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WA tenants owe at least 20 days' written notice, and leases may require more (RCW 59.18.200; WashingtonLawHelp). The action date is the notice deadline. 31 Mar 2027 minus 60 days is Sat 30 Jan 2027, one day before the Sun 31 Jan notice deadline, so the sample reminder arrives too late to act. We found no evidence that 60 days is the lead everyone picks.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep 60 as an option. Make Lease ends ask for the required notice (20/30/60/other), create the Notice deadline row from it, and anchor reminders to that deadline. Redraw the sample so the leader line lands well before 31 Jan 2027, and show the weekday ('Sun 31 Jan').

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Lease ends · May 31, 2027 · Reminder set 60 days before' next to 'Notice deadline · April 1, 2027'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: 31 May 2027 minus 60 days is Thu 1 Apr 2027, the notice deadline itself. The reminder fires on the last day the tenant can act (RCW 59.18.200).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Show the reminder on the Notice deadline row ('Reminder set 14 days before · Thu 18 Mar'), or link the two rows so the lease reminder visibly points at the notice date.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Remind me' is a four-segment single choice (60/30/7/1) with one leader line to one labelled day.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The design doc (F5 Reminders) fires reminders at the lead, the day before and the day of. Multi-reminder series (7/3/1 days) had strong field effects (Fishbane et al. 2020, 13–21% fewer failures to appear), and calendars support more than one alert.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw all three ticks with their real dates, or add the caption 'We'll also remind you the day before and on the day.' The control must not understate what will fire.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The leader-line example labels 'Mon 30 Nov 2026'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Date arithmetic: no sample event minus 60, 30, 7 or 1 days gives Mon 30 Nov 2026. For the warranty ending Sat 12 Dec 2026, 30 days before is Thu 12 Nov and 7 days before is Sat 5 Dec.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use a consistent example, e.g. 'Water heater warranty ends Sat 12 Dec 2026 · remind 30 days → Thu 12 Nov 2026'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Every kind is entered through a 'native date control', with no approximate-date path.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: GOV.UK: allow approximate dates when users may not know the exact one. Warranty end and insurance renewal dates are often not remembered.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add 'Not sure of the day' (month + year) with an 'about' treatment used on every surface, and a reminder at the start of that month.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Android: 'ModalBottomSheet, M3 date picker' for all kinds, including dates about 2 years out.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Material docs: docked pickers suit near and distant dates, and modal date input takes keyboard entry. The m3.material.io snippet (seen via search; the page would not render) advises against the modal calendar picker for distant dates. NN/g: calendars suit dates within less than a year.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Specify the docked picker, or the date picker opened in INPUT_MODE_TEXT, for Lease, Notice, Insurance and Warranty. Keep the calendar mode for pickup's first date and dates within a few weeks. Draw the keyboard toggle.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Validation frame: 'past date 1 Sep 2026' treated as an error in general. The same sheet also has a Move-in date kind.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: A move-in date is normally in the past (f6-home-basics-rows saves dates more than 60 days ago). NN/g says to suggest corrections rather than reject input.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Make validity ranges per kind. Show the past-date error only for future-only kinds (Notice, Insurance, HOA, Lease), and pair it with a suggested fix. For a lead that has already passed, offer the nearest one still possible.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Seeded: 'Clark County property-tax appeal — closes 1 Jul 2027'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Clark County BOE: the deadline is 'July 1 of the assessment year or within 60 CALENDAR DAYS of when your Notice of Value was mailed', and late appeals are not accepted.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Seed it as a rule ('July 1, or 60 days after your value notice was mailed') with an input for the notice's mailing date. The single computed date appears only after that input.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Online or by mail — by Mon 26 Oct 2026'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: RCW 29A.08.140: registrations must be received by an election official no later than eight days before the election. The date is right, but 'by mail — by' reads as a postmark date.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Reword to 'Online or by mail — must arrive by Mon 26 Oct 2026'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 14 equal cells at phone width, and cells act as entry points ('the 14-day strip's tonight cell' in f4, 'a row tap in Today's 14-day strip' in x-date-sheet).
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: About 23.5 pt per cell on a 393 pt phone. That is below Apple's 28 pt minimum and 44 pt default and Android's 48dp, and meets WCAG 2.5.8 only through the equivalent-control exception.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: State that cells are not tap targets. Tapping the strip scrolls to and highlights the list, and list rows (at least 44 pt) are the entry points. Update f4's 'reached by' line to say 'the strip's tonight row'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Dots coloured by class (4 hues) and carrying three provenance states including FILLED-WITH-TICK, up to three dots plus '+1' per cell.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for meaningful graphic parts, and 1.4.1 forbids colour-only meaning. A tick inside a dot a few points wide will not be perceivable, which conflicts with the house rule that honesty must be visible in the pixels.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: In cells, use fill versus outline plus a class shape or glyph. Keep the tick for list rows. Add a frame at 1x in dark and tinted rendering to prove the marks can be told apart.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Fri 30 Oct: 'Property-tax appeal window closes' labelled Clark County. The 2nd-half property tax due Sat 31 Oct is absent. Sat 31 Oct: 'Bulk pickup — curbside by 6am'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Clark County's appeal deadline is July 1 or 60 days after the notice (conflicting with x-date-sheet and x-place-file, which say 1 Jul 2027). RCW 84.56.020 sets the 2nd half due Oct 31. The Camas 2026 brochure says the city takes no large items and lists only weekday service, with carts out by 6:30 AM.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Replace with 'Property tax, 2nd half — due Sat 31 Oct · Clark County Treasurer'. Show the appeal row only as a household-specific computed date. Remove the Saturday bulk pickup or mark the frame as fictional data.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: There are 10 states and none is a holiday move. The instruction line is a fixed 'Bins out tonight.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The Camas 2026 calendar moves 10 holiday routes to the next business day. Waste apps treat holiday moves as the core alert. Camas set-out is 'by 6:30 a.m.'
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add a 'Moved for <holiday>' state: the headline on the moved day, a struck usual day, and a source caption. The push fires the evening before the moved day. Write the instruction as 'Bins out tonight — curbside by 6:30 AM' and take the time from the source.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Year band: 'one marker per rule, positioned at its date', drawn on 390 pt phones. Recurring pickup is 'an evenly repeating rhythm of small hollow marks'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: About 0.7 pt per day at phone width makes the Oct 26 / Oct 31 / Nov 3 markers overlap (EventLines on clutter in bursty timelines). Thanksgiving Thu Nov 26 2026 moves Camas Thursday pickup to Fri Nov 27, so an even rhythm is wrong.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: On phones, group markers by month within each lane, with counts. Keep exact-day placement for desktop. Draw the holiday move in the pickup lane, and show dates after the last published city calendar as projected.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Camas garbage Thursdays, recycling every other Thursday' as the hollow city default (f5 similarly says 'recycling is biweekly').
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The City of Camas recycling page says Waste Connections collects recycling 'each week'. The Camas garbage pages describe weekly or every-other-week garbage 'depending on individual need'. Every-other-week recycling is the Clark County/Vancouver rule.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Do not present every-other-week recycling as the Camas city default. Seed the weekday only, leave frequency 'Not set' until confirmed, and caption the exact source. If the demo needs every-other-week recycling, set it at a Vancouver or unincorporated Clark County address.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Garbage + recycling' every Wednesday from Sep through Dec 2026 at real density, drawn as a plain weekly rule.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Camas's 2026 calendar moves Veterans' Day, Wed Nov 11, to Thu Nov 12.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw the Nov 11 → Nov 12 move in the agenda, with the moved row, a struck original and the holiday source. It is a real in-range example of the state.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Year sample: 'Clark County — property tax 2nd half 30 Oct' and 'Washington — … tax appeal window opens 1 Jul'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: RCW 84.56.020 sets the second half due on or before October 31. Clark County BOE: July 1 is the appeal deadline (or 60 days after the notice), with filing possible from January 1. It is a county matter, not statewide.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Change to 'property tax 2nd half 31 Oct' and 'Clark County — tax appeal deadline 1 Jul (or 60 days after your notice)', and move the appeal to the county lane.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Mark paid only in the row overflow menu. No undo is specified.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Bill apps reduce mark-paid friction (Chronicle marks from the widget and confirms later, and reviewers complain about multi-step saves). The prompt's reason, that marking notifies the household, is valid. An undo removes the harm of a mis-tap without adding steps.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the overflow placement. Add an Undo toast and hold the bill_paid household notification until the undo window closes. On a repeating bill, show 'Next due <date>' after marking.

numbers: NN/g: use calendar pickers for dates within less than 1 year. Use dropdowns only when there are fewer than 10 date options.
Apple HIG (iOS): default control size 44x44 pt, minimum 28x28 pt, about 12 pt padding around controls.
Android / Material: touch targets at least 48x48dp, at least 8dp apart.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA): targets at least 24x24 CSS px, unless spaced or an equivalent control exists. WCAG 1.4.11: at least 3:1 contrast for meaningful graphic parts.
14-day strip on a 393 pt phone with 16 pt page margin and 16 pt card padding: 329 pt / 14 ≈ 23.5 pt per cell.
12-month band at phone width after about 72 pt of lane labels: about 21 pt per month, about 0.7 pt per day. Weekly pickup is about 5 pt between marks, every-other-week about 10 pt.
Fishbane, Ouss & Shah (Science 2020): three texts at 7, 3 and 1 day before court. Interventions cut failures to appear by 13–21%. A plan-making text alone cut them by 6 pp (15.8%).
Karlan et al. (NBER w16205): reminders raised total savings by 6%. Reminders naming a specific goal were 2x as effective.
WA tenant notice: at least 20 days' written notice before the end of the rental period (RCW 59.18.200). Leases may require more.
WA insurance (RCW 48.18.2901): nonrenewal notice at least 60 days before expiry. A renewal offer with premium at least 20 days before expiry.
WA property tax (RCW 84.56.020): 1st half due Apr 30, 2nd half due Oct 31. Oct 31 2026 is a Saturday, and we could not confirm any weekend rule.
WA voter registration (RCW 29A.08.140): online or mail must be received 8 days before the election (Mon 26 Oct 2026). In person until 8:00 PM on election day (Tue 3 Nov 2026).
Clark County property-value appeal: July 1, or within 60 calendar days of the Notice of Value mailing. Late appeals are not accepted.

City of Camas: carts at the curb by 6:30 AM on pickup day. 10 observed holidays in 2026, each moving that day's route to the next business day (e.g. Veterans' Day Wed Nov 11 → Thu Nov 12; Thanksgiving Thu Nov 26 → Fri Nov 27; Christmas Fri Dec 25 → Mon Dec 28).

Clark County / Vancouver: recycling every other week, on the garbage day, which is assigned when the household signs up. Waste Connections stopped auto-mailing printed calendars to unincorporated Clark County and Vancouver from January 2026.
RecycleRight Vancouver ClarkCo (ReCollect): 4.8 stars, 1.4K App Store ratings. Recycle Coach: 4.8 stars, 25K ratings. Chronicle: 4.8 stars, 3.8K ratings.
Apple Reminders: all-day reminders notify at 9:00 AM by default. Pantopus defaults in f4-notification-settings are morning 7:00 AM and evening 6:00 PM Pacific.
Rocket Money's Upcoming view covers 2 weeks. Chronicle's list covers 30 days (a reviewer complaint), and its Pro Forecast covers the next year.
NN/g push notifications: combine into one message when more than 5 would go at once. Average user received 56 notifications per day (Telefonica, 2016).
Recommended Date-sheet lease notice options: 20 (WA minimum) / 30 / 60 / other days. A reminder anchored to the notice deadline makes a 60-day lead unnecessary for most leases.

topic: companion-progress-ethics: companion characters, progress display and celebration without dark patterns (Finch, Duolingo, Apple Fitness rings, Tamagotchi-style pets, digital-wellbeing guidance, streak and gamification research) applied to f11-keeper-strip, f11-keeper-naming, x-place-file, f9-invite-rewards-card, f9-block-founders-panel and neighbours

principles.principle: When nothing has happened, show a calm, sparse state. Never show decay, wilting or sadness, and never draw an empty placeholder that the user is supposed to fill.
principles.evidence: UbiFit Garden (Consolvo et al., UbiComp 2008, 28 participants, 3-month field experiment) used only positive reinforcement. The authors say the garden has no wilting flowers, weeds or stormy sky, and inactivity shows as a sparse or empty garden under a blue sky. Participants who had the glanceable display kept up their activity through the holidays, while activity in the no-display group dropped significantly. The same paper reports that in Fish'n'Steps (Lin et al., UbiComp 2006, 19 participants), some people ignored the display when their fish was not happy. The authors' reading is that punishment led people to avoid the system rather than change their behaviour.
principles.implication: The keeper's lowest state must never show the creature suffering: no drooping, crying, sick or shivering pose, and no darker sky or wilted props. For the overdue-bill state, draw an alert, helpful pose, such as the keeper holding the envelope or pointing at the line. Let the fact line carry the severity. In the place file and the keeper ring, draw the categories that are known. Do not draw hollow outlined slots for categories that are not known. Unknown categories go in a separate plain list headed 'You can also add'.

principles.principle: Compute the companion's mood only from facts about the world, meaning obligations that are due. Never compute it from how often the user opens the app, and blame the obligation, never the person.
principles.evidence: Silverman & Barasch (Journal of Consumer Research, 2022/2023, 7 studies) found that highlighting an intact streak raised later engagement compared with highlighting a broken one. The effect grew when people blamed themselves for the break and shrank when they could repair it. In the strength-exercise study, 66.23% continued with an intact streak versus 57.86% with a broken one, with identical actual behaviour (INSEAD Knowledge summary). Duolingo's disappointed-owl notifications are widely criticised as guilt-based (The Decision Lab). Slate's September 2026 Finch review describes the reviewer quitting after yet another notification from the bird saying it missed them.
principles.implication: Mood inputs are limited to due and overdue bills, tasks and calendar rows. The mood never uses days since last open, and it does not decay while the user is away. Someone returning after 30 days sees the mood computed from today's obligations and nothing like 'I missed you'. In mood-line copy the grammatical subject is always the thing, never the person: 'The water bill is past its due date', not 'You missed the water bill'. Never give the keeper feelings about the user.

principles.principle: Do not build streaks. If any continuity measure survives, make it weekly, repairable and pausable, and never show a broken one.
principles.evidence: A PLOS One qualitative study (17 recreational runners who ended streaks of 100 or more consecutive days) found people ran through injury to keep a streak going, and some described a grieving process for weeks or months after it ended. Silverman & Barasch found that a repair option weakens the demotivating effect of a broken streak. Duolingo's own blog reports that allowing two equipped Streak Freezes raised daily active learners by 0.38%. watchOS 11 lets people pause Activity rings for 1 to 90 days without losing the streak. In Consolvo et al. (Persuasive 2009), most participants did not like daily goals because they needed rest days, and the recommended default was a Monday-to-Sunday calendar week.
principles.implication: No streak count appears on the keeper strip, widget, Today or place file. The design doc says the Mail Day backend already tracks a streak (§F10). Keep it off every designed surface. If it is ever shown, it counts weeks, not days, and offers a pause. Keep the keeper's time horizon at a week, but word it as a rolling window ('in the next 7 days') so a bill due Monday doesn't disappear when a calendar week resets.

principles.principle: Any visible denominator (X of Y, or a closed shape with unfilled segments) turns 'what we hold' into an unfinished task. To show how much is on file without implying incompleteness, show what is present and nothing about what is absent.
principles.evidence: Nunes & Drèze (JCR 2006) gave car-wash customers loyalty cards needing the same 8 purchases. The 10-stamp card with 2 stamps pre-filled was completed by 34%, against 19% for the plain 8-stamp card, because the task now read as started and unfinished. Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng (JMR 2006) found that effort depends on the proportion of the distance that remains, and people speed up as they near the goal. Both results show that denominators and part-filled shapes create pressure to complete.
principles.implication: A 5-segment ring with 4 filled segments reads as 'one to go' whatever the caption says. Options: (a) show an absolute count with no denominator ('11 on file') next to category chips that appear only once something is known; (b) if the ring stays, draw no outline for empty categories, leaving a plain gap, and for a saved place (T1) draw only the categories that tier can hold. Use a real 'X of Y' only where finishing is the user's own goal, such as the three first-week questions, and then call it a checklist that can be dismissed.

principles.principle: Measuring an activity raises output but can drain the enjoyment and motivation behind it. Keep counts informational and never turn them into a score.
principles.evidence: Etkin (JCR 2016, six experiments) found that measurement makes people do more of an activity but enjoy it less, because it makes the activity feel like work, and this can reduce continued engagement. Hanus & Fox (Computers & Education 2015) compared a course with leaderboards and badges against the same course without them over 16 weeks. The gamified group showed lower motivation and satisfaction over time and lower final exam scores (per the published summary). A meta-analysis by Sailer & Homner (2020) found only small effects of gamification on motivation (g = .36) and behaviour (g = .25), and these were less stable in rigorous studies. Diefenbach & Müssig (IJHCS 2019) found that every one of 45 Habitica users experienced counterproductive effects, such as being punished during especially productive periods.
principles.implication: The fact count is never the keeper's level. The design doc's 'Growth: level = count of distinct facts' stays a backend concept only. Never add '+1 on file' toasts, count-up animations, a new keeper accessory for each fact, or a 'next milestone' number. The count updates silently. Do not judge the keeper by facts added. Judge it by week-4 return and by how many people remove it.

principles.principle: Word decline options neutrally and give them the same visual weight as the accept option. Guilt-laden wording erodes trust.
principles.evidence: NN/g ('Stop Shaming Your Users', 2018) recommends plain wording such as 'No thanks' and equal prominence for accepting and declining, and reports that users recognise shaming as manipulation. Gray et al. (CHI 2018) document practitioners' concern about becoming complicit in manipulative design. The FTC's 2022 staff report lists asymmetric choice and interface interference among its dark-pattern categories.
principles.implication: 'Skip' on the naming sheet stays a full-weight button, as the v1 prompt already requires. Remove, Skip and any keeper-related decline must not use creature emotion ('Ollie will be lonely') or loss framing. The Remove confirm names the consequence plainly. The same rule applies to 'Not now' on the invite rewards and compare sheets.

principles.principle: Once the user skips something, it disappears from the main surface. Re-entry lives somewhere the user goes deliberately, and asking again later is nagging.
principles.evidence: Apple's HIG on onboarding says that if people skip a tutorial, don't present it again on later launches, but keep it easy to find in a help, account or settings area. Deceptive.design defines nagging as a way of using up the user's time and attention, and cites Instagram's 'Not Now'-only notification prompt, which kept returning for months. In December 2023 the European Parliament adopted a resolution on addictive design that calls for a digital 'right not to be disturbed', with attention-seeking features off by design.
principles.implication: After Skip, the keeper slot on Today closes completely, with no remaining 'Give your place a keeper' row, dot or silhouette. Re-entry is a single row in the place file's Place section and an item in Settings. Before any skip, the unnamed invitation should show for a limited period, and never as a modal or a badge.

principles.principle: Offer personalisation after the user has got value, keep it to one short screen, and pre-fill defaults so it takes one tap.
principles.evidence: Apple's HIG says to postpone nonessential setup and customisation and to provide reasonable defaults. NN/g's mobile onboarding article says visual customisation doesn't belong in onboarding and skip controls should be highly visible. Revyl Atlas maps Finch's full first run at 45 screens (egg colour from a 6-colour picker, pronouns, name, trait, survey, paywall, streak commitment, widget prompt), with a pre-filled random pet name. Chernev et al.'s choice-overload meta-analysis (99 observations, N = 7,202) found overload increases with task difficulty, preference uncertainty and an effort-minimising goal.
principles.implication: Keep the naming sheet to one screen with at most 6 species, a pre-filled name for each, and no pronouns, traits, colours or personality quiz. Never offer it in the /start funnel or the first session. It fits best after the first value moment, such as a confirmed pickup day or a saved date. The design doc (§F11) auto-opens it on the second Today open, while the v1 prompt's tap-to-open is the evidence-aligned choice. Update the doc to match the prompt. People who just want to check recycling are exactly the effort-minimising users for whom choices cause overload.

principles.principle: The companion never speaks through notifications, and every notification's urgency level matches the real event.
principles.evidence: Apple's HIG on managing notifications: build trust by representing urgency accurately, and use Time Sensitive only for events happening now or within an hour. App Review Guideline 4.5.4 says push must not be required for the app to work, and promotional push needs explicit opt-in plus an in-app opt-out. Android notification channels give users full control of each channel, with one channel per notification type. Duolingo's KDD 2020 paper found that repeating the same reminder template desensitises users. Its novelty-optimising algorithm gained only +0.5% DAU and +2.0% new-user D7 retention.
principles.implication: No push notification carries the keeper's name, avatar or voice, and a mood change never triggers a push. The Notifications settings page therefore needs no keeper group. If one is ever added, it is a separate channel that is off by default. Pickup and bill pushes stay factual ('Recycling tomorrow — city schedule, not yet confirmed') and never say 'Ollie says…'.

principles.principle: Motion should have a purpose, be brief and be optional. Celebrate with a quiet acknowledgement, not a show.
principles.evidence: Apple's HIG on motion: don't add motion for its own sake, make it optional, keep feedback animations brief and precise, and let people cancel them. Apple's HIG on feedback: reserve completion confirmations for important actions, because people only need to know when something fails. WCAG 2.2.2 (Level A) requires a way to pause, stop or hide any motion that starts automatically, lasts more than 5 seconds and runs alongside other content. WCAG 2.3.3 (AAA) asks that interaction-triggered animation can be turned off (prefers-reduced-motion). Duolingo reports that streak milestone animations raised new-learner D7 retention by 1.7%, which shows how tempting celebration is.
principles.implication: The keeper's idle animation (Rive/Lottie) runs 5 seconds or less and then holds still, or doesn't loop at all. Under Reduce Motion or prefers-reduced-motion it shows a static pose. A mood change is one short pose transition. After naming, after 'all known' in the place file, and on the claim receipt, the only 'celebration' is the pose settling to relaxed plus one factual line. No confetti, particles, sound, haptic fanfare or full-screen takeover.

principles.principle: A companion that summarises data must let the user correct that data, and it must never show a confident mood built on a failed or wrong reading.
principles.evidence: Consolvo et al. (2008) report that in the Houston step-count study, several participants complained that step counts did not reflect their activity, and some stopped doing activities the pedometer could not detect. When the metric misrepresents reality, people change their behaviour to suit the metric. WCAG 1.4.1 says colour must not be the only way information is conveyed.
principles.implication: Every non-relaxed mood line is a tap target that leads to the item it summarises, and that item offers a correction ('Already paid', 'Not my schedule'). Keep the v1 'mood unavailable' state. The avatar's accessible label is the fact line ('Ollie: A bill is overdue'), never only the mood word, and mood is shown by pose, never by colour alone.

principles.principle: Ambient companions work because users can ignore them and because they are abstract. Abstraction also protects privacy on screens other people can see.
principles.evidence: Consolvo et al. (2008): the glanceable wallpaper kept people aware 'in a persistent yet subtle way', and the system was deliberately designed so users could ignore it at times. A pilot user of Breakaway, a desk sculpture that slumps the longer its user stays seated, appreciated being able to ignore it during busy periods. One participant worried about a revealing display on a phone left on the desk: 'What if somebody saw that?' The authors argue that stylised, abstract representations give a sense of privacy.
principles.implication: The keeper strip requires no action: no badge, no unread dot, no 'check in' button. If the keeper ever appears on a widget or lock screen, show the pose plus a generic line ('1 thing due'), never 'A bill is overdue'. On a shared household keeper, compute mood only from data the viewer is allowed to see. A member without finance.view must not learn about an overdue bill through the keeper's pose. (This last point follows from the product's own honesty rules, not from a published study.)

principles.principle: Real scarcity and real deadlines are fine to show. Alarm styling or a ticking countdown on a perk borrows urgency from genuine obligations.
principles.evidence: Mathur et al. (CSCW 2019) crawled about 11K shopping sites and found 1,818 dark-pattern instances, with countdown timers and limited-time messages in the urgency category. The FTC's 2022 report names baseless countdown timers and false limited-time messages. Apple's HIG says to build trust by representing urgency accurately.
principles.implication: The Founding Neighbor window states its closing date ('Closes Tue, Sep 22') in a neutral or info pill. Reserve warning tokens for obligations with real consequences: voter registration, tax, overdue bills. The window continues to fail closed. Never show a live hours-and-minutes countdown.

principles.principle: A companion mainly serves relatedness, the sense that the place is somewhere. Don't use it as a lever for completion or referrals.
principles.evidence: Sailer et al. (Computers in Human Behavior, 2017) ran a randomised study and found that badges, leaderboards and performance graphs affected competence, while avatars, meaningful stories and teammates affected social relatedness. NN/g's article on autonomy, relatedness and competence says users are motivated when they can make choices that fit their own priorities, and that irrelevant messages damage trust. The Tamagotchi effect: people form real attachments to software agents, and neglect-driven death in the original toy caused real distress.
principles.implication: The keeper never asks for anything: no 'Ollie wants you to add a bill', no 'Ollie wants neighbours', and it never appears on the invite rewards or Block Founders cards. It never dies, runs away or leaves. Removing it is the user's choice and can be undone.

principles.principle: Saying the app or its creature 'knows' things about your home makes data-holding sound like surveillance. Describe the file as the user's own record.
principles.evidence: Ur et al. (SOUPS 2012, 48 interviews about behavioural advertising) found participants saw data-driven tailoring as useful and privacy-invasive at the same time, and were surprised by what was being used. Tamagotchi-effect research shows people attribute agency to software characters. The link to the 'knows' wording is an inference from these findings, not a tested result.
principles.implication: Use 'on file for this address' or 'you've added', not 'Ollie knows 11 things' or 'See what we know'. The keeper's pose and line summarise obligations. The keeper is never shown as the thing that holds the data.

patterns.name: Additive garden (show presence, not absence)
patterns.exemplars: UbiFit Garden: a flower for each activity, butterflies for goals met, and an empty garden under a blue sky when nothing happened. No wilting, weeds or storms. Finch: the bird grows when the user shows up, and missed days carry no penalty.
patterns.howToApply: In the place file, the keeper ring and any 'how much is on file' view, a known category adds a mark. An unknown category adds nothing to the shape and is listed separately as a neutral invitation. A saved place (T1) shows a smaller complete instrument, not a larger incomplete one.
patterns.pitfalls: Outlined empty slots bring the denominator back. 'Growth' animations tied to data entry turn the display into XP.

patterns.name: Face summarises, text states
patterns.exemplars: Breakaway: a desk sculpture's slump shows how long its user has been sitting, and the user can ignore it. Fish'n'Steps: the fish's emotional state shows step count, which also shows the risk, because people avoided the unhappy fish. The v1 keeper prompt already requires the mood word to sit beside the fact line.
patterns.howToApply: The pose is never more alarming than the fact line. The top state is 'on it', helpful, not distressed. The fact line is the accessible label and the tap target that leads to the correctable item.
patterns.pitfalls: Pose states named for anxiety ('fidgeting', 'worried') tend to get drawn as distress. An overdue bill paid outside the app leaves a worried keeper with no way to correct it.

patterns.name: Pause and repair instead of loss
patterns.exemplars: Apple watchOS 11 lets users pause rings for a day, week, month or a custom 1–90 days while keeping the streak, and reports describe paused rings as greyed with a resume date. Duolingo Streak Freeze: two equipped freezes raised daily active learners by 0.38%. Silverman & Barasch found that repair options weaken the effect of a broken streak.
patterns.howToApply: Pantopus should not have streaks. The same idea applies to briefings and the keeper: 'Pause briefings until…' in Notifications, and 'Hide keeper for now' next to Remove. Any hidden or paused state names the date it ends.
patterns.pitfalls: A pause that silently resumes without saying so. A freeze sold as a currency item, which is a monetised guilt mechanic.

patterns.name: One-sheet, pre-filled companion naming
patterns.exemplars: Finch pre-fills a random name that the user can change (Revyl Atlas), but buries it in a 45-screen first-run flow, which is the counter-example. Apple's HIG calls for reasonable defaults and postponing nonessential setup.
patterns.howToApply: Keep the v1 sheet: 6 species, a default name for each, a full-weight Skip, and Rename, Change species and Remove afterwards. Offer it only from a tap, after a value moment. Skipping closes the Today slot.
patterns.pitfalls: Adding pronouns, traits or colours. Auto-presenting it on the second open, as design doc §F11 does. Leaving a permanent invitation in place after Skip.

patterns.name: Equal-weight neutral decline
patterns.exemplars: NN/g recommends 'No thanks' with equal prominence, and says WebMD's plain prompt was trusted where a 'manipulink' was not.
patterns.howToApply: Every opt-in surface (naming, compare, notification primer, invite) uses buttons of the same height and weight, with a plain verb for declining. No creature emotion appears in decline or remove copy.
patterns.pitfalls: A grey text link for Skip. Remove confirms like 'Say goodbye to Ollie?'.

patterns.name: Quiet acknowledgement instead of celebration
patterns.exemplars: Apple's HIG on feedback: confirm only significant completions, with the Apple Pay confirmation as the example. Apple's HIG on motion: brief, precise, cancellable animation.
patterns.howToApply: On naming, on the 'Everything we can hold is on file' state and on the claim receipt, the only feedback is one factual sentence and, for the keeper, its pose settling to relaxed. Under Reduce Motion it is a static swap.
patterns.pitfalls: 'Congratulations' copy, badge unlocks, sound, count-up numbers, animation longer than 5 seconds with no way to pause it (WCAG 2.2.2).

patterns.name: Real deadline stated as a date, fail closed
patterns.exemplars: The f9-founding-meter-preview prompt already uses a date rather than a live countdown and shows nothing when the lookup fails. Mathur et al. and the FTC single out baseless or resetting countdowns.
patterns.howToApply: Block Founders and the preview use the same neutral date pill and the same fail-closed rule. Warning styling appears only where a missed date has a real consequence for the household.
patterns.pitfalls: A warning-tinted 'closes in 6 days' pill next to a depletion bar reads like an obligation alarm for a social perk.

patterns.name: Next reachable reward only
patterns.exemplars: UbiFit added an optional 'alternate weekly goal' so goals stayed reachable during hard weeks (Consolvo 2008/2009). Goal-gradient research shows pull is strongest when the remaining distance is small.
patterns.howToApply: Invite rewards show the unlocked rows, the next locked tier with its remaining count, and a collapsed 'More rewards (2)' row for the rest. With 30 pilot users, the 10- and 25-join tiers are effectively out of reach.
patterns.pitfalls: A list of distant locked tiers ('22 more neighbors who join') becomes a record of failure. Any leaderboard of top inviters invites social comparison, which reduced motivation over time in Hanus & Fox.

antipatterns: A streak counter anywhere: keeper, Mail Day, widget, Today. Streak attachment led runners to run injured and grieve for weeks (PLOS One), and a highlighted broken streak lowers later engagement (Silverman & Barasch).

The keeper expressing its own feelings about the user ('Ollie misses you', 'Ollie is sad you didn't check in'). Guilt-based mascot messages are the core criticism of Duolingo, and they drove the Slate reviewer to quit Finch.
A mood that decays with time away or is computed from app opens. Mood must come from obligations only. Fish'n'Steps participants avoided the unhappy fish.
Distress poses (crying, drooping, shivering, sick) or darker scenery for a high-obligation state. UbiFit deliberately avoided wilting and storms.
The keeper's avatar, name or voice in a push notification or notification icon. It turns a factual reminder into an emotional one and misstates urgency (Apple HIG on managing notifications).
'X of Y things on file', or a closed segmented ring whose empty segments are outlined. Endowed-progress and goal-gradient research show these read as unfinished tasks.
Outlined segments a T1 saved place can never fill (money, people, proof). An unreachable goal drawn as a gap.

'+1 on file' toasts, count-up animations, keeper levels, accessories unlocked by adding facts. Measurement reduces enjoyment (Etkin 2016), and points and levels raise output but not intrinsic motivation.

Confetti, particle bursts, celebration sounds or haptics, full-screen success takeovers. Motion must have a purpose and be optional (Apple HIG), and auto-playing motion over 5 seconds must be pausable (WCAG 2.2.2).
Ignoring Reduce Motion or prefers-reduced-motion for the Rive/Lottie keeper (WCAG 2.3.3).
A grey text-link Skip, or decline copy that shames or plays on the creature's feelings (NN/g on confirmshaming).
Keeping a 'Give your place a keeper' invitation on Today after the user tapped Skip. That is nagging, and Apple's HIG says a skipped tutorial should not be presented again.
Auto-presenting the naming sheet on any launch, including the 'second Today open' in design doc §F11.
Multi-step pet setup (pronouns, traits, colours, quiz). Finch's 45-screen first run is the counter-example, and NN/g says visual customisation doesn't belong in onboarding.
Gating any feature, reward or referral payout behind naming or keeping the keeper.
Using the keeper to sell referrals or Founding slots ('Ollie wants neighbours').
Warning-tinted countdown pills or ticking timers for social perks. This borrows urgency from real obligations (Mathur 2019, FTC 2022).
Leaderboards or 'top inviter' ranks. Leaderboards and badges reduced motivation over time in Hanus & Fox 2015.
'Ollie knows 11 things about your home' or 'See what we know'. Anthropomorphised data-holding sounds like surveillance.
Showing 'A bill is overdue' on the widget or lock screen, or to household members without finance.view, through the keeper's mood.
Letting the keeper sit above an active safety alert, or appear beside one. The v1 prompt's suppression rule is right.

Citing the widely circulated statistics '63% more likely to abandon a habit after one missed day' and 'CHI 2020: streak anxiety is the top reason for abandonment'. I could not trace either to a primary source, so keep them out of prompts and specs.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The place file is reached from 'a single progress row on Today during the first 14 days reading "3 of 6 things on file →"', while the same prompt says nothing may read as 'you are 60% complete'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: A visible denominator turns the task into one that is started and unfinished, and that raises pressure to complete: 34% vs 19% completion with endowed progress (Nunes & Drèze 2006), and effort follows the proportion remaining (Kivetz et al. 2006). '3 of 6' is exactly the '50% complete' framing the prompt forbids. The design doc's own F2 checklist has seven keys, so 6 also matches no defined set.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Drop the denominator. Either name the single next useful fact ('Add your pickup day →'), or show '3 things on file →'. If the F2 three-question checklist is kept, call it a checklist, let each step be dismissed, and remove each step when it is done. Apply the same fix to the Today composition.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The Today content list includes 'Progress row: "3 of 6 things on file →"'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Same evidence as for the place file: X-of-Y framing is how endowed progress and goal-gradient effects create completion pressure (Nunes & Drèze 2006; Kivetz et al. 2006). It also contradicts the house rule, repeated across prompts, that nothing may read as a percentage complete.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Replace it with a denominator-free invitation row that points to one specific missing fact, and hide it once the first-week facts exist or the user dismisses it.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The fact count is a five-segment ring. Unknown categories are 'drawn as a border.strong hairline outline'. The T1 frame shows 'money/people/proof as outlined segments', and the prompt claims this 'is deliberately NOT a progress bar' and makes a saved place read as 'a smaller instrument rather than a failing one'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: A closed shape with filled and outlined segments carries a visible denominator (4 of 5), which people read as the proportion of the goal remaining (Kivetz et al. 2006; Nunes & Drèze 2006). UbiFit showed absence as a neutral sparse garden, never as empty slots (Consolvo 2008). For T1, three of the outlined segments cannot be filled at that tier. Apple's HIG also warns that ring-like elements get confused with Activity rings, which iOS users associate with closing the ring. That last point is an inference for non-fitness data.
