An 'Are you sure?' dialog on Decline or on routine actions. NN/g says overused confirmation dialogs stop being read; use Undo.
Showing residents' full names to anyone holding an invitation link before acceptance, because links get forwarded.
Reminders that keep firing after a co-resident has resolved the item. Apple warns that repeated notifications about the same thing lead people to turn off all notifications from the app.
The app name in the push title, or a title over 30 characters with the important part at the end. Android truncates it, and the app name is already in the header.
Bill amounts and street addresses in push bodies by default. Apple warns against private information visible to others on the lock screen.

Reusing the keyboard focus-ring token (border.focus) as a decorative highlight. Keyboard users may think focus is on that row. This is inferred from the purpose of WCAG focus indicators; I did not fetch SC 2.4.7.
Color alone for expiry, overdue or unread. Apple says 'Convey information with more than color alone'.

Putting household sharing behind a paywall in a product whose retention loop depends on it. Sweepy App Store reviewers complain about needing a subscription to share with their household. This is weak, anecdotal evidence.

A visible manage control that silently does nothing for a member (the Android canPerform early-return that v1 already targets). Participants in Zeng and Roesner's study struggled to tell what they could and couldn't use.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: For push, 'the caveat rides the TITLE', drawn as 'Garbage + recycling is tomorrow (not yet confirmed)' (51 characters) with the caveat at the end. Household row titles such as 'Dana added Chimney sweep to the calendar' (40 characters) are also over 30.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android's notification design guide limits the content title to 30 characters and the content text to 40. A 51-character title with the caveat last is truncated in exactly the place v1 is trying to protect, just as the body tail would be. Apple likewise asks for brief titles readable at a glance.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the caveat in the title, but put it first and keep the title at 30 characters or fewer: 'Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow' (28) with body 'Wed Sep 17 - Camas city schedule' (under 40). Household titles: 'Sam marked Clark PUD paid' (25), 'Dana added Chimney sweep' (24), 'Priya finished HVAC filter' (26). Add a 30/40 character budget to the prompt.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Each household event is its own notification (in-app row plus push when enabled, per design doc F3). Grouping is specified only as a same-day, same-actor in-app row ('Sam paid 3 bills'). The OS push tray is drawn only for reminders, so no push grouping, coalescing or interruption level is decided for household activity.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Zeng and Roesner's field study found co-resident activity notifications were often overwhelming or ignored. The most valued uses were security and confirming automations, and a single event produced several notifications. NN/g says to merge bursts, Apple says not to send several notifications for the same thing and defines Passive for 'view at their leisure', and Android auto-groups four or more and prefers updating an existing notification.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: In the prompt, set the Household activity channel to deliver quietly by default (iOS Passive, Android Medium importance, no sound), with the in-app row always present. Merge events for the same home within a window into one push that updates in place, and draw that grouped push on iOS and Android. Reserve Active delivery for bill_paid to members who still see that bill as unpaid and due soon, and send task_completed only to the task's creator or assignee.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Push and row content carries the amount and the street-derived home label: bill reminder push body '$84.00 - Maple St'; bill_paid caption '$84 - due Sep 20 - Maple St' (design doc push body '${amount} - due {date}').
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG: 'Avoid including sensitive, personal, or confidential information in a notification... private information that could be visible to others.' Amounts owed plus a street name on a lock screen are the kind of detail this warns against.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep amounts in the in-app row, but default push bodies to 'Due Sunday - Maple St' without the amount. Where the user has named the home (e.g. 'Home'), use that name instead of the street.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The Paid state is designed for 'arriving here from a reminder', which implies bill reminders can still fire after a co-resident has marked the bill paid.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple: sending several notifications about the same thing makes people turn off all notifications from the app. Android: update the existing notification when separate ones add nothing, and don't notify when no action is needed.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the reassurance frame for race conditions only. Add to the f3-bill-detail-web and f3-household-notifications prompts that marking a bill paid cancels its scheduled reminders for every member and replaces any delivered reminder (same thread or tag) with the bill_paid notice.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Member read-only: 'no Mark paid on the row at all'. The member holds finance.view only, yet the screen's stated job is 'so two people do not pay the same bill'. f3-bill-detail-web likewise draws 'Mark paid' as absent for members.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Geeng and Roesner found the person who sets things up ends up holding most of the control, and recommend designing for other household members. Song et al. (CHI 2021) found shared-account conflict comes from members seeing ownership differently. Zeng and Roesner warn that restrictive setups widen the gap between the setup person and everyone else. If a member who actually paid cannot record it, the double-payment problem this screen exists to prevent remains. The papers do not test bills directly; this conflict is between v1's own stated job and the permission it draws.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Give members an attributed, undoable 'I paid this' action (in the overflow and on bill detail), even if adding, editing and removing bills stays manager-only. If the product decides against that, the member caption must name who can mark it paid ('Dana or Marcus can mark this paid'), not just say why the member can't.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Role chips 'Member - Guest' carry no capability description. The review step is 'a plain manifest - four label/value rows' in which the role appears only as 'Role offered - Member'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Google Home, Ring and Apple Home all explain each role in plain terms at the point where it is chosen. Google also lets the invitee review what is shared before joining. The sender is choosing what a stranger will see of the household calendar and bills, so the role name alone does not make the manifest checkable.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add a one-line capability caption under each chip, and expand the 'Role offered' manifest row to the same grant list f3b shows the invitee (sees and edits the calendar; sees bills and who paid; sees who lives here), generated from one shared string. The manifest stays plain; only that row gains a second line.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The link channel is warned with 'Anyone with this link can join your household until it expires. Send it to one person.', and the example manifest shows 'Expires - Sep 30, 2026 (14 days)'. The prompt draws no use limit and no owner approval for link joins.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Exemplars limit open links in the system rather than in the copy. 1Password requires an organizer to confirm each new member, Life360 codes expire in 72 hours (snippet), Discord lets the creator cap uses and duration (snippet), and Slack lets admins shorten or deactivate links.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: If the backend can, make link invitations single-use and say 'Works once' in the manifest. Otherwise add an approval step: link joiners appear in the roster's pending group as 'Waiting for your OK' and see no household data until approved, and the active link is a pending row with 'Turn off link'. Keep the warning at the point of choice, as v1 does.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The locked column lists product names as rows: 'a residency letter; your Residency Pass; neighbor messages; Real Rent; Block Founder rank'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g plain-language guidance: unexplained jargon frustrates even expert readers. Platform exemplars describe permissions as actions. An invitee who has never used Pantopus cannot tell what 'Real Rent' or 'Block Founder rank' is, and this screen is the moment consent is given.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Rewrite each locked row as a verb phrase, with the product name only in parentheses if at all: 'Message your neighbors', 'Get a residency letter', 'Show your Residency Pass', 'Share what you pay in rent (Real Rent)', 'Earn a Block Founder rank'. Keep row height and type as v1 specifies.

numbers: Apple Family Sharing invitations expire after 15 days, and Apple keeps no record of expired invitations. Declined invitations sent through Messages are kept 30 days so both sides see they were declined (apple.com/legal/privacy/data/en/family-sharing).

Ring shared-user invitation is valid for 14 days per the current 'Adding and managing shared and Guest Users' page. Another Ring page surfaced in search said 7 days, so treat the figure as changing (ring.com/support/articles/clv68).
Ring professional-installer access is removed automatically after 48 hours. Shared access can take up to 15 minutes to appear.
1Password Families invitations expire after 5 days and can be resent at any time. Removed members have 30 days to move their personal items (support.1password.com/add-remove-family-members).
Life360 invite codes expire after 72 hours (support.life360.com; search snippet only, page returned 403).

Slack invitations and invite links expire after 30 days. Owners can shorten links to 1 or 7 days or set them to never expire. A snippet says one link can be used by up to 400 people (slack.com/help/articles/360060363633).
Discord invite links default to 7 days, with durations from 1 minute to 7 days or never, and a configurable maximum number of uses (support.discord.com Invites 101; search snippet only).
NN/g: if more than 5 notifications need to go out at once, combine them into one (nngroup.com/articles/push-notification).
Android groups 4 or more notifications automatically on Android 7.0+ if the app doesn't specify a group (developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/notifications/group).
Android notification content title: 30 characters or fewer. Content text: 40 or fewer. No app name in the title (developer.android.com/design/ui/mobile/guides/home-screen/notifications).
Apple: use Time Sensitive only for an event happening now or within an hour. Critical is extremely rare and needs Apple's approval (HIG managing notifications).
NN/g transactional notifications: push text is limited to 240 characters at most.
US Census 2024: 38.5 million one-person households = 29% of all US households (19% in 1974).
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8: pointer targets at least 24x24 CSS px, or spaced so a 24px circle around each doesn't overlap another target.
Apple HIG: default control size 44x44 pt on iOS (28x28 pt minimum). Text contrast at least 4.5:1 up to 17pt, 3:1 at 18pt+ or bold.
Material Design: touch targets at least 48x48dp (about 9mm), with about 8dp between targets (search snippet of m3.material.io).
NN/g plain language: keep sentences under 15-20 words.

Zeng and Roesner (USENIX Security 2019): 7 households, 19 participants, one month. 14 participants kept activity notifications on for all devices, 4 mixed on/off/proximity. One front-door entry produced 4 notifications.
Geeng and Roesner (CHI 2019): 18 participants in multi-user smart homes.
Freed et al. (CHI 2018): 89 participants in a study of how intimate-partner abusers exploit technology.

Apple Home: two roles (Resident, Guest) plus two toggles. Google Home: two roles (Admin, Member) plus two Member toggles (Activity, Settings). Ring: three levels (Limited, Standard, Advanced) plus a temporary installer role.

topic: trust-provenance-privacy: where facts come from, how to dispute them, what verification means, locked features, "see what others see", and confirming that a report was received

principles.principle: The provenance mark has to explain itself where it appears. Almost nobody opens the detail view.
principles.evidence: Piccardi et al. (WWW 2020) logged 96M citation events on English Wikipedia. About 1 in 300 page views leads to a reference click (0.29% overall, 0.56% desktop, 0.13% mobile), and 93% of citation links got no click in a month. Clicks were more common on short or low-quality pages, where the article itself lacked the information.
principles.implication: Design as if under 1% of mobile users will ever open 'Where this comes from'. A caveat that changes what someone should do (city default pickup, county-level radon, preliminary AQI) must be readable on the row, card, widget or share card itself. The provenance sheet is the audit trail for the rare person who wants it. Do not put any essential caveat only inside the sheet.

principles.principle: A shape that carries meaning needs a visible word next to it, at least once per surface. Hollow or empty marks are especially easy to misread.
principles.evidence: NN/g: universal icons are rare, and icon labels should be visible at all times, without any interaction from the user. Hover-only labels fail on touch. Kelley et al. (SOUPS 2009, n=24 lab plus focus groups) found that many participants were unclear what the blank cells in their privacy label meant. Some read blank as 'never happens', others as 'anything goes' or 'not decided yet'.
principles.implication: Keep the filled, hollow and tick shapes, but every surface that shows them needs a one-line legend or a first-occurrence label, e.g. '○ on record, not confirmed'. Surfaces that stand alone (widget, OG card, push) print the word next to the glyph. Each mark gets an accessible name ('Trash day Tuesday, on record, not confirmed'). A hollow circle must never also mean 'empty', 'open slot' or 'zero' elsewhere in the product.

principles.principle: Keep three facts apart: who says it (source), how sure anyone is (confidence), and what it covers (scope). The authorities themselves limit what their data means.
principles.evidence: EPA says its Map of Radon Zones should not be used to determine if individual homes need to be tested, and that you should test your home no matter where you live. AirNow says its data are not subjected to the full validation used for EPA's regulatory database. Wikipedia's [citation needed] tag carries a reason and a date parameter, so a reader sees why a claim is flagged and since when.
principles.implication: Add a 'Covers' line to the provenance sheet: 'All of Clark County', 'This parcel' or 'Your household'. Give each dataset its own confidence sentence. For radon: 'County zone from EPA. It says nothing about your home's level; only a test does.' Put the free-kit action beside it. For air: 'Preliminary reading from AirNow, observed 8:00am.' The row-level radon and flood marks should also show county-wide vs parcel scope, so a county zone never reads as a finding about the home.

principles.principle: A report flow is only finished once it has confirmed receipt, said what happens next and roughly when, and delivered the outcome somewhere the reporter can find it.
principles.evidence: EU DSA Art. 16(4): send a confirmation of receipt without undue delay. Art. 16(5): notify the notifier of the decision and the options for redress. Art. 16(6): disclose any automated decision-making. Google Maps keeps a private 'Your contributions' list with Pending ('Google is confirming your edit'), Accepted and Not accepted statuses, and says only you can find the list. NN/g heuristic #1 says to keep users informed through appropriate feedback within a reasonable amount of time.
principles.implication: After 'This isn't right', the sheet should say: 'Reported Sep 16. We'll check it against City of Camas Public Works by Sep 23 and tell you here.' Then the mark and sheet keep a 'You reported this · checking' state. Later a resolution line appears on the same sheet ('Fixed Sep 20' or 'The city still lists Tuesday. Here's their page'), with an optional in-app notice. A solo founder should commit only to a window they can actually meet.

principles.principle: Let people fix their own copy of a fact immediately. Send only shared or authoritative records to a review queue, and send facts owned by an outside authority to that authority's process.
principles.evidence: On Zillow, a verified owner uses 'Edit Facts' directly on the owner view (Zillow help, via search results; the help pages returned 403 to fetch). Public Google Maps edits go through moderation instead. A FEMA flood-zone designation can only be changed by FEMA through a LOMA or LOMR-F request, submitted via Online LOMC or eLOMA.
principles.implication: 'That's not my schedule' should lead first to 'Set my pickup day'. That turns the hollow mark into a tick immediately. 'Also tell us the city's map looks wrong' is a secondary checkbox. For a flood zone, 'This isn't right' opens a line such as 'Only FEMA can change this. Here's how (Letter of Map Amendment)' with the link. Pantopus must not promise to 'check' a FEMA determination.

principles.principle: To explain privacy, show exactly what the audience sees, and put the controls right beside that view.
principles.evidence: Lipford, Besmer & Watson (UPSEC 2008, within-subjects, n=16) tested an audience-view privacy interface. Accuracy rose from 66.14% to 93.86%, time fell from 7.7 to 4.5 minutes, and comfort rose from 5.4 to 6.4 out of 7. The authors recommend interactive controls inside the audience view, plus visual indicators for hidden information so users don't get a false sense of security. Facebook's 'View As' does the same job; it was pulled in Sep 2018 over an access-token bug and restored in May 2019.
principles.implication: The privacy mirror should render the neighbor's actual feed card and the neighbor's actual map pin, not a diagram of the mechanism. Keep 'Change' and 'Edit profile' beside each row (v1 already does). Add an explicit hidden row, e.g. 'Hidden from neighbors: your street address, your home on the map'. Build the mirror from server-rendered output for a synthetic viewer rather than client-side re-projection, so it cannot drift from reality. Facebook's breach shows that a 'view as' feature must never issue a viewer-scoped token.

principles.principle: A privacy picture that claims to be checkable must match the real transform. Stable offsets protect people; offsets re-drawn on every post do not.
principles.evidence: Pantopus backend/utils/locationPrivacy.js, approx_area case: a keyed HMAC offset of ±0.005° lat and lng, 'stable per entity so pins do not flicker', rounded to 3 decimals. At Camas (45.6°N) that is about ±556 m north–south and ±389 m east–west, a box of about 1.1 × 0.78 km. Andrés et al. (CCS 2013, Geo-Indistinguishability): applying noise independently to each report gives nε privacy, 'only useful when the number of points is small'. Heaton's 2021 Bumble fix was to round locations before any distance calculation, so exact coordinates are never used.
principles.implication: Never write 're-rolled every time you post'. It is untrue of the code, and it would be the weaker design. The mirror should say 'Neighbors see your posts at this spot, the same spot every time, about 0.3 mi from your address' and draw that public point. If a range is drawn at all, it must be the real ±0.005° box (about 1.1 × 0.8 km), with a scale bar in tenths of a mile. A 150 m circle holds only about 8% of that box.

principles.principle: Verification badges on people are widely misread and quickly lose value. Attach verification to actions, and state precisely what it proves.
principles.evidence: In a US survey (n=299, Jan 2023), 61% thought Twitter verification meant identity was confirmed, 7% equated it with credibility, over 80% misread the gold and gray checks, and only 52% knew the blue check no longer required ID. Edgerly & Vraga (2019) found little attention paid to the verification mark when judging credibility. Airbnb says verification doesn't guarantee that someone is who they say they are, and that verified status can be lost. Recent Nextdoor App Store reviews (Jul–Sep 2026) complain about fraud rental ads from 'verified' accounts.
principles.implication: Keep the roster free of status chips (v1 already decides this). Wherever verification is shown, name the method and date instead of a bare 'Verified': 'Address confirmed by postcard · Sep 8, 2026', or 'Confirmed by Sam Ortega · Sep 16, 2026' after an attestation. Never use a check-badge shape that could read as endorsement. The attestation sheet's consequence line should also say what confirming does not do (v1 already does).

principles.principle: Keep a locked control visible, dimmed, and explained, with the way to unlock it. Hide it only if this person can never get it.
principles.evidence: Jakob Nielsen reviewed 60 sources: 76% recommend showing inactive controls in a muted state, and 24% prefer always-clickable controls that show an error. He says disabled controls must never be communication dead ends; on touch, tapping one should explain what is required. His exception: hide features the user can never access, such as role-based ones. The NN/g video on disabled buttons says to clearly explain why a button is disabled.
principles.implication: The locked-action row is the right pattern for household-verified members, who can verify through owner attestation. Tapping the dimmed control opens the same explanation as the row. Someone with only a saved place (T1) should not see attested home controls at all; offer 'Claim this address' instead. A household invitee whose owner has disabled attestation, and who has no other method available, should see the reason and no dead 'Verify address' link.

principles.principle: Explanatory text must pass 4.5:1 contrast, and informative marks must pass 3:1. Only the disabled control itself is exempt.
principles.evidence: WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for normal text and exempts only text in an inactive UI component, pure decoration, or text nobody can see. WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for graphics needed to understand content and exempts inactive components. Contrast computed from house tokens: text.muted #9CA3AF on sunken #F3F4F6 = 2.31:1; text.secondary on sunken = 4.39:1; text.secondary on base = 4.83:1; text.strong on sunken = 9.37:1; primary.DEFAULT #0284c7 on white = 4.10:1; info text on info bg = 3.84:1; primary.700 on info bg = 5.57:1; success #059669 on white = 3.77:1.
principles.implication: The locked-row reason, the locked-column rows, and the ETA and 'Varies' chips are information, not inactive controls, so they need 4.5:1. Use text.strong on sunken, or text.secondary on base or raised. Inline links such as 'Verify address' use primary.700, not primary.DEFAULT, at 13–14px. Draw the hollow provenance ring in text.secondary or darker (at least 3:1), never border or muted tokens. Success-green text needs a darker shade, though a success-green tick glyph passes at 3:1.

principles.principle: A tiny mark is never the tap target. The row or cell that contains it is.
principles.evidence: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA): pointer targets must be at least 24×24 CSS px, unless a 24px circle centred on each undersized target does not intersect a neighbor, or one of the Inline, Essential or User-agent exceptions applies. Platform minimums are 44×44pt (Apple HIG) and 48×48dp (Material); these are well established but were not re-fetched in this session.
principles.implication: In the 14-day strip, the whole day cell (at least 44pt / 48dp / 24px) opens the provenance sheet, and the 8px dot is just its content. On calendar rows the whole row is the target. The AQI band marker gets an invisible hit area of at least 44pt. Specimen frames should draw the hit area as an overlay.

principles.principle: Give verification lead times as honest ranges. Add a 'what if it's late' path, and do not let people start a second attempt while one is in flight.
principles.evidence: Google Business Profile: 'Most codes arrive within 14 days', codes expire after 30 days, and requesting a new code invalidates the one already in the mail. USPS First-Class Mail takes 1–5 business days, excluding print and hand-off time. Recent Nextdoor App Store reviews (Jul–Aug 2026) describe week-long unexplained waits, rejected bill photos with no stated reason, and nobody to contact.
principles.implication: The postcard chip should show a range with a real upper bound, e.g. '5–10 days'. The pending state shows: mailed date · expected window · code expiry date · 'Didn't arrive by Sep 26? Send a new code' (enabled only after that date, with a note that the old code will stop working). The document method lists accepted document types before upload. A rejected document gets a specific reason and a retry, never a bare 'doesn't meet standard'.

principles.principle: Ask for verification at the moment someone tries a gated action, not as a welcome step.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG: request permission only when the app clearly needs it, and ideally wait until people actually use a feature that requires access. Avoid requesting at launch. Airbnb asks guests to verify identity when they book, with 12 hours to finish (1 hour if check-in is sooner), and the reservation shows as pending until then.
principles.implication: The primary action after accepting an invitation should be the thing the person came for ('Open Home'). Verification belongs in the locked rows and the verify sheet's reason header ('To send neighbor messages, we need to confirm you live here'). Because a postcard takes days, a secondary 'Start address verification now' on the success screen is still worth keeping.

principles.principle: A 'Why am I seeing this?' answer must be complete, literally true, and come with a control.
principles.evidence: Andreou et al. (NDSS 2018) found Facebook's ad explanations often incomplete and sometimes misleading. Meta's 2019 launch of 'Why am I seeing this post?' said transparency wasn't enough without corresponding controls, and linked Unfollow and feed preferences. Rader, Cotter & Cho (CHI 2018): explanations made people more aware of how the system works, but were less effective at helping them judge whether its output was correct.
principles.implication: Generate each curator explainer line from the same fields that drive behaviour: origin, source feed name, and exclusion from organic counts. Ship a line such as 'doesn't count as neighborhood activity' only once the de-curation code is live. Keep the mute toggle inline (v1 already does). The source line should link to the publisher's own page, so a reader can check the fact itself and not just its origin.

principles.principle: Name identities, tiers and roles in the user's words. Internal jargon and near-identical names defeat even a well-built label.
principles.evidence: Zhang et al. (iOS privacy labels, n=24): most participants had never noticed the labels, and they could rarely tell 'Data Linked to You' from 'Data Used to Track You'. Confusing terms and a disconnect from settings got in the way. NN/g heuristic #2: speak the users' language rather than internal jargon.
principles.implication: Change the chip text 'Pantopus curator' to 'From Pantopus'. 'Block Founder' and 'Founding Neighbor' share a stem and are the kind of pair people confuse. Keep the distinct chip shapes, and test whether a more distinct name for one of them (e.g. keep 'Block Founder #3' and describe the tier as 'First 5 on this block') reduces confusion. Every 'Only you' or 'Your household' chip should open the control that changes it.

principles.principle: A caveat repeated identically on every row stops being read. Use a quiet persistent mark, and put a prominent caveat only where the stakes are highest.
principles.evidence: Anderson, Vance, Kirwan et al. (CHI 2015; MIS Quarterly 2018), using fMRI and eye tracking, report a dramatic drop in visual processing of a security warning after only its second exposure. Polymorphic warnings, whose appearance varies, resisted habituation much better.
principles.implication: This supports v1's approach: a mark on each row plus a caveat in the push title. Reserve the full-sentence caveat for moments someone will act on: the night-before push, the first pickup card, the first share of a compare card. Vary its wording by context rather than stamping one suffix everywhere.

principles.principle: Scarcity claims must be real, dated, and disappear when they can't be backed.
principles.evidence: Mathur et al. (CSCW 2019) crawled about 11K shopping sites and found 1,818 dark-pattern instances, including 157 deceptive countdown timers on 140 sites (timers that reset, or offers still valid after expiry). They also list 'limited-time messages' with no deadline and low-stock messages shown on every product.
principles.implication: This supports v1's founding meter: always five segments, a printed closing date, no live countdown, and no card on a failed lookup. The 'first here' CTA must be computed from the same founding_open value as the meter. Log the window's closing date, and never extend it silently.

patterns.name: Inline marker, detail on demand
patterns.exemplars: Wikipedia's [citation needed] is a small italic superscript placed right after the claim. Its tooltip gives the reason ('This claim needs references to reliable sources'), and the tag carries a date. Reference numbers are superscripts that expand to the source.
patterns.howToApply: The filled/hollow/tick mark sits on every data row. Tapping the whole row opens x-provenance-sheet with the authority, the reading date, a 'Covers' scope line and the source link. Show a legend once per surface.
patterns.pitfalls: Hardly anyone opens the detail (0.29% on Wikipedia), so the mark plus a short word has to carry the caveat by itself. An unlabeled hollow mark will be misread.

patterns.name: Context attached to the item, with its sources
patterns.exemplars: X Community Notes put reader-written context directly under the post with source links. A peer-reviewed study (Chuai et al.) found notes cut reposts of misleading posts by 62% and roughly doubled the odds of deletion (+103%), but they often arrive too late for the early viral spread.
patterns.howToApply: When a reported fact is corrected or confirmed, show the outcome on the same row and sheet ('Corrected Sep 20: the city moved recycling to Wednesday'), with the source. The fix goes where people already look, not into a separate inbox.
patterns.pitfalls: Speed matters. A correction that lands after the night-before push has already fired is too late. For schedule facts, prefer the self-fix ('Set my pickup day') over waiting for review.

patterns.name: A private list of your reports and their status
patterns.exemplars: Google Maps 'Your contributions' shows each edit as Pending ('Google is confirming your edit'), Accepted or Not accepted, and states 'Only you can find your list'. Apple Maps keeps a Reports section; per Apple support search results, reports stay visible for about 90 days (not confirmed on the fetched page).
patterns.howToApply: A 'Your reports' row in x-place-file lists each 'This isn't right' submission with Checking / Fixed / No change, a date and a one-line reason. The provenance sheet shows the same status for that fact.
patterns.pitfalls: Google community threads complain that edits sit in Pending with no reason given. Every closed report needs a sentence of reason, not just a status word.

patterns.name: The owner edits their own record; others suggest changes to the shared one
patterns.exemplars: Zillow: after claiming a home, the owner uses 'Edit Facts' directly. Google Maps: anyone can suggest an edit, and it goes to moderation.
patterns.howToApply: A household member confirms or corrects the pickup day with one tap: the hollow mark becomes a tick and the change applies to the household only. Reporting that the city-wide default is wrong is a separate, optional step.
patterns.pitfalls: Don't let a household correction silently rewrite the city default for other addresses. Label the correction's scope ('For your household').

patterns.name: Send disputes of authoritative data to the authority
patterns.exemplars: FEMA: only a LOMA or LOMR-F request (Online LOMC, eLOMA, or paper MT-EZ/MT-1) changes a flood-zone determination. EPA: the radon map is not for individual homes, and the fix is to test the home.
patterns.howToApply: For flood, 'This isn't right' opens 'Only FEMA can change this. How to request a Letter of Map Amendment' with the link. For radon, it leads to 'Get a free test kit'. Pantopus can still accept 'you have the wrong parcel' reports about its own geocoding.
patterns.pitfalls: Don't imply that Pantopus will 'check' or change a federal determination. Separate 'we matched the wrong spot' (Pantopus's error) from 'the map is wrong' (the authority's).

patterns.name: Audience view next to its controls
patterns.exemplars: Facebook 'View As' / 'View as Public'. LinkedIn's public-profile preview on the page where you edit public visibility. Lipford's audience-view prototype put tabs per audience next to the controls and raised accuracy from 66% to 94%.
patterns.howToApply: f9-privacy-mirror renders the literal neighbor feed-card header and the literal public map pin. The control ('Change', 'Edit profile', 'Manage where your posts appear') sits on the same row, with an explicit 'Hidden from neighbors' row.
patterns.pitfalls: Facebook's View As caused a 2018 breach through token handling. Render the mirror from server output for a synthetic viewer and never issue a viewer-scoped credential. If the mirror hides content a neighbor could see through another path (saved posts, the post API), it gives false comfort.

patterns.name: Show the area, not the point
patterns.exemplars: The iOS 14 permission sheet has a 'Precise' toggle. Off, the map preview shows a wide circular region a few miles across instead of a dot. Android 12's dialog shows map images for Precise and Approximate (about 3 km²; precise is usually within about 50 m).
patterns.howToApply: Wherever Pantopus describes how precise something is (post location, the compare card's city-only reveal), draw it at true scale with a scale bar, sized from the real server parameters.
patterns.pitfalls: A region drawn centred on the true home gives the home away in a screenshot, because its centre is the home. Prefer drawing the public point, or a region that isn't centred on the home.

patterns.name: Stable obfuscation instead of fresh noise each time
patterns.exemplars: Pantopus's own keyed HMAC jitter, stable per coordinate. Heaton's Bumble fix rounds locations before any distance maths. Andrés et al. show that independent noise on each report adds up privacy loss linearly.
patterns.howToApply: Copy and visuals say 'the same approximate spot every time'. Build the mirror from the stable public point.
patterns.pitfalls: A stable point makes a person's posts linkable to one another (all of this household's posts appear at one spot). Say so in the mirror's detail if the pilot finds it matters.

patterns.name: 'Why am I seeing this?' with a control built in
patterns.exemplars: Facebook (2019) put 'Why am I seeing this post?' in the post's overflow menu. It shows the source relationship and the main ranking signals, with shortcuts to See First, Unfollow and News Feed Preferences.
patterns.howToApply: The curator chip's overflow expands in place into four short lines generated from post.origin and the source feed, plus the 'Show Pantopus posts in Nearby' toggle.
patterns.pitfalls: Andreou et al. found such explanations incomplete or misleading. Every line must be enforced by code, not aspirational.

patterns.name: Verification with explicit methods and lead times
patterns.exemplars: Nextdoor offers postcard, phone and other methods, depending on location (from Nextdoor Help via search; the page failed to fetch with a TLS error). Google Business Profile: 'Most codes arrive within 14 days', codes expire after 30 days, and you shouldn't request a new code while one is in the mail. Airbnb asks at booking and shows the reservation as pending, with a 12-hour window.
patterns.howToApply: f3b-verify-address-sheet lists methods with right-aligned ETA ranges, requirements, and a pending state that shows mailed date, expected window, expiry, and a late path that stays disabled until the window has passed.
patterns.pitfalls: Nextdoor reviews: 'a week and no one to talk to', and bill photos rejected with no reason. Every pending and rejected state needs a reason and a next step.

patterns.name: Disabled control plus a reason and a path
patterns.exemplars: Nielsen's synthesis: muted appearance plus a tooltip, a popover on touch, or a nearby hint. The control is never a dead end.
patterns.howToApply: The locked-action row sits under or instead of the control. Tapping the dimmed control opens the same reason. 'Verify address' opens the sheet with a reason parameter.
patterns.pitfalls: A reason in muted grey text fails WCAG 1.4.3. A generic 'Verification required' teaches nothing. If no path exists for this person, drop the link rather than offer a dead end.

patterns.name: Layered privacy label
patterns.exemplars: The CMU privacy nutrition label (Kelley 2009): participants answered more questions correctly (mean 10.13 vs 6.83 correct) and faster than with natural-language policies. Apple's App Store privacy labels, whose study users mostly never noticed and whose terms confused them.
patterns.howToApply: f10-mail-snap-privacy and the privacy mirror use a short fixed grid: what is stored, who can see it, how to delete it. Each cell links to the control that changes it.
patterns.pitfalls: Blank cells are ambiguous; write 'None' explicitly. Labels cut off from the controls confuse people (the iOS finding).

patterns.name: Honest, dated scarcity
patterns.exemplars: The counter-example is Mathur et al.'s deceptive timers and low-stock messages. The honest version is a fixed denominator, a printed closing date, and no display when the data is unknown.
patterns.howToApply: The founding meter always shows five segments, a closing-date caption, and nothing at all when the lookup fails.
patterns.pitfalls: Don't reuse filled/hollow semantics that the provenance mark already owns product-wide.

antipatterns: Saying post locations are 're-rolled every time you post'. The code uses a keyed stable offset, and independent per-post noise is the weaker design, since averaging several posts narrows the home down (Andrés et al.).
Drawing a 150 m privacy ring when the server applies ±0.005° (about 1.1 × 0.8 km at Camas). A 'checkable' picture that is wrong is worse than prose.
Centring any privacy region on the true home in a screenshot-able view. The centre is the home.
A hollow mark with no word anywhere on the surface. Blank or hollow cells are read inconsistently (Kelley 2009), and icons need visible labels (NN/g).
Using filled vs hollow for three different meanings (confirmed/unconfirmed, taken/open slot, density count) across the same product.
Making an 8px dot the tap target. WCAG 2.5.8 requires 24×24 CSS px, and platforms use 44pt / 48dp.
Informational text in text.muted on sunken (2.31:1) or text.secondary on sunken (4.39:1). Only inactive controls are exempt from 4.5:1.
Inline links and ETA chips in primary.DEFAULT (4.10:1 on white) or info on info-bg (3.84:1) at caption size. Use primary.700.
Ending a dispute at 'Thanks, we'll check it' with no date, no status and no outcome. DSA Art. 16 requires receipt and a decision notice, and Google and Apple Maps show status.
Offering schedule-specific reasons ('The date is wrong') on facts that have no date (AQI, flood zone, radon zone).
Promising to 'check' a FEMA flood determination or an EPA radon zone that Pantopus cannot change. Route to LOMA, or to a home test.
Treating a county-level radon zone or a preliminary AirNow reading as a finding about this home, e.g. a bare 'official' mark with no scope line.
Status chips on people ('Verified', 'Household member') in the roster. People misread badges as endorsement or identity proof (61% in the 2023 survey).
A bare 'Verified' with no method or date. Say 'Address confirmed by postcard · Sep 8'.
Internal jargon in user-facing labels ('curator'). The iOS label study shows unfamiliar terms defeat comprehension.
Promising something 'permanent' (rank, fee, slot) the system can't guarantee after staleness, move-out or a policy change.
A single optimistic postcard ETA ('5–7 days', 'expected by Sep 19') with no late path, no expiry, and a 'send another' that silently invalidates the first code.
Rejecting a verification document with no specific reason (the Nextdoor review pattern).
Making verification the primary welcome action right after an invitation is accepted, instead of asking when a gated action is tried.
A 'Why am I seeing this?' line the code does not enforce (e.g. 'doesn't count as neighborhood activity' before de-curation ships).
A pre-permission screen with a cancel or close button, or an 'Allow'-titled button. Apple HIG allows one 'Continue'-style button that opens the system alert.
A 'view as' feature that mints a viewer-scoped token or renders client-side from different data than neighbors actually get.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Caption: 'Your post lands somewhere inside this circle. It is re-rolled every time you post.' Ring about 150 m radius, scale bar '500 ft'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The shipped transform (backend/utils/locationPrivacy.js, approx_area) is a keyed HMAC offset of ±0.005° in lat and lng, 'stable per entity so pins do not flicker', rounded to 0.001°. At 45.6°N that is a box of about ±556 m × ±389 m, so roughly 92% of possible public points fall outside a 150 m circle. The caption is false twice over: the offset is not re-rolled, and the area is about 12× larger than drawn. Andrés et al. (Geo-Indistinguishability) show that independent noise per report degrades privacy linearly with the number of reports, so the stable offset is the better design and the copy describes the worse one.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Rewrite as: 'Neighbors see your posts at this spot, the same spot every time, about 0.3 mi from your address.' Take the drawn geometry from the server parameters: either the single public point, or the true ±0.005° box with a scale bar in tenths of a mile. Add a contract test that fails if the mirror's radius or box constant differs from locationPrivacy.js.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Draw a jitter ring centred on the user's location, with no pin, no house marker and no dot at the centre, because 'the centre is the thing being hidden'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The audience-view research (Lipford 2008: accuracy 66%→94%) and Facebook's 'View As' show the audience's literal view, not a model of the mechanism. What a neighbor literally sees on the Nearby map is one jittered pin. A ring drawn centred on the home still encodes the home's position as its geometric centre, so a shared screenshot gives away the very point the design is meant to hide.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw the public pin exactly where neighbors see it, labelled 'What neighbors see', with no home marker and no region centred on the home. Add a caption giving the distance from the address, and an explicit row 'Hidden from neighbors: your street address'. If a range must be shown, don't centre it on the home in any shareable frame.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Provenance is a mark everywhere and prose in exactly one place.' Confidence is carried by shape alone, and the word 'Unverified' must not be printed as a suffix.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Hardly anyone opens a detail view: Wikipedia citations are clicked on 0.13% of mobile page views, and 93% of citation links go unclicked in a month. NN/g says icons need text labels that are always visible. Kelley 2009 found blank or empty cells ambiguous. A hollow glyph with no word will be read inconsistently, and screen readers get nothing without an accessible name.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the shapes, and do not bring back a suffix on every row. Require a one-line legend per surface (or a label on first occurrence), the printed word next to the glyph on standalone surfaces (widget, OG card, push), and an accessible name on every mark. Caveats that change what someone should do must appear on the surface, not only in the sheet.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'This isn't right' offers two fixed options, 'The date is wrong' and 'That's not my schedule', on every frame (including AQI), then ends at 'Thanks — we'll check it.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: DSA Art. 16(4)–(6) requires confirmation of receipt, a notice of the decision with redress, and disclosure of any automation. Google Maps shows Pending/Accepted/Not accepted in a private list. NN/g heuristic #1 says to keep users informed within a reasonable time. FEMA flood zones can only be changed through LOMA/LOMR-F. Owners fix their own records directly (Zillow 'Edit Facts').
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Tailor reasons to the fact type (schedule: wrong day / not my service; hazard: wrong place matched / map is wrong → FEMA link; air: reading looks wrong). For schedules, lead with the self-fix 'Set my pickup day'. The confirmation should state a check-by date, and there should be persistent 'You reported this · checking' and resolved states on the sheet. Add a frame for the resolved outcome, and one for authority-owned data that links out instead of promising a check.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Three shapes (official/confirmed, on record/unconfirmed, you entered it) carry all confidence. No number, bar or meter. Payloads cover schedule, lease and AQI.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: EPA says the radon zone map should not be used to decide whether individual homes need testing. AirNow says its data are not fully validated like regulatory data. Confidence (how sure) and scope (county vs parcel vs household) are different facts, and one filled 'official' mark merges them.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep 'no numeric confidence', but add a 'Covers' line (county-wide / this parcel / your household) and per-dataset confidence sentences ('Preliminary reading'; 'County zone, not a reading of your home, test to know'). Add a radon or flood payload frame to prove the scope line.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The sheet is reached by tapping a data mark, e.g. 'a dot in Today's 14-day strip'. The specimen includes an 8px dot inside a strip cell.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 requires a pointer target of at least 24×24 CSS px, or spacing equivalent. Platform minimums are 44pt (iOS) and 48dp (Android). An 8px glyph cannot be the target.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: State that the whole day cell or row is the target (at least 44pt / 48dp / 24px), and draw the hit areas on the specimen frame. The hollow ring's stroke must be at least 3:1 against its background (WCAG 1.4.11), so use text.secondary or darker, never border tokens.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Colour: muted text on the sunken surface with a border-subtle hairline.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 1.4.3 exempts only text inside an inactive component. This row is live explanatory text with a working link, so it needs 4.5:1. House tokens give text.muted on sunken 2.31:1 and text.secondary on sunken 4.39:1, both failing. The 'Verify address' link in primary.DEFAULT on white is 4.10:1, also failing at 13–14px.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the calm, non-error tone, but specify text.strong on sunken (9.37:1) or text.secondary on base/raised (4.83 / 4.63:1), a lock glyph of at least 3:1, and the link in primary.700. Only the disabled control above the row may drop below 4.5:1.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The locked column uses 'lock glyph rows in the muted text token on the sunken surface'. The accepted state makes 'Verify this address' the primary CTA and 'Open Home' secondary.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The same contrast rule applies: these rows are read-only information, not inactive controls, and text.muted on sunken is 2.31:1. On timing, Apple HIG says to ask when a feature is actually used, not up front, and Airbnb asks for verification at booking. The person accepted in order to use household tools.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Set the locked rows in text.secondary on base or text.strong on sunken. Make 'Open Home' primary on the accepted screen. Keep verification as a clearly visible secondary ('Start address verification — postcards take about a week'), and rely on the locked rows' reason-parameterised sheet for the just-in-time ask.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: ETA chips 'in the info token'. Postcard 'Postcard code · 5–7 days'. Pending state 'mailed Sep 12, expected by Sep 19', with no late or expiry path.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Info text on info bg is 3.84:1 at caption size, which fails 4.5:1; primary.700 on info bg is 5.57:1. Google says 'most codes arrive within 14 days', codes expire after 30 days, and asking for a new code invalidates the one in the mail. USPS First-Class is 1–5 business days before print lead time. Nextdoor reviews show that unexplained waits and rejections drive 1-star reviews.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use primary.700 on info bg for the chips. Show the postcard as a range with a real upper bound (e.g. '5–10 days'). The pending state should show mailed date, expected window, code expiry, and a 'Didn't arrive? Send a new code' action enabled only after the window, warning that the old code will stop working. Add a rejected-document state with a specific reason and a retry.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The chip label is 'Pantopus curator', even though the same prompt says 'curator' is internal vocabulary.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g heuristic #2 says to use the users' words, not internal jargon. The iOS privacy-label study found unfamiliar terms stop people understanding what a label means.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Label the chip 'From Pantopus' (or 'Posted by Pantopus'), keep 'Source: Clark Public Utilities' as a separate caption line, and word the overflow item 'Mute posts from Pantopus'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The slot meter uses filled = taken and hollow = open, next to density dots where filled = count. Meanwhile x-provenance-sheet declares filled / hollow / tick 'the three shapes used everywhere in Pantopus' for confirmed / unconfirmed / you-entered.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Kelley 2009 found empty or blank cells read inconsistently, and NN/g stresses that icon meaning comes from consistent prior exposure. Here one visual variable (filled vs hollow) carries three different meanings on the same pre-auth preview, where provenance marks also appear on chips.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Reserve the hollow circle product-wide for 'on record, not confirmed'. Encode slots with a different variable, e.g. segment length or a solid-vs-hatched fill, with a numeral label ('3 of 5 open'). Encode density with the qualitative label plus a different glyph. Show the two encodings side by side in one frame to prove they can't be confused.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Block Founder #3 — your permanent rank on this block'. 'You are Block Founder #3. That rank is permanent.' 'Verify and you're Block Founder #3 here — permanently.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The design doc says isVerifiedResident checks both verification status and staleness, so verification can lapse. Airbnb warns that verified status can be lost when information changes. The product's own fail-closed rule (f9-founding-meter-preview) is to never promise what the system can't honour. Mathur et al. document how inflated promises erode trust.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Before shipping the copy, confirm in the data model that the rank survives staleness, move-out and re-verification. If it doesn't, say 'your rank on this block' plus a precise condition (e.g. 'kept even if you move') only if that condition is actually true.

numbers: Wikipedia citation click-through: 0.29% of page views overall, 0.56% desktop, 0.13% mobile. 93% of citation links get no click in a month (Piccardi et al., WWW 2020).
Community Notes: 62.0% average cut in reposts of noted misleading posts, +103.4% odds the author deletes, across 237,677 cascades; often too slow for the early viral phase (Chuai et al.).
Audience-view privacy UI: accuracy 66.14% → 93.86%, task time 7.7 → 4.5 min, comfort 5.4 → 6.4 out of 7 (Lipford et al. 2008, n=16).

Twitter verification survey (n=299, Jan 2023): 61% thought verified = identity confirmed, 7% equated it with credibility, over 80% misread the gold/gray checks, 52% knew the blue check no longer needed ID.
Privacy nutrition label: mean 10.13 vs 6.83 questions correct against a natural-language policy (Kelley et al. 2009, n=24).
iOS privacy label study: n=24; most participants had never noticed the labels.
Inactive controls: 76% of 60 sources recommend a muted disabled state; 24% prefer always-clickable controls with an error (Nielsen).
WCAG contrast: 4.5:1 normal text, 3:1 large text (18pt, or 14pt bold) and informative graphics or UI boundaries. Inactive components are exempt.
WCAG 2.5.8 target size: at least 24×24 CSS px, or a 24px-diameter spacing circle. Platform minimums (not re-fetched this session): 44×44pt iOS, 48×48dp Android.

House-token contrast (computed): text.muted on sunken 2.31:1; text.muted on base 2.54:1; text.secondary on sunken 4.39:1; text.secondary on base 4.83:1; text.strong on sunken 9.37:1; primary.DEFAULT on white 4.10:1; info on info-bg 3.84:1; primary.700 on info-bg 5.57:1; success on white 3.77:1; dark text.secondary on dark raised 5.71:1.

Pantopus post jitter (backend/utils/locationPrivacy.js): ±0.005° lat/lng, keyed and stable, rounded to 0.001°. At 45.6°N that is about ±556 m N–S and ±389 m E–W (a box of about 1.11 × 0.78 km). A 150 m circle covers about 8% of it (computed).
Android location: approximate is about 3 km²; precise is usually within about 50 m, sometimes a few metres (Android developers).
iOS 14 approximate location: a map region 'a few miles in diameter', updated about 4 times per hour in the background (9to5Mac on WWDC20).
Google Business Profile postcard: 'most codes arrive within 14 days'; codes expire after 30 days; requesting a new code invalidates the old one.
USPS First-Class Mail: 1–5 business days, excluding Sundays and holidays, before any print lead time.
Airbnb identity verification: guests have 12 hours to finish (1 hour if check-in is within 12 hours); the reservation stays pending until then.
DSA Art. 16: confirmation of receipt 'without undue delay' (para. 4); decision plus redress info (para. 5); disclosure of automated decisions (para. 6).
Apple Maps reports: past reports reviewable for about 90 days (Apple support via search result; not confirmed on the fetched page).
Dark patterns: 1,818 instances on about 11K shopping sites, including 157 deceptive countdown timers on 140 sites (Mathur et al., CSCW 2019).
Habituation: a large drop in visual processing of a warning after its second exposure (Anderson/Vance/Kirwan, fMRI).
FEMA: no fee to review a LOMA request; LOMA/LOMR-F is the only way to change a flood-zone determination.
EPA radon: fix at 4 pCi/L or higher, consider fixing at 2–4 pCi/L; the zone map is not for deciding whether individual homes should test.

topic: notifications-permissions: push and permission UX on iOS 17-18 and Android 13-15, covering permission priming and denial recovery, provisional authorization, POST_NOTIFICATIONS, notification content and truncation, interruption levels and channels, grouping and summaries, the settings page structure, calm and threshold-based alerts, why people turn notifications off, and in-app equivalents. Research gap: the web-search budget ran out before I could collect real user reviews (Reddit, App Store, Google Play). Everything user-side below comes from peer-reviewed studies and NN/g, not from reviews.

principles.principle: Ask for notification permission only right after a user action that makes the benefit obvious. Never ask at cold launch, at sign-up or at save.
principles.evidence: Apple's developer guide says to make the request "in a context that helps people understand why", for example after the person schedules a first task. It calls this better than "automatically requesting authorization on first launch". The guide also notes that only the first request prompts the person; later requests don't. HIG Privacy says: "Avoid requesting permission at launch unless the data or resource is required for your app to function". Android's guide says to wait until users are familiar with the app, then ask on a user action (tapping an alert bell, following an account, placing an order) or after the 3rd or 4th launch, because "new users are more likely to grant permission when they understand the benefit". NN/g reports that in its studies the immediate response to an early ask is often "Don't Allow". It recommends letting people experience the app first (reciprocity) and saying what kind of notifications they will get. Its examples: a game that asks after a level-up, and Night Sky, which names "stargazing conditions, object rise times".
principles.implication: Only three moments may start the permission flow: (1) tapping Yes on 'The night before pickup?' or 'A morning heads-up?' on the briefing card; (2) the first 'That's my day' on the pickup card, answered inline with 'Remind you the night before?'; (3) switching on household activity. Saving a place, the save confirmation, sign-up and first launch never start it. Draw the save confirmation with no permission ask on it.

principles.principle: If a custom pre-permission screen is shown, its forward button must say it opens the system prompt ('Continue'), not something that means 'Allow'. It must never imitate the system alert. Skip the screen entirely when the tap that led to it was already an explicit opt-in.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Privacy, 'Pre-alert screens': "Include only one button and make it clear that it opens the system alert". It names using a term like "Allow" as manipulation, because a button similar in meaning and weight to the alert's Allow makes people tap Allow without meaning to, and says "Use a term like 'Continue' or 'Next'". It also says: "don't provide a way for people to leave the screen or window without viewing the system alert — like offering an option to close or cancel". Caveat: Apple lists camera, microphone, location, contacts, calendar and tracking, and does not name notifications. The same page opens with: "Ideally, the current context helps people understand why you're requesting their permission. If it's essential to provide additional details, you can display a custom screen". Android points the other way on cancelling: "Always provide the option to cancel an educational UI flow". The widely used 'double permission' pattern keeps a second chance by letting people decline the custom ask without spending the OS prompt (Stephanie Walter, citing Luke Wroblewski).
principles.implication: Label the primer's forward action 'Continue' and add a caption: 'Your phone will ask next.' Don't use 'Yes', 'Allow' or 'Turn on'. 'Not now' may stay: Android explicitly endorses a cancel, and on iOS notifications are not on Apple's list. Record the iOS choice as a deliberate one. When the entry is a Yes tap on the briefing card, go straight to the OS prompt: the card row is already the context. Never draw an arrow, highlight or annotation pointing at the OS dialog's Allow button.

principles.principle: iOS and Android handle a denied permission differently, so design denial recovery separately for each.
principles.evidence: iOS: "Subsequent authorization requests don't prompt the person", so after a denial only Settings can change it. UIApplication.openNotificationSettingsURLString opens the app's notification page in Settings directly. Android 13+: "If a user installs your app on a device that runs Android 13 or higher, your app's notifications are off by default". Swiping the dialog away leaves the state unchanged. "if the user taps Deny for a specific permission more than once during your app's lifetime of installation on a device, the user will no longer see the system permissions dialog". After one denial, shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale() returns true, which tells the app to show explanatory UI and ask again. Deep links exist for app-level settings (ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS) and for one channel (ACTION_CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS).
principles.implication: Split the primer's 'already denied' frame in three. iOS denied: 'Open Settings', which lands on Pantopus's notification page, not the app's root settings. Android denied once: the same primer with 'Continue', which re-fires the system dialog. Android denied twice (blocked): 'Open Settings'. The Android 'Not now' on the primer must not fire the system dialog, because each system 'Don't allow' uses up one of the two chances.

principles.principle: After a denial, keep the app fully working, say exactly what still works, and don't pressure. Show a Settings link only where the person is actively trying to switch something on, or where an in-app switch they turned on cannot deliver.
principles.evidence: Android: "gracefully degrade your app experience"; "Don't display a generic message. Instead, make clear which features are unavailable"; "Don't block the user"; users "should not feel pressured to change their mind"; "Don't link to system settings in an effort to convince the user to change their decision." App Store Review Guideline 4.5.4: "Push Notifications must not be required for the app to function". NN/g lists reversibility (content, timing, decision reversal) as a core requirement.
principles.implication: Denied copy must name the in-app twin, e.g. 'Pickup still shows here on Today'. Use the warning colour only when a Pantopus switch is ON while the OS blocks delivery, i.e. a mismatch the person created. If someone simply declined, show nothing on Today, or one neutral text.secondary line once. Offer the widget as the alternative once, not as a permanent banner. On the Settings page a denied banner with 'Open Settings' is appropriate, because the person came there to manage notifications.

principles.principle: Consider iOS provisional authorization only for low-urgency categories, where a quiet trial in Notification Center is the honest 'show before asking'. Don't use it for the pickup reminder, which has to be seen the evening before.
principles.evidence: Apple: provisional notifications are "delivered quietly — they don't interrupt the person with a sound or banner, or appear on the lock screen". They appear only in Notification Center history, with Keep and Turn Off buttons. Choosing Keep, then 'Deliver Immediately', still delivers quietly, with no alerts, sounds or badges. Provisional can be requested at first launch without a prompt. Not verified in the sources I fetched: whether an app in provisional status can later show the explicit prompt to upgrade to prominent delivery. Confirm this on a device before relying on it.
principles.implication: This is a product call. If adopted (for example for household activity), the settings page needs a 'Delivered quietly — only in Notification Center' state. Funnel metrics must not count provisional as 'briefing on' for activation. The primer is still required for pickup.

principles.principle: Match every notification type's interruption level (iOS) and channel importance (Android) to its real urgency. The night-before pickup is Active / DEFAULT, not Time Sensitive. Air and NOAA threshold crossings may be Time Sensitive / HIGH. Household activity is Passive / LOW. Never use Critical.
principles.evidence: Apple: Passive is information to view "at their leisure"; Active is the default; Time Sensitive is information that "requires their immediate attention, like an account security issue or a package delivery". Use it only when the event is "happening now or will happen within an hour". The system asks people whether to keep Time Sensitive after the first one arrives. Critical needs an entitlement and is "typically" for government or health and safety. "Build trust by accurately representing the urgency of each notification." Only Time Sensitive and Critical override scheduled delivery and break through Focus. Android importance: HIGH for time-critical items; DEFAULT for "traffic alerts, task reminders"; LOW for subscribed content and social invitations; MIN for "weather, promotional content". "When an unimportant notification is disguised as urgent, it can produce unnecessary alarm." Android: "Once you submit the channel to the NotificationManager, you can't change the importance level."
principles.implication: Write this mapping into the settings prompt and the push-tray frames. Briefings: Active / DEFAULT. Dates and bills: Active / DEFAULT. Household activity: Passive / LOW. Air ≥151 and NOAA warnings: Time Sensitive / HIGH. Air 101–150: Active / DEFAULT. Security: Time Sensitive / HIGH. Only the air group's helper text may say it can 'come through Focus'. Tray frames draw household activity without a heads-up banner.

principles.principle: Assume the OS may delay or rewrite a push. Scheduled Summary and Focus hold Active notifications, and Apple Intelligence summaries rewrite the text. The in-app twin is the only guaranteed delivery, and the app should say when the OS is holding its pushes.
principles.evidence: Apple: people can choose to get alerts "in a summary that's delivered at times they choose", and Passive and Active alerts do not override scheduled delivery. UNNotificationSettings exposes scheduledDeliverySetting and timeSensitiveSetting. For alertSetting: "Authorization does not guarantee that alerts always appear on the user's screen." relevanceScore (0–1) decides which notification is featured in the summary. Apple Intelligence summaries: after the BBC complained about a false summary, Apple paused summaries for News & Entertainment apps in the iOS 18.3 betas, set all summaries in italics, and added a per-app switch on the Lock Screen (TechCrunch, 16 Jan 2025). A machine summary can therefore drop or change a caveat.
principles.implication: Add a Settings caption state: 'Your iPhone holds Pantopus notifications for your Scheduled Summary, so pickup reminders may arrive late.' with a link to the app's notification settings. Give the pickup push the highest relevanceScore. The pickup card on Today is the product's guarantee, so it always renders, push or no push. Never rely on a summary, or on the iOS subtitle, to carry the 'not yet confirmed' caveat.

principles.principle: Keep push titles to 30 characters or fewer, on one line, and put the honesty caveat at the start of the title (or in the first ~40 characters of the body), never at the end of a long title.
principles.evidence: Android design guidance: "Android truncates content titles to a single line (even when expanded)", titles should "not exceed 30 characters", and collapsed content text should stay under a 40-character limit and not repeat the title. Android's build guide: "By default, the notification's text content is truncated to fit one line." Apple HIG: "Prefer brief titles that people can read at a glance", "don't truncate your message — the system does this automatically", and use title-style capitalization with no ending punctuation. The iOS subtitle "isn't displayed in all cases". Vendor figures for iOS disagree (CleverTap: title 25–50 characters, body about 150; developer-forum reports of about 255-character body truncation on iOS 14–16). Treat iOS numbers as approximate.
principles.implication: Use one canonical string on every surface. Unconfirmed: title 'Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow' (28 characters), body 'Recycling + garbage · City of Camas schedule. Bins out tonight.' Confirmed: title 'Recycling + garbage tomorrow' (28), body 'Bins out tonight · Lacamas Dr'. Air: title 'Unhealthy air: AQI 176' (22), body 'AirNow, 4:00 PM · Lacamas Dr'. Draw the tray frames at true truncation so the caveat visibly survives.

principles.principle: Keep the full street address off the lock screen. Use the place's short label, and set a generic placeholder for when previews are hidden.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG: "Avoid including sensitive, personal, or confidential information in a notification. You can't predict what people will be doing when they receive a notification". It also says to provide generic text for when previews are hidden, such as "Reminder" or "Shipment"; the API for this is hiddenPreviewsBodyPlaceholder. App Store Review Guideline 4.5.4: push "should not be used to send sensitive personal or confidential information". Android: VISIBILITY_PRIVATE plus setPublicVersion() hides sensitive details on the lock screen.
principles.implication: The push body carries a street-name label ('Lacamas Dr') or the user's nickname, with no house number, and only when the person has more than one place. Hidden-preview placeholders: 'Pickup reminder', 'Air quality alert', 'Household update'. The Android public version reads 'Pantopus · Pickup reminder'. The full address and the 'Saved place · Only you' chip appear on the landing screen, not in the tray.

principles.principle: Send one notification per real-world thing. Stop reminders once they are acknowledged, update a notification instead of stacking a new one, and batch low-urgency items into predictable delivery times.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG: "Avoid sending multiple notifications for the same thing, even if someone hasn't responded... people may turn off all notifications from your app." NN/g lists bursts as a mistake (users averaged 56 notifications a day in 2016). It advises combining more than five simultaneous notifications into one, as Instagram does with likes, and sending only relevant items, as Reddit does with followed subreddits. Android auto-groups four or more ungrouped notifications (API 24+). It says to group only when each child notification is complete on its own, and otherwise to update the existing notification. Android shows users how many notifications per day an app sends. Fitz et al. 2019 (randomized field experiment, n=237, 2 weeks): people whose notifications were batched three times a day felt more attentive, productive, in a better mood and more in control, and reported lower stress. Hourly batching did not differ from the control group. People who got no notifications at all saw few of those benefits and reported higher anxiety and fear of missing out (FoMO). Press reports describe an Android 15 'notification cooldown' that lowers the volume of successive alerts from the same app. Other reports say it was pulled from the betas, so don't design around it.
principles.implication: Household activity pushes carry one thread per home and collapse same-day events into one push, e.g. 'Sam paid 3 bills'. Anything non-urgent can ride the evening briefing instead of pushing on its own. The date sheet's lead / day-before / day-of reminders stop as soon as the row is marked done or paid. A worsening AQI replaces the earlier air notification rather than adding a second one. Keep the design doc's cap of one push per trigger per day, and consider a cross-trigger rule that merges items due within the same hour.

principles.principle: Make silence readable. Wherever pushes are withheld on purpose, show the product's last successful check so 'nothing sent' doesn't look like 'broken'.
principles.evidence: Fitz et al. 2019: getting no notifications at all brought higher anxiety and FoMO. Pielot & Rello, MobileHCI 2017 (N=30, 24 hours with notifications off): people felt less distracted and more productive, but some became anxious about not being responsive and felt less connected. About two-thirds intended to change how they manage notifications. The principles of calm technology include "inform and create calm", "make use of the periphery" and "work even when it fails".
principles.implication: Pair the silence contract ('Only when something needs you. No news means nothing's up.') with a receipt: 'Checked 6:00 PM · nothing needs you tonight'. Show it only when every check succeeded (honesty rule 4); a failed check reads as a failure. On Settings, the evening briefing row can show 'Last sent Mon 6:00 PM (pickup)' or 'Skipped tonight — nothing needed you'. That answers the person who opened the page because pushes stopped.

principles.principle: The in-app settings page must mirror the OS per category, not just as one global on/off. Each group maps 1:1 to an Android channel and an iOS category/thread, using one fixed list of categories (taxonomy) that does not change after launch.
principles.evidence: Android: "Create a channel for each type of notification". After creation, "The user has complete control" and importance cannot change. "The notification settings screen displays the number of deleted channels, as a spam prevention mechanism." Channel groups organise same-named channels per account, and apps can read each channel's importance and deep-link to it. Apple: "you must also provide an in-app settings screen". The providesAppNotificationSettings option makes iOS Settings show a button that opens the app's own notification page. NN/g's 'hidden controls' mistake: forcing people into phone settings "decreases trust"; its example is Elevate's in-app per-type toggles. WCAG 2.2 SC 2.2.4 Interruptions (AAA): "Interruptions can be postponed or suppressed by the user, except interruptions involving an emergency."
principles.implication: Each group's master row reads the OS state. If a channel is blocked, the row shows 'Off in Android settings · Open', and the in-app switch never shows ON. Settle the group names before the first Android build ships. The 'Pantopus Notification Settings' link in iOS Settings lands on this page. Keep a switch for air alerts too: they are important but not a civil emergency, since Pantopus is not the issuing authority.

principles.principle: Give a notification at most one or two actions, each a non-destructive, time-saving task that completes without opening the app. Never add an action that just opens the app, and never tell people to go do something inside the app.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG: up to four buttons. "Prefer actions that let people perform common, time-saving tasks that eliminate the need to open your app"; "Avoid providing an action that merely opens your app"; "Prefer nondestructive actions"; short title-case labels. It also says to avoid notifications that tell people to perform tasks in the app. Its example is Calendar's Snooze. Android allows up to three actions, which "must not duplicate the tap action".
principles.implication: Unconfirmed pickup push: one action, 'That's My Day', which confirms in the background; tapping the body opens the pickup card, where 'Not my schedule' lives. Bill reminder: 'Mark Paid'. Date reminder: 'Done'. Air alerts and household activity get no actions. Draw the long-press/expanded tray state for the pickup push. Never write body copy like 'Open Pantopus to confirm'.

principles.principle: Every push needs an in-app twin with the same content, landing on the exact object. A push that arrives while the app is open is slipped quietly into the current view, and the badge means unread notifications only.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG, on handling notifications in the foreground: "present the information in a way that's discoverable but not distracting or invasive, such as incrementing a badge or subtly inserting new data into the current view" (Mail simply adds the new message to the list). "Use a badge only to show people how many unread notifications they have", and never for weather-type numbers. "Make sure badging isn't the only method". Android says not to use notifications "as the primary method of communication" or "to encourage the user to return to an app, but provide no direct value".
principles.implication: If Today is open at 6:00 PM, don't show a banner; highlight the pickup card instead. The header bell shows only the unread count and never an AQI number. Each tray frame is paired with its landing frame (pickup card, air band scrolled into view with the crossing marked, bill detail). A deleted target falls back to the list with 'That bill was removed.'

principles.principle: Never use these channels for marketing, re-engagement, referral, streak or mood pushes. Any promotional push needs its own explicit, separately worded opt-in.
principles.evidence: Apple: "Don't use notifications to send marketing or promotional content unless people explicitly agree" and "Never use the Time Sensitive interruption level to send a marketing notification." App Store Review Guideline 4.5.4 requires explicit opt-in through consent language in the app's UI, plus an in-app opt-out. Android's 'don't' list: "To encourage the user to return to an app, but provide no direct value", "For requests to rate your app", "For holiday or birthday messages", cross-promotion ("strictly prohibited by the Play Store"), and not "If the user has never opened your app". NN/g lists irrelevant content as a top mistake.
principles.implication: The primer's promise ('nothing else unless something needs you') is only true if no Founding-slot, referral, keeper-mood or 'you haven't checked in' push ever exists. The settings page has no 'Tips and news' switch unless a separately worded marketing opt-in is built. The phase-2 keeper's mood lives on Today and the widget, never in a push.

principles.principle: A threshold alert must land on a screen showing the threshold the person actually chose, and should fire once per crossing episode, not on every wobble around the line.
principles.evidence: Apple: represent urgency accurately, and avoid multiple notifications for the same thing. Calm technology: use the smallest possible amount of attention. I found no authoritative source for a specific re-alert or hysteresis margin; any number is a product decision, not evidence.
principles.implication: The air band marks the person's chosen threshold (101, 151 or 201) with the crossing time ('Crossed 151 at 4:00 PM'), not a hard-coded 101. The Settings segmented control and the backend default must agree. Draw one 'still unhealthy, no new push' frame so the designer shows that repeated readings above the threshold stay quiet.

principles.principle: Settings controls follow platform rules: switches only in list rows, touch targets at least 44 pt on iOS and 24 CSS px on web, never colour alone for state, and save results announced to screen readers without moving focus.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG: "Use the switch toggle style only in a list row"; "Avoid relying solely on different colors to communicate state"; minimum control size 44x44 pt.
