WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (AA): targets at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, unless spaced out enough. SC 4.1.3 Status Messages (AA): status messages must be programmatically determinable "without receiving focus"; examples include save confirmations and error counts.
principles.implication: The briefing card's two asks are list rows. Its time chips are at least 44 pt tall on iOS and at least 24 px on web, with a selected state shown by more than colour (a check or fill change). 'Saved', 'Couldn't save — Retry' and the 'saving' states on the settings page and the card are live-region status messages.

patterns.name: In-context soft ask (double permission)
patterns.exemplars: Apple's own guidance: a task app asks after the person schedules a first task. Android's guidance: ask on an alert-bell tap, a follow, or a food order. NN/g: the Conquest game waits until a level-up; Night Sky names the exact content ('stargazing conditions, object rise times').
patterns.howToApply: The first 'That's my day' on the pickup card expands inline into 'Remind you the night before? 6:00 PM', with a forward action that fires the OS prompt. A Yes on the briefing card fires the OS prompt directly. The custom sheet is only for entries where the context is weaker (household activity from Mail).
patterns.pitfalls: Asking three times in a row (card, primer, OS). Labelling the custom button 'Yes' or 'Allow'. Firing the system dialog from Android 'Not now', which spends one of the two denials.

patterns.name: Show the real notification before asking
patterns.exemplars: Apple's provisional authorization exists so people can "evaluate the notifications and decide" from a real delivered notification. NN/g's Night Sky example describes the content concretely. I found no verified third-party app that renders a tray preview inside its primer, so this part is Pantopus's own extension.
patterns.howToApply: The primer's hero is a true-proportion tray card carrying the canonical 30-character pickup title with the caveat first, captioned 'This is the whole thing.'
patterns.pitfalls: Drawing the OS permission alert itself, which Apple prohibits for tracking primers and which is misleading anywhere. A preview that does not match what actually ships. A preview that shows the full street address.

patterns.name: Per-platform denial recovery
patterns.exemplars: iOS: openNotificationSettingsURLString opens the app's notification page in Settings. Android: shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale(), then a second system dialog; after two denials, ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS or ACTION_CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS.
patterns.howToApply: The primer, briefing card and settings page each carry three OS states: not asked, denied but re-askable (Android only), and blocked (open Settings). Copy names what still works in-app.
patterns.pitfalls: Persistent amber nags on Today for people who chose to decline. Linking to Settings 'to convince' (Android advises against it). Deep-linking to the app's root settings instead of its notification page.

patterns.name: Settings groups that mirror OS channels
patterns.exemplars: NN/g cites Elevate's in-app per-type toggles. Android notification channels, and channel groups per account. iOS providesAppNotificationSettings adds a button in iOS Settings that opens the app's page.
patterns.howToApply: Settle on five groups: Briefings, Air & weather alerts, Dates & bills, Household activity, Account & security. Each has one master row with helper text directly under it, and each row reads its own OS channel or attribute state.
patterns.pitfalls: Renaming or deleting channels after launch: Android shows users the count of deleted channels, and importance is frozen. Two prompts defining different taxonomies. A row that reads ON while its channel is blocked.

patterns.name: Urgency ladder (interruption levels and importance)
patterns.exemplars: Apple's examples: a restaurant recommendation is Passive; a sports score is Active; account security or a package delivery is Time Sensitive; severe-weather and safety alerts from agencies are Critical. Android's examples: traffic alerts and task reminders are DEFAULT; subscribed content and social invitations are LOW; weather and promotions are MIN.
patterns.howToApply: Pickup and briefings: Active / DEFAULT. Air ≥151 and NOAA warnings: Time Sensitive / HIGH. Household activity: Passive / LOW. Bills and dates: Active / DEFAULT. Only the air group's settings row mentions breaking through Focus.
patterns.pitfalls: Marking pickup Time Sensitive to get around Scheduled Summary. Apple limits Time Sensitive to events happening now or within an hour, and asks users whether to keep it.

patterns.name: Bundle and batch
patterns.exemplars: NN/g: Instagram bundles likes into one notification. Android auto-groups at 4+ notifications and recommends updating an existing notification instead. Fitz et al.: batching three times a day improved attention, mood and control.
patterns.howToApply: One iOS thread and one Android group per place. A same-day household roll-up ('Sam paid 3 bills'). Non-urgent items ride the evening briefing. A worsening AQI updates the existing alert.
patterns.pitfalls: Hourly batching showed no benefit over the control group in Fitz et al. Grouping children that are not complete on their own.

patterns.name: Actionable notification that finishes the job
patterns.exemplars: Apple Calendar's Snooze action (HIG): a time-saving task completed without opening the app.
patterns.howToApply: 'That's My Day' on the unconfirmed pickup push, 'Mark Paid' on bill reminders, 'Done' on date reminders. The same actions appear on the in-app row.
patterns.pitfalls: An 'Open' action that duplicates the tap. Destructive actions without context. More than 3 actions (Android maximum).

patterns.name: Quiet insert when the app is already open
patterns.exemplars: Apple Mail adds a new message to the visible unread list instead of alerting (HIG).
patterns.howToApply: When the evening briefing fires while Today is open, highlight the pickup card and don't show a banner. The bell badge increments only.
patterns.pitfalls: Custom in-app banners that duplicate the OS banner. Badge numbers carrying non-notification data such as AQI.

patterns.name: Private lock-screen rendering
patterns.exemplars: Apple's hidden-preview placeholders ('Friend request', 'Reminder', 'Shipment'). Android VISIBILITY_PRIVATE with setPublicVersion().
patterns.howToApply: Placeholders 'Pickup reminder', 'Air quality alert' and 'Household update'. The body uses a street-name label with no house number. The full address and privacy chip live on the landing screen.
patterns.pitfalls: Dropping the place label entirely when the person has two places, which makes the push ambiguous.

patterns.name: Readable silence (heartbeat receipt)
patterns.exemplars: No verified product example was gathered. Basis: Fitz et al. (no notifications raised anxiety and FoMO), Pielot & Rello (anxiety about missing things), and the calm-technology principle 'inform and create calm'.
patterns.howToApply: 'Checked 6:00 PM · nothing needs you tonight' on Today, the widget and the evening-briefing settings row. Shown only when every check succeeded.
patterns.pitfalls: Showing the all-clear when a provider failed, which turns silence into a false claim.

antipatterns: Firing the OS notification prompt at cold launch, sign-up, or on saving a place. Apple and Android both say to ask in context, and on iOS the prompt can be shown only once.
A primer button labelled 'Yes', 'Allow' or 'Turn on'. Apple HIG calls Allow-like labels on pre-alert screens manipulative; use 'Continue'.

Drawing or imitating the system permission alert, or adding arrows or highlights toward its Allow button. HIG Privacy lists these as prohibited designs for tracking primers, and they mislead in any primer.
Asking three times in a row (card Yes, then primer Yes, then OS Allow). The card is already the context Apple says should make a custom screen unnecessary.
Benefit bullet lists, incentives or rewards for granting permission. Apple prohibits incentives for tracking permission, and NN/g says to state concretely what will be sent.
Putting 'not yet confirmed' at the end of a long title. Android truncates titles to one line even when expanded (keep them to 30 characters or fewer), so the caveat is the first thing lost.
Relying on the iOS subtitle or an Apple Intelligence summary to carry a caveat. Subtitles aren't always shown, and AI summaries have rewritten notifications inaccurately.
A full street address with house number in the push title or body. Apple HIG and App Review 4.5.4 say not to put personal information in notifications.

Time Sensitive for the night-before pickup, bill or date reminders, or any marketing. Apple limits it to events happening now or within an hour. Critical requires an entitlement and is not Pantopus's role.
Re-sending the same reminder because the person hasn't responded. Apple warns that people may turn off all of an app's notifications.

Re-engagement, streak, referral, Founding-slot or keeper-mood pushes. Android's guidance lists 'encourage the user to return... no direct value' as a don't, and Apple and App Review require an explicit opt-in for promotions.
An in-app switch that reads ON while the OS blocks that category or the whole app. Android channels and iOS alert settings can each be off independently.
Renaming, deleting or re-creating Android channels after launch to reset user choices. Importance is frozen, and Settings shows users the count of deleted channels.
A permanent amber 'Turn on notifications' banner on Today for someone who declined. Android says not to pressure users or link to Settings to change their mind.
Badge counts carrying anything but unread notifications (for example AQI), or a custom badge look-alike on the app icon (Apple HIG).
Push copy that tells people to do something inside the app ('Open Pantopus to confirm'), or an action button that only opens the app (Apple HIG).
A push with no in-app twin, or one that lands on a generic list when the object exists. App Review 4.5.4 says push must not be required for the app to function.
A 'No news' all-clear shown when a data check failed. Silence is only honest when every check succeeded.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Actions 'Yes' / 'Not now' at equal weight, under the title 'Can we tell you about pickup night?'. 'Yes' leads to the OS prompt.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG Privacy, 'Pre-alert screens': the one forward button should make clear that it opens the system alert and use a term like 'Continue' or 'Next'. Allow-like wording that resembles the alert's Allow button in meaning and weight counts as manipulation. The page names camera, microphone, location, contacts, calendar and tracking, not notifications, so 'Not now' is defensible, and Android explicitly wants a cancel option.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Rename 'Yes' to 'Continue', with the caption 'Your phone will ask next.' Keep 'Not now' visible, and record it as a deliberate iOS choice. On Android it must not fire the system dialog.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The primer opens after the person taps Yes on the briefing opt-in card, so the flow is card Yes, then primer Yes, then OS Allow.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple: "Ideally, the current context helps people understand why you're requesting their permission. If it's essential to provide additional details, you can display a custom screen". Android's recommended flow is: the user interacts with the feature, the app explains, the user confirms, then the system dialog appears. The card row is already that explanation and confirmation.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: A Yes on the card fires the OS prompt directly. Keep the primer for indirect entries (the first 'That's my day', household activity from Mail), and redraw state 2 accordingly.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Example tray title: 'Recycling and garbage tomorrow - City of Camas schedule, not yet confirmed' (about 73 characters), with the caveat at the end of the title 'because a truncated tray line must not eat the honesty'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android truncates content titles to a single line even when expanded, and advises 30 characters or fewer. Apple asks for brief titles readable at a glance. The caveat at the end of a 73-character title is exactly what gets cut.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Put the caveat first in a title of 30 characters or fewer: 'Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow'. Body: 'Recycling + garbage · City of Camas schedule. Bins out tonight.' Draw it at true truncation, and use this same string in the pickup-card and household prompts.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Body copy: "We'll tell you the night before pickup, and nothing else unless something needs you tonight." Meanwhile the settings page shows Household activity, Date reminders, Bill reminders and Air alerts all ON by default.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g: vague or inaccurate descriptions of what will be sent undermine the decision and the app's credibility. Apple: describe the types of notification you will send, and represent urgency accurately. Once granted, OS permission covers every category the app then sends.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Either grant only pickup plus air alerts by default and leave the other groups OFF until switched on in context, or change the primer copy to list the real defaults ('Pickup the night before. Air alerts when it's unhealthy. Nothing else unless you turn it on.').

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: State 4, 'already denied at OS level': the same sheet with 'Open Settings' and no Yes, drawn identically on iOS and Android.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android can ask again after one denial: shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale() returns true and the app should explain and re-request. The dialog is suppressed only after the person denies more than once, and Android advises against linking to Settings to change someone's mind. iOS never prompts twice, and openNotificationSettingsURLString goes straight to the app's notification page.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw three frames. iOS denied: 'Open Settings' to the notification page. Android denied once: 'Continue', which re-fires the system dialog. Android blocked: 'Open Settings'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Push title 'Recycling and garbage tomorrow — not yet confirmed' (about 50 characters); body 'Bins out tonight. 2418 NW Lacamas Dr.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android: titles are one line and 30 characters or fewer, so the ending '— not yet confirmed' gets cut. Apple HIG and App Store Review 4.5.4: keep personal information such as a home address out of notifications, and provide a hidden-preview placeholder.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Title 'Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow' (confirmed: 'Recycling + garbage tomorrow'). Body 'Bins out tonight · Lacamas Dr' (street name only, and only when the person has more than one place). Placeholder 'Pickup reminder'. Add a 'That's My Day' notification action for the unconfirmed case.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Push tray card: 'Air is unhealthy for sensitive groups at 2418 NW Lacamas Dr'. The alert landing marks 'the 101 threshold' on the bar.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The title is about 59 characters, past Android's 30-character single-line limit, so the address or category is cut. Apple and App Review 4.5.4 say to keep home addresses off the lock screen. Separately, f4-notification-settings gives the person a threshold choice (101/151/201, with 151 selected), so a hard-coded 101 mark can contradict the rule that actually fired. Apple says urgency must be represented accurately.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Title 'Unhealthy air: AQI 118' (or the band name). Body 'AirNow, 4:00 PM · Lacamas Dr'. Placeholder 'Air quality alert'. The bar marks the person's selected threshold and its crossing time. Set the iOS level by severity (Time Sensitive only at 151 or above).

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: OS tray reminder title: 'Garbage + recycling is tomorrow (not yet confirmed)'. Same-day grouping is drawn only for the in-app list, and each activity event pushes as it happens.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android cuts titles past about 30 characters on one line, so the bracketed caveat is lost. Apple: Passive is for information to view at leisure. NN/g and Android say to bundle bursts, and to group only complete children or update in place. Fitz et al.: predictable batching improves attention and control.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use the canonical 'Unconfirmed: pickup tomorrow' title. Household activity is Passive / LOW, with one thread or group per home, and a same-day roll-up in the tray too ('Sam paid 3 bills'). Consider delivering activity inside the evening briefing instead of immediately.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The settings list shows the channels 'Household activity', 'Security', 'Reminders' and 'Briefing'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android channels are permanent once shipped: importance cannot change, and Settings shows users a count of deleted channels. The in-app page and the channels must therefore share one stable set of categories. f4-notification-settings defines a different set of four (Briefings, Household activity, Dates and bills, Air and weather alerts) and has no Security group.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Settle on one five-group set in both prompts before the Android build ships: Briefings; Air & weather alerts; Dates & bills; Household activity; Account & security.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The OS permission state appears only as one global 'Notifications are off for Pantopus' banner; the group switches otherwise read their saved in-app value.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: On Android a user can block a single channel while the app keeps permission ("The user has complete control"). On iOS, alerts can be off while the app is still authorized ("Authorization does not guarantee that alerts always appear"), notifications can be held for Scheduled Summary, and Time Sensitive can be switched off. v1's own rule is that a switch must never read ON when nothing will be delivered.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add frames for: an Android group blocked ('Off in Android settings · Open', using ACTION_CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS); iOS Scheduled Summary ('Pickup reminders may arrive with your summary'); and air alerts with Time Sensitive off. The 'Pantopus Notification Settings' link in iOS Settings (providesAppNotificationSettings) should land on this page.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The 'OS notifications denied' state shows an amber permission line with 'Open settings' inside the card on Today, with the widget row promoted above it.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android: respect a denial, don't make people "feel pressured to change their mind", and "Don't link to system settings in an effort to convince the user to change their decision". Stating that something the person switched on cannot be delivered is honest; repeating an amber call to action at someone who declined is pressure.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use amber plus 'Open settings' only when a briefing row is ON in-app and the OS blocks delivery. If the person declined at the OS prompt, collapse the card (as the 'asked and declined' state already does), or show one neutral text.secondary line once, and offer the widget once.

numbers: Android notification title: one line even when expanded, 30 characters or fewer; collapsed content text 40 characters or fewer, not repeating the title (developer.android.com/design/ui/mobile/guides/home-screen/notifications).
Android content text is cut to one line by default; BigTextStyle expands it (developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/notifications/build-notification).

iOS character limits are not published by Apple. CleverTap recommends a 25–50 character title and about 150 characters of body. A developer-forum report says bodies were cut at about 255 characters on iOS 14–16. Treat iOS figures as approximate and design to Android's 30-character title.
iOS notification detail view: up to 4 action buttons (Apple HIG). Android: up to 3 actions, which must not duplicate the tap action.
Android auto-groups 4 or more ungrouped notifications from one app (API 24+).
NN/g: combine more than 5 simultaneous notifications into one; users averaged 56 notifications a day (2016 figure cited by NN/g).
Apple Time Sensitive: only for an event happening now or within 1 hour. The system asks the user whether to keep Time Sensitive after the app's first one. Critical requires an Apple entitlement.
iOS relevanceScore ranges from 0 to 1; the highest-scoring notification is featured in the Scheduled Summary.

iOS shows the permission prompt only once per install. Android 11+: denying a permission more than once stops the system dialog for that install. Android 13+: notifications are OFF by default for new installs.
Android channel importance cannot change after creation, and Settings shows users the count of deleted channels.

Fitz et al. 2019: randomized field experiment, n=237, 2 weeks. Batching 3 times a day improved attention, productivity, mood, control and stress. Hourly batching did not differ from control. No notifications at all brought higher anxiety and FoMO.
Pielot & Rello 2017: N=30, 24 hours with notifications off; about 2/3 intended to change how they manage notifications.

Opt-in benchmarks, seen only in a secondary search summary and not verified against Airship's gated report: Airship 2025 median opt-in of 44.5% on iOS and 71.3% on Android; Batch (Jul 2024–Jul 2025) Android 85%→67% and iOS 58%→56%. Do not quote these as fact.
A '90% of permission prompts are dismissed or ignored' figure, attributed to Chrome Dev Summit 2018 via Stephanie Walter's guide, was not verified in the primary source.
Minimum touch target: 44x44 pt on iOS (Apple HIG Accessibility); 24x24 CSS px on web (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, AA).
WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 (AA): 'Saved' and 'Couldn't save' messages must reach assistive technology without moving focus. SC 2.2.4 (AAA): interruptions can be postponed or suppressed, except emergencies.
APNs payload limit: 4096 bytes.
Apple Intelligence summaries: the iOS 18.3 betas paused News & Entertainment summaries, set summaries in italics, and added a per-app switch on the Lock Screen (Jan 2025).
Android 15 'notification cooldown' (press reports): successive alerts from one app get quieter and reset after about 1 minute of quiet. Reports conflict on whether it shipped, so don't rely on it.

topic: risk-and-place-dataviz: showing environmental risk and place data (flood, wildfire, air, radon) to non-experts, comparing two places, and showing provenance

principles.principle: Show each hazard on its own authority's scale, in that authority's category words. Never combine layers into one grade, score or rank.
principles.evidence: Zillow added First Street climate risk scores in Sep 2024 and removed them sitewide on Nov 14 2025, after the California Regional MLS (CRMLS) questioned their accuracy. Zillow now only links to First Street. Insurance Journal reports two findings: a UK Climate Financial Risk Forum comparison of 13 providers found ratings 'all over the place', and Bloomberg Green found First Street's flood model matched a UC Irvine model only 21% of the time. Zillow's own analysis found that of homes listed in June 2024, 52% of high-flood-risk homes had sold by March 2025, against 71% of low-risk homes. Each official authority defines its own classes: FEMA zones, USFS Wildfire Hazard Potential (5 classes), EPA radon zones 1-3, and the EPA AQI (6 categories).
principles.implication: Each layer is its own scale strip, with the authority's own bands and words. No surface draws a letter grade, score, star rating, radar chart or overall verdict. That includes the share card, the compare reveal and the aha card's grade chip when it summarises more than one layer. The compare token should carry band IDs (e.g. flood:'X', wildfire:3, aqi:42, radon:1), not the A-D grades the design doc still specifies.

principles.principle: Use each authority's exact term, including its word for what is measured: 'hazard' or 'potential', not 'risk', unless the source itself says risk.
principles.evidence: FEMA calls unshaded Zone X 'minimal flood hazard' and shaded Zone X 'moderate flood hazard', both describing areas. USFS says 'On its own, WHP is not an explicit map of wildfire threat or risk' and that it 'is not a forecast or wildfire outlook for any particular season'. The WRC service describes WHP as an index of 'relative potential for wildfire that may be difficult to manage'. EPA radon zones describe predicted county average indoor levels ('highest potential' for Zone 1).
principles.implication: Use one approved string per band, the same on every surface. Examples: 'Zone X — minimal flood hazard' (not 'minimal risk'), 'Wildfire hazard potential: Moderate (3 of 5)', 'Radon Zone 1 — highest potential (county)'. Name the layer rows 'Flood zone', 'Wildfire hazard', 'Air today' and 'Radon zone', not the bare hazard name. Keep the list of approved strings in the design system so the OG card, compare views and the in-app page cannot drift apart.

principles.principle: Give flood probability per year and over a planning horizon. Never write '100-year flood' or '100-year floodplain'.
principles.evidence: USGS says '100-year flood' is 'a misinterpretation of terminology that leads to a misconception' and prefers the 1-percent annual chance / annual exceedance probability. Lee, Torell and Newman (2021, J. Environ. Manage.) surveyed people on FEMA flood terms. Whether people read them correctly depended on understanding independent probabilities, not on education or having been near a flood. First Street defines Flood Factor over the life of a 30-year mortgage, and Realtor.com shows how each risk changes over 15 and 30 years. The arithmetic: 1 − 0.99^30 = 26% for a 1% zone, and 1 − 0.998^30 = 5.8% for a 0.2% zone.
principles.implication: SFHA rows and aha lines read 'Zone AE — 1% chance of flooding each year (about 1 in 4 over 30 years) · FEMA'. Shaded X reads '0.2% each year (about 1 in 17 over 30 years)'. Put the 30-year phrase in the provenance sheet and the risk detail. The compact OG row can stop at the annual phrase.

principles.principle: Put the verbal category and the number side by side, inline. Do not hide the number behind a tap or tooltip.
principles.evidence: Wintle et al. (2019, PLOS One, n=924) showed people verbal probability terms in four formats. Readers matched the intended meaning only when the numeric range sat in brackets in the text: 66% correspondence, against 32% with no numbers. Tooltips and click-to-see tables did not help much. Budescu, Broomell and Por (2009, Psych Sci) found people's readings of IPCC verbal terms deviated from the guidelines even when the guidelines were available, and proposed a combined verbal-numeric format.
principles.implication: Every strip value pairs a word and a number: 'Moderate · 3 of 5', 'AQI 42 · Good', '1% each year'. The number is never available only in the provenance sheet. The '3 of 5' form only works when a higher number means more hazard, so radon must not use 'N of M' (see contradictions).

principles.principle: The AQI is the one scale in the product with official colours. Use EPA's colours (standard or EPA's ColorVision Assist set), EPA's exact category names and EPA's health statements, the same way on every surface.
principles.evidence: From EPA's Technical Assistance Document (May 2026). The standard colours in RGB are Green 0,228,0; Yellow 255,255,0; Orange 255,126,0; Red 255,0,0; Purple 143,63,151; Maroon 126,0,35. The document says 'While the standard AQI colors listed in Table 2 are required, reporting entities may also use ColorVision Assist colors', and gives a separate RGB table for that set. Reports must include the category descriptor and colour 'if your report uses color'. Reports must also list sensitive groups whenever the AQI is over 100. The legal duty falls on MSAs over 350,000 people; the document notes the US AQI also appears 'in many private applications'. It lists 'inconsistent AQI colors or terminology' and 'inaccurate cautionary statements' as common reporting errors. Apple HIG says to keep colours and marks consistent across charts of the same data.
principles.implication: Draw one air track and use it on Today, in the scale strip, on the OG card, in the widget micro-band and in the provenance sheet. It uses the same six EPA hues (pick standard or ColorVision Assist once, product-wide), EPA's names (Good, Moderate, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, Unhealthy, Very Unhealthy, Hazardous) and EPA's verbatim descriptions. Pantopus-written context such as 'Smoke from the Gorge' is visibly separate from the EPA health statement.

principles.principle: Colour is never the only carrier of meaning. Where colour areas touch, separate them, and give the marker 3:1 contrast against everything around it.
principles.evidence: WCAG 1.4.1: colour must not be 'the only visual means of conveying information'. WCAG 1.4.11: graphics needed for understanding need 3:1 contrast against adjacent colours, unless a text label conveys the same information. Apple HIG says 'Aid comprehension by adding visual separation between contiguous areas of color' and 'Avoid relying solely on color'. My calculation from EPA's RGB values: adjacent standard AQI hues contrast only 1.57-2.37:1 with each other. Yellow is 1.07:1 and green 1.74:1 against white. Maroon is 1.62:1 and purple 2.83:1 against the dark base #0F172A. About 8% of men and 0.5% of women have a colour vision deficiency (Crameri 2020).
principles.implication: On the AQI track: leave a 2px surface-colour gap between segments, draw a 1px border.strong keyline round the whole track in light and dark, and give the marker a two-tone ring (surface plus text.primary) so it reaches 3:1 on any segment. Always print the band name beside the marker. The widget's tinted/accented mode drops the colour, so there the name and marker position must carry the reading alone. On neutral strips, the occupied band's name label is the accessible cue; its fill difference is decoration.

principles.principle: Draw hazard scales as a few ordered, discrete classes running low to high, left to right. No rainbow or continuous gradients.
principles.evidence: Schneider et al. (2023, NHESS) set out five colour criteria for public hazard maps: perceptual order, perceptual uniformity, discriminability, fitting associations and accessibility for colour-blind users. They cite evidence that discrete classes produce fewer errors than continuous ones (Padilla 2016), that 5-7 classes can be told apart, and that rainbow palettes fail. Their redesigned seismic map raised correct understanding from 36.8% to 81.6% on one item. Crameri et al. (2020) say rainbow-like maps distort data and fail colour-blind readers. NN/g says colour should not encode quantity; position and length are read most accurately.
principles.implication: Every track runs from least to most hazard, left to right. The marker's position carries the reading. Radon runs Zone 3 → 2 → 1 because EPA numbers its zones backwards, so the label must say 'highest potential' in words. Keep neutral tracks for flood, wildfire and radon. The only coloured track is the official AQI one.

principles.principle: To compare two places, put both marks on one shared track per layer. Keep the rows in a fixed order and name differences in neutral words; don't re-sort the rows.
principles.evidence: Ondov et al. (IEEE InfoVis 2018) found overlaid (superposed) charts beat side-by-side or stacked small multiples for spotting differences. Mirrored side-by-side charts beat unmirrored ones. Gleicher et al. (2011) group comparison designs into three kinds. Side-by-side costs the most memory. Overlaying both marks costs less but needs a shared axis. Encoding the difference directly costs least. Kelley et al.'s standardized privacy label, per the CHI 2010 talk, works partly because information is 'found in the same place every time'.
principles.implication: The compare reveal keeps v1's single track with a filled sender mark and a ringed 'You' mark. Rows stay in the fixed order used by the card and the arrival header. Where the two marks fall in different bands, add a neutral text tag ('Different band') rather than an arrow, a colour or a re-sort. On desktop, the two-column view should be a wider version of the same overlaid tracks, not two facing cards.

principles.principle: Treat the instrument as a standardized disclosure label: same rows, same order, same terms, and an explicit row for missing data.
principles.evidence: Kelley, Cesca, Bresee and Cranor (CHI 2010) tested five formats with 764 participants. Standardized formats beat full-text and layered policies. The benefits they cite: structured layout, 'clear labeling of information that is not used or collected', standard terms with definitions, and information in the same place every time. A shorter table saved space but made comparisons, and questions about data not collected, harder. The CUPS project page says the FTC endorsed the approach in 2010.
principles.implication: Keep v1's rule that a missing layer is a greyed track reading 'Not on record', never a dropped row. Add distinct states for 'FEMA has not studied flood hazard here' and 'Non-burnable land cover' (developed land that WRC treats as non-burnable) so they are not mistaken for missing data or 'very low'. The OG and compare versions may shrink the captions but must keep all four rows and the order.

principles.principle: Show the minimum provenance on the value itself: who says it, how local it is, and as of when. The sheet is for method and corrections, because few people open it.
principles.evidence: In Kelley's study, 'few people clicked through' from layered notices to the full policy, and layered notices performed about as well as the full text. NN/g lists 'comprehensive, correct, and current' content and being connected to outside sources among its credibility factors. Redfin credits First Street by name and links its methodology pages.
principles.implication: Captions follow one pattern: authority · scope · as-of. For example: 'FEMA · area zone · effective Sep 2021', 'USFS · relative hazard, 30 m model · 2023', 'AirNow · nearest monitors · 3:10 PM today', 'EPA · county-wide'. At narrow widths the sources can merge into one line, but time-varying rows keep their own 'today · 3:10 PM', and frozen compare rows keep 'as of'.

principles.principle: Keep two things apart: how official a fact is, and how specific it is to this home. A county or area designation is official but not a statement about the house.
principles.evidence: EPA says its radon map 'should not be used to determine if a home in a given zone should be tested' and that 'Homes with elevated levels of radon have been found in all three zones'. WRC says 'The only way to truly assess home susceptibility is through individual home assessments' and that its model does not account for mitigated homes. National WHP is 270 m and the WRC version 30 m. van der Bles et al. (2019) separate what is uncertain (facts, numbers, science) from direct versus indirect uncertainty.
principles.implication: A published dataset gets the FILLED (official) mark plus a scope word in its caption ('county-wide', 'area zone', 'modelled, quarter-mile'). Reserve HOLLOW for facts the household can confirm or correct, like pickup day or seeded deadlines. The radon row keeps the grey disclaimer and the test-kit action as the way from county to house.

principles.principle: State uncertainty and limits openly, preferably as explicit scope or numbers rather than vague hedges.
principles.evidence: van der Bles et al. (2020, PNAS) ran five experiments, including a field test on BBC News (n=5,780). People noticed uncertainty when it was communicated, but trust in the numbers and the source dropped only slightly, and mostly when the uncertainty was verbal.
principles.implication: Write 'County-wide estimate — only a test tells you about this house' and 'Observed 6:00 AM — 9 hours ago'. Avoid 'may', 'possibly' or 'approximately risky'. Don't avoid a caveat for fear of lowering trust.

principles.principle: Risk graphics need a visible denominator. Showing only the affected count inflates perceived risk. An icon array is optional; a clear bar or number is not.
principles.evidence: Ancker et al. (2006 systematic review): graphs that show only the numerator 'appear to inflate the perceived risk and may induce risk-averse behavior'. People often preferred simple, familiar designs that did not make their judgments more accurate. Garcia-Retamero and Cokely (2017; 36 publications, 27,885 participants) found clear visual aids reliably improve risk understanding, especially for people with less numeracy. Scalia et al. (2021, n=407) found no difference in understanding between an icon array and a bar graph, and most participants preferred the bar graph.
principles.implication: If the risk detail or provenance sheet adds a picture for '1 in 4 over 30 years', use a 4-cell or 100-cell array with the whole population shown. Never show a bare count such as 'X flood claims nearby' without its base. The strips don't need icon arrays.

principles.principle: A time-varying reading must show when it was observed, and a frozen copy must say it is frozen.
principles.evidence: EPA's NowCast turns up to 12 hours of recent readings into a current AQI that changes during the day. EPA says 'As a general matter, EPA does not advise applying AQI values to realtime sensor data, especially 1-minute readings'. Official daily AQI reports are in effect for the previous day.
principles.implication: Air rows always carry 'today · observed H:MM', plus the age once stale. Compare tokens show 'as of <date>'. Don't colour a raw low-cost-sensor reading with the AQI palette unless it has EPA's correction, as AirNow's Fire and Smoke Map applies.

principles.principle: Marks are visual only. The tap target is the row or cell around them.
principles.evidence: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 requires pointer targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS px (or enough spacing). Apple HIG lists 44x44 pt as the default iOS control size and 28x28 pt as the minimum. Apple's chart guidance notes that chart marks are often too small to tap.
principles.implication: An 8px strip dot or 16px mark opens nothing by itself. The day cell or list row opens the provenance sheet, with a hit area of at least 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android (Material convention, not re-checked in this pass) and 24px on web.

principles.principle: Showing a place's hazard can affect decisions and home value, so comparison copy describes places and datasets, never a person's home.
principles.evidence: Zillow's analysis (reported with the removal) found that of homes listed in June 2024, 52% with high flood risk had sold by March 2025, against 71% with low risk. Agents said the scores discouraged buyers, and the scores were removed after CRMLS objected. Severtson (2013) found that hazard level and proximity shown on a map strongly changed people's beliefs and intentions.
principles.implication: Sender columns read 'Dana · Camas, WA — what's on record for this area'. Values name the designation ('in FEMA Zone X'), never the house ('Dana's home floods'). Merged marks read 'Same band', not 'Both highest'.

patterns.name: Banded track per authority (scale strip)
patterns.exemplars: Apple Weather shows AQI as a coloured bar running from green to maroon with the current value on it, using data AirNow feeds through The Weather Channel (secondary sources How-To Geek and iDownloadBlog, found by search and not opened). Redfin and Realtor.com show First Street's 1-10 Factors with fixed labels: 1 minimal, 2 minor, 3-4 moderate, 5-6 major, 7-8 severe, 9-10 extreme. WRC shows community Risk to Homes as percentile classes against the state and nation.
patterns.howToApply: One horizontal track per layer, split into that authority's own classes. The marker sits in the occupied class, with the class name beside it and an 'authority · scope · as-of' caption below. Row height is 48pt at detail size. Only the AQI track uses colour.
patterns.pitfalls: First Street and ClimateCheck (1-100 through 2050) are model scores, not official designations; don't borrow their look and imply one. A 1-10 score with a colour ramp is exactly the kind of grade that was removed from Zillow. Tracks that line up across rows imply a shared axis. v1 already avoids this; keep it that way.

patterns.name: Word + number, inline
patterns.exemplars: AirNow and the EPA AQI always pair the number with the category name ('42 · Good'). Redfin pairs the number with a label ('Flood Factor 6 · major'). In Wintle 2019, readers understood verbal terms well only when the numeric range sat in brackets in the text itself.
patterns.howToApply: Always print both on the value line: 'Moderate · 3 of 5', 'Zone AE · 1% each year', 'AQI 118 · Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups'. On OG and 390px widths, shorten the word ('USG' only if the full name also appears in the provenance sheet), never the number.
patterns.pitfalls: 'N of M' only works when a higher N means more hazard. Radon zones run the other way.

patterns.name: Overlaid two-mark comparison with a neutral difference tag
patterns.exemplars: Ondov et al. 2018: overlaying both datasets beat side-by-side and stacked layouts for finding the biggest difference. Gleicher 2011: directly encoding the difference is the lowest-memory form of comparison.
patterns.howToApply: One track per layer. The sender's mark is filled; the recipient's is ringed and labelled 'You'. Rows keep the fixed order Flood · Wildfire · Air · Radon. Rows whose marks fall in different bands get a small neutral tag, 'Different band'. When both marks share a band, merge them and label it 'Same band'. An optional line above the table ('Your readings differ on flood and wildfire') gives the headline without re-sorting.
patterns.pitfalls: Arrows between marks, red/green difference colours, a 'versus' badge, and sorting rows by distance all turn readings into a contest. Distance is not comparable across tracks with different numbers of bands.

patterns.name: Standardized disclosure label (nutrition label)
patterns.exemplars: Kelley et al. (CHI 2010) standardized privacy table: 764 participants, and it beat full-text and layered policies. Its features were fixed rows, explicit 'not collected' cells, standard terms and a legend of definitions. The FTC endorsed the approach in 2010, per the CUPS project page.
patterns.howToApply: The four-row instrument is the label. It keeps the same rows, order, terms and missing-data rows on the in-app page, compare views, the compare sheet preview and the OG card. A legend of band definitions is one tap away in the provenance sheet.
patterns.pitfalls: Short variants that drop rows made comparisons harder in Kelley's study. Keep all four rows even at 400x210.

patterns.name: Inline provenance caption + one deep sheet
patterns.exemplars: Redfin names First Street on the page and links its methodology. EPA's own AQI reporting rules require the reporting area, the reporting period and the main pollutant alongside the value. In Kelley's study, few people clicked from layered notices through to the full text.
patterns.howToApply: Caption pattern 'authority · scope · as-of' under each value. Tapping the row opens x-provenance-sheet, which holds method, resolution, effective date, the full EPA health statement and 'This isn't right'.
patterns.pitfalls: Merging the captions into 'Sources: FEMA, USFS, AirNow, EPA' at 320-360px drops the effective dates. Keep 'today · time' on the air row and 'as of' on frozen rows.

patterns.name: Scope qualifier separate from confirmation mark
patterns.exemplars: EPA radon map: official, county-level, 'should not be used to determine if a home ... should be tested'. WRC: community-level results, with individual home assessments as the only true measure.
patterns.howToApply: Filled mark plus a scope word ('county-wide', 'area zone', 'modelled') for public datasets. Hollow mark only for facts the household can confirm, such as pickup day or seeded deadlines. The radon card's free-kit action is the step from county to house.
patterns.pitfalls: A hollow mark on an official EPA or USFS designation suggests the designation itself is doubtful, and it wears down the meaning of hollow elsewhere, such as unconfirmed pickup days.

patterns.name: Threshold rule on the official scale
patterns.exemplars: EPA: above AQI 100, reports must name the sensitive groups, and air-quality action days are called at Orange or Red. AirNow's Fire and Smoke Map has a colour-wheel toggle for the ColorVision Assist palette (EPA 2022 news release, seen only in a search summary: https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/air-quality-awareness-week-2022-airnow-fire-and-smoke-map-adds-new-feature-improve).
patterns.howToApply: On alert variants, a thin rule at 101 on the same AQI track, the EPA sensitive-groups statement, and the 'Saved place · Only you' chip.
patterns.pitfalls: Don't invent thresholds on non-AQI tracks. FEMA, USFS and EPA radon designations have no 'alert' crossing.

patterns.name: Planning-horizon translation for annual probabilities
patterns.exemplars: First Street defines Flood Factor over a 30-year mortgage. Realtor.com shows how each risk changes over 15 and 30 years. USGS explains annual exceedance probability.
patterns.howToApply: '1% each year · about 1 in 4 over 30 years' in the detail and the provenance sheet; the annual phrase alone on compact rows.
patterns.pitfalls: Don't project FEMA zones forward with climate scenarios. That is a model claim FEMA does not make.

antipatterns: A combined letter grade, 0-100 score, stars, or 'Quiet/High' verdict across layers. Four authorities have no common scale, and property-level scores were removed from Zillow after accuracy complaints, with models matching each other as little as 21% of the time.
Radar or spider charts. They encode area, which people judge poorly (NN/g), and they put unrelated axes on one scale.

Rainbow, red-to-green or continuous gradient ramps on hazard tracks. They are not perceptually uniform, fail colour-blind readers, and discrete classes produce fewer errors (Crameri 2020; Schneider 2023).
Colour as the only cue (for example a row of four coloured dots). This violates WCAG 1.4.1 and Apple HIG, and position on a scale is the encoding that carries meaning.
Touching AQI colour segments with no separator. Adjacent EPA hues contrast only 1.57-2.37:1, below the WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 threshold.
'100-year flood' or '100-year floodplain'. USGS calls the term misleading; write '1% chance each year'.
'Minimal risk' for FEMA Zone X. FEMA's designation is 'minimal flood hazard' and describes an area, not a house.

'Wildfire risk' for WHP, or using WHP as a sign of fire danger this season. USFS says WHP is 'not an explicit map of wildfire threat or risk' and 'not a forecast or wildfire outlook for any particular season'. The design doc's Jun 15-Sep 30 rule that promotes 'wildfire hazard High' must not read as current fire danger; pair it with current AirNow or NOAA conditions, or present it as a standing fact.
Any copy suggesting a county radon zone tells someone whether to test. EPA says the map should not be used for that, and elevated homes have been found in all three zones.
An AQI track closed at 500. EPA: all values above 300 are Hazardous, 'This includes values above 500'.
Paraphrased EPA health statements (e.g. 'satisfactory for everyone'). EPA lists inaccurate cautionary statements and inconsistent terminology as common reporting errors.
AQI colours on raw one-minute low-cost sensor readings. EPA does not advise it.
Re-sorting comparison rows per pair. It breaks the 'same place every time' benefit of a standardized label, and 'distance' across tracks with different band counts is itself a cross-layer ranking.

Arrows, winner badges, 'better/worse' or red/green difference colouring between two places. This turns area readings into judgments of a friend's home, and hazard displays measurably move sale outcomes (52% vs 71% sold).
'N of M' phrasing for radon zones. Zone 1 is the highest, so '1 of 3' reads as the lowest next to wildfire's '3 of 5'.
Graphics that show only the number affected (e.g. 'X flood claims nearby'). Ancker 2006: this inflates perceived risk.
Vague verbal hedges ('may', 'possibly') instead of explicit scope or numbers. Verbal uncertainty cost slightly more trust than numeric (van der Bles 2020).
8px dots or 16px marks as the only tap target. WCAG 2.5.8 requires 24x24 CSS px; Apple HIG's default iOS control size is 44x44pt.

Putting the essential number or source only behind a tooltip or 'learn more'. In Wintle 2019, inline brackets worked and tooltips or click-throughs did not help much; Kelley found few people click through layered notices.
Borrowing First Street or ClimateCheck styling (1-10 or 1-100 with a colour ramp) for official designations. It implies a property-level model score Pantopus does not have.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The Air row is drawn like the other rows: 'draw segments as neutral surface tokens … let the marker be the one saturated element' and 'Do not run a green→amber→red ramp across or within the tracks.' Meanwhile f1-today-air-band draws the same reading in the six EPA hues.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: EPA's Technical Assistance Document (May 2026) defines the standard AQI colours, lists 'inconsistent AQI colors or terminology' as a common reporting error, and allows only its ColorVision Assist set as an alternative. Apple HIG says charts of the same data should keep the same colours and marks. v1 now shows one AQI reading in two visual languages: coloured on Today, neutral in the instrument, the OG card and the risk page.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the rule against a shared ramp across layers, but make the Air row the single coloured track inside the instrument. Use the same EPA palette (standard or ColorVision Assist, chosen once), separators and marker as f1-today-air-band and the widget. Flood, wildfire and radon stay neutral.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Hazardous 301+' but 'segment widths proportional to their ranges'. f8-scale-strips spells the ranges out as '(0–50, 51–100, 101–150, 151–200, 201–300, 301–500)'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: EPA: 'All AQI values above 300 are part of the Hazardous category. This includes values above 500.' A track capped at 500 cannot place such readings. Proportional widths also give Hazardous 40% and Very Unhealthy 20% of the track, leaving the everyday 0-100 range 20% (about 70px at 390 wide).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use equal-width category segments with the marker placed within its segment, or proportional widths ending in a short open-ended '301+' stub. Either way, clamp values above the end with the number printed. Apply the same spec to f8-scale-strips, f6-place-section-details, f7-today-widget and x-provenance-sheet.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Default health message 'Air quality is satisfactory for everyone.' and Pantopus-written alert lines ('Everyone should limit time outdoors. Keep windows shut tonight.').
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: AirNow's official Good text is 'Air quality is satisfactory, and air pollution poses little or no risk.' EPA lists 'inaccurate cautionary statements and health information' as a common reporting error. Above AQI 100, reports must name the pollutant-specific sensitive groups (TAD Table 4).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use EPA's exact category description and pollutant-specific sensitive-group statement as the health line. Show Pantopus context ('Smoke from the Gorge', 'Keep windows shut tonight') as a separate, clearly Pantopus line under it.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Do not restyle the EPA ramp…' with the six EPA hues as the only exception to the token rule, drawn in light and dark, with no contrast or separation treatment specified.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: EPA itself allows the ColorVision Assist palette. Computed from EPA's RGB values: adjacent standard hues contrast 1.57-2.37:1, yellow is 1.07:1 and green 1.74:1 on white, and maroon is 1.62:1 on the dark base #0F172A. All are below WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1. Apple HIG asks for visual separation between touching colour areas.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Clarify that switching to EPA's ColorVision Assist palette is allowed and does not count as restyling. Require 2px surface gaps between segments, a border.strong keyline in both modes, a two-tone marker ring that reaches 3:1 on every segment, and the band name always printed.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Flood value 'Zone X — minimal risk' (the arrival header and compare sheet use the same wording; the OG card shortens it to 'Zone X — minimal'; f6 says 'minimal hazard').
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: FEMA defines unshaded Zone X as an area of 'minimal flood hazard'. It describes an area, not a property's risk. Property-level risk models disagree with each other and with zones, which is the dispute behind Zillow removing its scores. Kelley's label research depends on standard terms.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use one approved string on every surface: 'Zone X — minimal flood hazard' with caption 'FEMA · area zone · effective <date>'. Never use 'risk' for a FEMA zone.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Flood track with '4 segments — X · X shaded · AE · VE'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: FEMA's high-risk zones (A, AO, AH, A1-30, AE, A99, AR, V, VE, V1-30) are all defined by the same 1% annual chance. Shaded X lies between the 1% and 0.2% floods; unshaded X is outside the 0.2% flood. So AE and VE are not successive steps of one ordered scale; V zones add coastal wave hazard (standard FEMA meaning, not in the glossary text I retrieved). An address in Zone A, AO or AH has no segment, and an unmapped or undetermined area has no state.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use three bands by annual chance: 'Minimal (X)', '0.2% a year (shaded X)', '1% a year or more (A/V zones)'. Print the actual zone code in the marker label, add a distinct 'FEMA hasn't mapped flood hazard here' state, and mention V-zone wave hazard in words, not as a fourth band.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The recipient's aha reads 'Zone AE — this address is in the 100-year floodplain'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: USGS calls '100-year flood' a term that 'leads to a misconception' and prefers the 1-percent annual chance. Lee et al. (2021) found correct readings depended on understanding independent probabilities. Over 30 years a 1% zone is about a 26% chance.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: 'Zone AE — 1% chance of flooding every year (about 1 in 4 over 30 years) · FEMA'. Use the same wording on f6-place-section-details and the seasonal and ranked aha.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Rows are ordered by the distance between the two marks, descending … never a fixed order.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Standardized labels help partly because information is 'found in the same place every time' (Kelley 2010), and Apple HIG asks for continuity across charts of the same data. The arrival header and OG card use a fixed order just before this step. Tracks have 3, 3-4, 5 and 6 bands, so 'distance' across rows is a cross-layer ranking, which the instrument's own rules forbid. The overlay already makes the biggest difference easy to spot (Ondov 2018).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the fixed order Flood · Wildfire · Air · Radon. Mark rows with different bands with a neutral 'Different band' tag, and optionally add a one-line summary naming those layers above the table.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Below 640px the sender column collapses to 'first name · city · four tiny markers in layer order'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: A marker means something only by its position on its own track (NN/g: position and length are the accurate encodings). Without tracks, four markers can only differ by fill or colour, which violates WCAG 1.4.1 and Apple HIG, and a row of four dots looks like a rating.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Make the collapsed line text: 'Dana · Camas, WA · Flood X · Wildfire Moderate · Air 42 · Radon Zone 1 ›', or 'Dana · Camas, WA · 4 readings ›' when space is short. No marker glyphs until the row is expanded.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Radon is drawn with the 'hollow mark, caption "On record, not yet confirmed"', and state 3 draws radon and wildfire hollow. f6-place-section-details and f8-og-compare-card repeat the hollow radon mark.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The EPA radon zone and USFS WHP are official published designations. Their limit is scope, not confirmation: EPA says the map 'should not be used to determine if a home … should be tested' and that high-radon homes exist in all three zones, and WRC says only home assessments show a home's susceptibility. The uncertainty framework in van der Bles 2019 treats these as different kinds of uncertainty. x-provenance-sheet defines hollow as 'on record but unconfirmed', which suggests the zone itself might be wrong.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw official datasets FILLED, with a scope word in the caption ('EPA · county-wide estimate — only a test tells you about this home'). Keep HOLLOW for facts a household can confirm (pickup, seeded civic dates). If radon must stay hollow, change its caption to 'County estimate · not a test of this home' instead of 'not yet confirmed'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Radon value 'Zone 1 — highest', on a card that can show the sender's first name.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: EPA's term is 'highest potential', meaning a predicted county average above 4 pCi/L, and the map is not meant for decisions about individual homes. On its own, 'highest' next to a person's name reads as a verdict on that person's home.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: 'Zone 1 — highest potential (county)', or 'County radon Zone 1 · highest potential' if width allows. Keep the EPA caption.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Wildfire '2 of 5 · Low' and, directly below it, Radon 'Zone 1 of 3 · highest potential'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The word-plus-number format only helps when the number means the same thing everywhere (Wintle 2019; Budescu 2009), and hazard scales should read in one direction (Schneider 2023). Here '2 of 5' means low while '1 of 3' means highest, so the 'N of M' form flips meaning between adjacent rows.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Radon reads 'Zone 1 — highest potential of EPA's 3 zones'. Keep 'N of 5' only for WHP, where a higher number means more hazard.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Calm fallback: grade chip 'Quiet', headline 'Quiet on every layer', detail 'Minimal flood risk, no active alerts, low earthquake demand. That's rarer than you'd think.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Clark County is EPA radon Zone 1 (county public-health brochure, seen in a search summary: https://clark.wa.gov/sites/default/files/dept/files/public-health/EPH_Misc/Radon_Brochure.pdf), and EPA says high-radon homes exist in all zones. So 'quiet on every layer' can't be true for a pilot address whose radon layer is shown. 'Rarer than you'd think' is an unsupported comparison. A cross-layer 'Quiet' chip is the summary verdict the scale-strip instrument forbids. 'Minimal flood risk' misstates FEMA's 'minimal flood hazard', and 'earthquake demand' is not one of the four layers.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Name only what is actually calm, with sources: 'No active alerts · Air Good today (AirNow) · Outside FEMA's mapped floodplain'. No cross-layer grade chip, no comparison unless it is computed and sourced, and never 'quiet' wording that takes in radon.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The sheet opens 'by tapping a data mark — a dot in Today's 14-day strip…', with an 8px specimen dot.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 requires at least 24×24 CSS px targets (or equivalent spacing). Apple HIG lists 44×44 pt as the default iOS control size and 28×28 pt as the minimum, and notes that chart marks are often too small to tap.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: State that marks are visual only. The tap target is the enclosing day cell (which opens the day's rows) or the list row (which opens this sheet), at least 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android and 24px on web.

numbers: EPA AQI categories: Good 0-50 · Moderate 51-100 · Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups 101-150 · Unhealthy 151-200 · Very Unhealthy 201-300 · Hazardous 301+ (open-ended; values above 500 are still Hazardous). Source: EPA TAD May 2026.
EPA standard AQI RGB: Green 0,228,0 · Yellow 255,255,0 · Orange 255,126,0 · Red 255,0,0 · Purple 143,63,151 · Maroon 126,0,35.
EPA ColorVision Assist RGB (allowed alternative): Green 158,255,145 · Yellow 255,201,5 · Orange 255,130,5 · Red 240,34,0 · Purple 137,9,151 · Maroon 100,0,21.

Contrast calculated from EPA RGB (WCAG formula): standard hues vs white — Green 1.74, Yellow 1.07, Orange 2.55, Red 4.00, Purple 6.31, Maroon 10.99. Vs dark base #0F172A — Purple 2.83, Maroon 1.62. Adjacent standard hues 1.57-2.37:1, all below 3:1.
WCAG 1.4.11: 3:1 for graphics needed for understanding (exempt when text labels carry the same information). Apple HIG text contrast: 4.5:1 up to 17pt, 3:1 at 18pt+ or bold.
Target size: WCAG 2.5.8 at least 24x24 CSS px. Apple HIG iOS default control 44x44 pt, minimum 28x28 pt.
AQI reporting is legally required for MSAs over 350,000 people. Sensitive groups must be named whenever the AQI is over 100. The PM NowCast uses the past 12 hours of data.
FEMA: high-risk (SFHA) zones = 1% annual chance. Shaded X = between the 1% and 0.2% floods (moderate flood hazard). Unshaded X = above the 0.2% flood (minimal flood hazard).
Calculated over 30 years: 1% a year → 26% (about 1 in 4); 0.2% a year → 5.8% (about 1 in 17).
EPA radon zones: Zone 1 predicted county average above 4 pCi/L (highest potential, red on EPA map); Zone 2 2-4 (orange); Zone 3 below 2 (yellow). Fix at 4 pCi/L or higher; consider fixing at 2-4.
USFS WHP: 5 classes (very low, low, moderate, high, very high). National version 270 m, WRC version 30 m. Latest national WHP is the 2023 version, released June 17 2024.

WRC Risk to Homes classes (from the methods page as summarised by the fetch tool; treat as moderately verified): Low below the 40th percentile, Medium 40-70th, High 70-90th, Very High above the 90th, nationally. Current WRC release v2.3 (April 2026).

First Street Factors (as shown on Redfin): 1 minimal, 2 minor, 3-4 moderate, 5-6 major, 7-8 severe, 9-10 extreme, over 30 years. Flood Factor 1 = less than 0.2% chance each year (First Street FAQ via search snippet).
ClimateCheck: 1-100 per hazard (heat, storm, fire, drought, flood), projected to 2050.

Zillow: climate scores added Sep 2024, removed Nov 14 2025. 52% of high-flood-risk vs 71% of low-risk homes listed in June 2024 had sold by March 2025. Bloomberg Green found First Street and UC Irvine flood models agreed 21% of the time.
Wintle et al. 2019 (n=924): numbers in brackets in the text raised correct interpretation of verbal probabilities to 66%, against 32% with no numbers.
van der Bles et al. 2020: 5 experiments, n=5,780. Communicating uncertainty caused only a small drop in trust, mostly when the uncertainty was verbal.
Kelley et al. CHI 2010: 764 participants, 5 formats. Standardized formats beat full-text and layered policies.
Garcia-Retamero & Cokely 2017: 36 publications, 27,885 participants, 60 countries. Scalia et al. 2021: n=407, no difference in understanding between icon array and bar graph.
Schneider et al. 2023: 5-7 classes can be told apart. The redesigned map raised correct understanding from 36.8% to 81.6% on one item.
Colour vision deficiency: about 8% of men and 0.5% of women (Crameri 2020).

OG card: 1200x630, and some clients crop to 400x210 (1/3 scale). Text must be at least 36px at 1200 to stay about 12px after the crop (calculated). Track height at least 30px at 1200 to stay about 10px.

topic: accessibility-inclusive: WCAG 2.2 AA (including the new criteria), iOS Dynamic Type, VoiceOver and motion/contrast settings, Android TalkBack and 200% font scaling, colour-blind-safe encodings for ordinal scales and filled/hollow provenance marks, plain language, accessible charts and timelines, and usability for older adults. Written for Pantopus movers aged about 25 to 70 on web, iOS and Android. Highest-risk surfaces, in order: f7-today-widget, f5-today-calendar-strip, f8-scale-strips (and the four places that reuse it: f8-compare-reveal, f8-og-compare-card, f8-compare-sheet, f6-place-section-details), f1-today-air-band, x-place-file (year band plus ring), f10-bill-trend, f11-keeper-strip, f9-nearby-cells-map, x-provenance-sheet (it defines the marks), x-date-sheet, f10-extraction-confirm, f10-mail-piece-photo, f10-mail-day-triage, f7-widget-howto-sheet, f4-notification-settings. Contrast ratios quoted for Pantopus tokens are my own calculations. I used the WCAG relative-luminance formula on the hex values in house-style-v1.txt and frontend/packages/theme/src/colors.ts, where primary.600 = primary.DEFAULT = #0284c7. On web, buttons are bg-primary-600 with white text. Neither house-style-v1 nor the design doc has any accessibility section today.

principles.principle: Readable text must reach 4.5:1 contrast, in both themes. Several Pantopus text tokens fail this today.
principles.evidence: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (AA): text needs at least 4.5:1. Large text needs 3:1. Apple HIG asks for 4.5:1 up to 17pt and 3:1 at 18pt and above. Apple also says to check light and dark mode and to offer a higher-contrast scheme when Increase Contrast is on. Android asks for 4.5:1 below 18sp (or below 14sp bold) and 3:1 otherwise. Apple's App Store 'Sufficient Contrast' criteria say to test with Bold Text, Increase Contrast and Reduce Transparency all on. Computed ratios on white (#FFFFFF): text.muted #9CA3AF = 2.54 (FAIL). primary.DEFAULT #0284c7 = 4.10 (FAIL for body or caption links). White on primary.DEFAULT, the web filled button = 4.10 (FAIL at 14 to 16px medium). warning #D97706 = 3.19, and 3.07 on warningBg (FAIL). success #059669 = 3.77 (FAIL). info on infoBg = 3.84 (FAIL). error on errorBg = 4.41 (FAIL, narrowly). text.secondary = 4.83 (pass), 4.51 on app #F6F7F9 (pass), 4.39 on surface.sunken (FAIL). Dark mode: primary.DEFAULT on base #0F172A = 4.36 (FAIL for text), dark text.secondary = 6.96 (pass). Passing replacements: primary.700 #0369a1 = 5.93, and white on primary.700 = 5.93.
principles.implication: Never use text.muted for text a person needs to read. It is only for placeholder text and truly disabled controls. Use text.secondary for captions, 'Not set', source lines and contrast clauses. Filled primary buttons use primary.700, not primary.DEFAULT, under white labels. Inline links use primary.700 in light mode and the dark focus blue #38BDF8 (8.33:1) in dark mode. Semantic tints (warning, success, info, error) carry text in text.primary or text.strong, and the semantic hue goes only on the glyph or border (3:1 is enough there). Text on surface.sunken uses text.strong, not text.secondary. Every prompt frame is checked in dark mode and with Increase Contrast on.

principles.principle: Any graphic that carries meaning needs 3:1 contrast against what touches it. That covers marks, band dividers, chart columns, ring segments, input borders and selected states. The exception is when the same fact is printed as text right beside it.
principles.evidence: WCAG 1.4.11 (AA) requires 3:1 for 'parts of graphics required to understand the content' and for the visual state of UI components. The Understanding doc says a darker border can supply that contrast. It also says visible data labels make the graphic supplementary: its example is a pie chart whose labels and values carry the same information. Input borders need 3:1. Computed ratios on white: border.default 1.24, border.strong 1.47, surface.raised 1.05, surface.sunken 1.10, primary.100 1.15, primary.200 1.33, primary.300 1.67, primary.600 4.10, text.secondary 4.83. Adjacent ramp steps: primary.100 vs 200 = 1.16, 200 vs 300 = 1.26, 300 vs 500 = 1.66. In dark mode, border.default #1F2937 against raised #1E293B = 1.00.
principles.implication: Hairline tokens (border.default, border.strong) are decoration only. They must never be the only thing that shows a band edge, an empty ring segment, a hollow mark's outline or an input boundary. Draw band dividers and hollow or tick strokes in ink of at least text.secondary strength (4.83:1), at least 1.5px. A light chart fill is fine only if it has an outline of at least 3:1 (for example primary.800 at 7.56:1). The occupied band is shown by the marker plus its printed name, which the text exception covers, not by a raised fill alone. Dark mode needs its own card-edge token, because border.default disappears on raised.

principles.principle: Never use colour as the only signal, and make every surface pass a greyscale test.
principles.evidence: WCAG 1.4.1 (Level A): colour must not be the only visual way to convey information. Apple's 'Differentiate Without Color Alone' criteria say to use placement, order, shape, icons or labels as well as colour. They add: 'If you can't use your own app in grayscale, rethink your app's design.' Apple HIG names red-green and blue-orange as hard pairs. Android asks for shapes, sizes, text, patterns, audio or haptics alongside colour. NEI: about 1 in 12 men have a colour vision deficiency, most often red-green. Okabe and Ito's Color Universal Design recommends combining colours with shapes, line types, patterns and direct labels.
principles.implication: Each prompt should say: 'this frame must still read correctly in greyscale'. Three concrete fixes. (1) The 14-day strip's class colours (pickup, civic, money, yours) need a second cue, or should be dropped from the strip and carried by the glyphs in the list rows. (2) 'Stale' must be told apart from 'fresh' by text ('Updated 7h ago'), not only by greyed marks. (3) The info-to-warning switch on deadline chips is fine only because the chip always prints the day count. Unread dots and ring fills also need a text equivalent for assistive technology.

principles.principle: For the AQI band, keep EPA's six categories and their hue order, but use EPA's ColorVision Assist palette. Always print the category name, separate the segments with ink lines, and never put text on a coloured fill.
principles.evidence: The EPA Technical Assistance Document (EPA-403/B-26-003, May 2026) requires the category descriptor, and the colour if colour is used. Table 2 gives the standard RGB values: Green 0,228,0 · Yellow 255,255,0 · Orange 255,126,0 · Red 255,0,0 · Purple 143,63,151 · Maroon 126,0,35. It says reporting entities 'may also use ColorVision Assist colors that enhance contrast'. Table 3 gives those values: Green 158,255,145 · Yellow 255,201,5 · Orange 255,130,5 · Red 240,34,0 · Purple 137,9,151 · Maroon 100,0,21. EPA says the standard scale 'can be difficult to discern', especially red and green. Hazardous is '301+', and values above 500 still fall in Hazardous. South Coast AQMD built the palette with DRI, USFS and EPA, tested it against eight types of colour impairment, and is piloting it on EPA's Fire and Smoke Map. Computed: standard yellow on white = 1.07:1, green = 1.74:1. Adjacent green/yellow = 1.62 and orange/red = 1.57. The ColorVision Assist pairs are still low (1.26 to 1.71). In dark mode, maroon on #0F172A = 1.62 and ColorVision Assist maroon = 1.32. White text on EPA orange = 2.55.
principles.implication: The sanctioned exception to the token rule should name the ColorVision Assist hex values, not generic 'EPA colours'. Put a separator line of at least 3:1 between every pair of segments and an outer keyline around the bar, because hue alone will not separate neighbours for low-vision users in either palette. Draw the marker two-tone, with a text.primary core and a 2px surface.base halo, so it clears 3:1 on both light and dark segments. Print the band name in text.primary on the card surface next to the marker, never on the fill. Label the last segment '301+', not '301–500'. The spoken label reads, for example: 'Air quality index 118, Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, category 3 of 6. AirNow, observed 4 PM.'

principles.principle: The three provenance shapes (filled, hollow, filled-with-tick) must be the only filled/hollow encoding in the product. They must stay legible at their smallest size and in tinted widgets, and each needs a spoken name.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG recommends 'distinct shapes or icons, in addition to color'. For widgets, Apple HIG says accented rendering tints content to one colour and vibrant rendering desaturates it, so what matters is brightness difference. Apple's VoiceOver criteria require that all visually conveyed information is also exposed through labels, traits and values. Android's stateDescription is the equivalent for state. WCAG 1.1.1 requires text alternatives for non-text content. I found no authoritative minimum size for a symbol. The ~12pt floor below is my own design judgement: at 8px, a tick stroke is one or two device pixels.
principles.implication: x-provenance-sheet should define: (a) a minimum drawn size of about 12pt/12dp for a mark that must be told apart from the others, scaling with Dynamic Type and sp; (b) a stroke and tick of at least 1.5px in ink of 3:1 or better; (c) fixed spoken names: 'official', 'on record, not confirmed', 'you added this'; (d) a check that the three shapes still differ in accented, desaturated widget rendering. No other surface may use filled against hollow/ringed for a different meaning (sender vs you, taken vs open slot). Where a mark would drop below the minimum size, the row text carries the provenance words instead.

principles.principle: Touch targets are at least 44×44pt on iOS, 48×48dp with 8dp gaps on Android, and 44×44 CSS px on web (WCAG AA allows 24×24 at minimum). A small mark or dot is never a tap target on its own.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG gives a default of 44×44pt and a minimum of 28×28pt on iOS. It recommends about 12pt of padding around controls with a bezel and about 24pt around those without. Android asks for 'at least 48dp×48dp'. Accessibility Scanner adds 'separated by 8dp of space or more', which it puts at about 9mm. WCAG 2.5.8 (AA) sets 24×24 CSS px, or 24px-diameter circles that don't overlap. 2.5.5 (AAA) sets 44×44. NN/g recommends at least 1cm×1cm, notes fingertips are 1.6–2cm wide, and says seniors with declining dexterity benefit from larger controls.
principles.implication: 'Tap the mark to open the provenance sheet' means the whole row or cell is the target, at 44pt/48dp or more. The 14-day strip cells are about 25pt wide at 393pt, so on native they cannot be 14 separate targets. The strip is one element that opens or scrolls to the day list. Text buttons ('This isn't right', 'Skip', 'Undo', 'Retry') get 44pt/48dp tall hit areas. Thumbnail delete and retake controls in the capture tray each get a 44pt target. Segmented controls are at least 44pt tall. The keeper ring's tap area is at least 44pt, not 36pt.

principles.principle: Design for iOS AX5, Android 200% and web 200% zoom and 320px reflow. Horizontal pairs stack, meaningful text wraps rather than truncating, and no sheet is forbidden to scroll.
principles.evidence: Apple Typography: the default body is 17pt. Accessibility body sizes are AX1 28pt, AX2 33pt, AX3 40pt, AX4 47pt and AX5 53pt (62pt leading). Guidance: 'Keep text truncation to a minimum', use 'a stacked layout where text appears above secondary items', 'Reduce the number of columns', and keep primary elements near the top. Apple's Larger Text criteria: support enlarging text to at least 200%. AX3 exceeds 200% and AX5 exceeds 300%. Side-by-side elements should wrap or go vertical. Tab bars are exempt, and the Large Content Viewer covers them. Android 14 scales fonts to 200% on a nonlinear curve and says to test at 200%, use sp for lineHeight, and not use sp for padding. WCAG 1.4.4 requires 200% resize without loss. 1.4.10 requires reflow at 320 CSS px (1280px at 400%), with exceptions for maps, diagrams and data tables. 1.4.12 sets text-spacing overrides.
principles.implication: Every prompt's STATES list adds one 'AX5 / 200%' frame. At that size: value-plus-caption pairs stack; segmented controls with three or more long labels become radio rows; grids of tiles drop to one column; sheets may scroll past their detent. Chart instruments keep their geometry but move labels above the track. Place labels and values wrap to two lines instead of ellipsising. The four-tab bar keeps its size and uses Large Content Viewer on long-press. Web frames include 320px width at 200% text.

principles.principle: Widgets follow Dynamic Type up to AX5 and must never show text smaller than 11pt. Text is never rasterised, and each size has a text-only fallback layout.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Widgets: 'Display text using 11 points or larger'. Widgets support Dynamic Type from Large to AX5 when using Font. Never rasterise text, so VoiceOver can read it. Margins are 16pt, or 11pt when tight. Offer one tap target on inline widgets and deep-link to the relevant place. Show 'last updated' text when people check more often than the widget updates. Accented rendering tints primary and accent groups, and vibrant rendering needs contrast in greyscale. Update animations can last up to 2 seconds.
principles.implication: A 14-cell strip about 120pt wide gives about 8.6pt per cell. That cannot hold 11pt weekday initials under every cell, so label only the anchors (for example 'Today' at the left and the date at the right edge), or give the strip more width. At AX sizes, the medium and large widgets drop the strip, band bar and year lanes and show the hero line, place label and air reading as text. The place label wraps and never ellipsises. Each widget exposes one combined VoiceOver or TalkBack label that reads the hero, its provenance, the air reading and 'updated 7:40 am'. Stale is always stated in words. Update animations are suppressed when Reduce Motion is on.

principles.principle: Every chart, strip, band, ring and timeline has a one-sentence plain-language summary, spoken labels for each mark, and a list or table of the same facts. Nobody should need to interact with it to understand it.
principles.evidence: W3C's Complex Images tutorial calls for a two-part alternative: a short description, plus a long one covering 'scales, values, relationships and trends'. USWDS says to provide text for axis values and a tabular view (a visually hidden table), to state the intended message in text, to keep each chart to two or three concepts, and that 'your audience shouldn't be required to interact with a visualization to understand its message'. Apple HIG Charting data: 'Make every chart in your app accessible'. A descriptive headline 'doesn't take the place of accessibility labels'. Swift Charts builds an accessibility tree and audio graphs automatically (search-level source, WWDC21 session 10122). Chartability sets 50 heuristics with a 14-test short list (Elavsky et al., EuroVis 2022).
principles.implication: Bill trend: a caption summary such as 'October $142. Your last 12 months ranged from $88 (June) to $199 (January).
