Average of 14 homes nearby: $127', plus a 'Show amounts' list of 12 rows with full month names, including 'no bill'. Scale strips: each row is one element, for example 'Wildfire: Moderate, 3 of 5, on the USFS scale from Very low to Very high. USFS 2023. Official.' Year band: the fact rows below already are the table, so say so and link the band to them. 14-day strip: 'Next 14 days: 9 items', with day-by-day adjustment. Cells-map sparkline: '14 neighbor posts in 30 days. 3 Pantopus posts not counted.' Keeper and place-file ring: '11 things on file. Known: place, dates, money, people. Nothing yet: proof.'

principles.principle: Screen-reader structure: group each row into one element with custom actions, make day strips adjustable, trap focus inside sheets, and give every sheet a unique title.
principles.evidence: Android: use mergeDescendants to group, keep only the parent clickable, and replace swipe, drag and long-press with CustomAccessibilityAction. Use stateDescription, heading(), onClickLabel, collectionInfo, and unique paneTitle values ('reusing generic titles... can cause unintended side effects'). Apple VoiceOver criteria: logical, complete reading order; the cursor must not reset when content reloads; modals must make the background inaccessible; custom actions for grouped behaviour and context menus. Apple accessibilityAdjustableAction lets VoiceOver users swipe up or down to increment or decrement.
principles.implication: Each calendar, date, bill or mail row reads in visual order: title, value, relative day, source, provenance. Its actions (Edit, Remind me, Where this comes from, This isn't right, Undo) are custom actions, not extra swipe stops. The 14-day strip is a single adjustable element: swiping up or down moves one day and reads 'Tuesday 20 October: Recycling and garbage, city schedule, not confirmed'. Its weekday initials are never spoken alone. Every sheet takes focus on open, hides the screen behind it, and has a unique title (for example 'Where this fact comes from', 'Add a date'). Deep-link arrivals that highlight a row move focus to that row.

principles.principle: Never make pinch, pan, drag, long-press, swipe or hover the only way to do something. Every sheet has a visible Close or Done and also closes with Back or Escape.
principles.evidence: WCAG 2.5.1 (A): multipoint or path gestures need a single-pointer alternative; the example is map pinch-zoom with +/- buttons. WCAG 2.5.7 (AA): dragging needs a single-pointer alternative (tap the slider track, move buttons, map arrow buttons). WCAG 1.4.13 covers content revealed on hover or focus. Apple HIG: 'Offer alternatives to gestures', for example a button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. NN/g bottom sheets: show a visible Close button, support the device Back button, and don't stack sheets; 'the grab handle alone is insufficient'. NN/g's seniors report: sliders and dropdowns are harder on touch for people with declining motor skills.
principles.implication: Photo viewer: add zoom-in and zoom-out buttons, or make double-tap cycle through 1x, 2x and 4x. Chrome does not auto-hide while VoiceOver, TalkBack or Switch Control is running. Capture tray: 'Retake' and 'Delete' are visible buttons on each thumbnail, not long-press or hover. Cells map: provide a 'List cells' view and pan buttons. The web drop target already has 'choose files'. Mail Day rows: no swipe-only triage. Every sheet (date, provenance, compare, widget how-to, verify, naming) draws a visible Close or Done. No slider anywhere; the air-alert threshold uses radio rows.

principles.principle: Undo must not depend on a short timer. Keep it in the row, or keep the toast until someone acts on it, and never show a ticking seconds countdown.
principles.evidence: WCAG 2.2.1 (A) covers time limits set by content. They must be possible to turn off, extend to ten times the default, or extend after a 20-second warning, unless the real-time, essential or 20-hour exception applies. The Understanding doc says transient messages are exempt only when the same thing can be reached another way. Apple HIG: controls that auto-dismiss on a timer 'can be problematic for people who need longer', so prefer dismissal by an explicit action. Flutter's Material SnackBar docs: a snackbar with an action 'will not time out when TalkBack or VoiceOver are enabled'. NN/g: undo is better than a confirmation dialog for most destructive actions ('go to great lengths to provide undo'). NN/g also found older adults make more mistakes and have more trouble recovering from them.
principles.implication: Keep 'delete with Undo' rather than a confirm dialog, but make Undo last. Two ways: a collapsed inline row 'Removed · Undo' that stays until the user leaves the screen (the f1-your-places pattern), or a snackbar that stays while a screen reader is on, with a recovery path elsewhere (such as the roster re-offer in f3-household-block). No '(4s)' labels. Cooldowns like 'You can resend in 0:47' are announced once, not every second.

principles.principle: Follow Reduce Motion (and prefers-reduced-motion on web): remove decorative motion, and turn meaningful motion into a fade or highlight.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG: when Reduce Motion is on, reduce 'automatic and repetitive animations, including zooming, scaling, and peripheral motion', replace x, y and z transitions with fades, and avoid animated blur. Apple's Reduced Motion criteria: if motion carries meaning, replace it with a dissolve, highlight fade or colour shift, and remove decorative motion entirely. Stop auto-advancing or ongoing motion. WCAG 2.2.2 (A) requires a way to pause auto-updating content. 2.3.3 (AAA) covers animation triggered by interaction. The repo's own mailbox audit flags that animate-pulse and animate-spin don't respect prefers-reduced-motion.
principles.implication: Loading skeletons are static under Reduce Motion (no shimmer). Deep-link landings (air band, strip row highlight) jump instantly and fade a highlight instead of scrolling or pulsing. Keeper poses change without idle loops. Ring and progress fills appear without sweeping. Sheet transitions become cross-fades. Live countdowns stop updating visibly.

principles.principle: Keyboard focus is always visible and never hidden by sticky bars, footers, banners or the software keyboard, and 'selected' looks different from 'focused'.
principles.evidence: WCAG 2.4.7 (AA) requires a visible focus indicator. 2.4.11 (AA, new in 2.2) says a focused component must not be entirely hidden by author content; sticky headers and footers and non-modal dialogs are the named failures, and scroll-padding is the named fix. 2.4.13 (AAA) asks for an indicator at least as large as a 2px perimeter with 3:1 change. Apple's VoiceOver criteria and Full Keyboard Access expect keyboard operability.
principles.implication: Sticky elements ('Finish day · 9 left', the WallBar, pinned permission banners, the pinned photo pane) reserve scroll padding equal to their height, so the last focused row scrolls clear. The focus ring (2px border.focus with a 2px offset) is never used as the selection style. Selected tiles need a second cue, such as a filled radio dot or a bold label with a 'Selected' state. OCR highlight rectangles on photos use a two-tone outline (dark plus white) so they reach 3:1 on any image.

principles.principle: Forms and sign-in: never ask for something twice in one process, never require transcribing a code, and keep help in the same place.
principles.evidence: WCAG 3.3.7 (A): information entered earlier in the same process is auto-filled or offered for selection; the exceptions are essential, security and no-longer-valid. 3.3.8 (AA): no cognitive function test (memorising, transcribing) in authentication. Email-link sign-in is a sufficient technique (G218). Paste and password managers must work. 3.2.6 (A): help mechanisms appear in the same relative order across a set of web pages; this is web-only, but it is a sound consistency rule for native. NN/g found older adults are frustrated by interfaces that reject alternative input formats.
principles.implication: Keep the magic-link email verification. Any code field accepts paste and one-time-code autofill, and is never split into boxes that block paste. The 'draft expired' address field is pre-filled if this device still knows the address. Bill mode in the Date sheet and the extraction confirm screen pre-fill every value read from a photo. The invite email field uses email autocomplete. 'This isn't right' always sits at the foot of the provenance sheet, and any Help or Contact entry sits in the same slot on every settings page.

principles.principle: Use plain language: 6th-to-8th-grade reading level, sentence case, buttons that start with a verb, links that make sense alone, and acronyms spelled out once.
principles.evidence: NN/g recommends 6th–8th grade for general audiences and 10th–12th for experts, and never above 12th: experts also prefer plain, scannable text. GOV.UK: sentence case everywhere except proper nouns; 'even specialist users prefer clear language'; link text must make sense in isolation for screen-reader users. GOV.UK button guidance: 'Write button text in sentence case, describing the action it performs'. Apple HIG Writing: 'When labeling buttons and links, it's almost always best to use a verb'; avoid 'Click here'; put errors next to the field and say how to fix them; skip 'oops'. NN/g: icon labels 'should be visible at all times'.
principles.implication: Plain value first, then the authority code: 'Minimal flood risk (FEMA Zone X)'. Spell out 'air quality index (AQI)' and 'fine particles (PM2.5)' once per surface, and always in spoken labels. Button labels are verb phrases ('Confirm Tuesday', 'Change pickup day', 'Add a date', 'Send invite'). Outbound links name their destination ('Order a free radon kit from WA Dept of Health'). Every kind glyph, tile and icon has a visible text label. Error text says what to do ('Pick a date after today').

principles.principle: Design for movers aged 25 to 70: large readable type, big well-spaced controls, every icon labelled, no hidden gestures, and error recovery that keeps what the person typed.
principles.evidence: NN/g studied 123 seniors aged 65 to 89 in six countries over 19 years and wrote 87 guidelines. Recurring problems: small fonts, tiny targets, poor contrast (especially on mobile), inflexible inputs, and error messages that are unclear or easy to miss. Older adults make more errors and struggle to recover. NN/g cites web usability ability declining about 0.8% per year between ages 25 and 60. Today's older users are more confident than 2001 cohorts, so design for capability, not incapacity. A 2025 systematic review of 132 studies (Aging Clinical and Experimental Research) repeatedly cites larger fonts, high contrast, bigger targets, error-tolerant interfaces and simple linear navigation, but gives no numeric thresholds.
principles.implication: Body text stays 16px/17pt/16sp with no body text below it. Captions are never below 12px on web or 11pt/11sp on native, and every caption carrying a source or provenance meets 4.5:1. Choices of five or fewer are radio rows or segments, not dropdowns. No sliders. Every error state keeps typed values (several prompts already require this). Test the pilot with at least a few participants over 60 running larger text.

principles.principle: Status changes are announced without moving focus. Progress is stated in words, not only drawn as a ring.
principles.evidence: WCAG 4.1.3 (AA): status messages must be programmatically determinable. Apple's VoiceOver criteria say temporary status banners and alerts should use AccessibilityNotification, and the cursor must not reset when content reloads. Android lists live regions and state descriptions among its semantics tools.
principles.implication: These are announced politely: 'Saved — Today now uses this address', 'Thanks — we'll check it', 'Uploading 2 of 3', 'Upload failed, Retry available', 'Synced 3 items from your other device'. Per-file progress rings carry text such as '2 of 3 uploaded, 40%'. Only real air or weather alerts use assertive or alert semantics. Routine banners do not.

principles.principle: Don't lock orientation, and don't let a pinned media pane take the screen when the keyboard is up or text is large.
principles.evidence: WCAG 1.3.4 (AA): content must not be restricted to one orientation unless that is essential. WCAG 1.4.10 exempts images such as maps and diagrams from reflow, but not the form fields around them. Apple HIG Typography: keep primary elements in view and reduce columns at large sizes.
principles.implication: In landscape, with the keyboard up, or at AX sizes, the extraction-confirm photo pane shrinks to a strip (for example 25% of height) showing the zoomed OCR region, or moves beside the fields. The field being edited must always stay visible. The capture tray and photo viewer work in landscape.

patterns.name: Value-first row with the category name and ordinal position in words
patterns.exemplars: The EPA AQI technical document requires the category descriptor (and colour, if used) for every AQI report, so the name, not the hue, carries the meaning. The AQI Hub guidance recommends combining accessible colours, icons, simple language and numbers. Pantopus's f8-scale-strips prompt already writes 'Moderate — 3 of 5' and 'Zone 1 — highest predicted'.
patterns.howToApply: Every scale row, band and chip prints the plain category name plus its position ('3 of 5', 'category 3 of 6', 'highest of 3 zones') in text next to the graphic. The graphic then covers the 1.4.11 text-label exception and works for colour-blind and screen-reader users unchanged. Spoken label order: layer, value, position, scale endpoints, authority, date, provenance.
patterns.pitfalls: Don't print only the code ('Zone AE', 'AQI 118') without the plain meaning. Don't print text on a coloured segment. Don't let the name ellipsise at narrow widths; wrap it or stack it above the track.

patterns.name: Chart plus summary sentence plus 'Show as list' table
patterns.exemplars: USWDS example charts carry a visually hidden table and a plain-text statement of the message. The W3C Complex Images tutorial pairs a short alt with a long description (bar-chart example). Swift Charts builds an accessibility tree and audio graphs automatically (WWDC21 10122).
patterns.howToApply: Each chart surface gets (1) a caption sentence stating the takeaway in words, (2) a 'Show amounts' / 'Show as list' disclosure or an adjacent list of the same facts, and (3) on iOS, Swift Charts or AXChartDescriptor so audio graphs work. On Android and web, the list is the accessible equivalent and the chart is marked as an image with a summary label.
patterns.pitfalls: The summary must not add a judgement the chart avoids: no 'higher than your neighbours', no percentages the prompt forbids. Months with no bill are listed as 'no bill', not dropped.

patterns.name: Adjustable day scrubber for dense strips
patterns.exemplars: Apple's accessibilityAdjustableAction lets a VoiceOver user swipe up or down to step a single element (Apple's example is a page control). Android's collectionInfo and collectionItemInfo give list and grid position.
patterns.howToApply: On native, the 14-day strip is one accessibility element. Swiping up or down steps through the days and reads the full weekday, date, item count and each item's title and provenance. Double-tap opens that day's rows. On web it is a list of 14 day buttons with full-date labels, or it is hidden from assistive technology when the rows below already list the same content.
patterns.pitfalls: Never let VoiceOver read 'T, T, S, S'. Don't make 14 separate 25pt tap targets on native.

patterns.name: One row, one element, with custom actions
patterns.exemplars: Android's CustomAccessibilityAction replaces swipe-to-dismiss with a named action ('Remove article from list'), and mergeDescendants groups metadata into one announcement. Apple's VoiceOver criteria ask for custom actions for grouped behaviours and long-press menus.
patterns.howToApply: Calendar rows, date rows, bill rows, Mail Day rows, member rows and fact rows each announce as one sentence. Their secondary actions (Edit, Remind me, Where this comes from, This isn't right, Undo, Resend, Retake) are custom actions and also visible controls.
patterns.pitfalls: Keep the merged description short. Don't also make inner children focusable, or TalkBack reads everything twice.

patterns.name: Inline, persistent undo
patterns.exemplars: f1-your-places already collapses a removed row to 'Removed … Undo'. Flutter's Material SnackBar with an action does not time out while TalkBack or VoiceOver is on. NN/g prefers undo to confirmation dialogs.
patterns.howToApply: After a delete or dismiss, replace the row in place with a one-line 'Removed · Undo' that stays until the user leaves the screen. Where a toast is used, it has an action and stays open while a screen reader is on, and the item is also recoverable elsewhere (for example 'Show again' in settings).
patterns.pitfalls: No seconds countdown. Don't use undo for a permanent photo deletion unless the deletion is really deferred; say exactly what survives, as the f10 prompts already require.

patterns.name: Stacked layout at accessibility sizes
patterns.exemplars: Apple's Larger Text criteria show a message header switching from horizontal (sender, receiver, date) to vertical. Apple HIG Typography says to reduce columns and stack text above secondary items at large sizes.
patterns.howToApply: Each prompt defines what stacks at AX sizes: label above value, value above source, the track below its text, two-column tile grids becoming one column, segmented controls becoming radio rows, and paired buttons becoming full-width stacked buttons (keeping equal weight).
patterns.pitfalls: Stacking must keep the reading order: primary fact first. Don't hide provenance to save space. Collapse it to a single 'Sources:' line, as f8-scale-strips already does at 320–360px.

patterns.name: Large Content Viewer for fixed-size chrome
patterns.exemplars: Apple's Larger Text criteria: tab bars don't grow with Dynamic Type, and the Large Content Viewer covers them.
patterns.howToApply: The four-tab bar (Place, Today, Nearby, Mail) keeps its size and shows a large preview of icon and label on long-press at accessibility sizes. Tab labels are always visible, never icon-only.
patterns.pitfalls: Don't ship a tab bar that scales and pushes content off-screen, and don't shorten tab labels to icons.

patterns.name: Visible close plus system back on every sheet
patterns.exemplars: NN/g bottom-sheet guidelines: a visible Close button, support for the device Back button, no stacked sheets; a grab handle alone is not enough.
patterns.howToApply: Every sheet in the pack (date, provenance, add place, compare, widget how-to, verify address, owner attestation, naming, notification primer, capture tray) draws a labelled Close or Done in the header or footer. It closes with Android Back, web Escape and the VoiceOver escape gesture, and returns focus to the control that opened it.
patterns.pitfalls: The provenance sheet opens from the date sheet and other sheets: replace the sheet's content with a back button instead of stacking a second sheet.

patterns.name: Zoom buttons for document and map viewers
patterns.exemplars: WCAG 2.5.1's example: map pinch-zoom paired with +/- buttons. WCAG 2.5.7: map arrow buttons as an alternative to drag-panning.
patterns.howToApply: The mail-piece viewer gets zoom-in, zoom-out and fit buttons, or double-tap cycles 1x, 2x, 4x. The cells map and privacy-mirror map get +/- buttons and a 'List cells' alternative. Chrome stays visible while assistive technology is running.
patterns.pitfalls: Auto-hiding chrome on the first tap strands VoiceOver users, because a single tap only moves focus under VoiceOver.

patterns.name: ColorVision Assist AQI palette with ink separators and a halo marker
patterns.exemplars: EPA's May 2026 technical document, Table 3 (ColorVision Assist). South Coast AQMD tested it against eight colour-impairment types, and EPA's Fire and Smoke Map pilots it.
patterns.howToApply: Replace the six standard hues with the Table 3 values as the single sanctioned exception to the token rule. Add at least 3:1 separators and a keyline, a two-tone marker, and the band name printed off the fill. Verify in greyscale and in dark mode.
patterns.pitfalls: The new hues still have low contrast between neighbours (1.26 to 1.71:1), so the separators are not optional. In dark mode, maroon and purple segments nearly vanish without a keyline.

patterns.name: Provenance marks built for accented and vibrant widget rendering
patterns.exemplars: Apple HIG Widgets: accented mode tints content to one colour and vibrant mode depends on brightness, so shapes and luminance must carry the meaning; group elements with widgetAccentable.
patterns.howToApply: Filled, hollow and tick are distinct in silhouette (a solid disc, a ring, and a disc with a knocked-out tick), not in hue. The tick is cut out of the disc so it survives one-colour tinting. The f7 prompt's frames 18–19 test exactly this and should run at the smallest real size.
patterns.pitfalls: A tick drawn in a second colour on top of the disc disappears in accented mode.

patterns.name: Paste-friendly, link-first verification
patterns.exemplars: WCAG 3.3.8 lists email-link authentication as a sufficient technique (G218) and requires allowing paste and password managers.
patterns.howToApply: Keep the magic-link flow on f1-email-verify-handoff. Any fallback code field is a single input with one-time-code autofill and paste allowed. Resend cooldowns are text announced once.
patterns.pitfalls: Six separate digit boxes that block paste, and CAPTCHAs that require transcription, fail 3.3.8.

patterns.name: Greyscale and AX5 gate in every prompt
patterns.exemplars: Apple's Differentiate Without Color criteria use a Grayscale filter test. Apple's Larger Text criteria ask for testing at the largest accessibility sizes. Android 14 guidance asks for testing at 200%.
patterns.howToApply: Add two standard frames to every STATES list: 'AX5 / 200% text' and 'greyscale plus Increase Contrast (dark)'. Designers check that every state is still readable and nothing meaningful truncates.
patterns.pitfalls: Checking only the default size in light mode, which is how the current 59 prompts are written.

patterns.name: og:image:alt for the share card
patterns.exemplars: The Open Graph protocol: 'If the page specifies an og:image it should specify og:image:alt', as 'a description of what is in the image (not a caption)'.
patterns.howToApply: The /api/og/place compare route emits og:image:alt describing the four readings in words ('Camas, WA: flood minimal (FEMA Zone X); wildfire moderate, 3 of 5; air good, AQI 42 today; radon zone 1, highest, not yet confirmed. Yours?'), without the address.
patterns.pitfalls: Alt text must follow the same privacy rules as the card: no street address and no sender surname.

antipatterns: text.muted (#9CA3AF, 2.54:1 on white) for any text a person needs to read: source captions, 'Not set', contrast clauses, reasons for disabled controls. It fails WCAG 1.4.3 for everyone with low vision.
White labels on primary.DEFAULT (#0284c7, 4.10:1) at 14–16px. This is today's web filled button, and it fails 4.5:1. Use primary.700 (5.93:1).
Warning, success or info hue as text colour on their tinted backgrounds (3.07 to 3.84:1). Put the hue on the glyph and the words in text.primary.
Hairline border tokens (1.24 to 1.47:1) as the only boundary of a scale band, an empty ring segment, a hollow mark or an input. That fails WCAG 1.4.11.

Encoding a category only by hue: strip dots by class, map cells by a 4-step light-blue ramp with adjacent steps at 1.16 to 1.66:1, stale versus fresh only by greying. It fails WCAG 1.4.1 and Apple's greyscale test.

Reusing filled against hollow/ringed for anything other than provenance, such as sender vs you or taken vs open slots. Shape is the only channel colour-blind users have, and overloading it makes 'hollow' ambiguous.
Standard EPA yellow (#FFFF00, 1.07:1 on white) with no keyline, or labels printed on AQI fills. Neighbouring bands are under 1.7:1 in both EPA palettes.
A tap target that is just an 8–16px mark, or 14 separate 25pt day cells. That is below Apple's 44pt, Android's 48dp and NN/g's 1cm.

'Must fit the detent without scrolling' or 'all tiles visible without scrolling' rules with no Dynamic Type exception. At AX5 (53pt body) that forces truncation or clipping, which Apple's Larger Text criteria reject.
Weekday initials at a pitch under 11pt in a widget. Apple sets 11pt as the widget text minimum.
Undo with a seconds countdown ('Undo (4s)') as the only recovery. It fails WCAG 2.2.1's intent, and Apple advises against timer-dismissed controls.
Actions available only by long-press, hover, pinch or drag (Retake, 4x zoom, map pan). WCAG 2.5.1 and 2.5.7 and Apple HIG require a visible single-tap alternative.
Chrome that auto-hides on first tap in a viewer. Under VoiceOver a tap only moves focus, so the controls vanish from reach.
Sticky footers or bars drawn overlapping the last rows without scroll padding. That is the named failure in WCAG 2.4.11.
The keyboard focus ring reused as the selection style. Focused and selected become indistinguishable for keyboard and switch users.
Moving focus automatically when a choice is made (auto-focusing a text field on tile pick). WCAG 3.2.2 treats a focus change on input as a change of context, and it throws screen-reader users.

Charts with no text summary and no list or table of the same values (bill trend, year band, sparkline). They fail WCAG 1.1.1, and Apple HIG says a headline 'doesn't take the place of accessibility labels'.
Looping or shimmer animation that ignores Reduce Motion or prefers-reduced-motion (skeletons, keeper idle poses, sweeping ring fills).
Segmented controls with three or more long labels ('Very unhealthy (201+)') that cannot wrap at 200% text. Use radio rows.
Button labels that aren't verbs, or that depend on surrounding context. Apple HIG and GOV.UK both call for action verbs in sentence case.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The token list has no accessibility constraints. text.muted #9CA3AF is offered as a text colour, primary.DEFAULT #0284c7 is the brand action colour (web buttons are bg-primary-600 with white text), and semantic hues are listed as text colours. No prompt's STATES list includes a large-text, greyscale or screen-reader frame, and neither the house style nor the design doc mentions Dynamic Type, touch targets, contrast or VoiceOver.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11, Apple HIG and Android all require 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for meaningful graphics. Computed: text.muted 2.54, primary.DEFAULT and white-on-primary 4.10, warning 3.19 (3.07 on warningBg), success 3.77, info on infoBg 3.84, error on errorBg 4.41, text.secondary on sunken 4.39, border tokens 1.24 to 1.47. Apple's Larger Text criteria ask for testing up to the largest sizes (AX5 body 53pt), and Android 14 asks for testing at 200%.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add an ACCESSIBILITY block to the house style. (1) Text is at least 4.5:1 and meaningful graphics at least 3:1, in light, dark and Increase Contrast. text.muted is never used for readable text. Filled buttons and inline links use primary.700 (dark mode links use #38BDF8). Semantic tints carry text in text.primary with the hue only on the glyph. (2) Targets are 44pt iOS, 48dp Android with 8dp gaps, and 44 CSS px on web; a mark is never a target by itself. (3) Every prompt adds an AX5/200% frame and a greyscale frame. Pairs stack, meaningful text wraps, and sheets may scroll. (4) Nothing relies on colour alone, and filled/hollow means provenance only. (5) Every chart has a summary sentence, spoken labels and a list or table. (6) No gesture-only or hover-only action, and every sheet has a visible Close. (7) No timed-only undo and no seconds countdowns. (8) Reduce Motion turns movement into fades. (9) Plain language at grades 6–8, sentence case, verb-led buttons, acronyms expanded. (10) Focus is visible and never under sticky UI, and selection looks different from focus.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The contrast line is set at 13/18 or 12/16 in text.muted, and clause one ('Nextdoor is what your neighbors say.') is at weight 400 in text.muted.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: text.muted on white is 2.54:1, well below WCAG 1.4.3's 4.5:1 for small text. NN/g's older-adult research names low-contrast small text as a persistent barrier.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Set clause one in text.secondary (4.83:1) at weight 400 and clause two in text.strong at 500–600. The weight difference still carries the contrast, and the line stays a caption. On mobile, use at least 13px.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: When the move-in date is unset, the value reads 'Not set' in text.muted.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: 2.54:1 fails WCAG 1.4.3. 'Not set' is information: it is the gate for the whole mover experience.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Write 'Not set' in text.secondary (or text.strong on a sunken row) and keep the helper line. Show emptiness with the words, not with faint colour.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Past-month columns are filled primary.200 and only the current month is labelled ('$142'). The y-axis has only $0 and $200. There is a 1px reference line. No text summary or table is specified.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: primary.200 on white is 1.33:1, and the unlabelled column heights are the information, so WCAG 1.4.11's 3:1 applies (the text-label exception does not). The W3C complex-images tutorial, USWDS and Apple HIG all require a text alternative and a way to read the values.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Either fill past columns with primary.600 (4.10:1) and mark the current month with its printed value plus the tick mark plus a heavier outline, or keep light fills with a 1px primary.800 outline (7.56:1). Add a caption summary (range, current month, nearby average) and a 'Show amounts' list of 12 rows with full month names, including 'no bill' months. On iOS, use Swift Charts so audio graphs work.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Segments use neutral surface tokens divided by hairline borders. The occupied band gets a raised fill and a strong border, and the marker is the only saturated element.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: surface.raised against base is 1.05:1, border.strong 1.47:1 and border.default 1.24:1. The number and position of bands, which is the point of the instrument, is therefore invisible to low-vision users (WCAG 1.4.11). The occupied band is covered only because its name is printed.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep neutral tracks with no colour ramp, but draw band dividers and the track keyline in ink of at least 3:1 (text.secondary-level). Show the occupied band with the marker plus the printed band name plus an outline of at least 3:1, not a raised fill. Make each row one accessible element that speaks value, 'n of N', scale endpoints, authority, date and provenance. Add an AX5 frame with the text above a full-width track.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The six-band bar uses 'the EPA colours users already recognise' (the standard palette) as the one sanctioned exception to the token rule.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: EPA's May 2026 technical document says the standard colours 'can be difficult to discern', especially red and green, and permits the ColorVision Assist palette (Table 3). Computed: standard yellow 1.07:1 on white, green/yellow 1.62, orange/red 1.57. In dark mode, maroon is 1.62:1 on #0F172A.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Name the ColorVision Assist RGB values in the exception. Add at least 3:1 separators between segments and a keyline. Draw a two-tone halo marker. Keep the band name printed in text.primary beside the marker, never on the fill. Label the top band '301+'. Give the whole band a spoken label with index, category and 'n of 6', and add an AX5 frame.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: One dot per event is 'coloured by class — pickup / civic / money / yours', using the 8px marks from the provenance sheet. The 14 cells span the card width with M T W T F S S initials. Weekend cells are tinted, and a reminder push highlights a row.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Class is carried by hue alone inside the strip (WCAG 1.4.1, Apple's greyscale test). The dot shape is already taken by provenance. 14 cells on a 393pt screen are about 25pt wide, below 44pt/48dp. The weekend tint (sunken vs base) is 1.10:1. Bare initials are ambiguous to screen readers.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Drop class colour from the strip (one ink), or add a second cue such as a tiny glyph at 12pt or more. Rely on the glyph list rows for class. Make the strip one adjustable accessibility element on native, and a full-date list on web. Don't make 14 separate small targets. Draw marks at about 12pt or more, and spell out full dates in spoken labels. Add AX5 and greyscale frames.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The specimen frame requires the three shapes to survive 'an 8px dot inside a 14-day strip cell' and a monochrome widget glyph. Users reach the sheet 'by tapping a data mark'. No spoken names or minimum stroke are defined.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Marks must reach 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) and need text equivalents (1.1.1, Apple's VoiceOver criteria). Targets need 44pt/48dp (or 24 CSS px at minimum). Apple's widget rendering modes remove hue. I found no authoritative symbol-size minimum; the ~12pt floor is a design judgement, since a tick at 8px is one or two device pixels.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Specify a minimum size of about 12pt/12dp, strokes of at least 1.5px in ink of at least 3:1, a tick knocked out of the disc, and spoken names ('official', 'on record, not confirmed', 'you added this'). State that the row or cell containing a mark is the 44pt/48dp target. Add a specimen at AX5 and in accented widget rendering.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The medium widget's 14-day strip has '14 equal cells, ~6pt each, ~120pt wide' with a weekday initial under each, plus an AQI micro band-bar. The large widget has a 12-month, four-lane year strip. The 19 frames include no large-text frame and no spoken-label spec.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG Widgets: text at 11pt or larger, and widgets support Dynamic Type from Large to AX5. About 8.6pt per cell cannot hold 11pt initials. A tick inside a 6pt dot won't survive accented or vibrant rendering. Text must not be rasterised, and it must be speakable.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Label only the strip's anchor days, or widen the strip. Draw marks at their minimum size or put the provenance words in the hero line. Add AX-size frames for all three sizes in which the strip, band bar and lanes drop out and the hero line, place label and air reading remain as wrapping text. Define one combined VoiceOver/TalkBack label per widget. Use ColorVision Assist AQI hues with separators.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Do not let the sheet scroll or grow past the medium detent.' The true-size preview takes about the top 45% and the three steps fit beneath it with no scrolling.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple's Larger Text criteria: support 200% or more and avoid truncation. HIG Typography: stack and let text use as many lines as needed. Three steps of AX5 text (53pt body) cannot fit under a 170pt preview in about 430pt.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep 'no scroll' at default sizes only. At accessibility sizes, allow the sheet to reach the large detent and scroll, keep the steps above the fold before the preview if needed, keep Done pinned with scroll padding, and give the step illustrations text labels.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Ten glyph tiles, all visible without scrolling' in a two-column grid, above a native date control, a four-segment 'Remind me' control and the footer.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: At AX5 (53pt) or Android 200%, ten labelled tiles plus a date control cannot all fit in one sheet viewport. Apple says to reduce columns and avoid truncation at large sizes.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the one-tap tile grid at default sizes. At AX sizes, switch to a one-column list of kinds and allow scrolling. Let the four-segment 'Remind me' control wrap to a 2×2 grid or radio rows. Keep the reminder date printed in words ('Mon 30 Nov 2026') as well as the leader line.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Delete immediately with an Undo toast; do not use a destructive confirm dialog.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g supports undo over confirmation. But WCAG 2.2.1 treats a timed-only way to undo as a time limit unless there is another way to recover. Apple HIG says auto-dismissing controls are hard for people who need more time. Material/Flutter action snackbars don't time out with TalkBack or VoiceOver on.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep delete-with-undo. Make Undo persist, either as an inline 'Removed · Undo' row on the calling surface or as a toast that stays until acted on while a screen reader runs. Announce the deletion as a status message.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: A native date control that must accept dates about 2 years out; on iOS it is described as the native inline date control.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g date-input guidance: calendar pickers suit dates within about a year. For far-off dates, typing is faster, and scrolling pickers are problematic on mobile. NN/g's older-adult research records frustration when typed input isn't allowed.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use a control that jumps straight to a month and year (iOS compact style with the month/year selector, M3 picker with keyboard input mode on Android, a typed date field on web), and accept typed dates in several formats. Keep the spelled-out date and weekday next to the field.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Reviewed rows show 'Comcast · Recycled · Undo (4s)' with a live countdown. A sticky footer 'Finish day · 9 left' overlaps the last rows. Unconfirmed rows use an amber (warningBg) state.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: A 4-second undo is a short time limit (WCAG 2.2.1), and a ticking countdown is auto-updating content (2.2.2). Sticky footers covering focused rows are the named failure in 2.4.11. Warning-hue text on warningBg is 3.07:1.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep per-item Undo in the collapsed 'Reviewed today' rows until the day is finished, with no seconds label (a static 'Undo' is enough). Add scroll padding equal to the footer height. Use text.primary for any words on warningBg, and leave amber and the hollow mark to the glyph and border.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: On a phone, the photo is a pinned pane of about 42% of the viewport that 'never scrolls away', and 'Do not collapse the photo behind a tap-to-expand.' Tapping a field outlines its OCR region with a 2px focus-border rectangle.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: With the keyboard up (about 40% of height), at 200% or AX text, or in landscape (WCAG 1.3.4), a fixed 42% pane leaves almost no room, so the focused field is hidden (2.4.11) and the form fails to reflow (1.4.10; the image exception doesn't cover the form). A single-colour focus-blue outline (#0284c7) has no guaranteed 3:1 against arbitrary photo content.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep photo beside fields, but let the pane shrink automatically (for example to about 25%, showing the zoomed OCR region) when the keyboard is up, text is at AX sizes, or the phone is landscape. In landscape, move the pane to the side. Draw the OCR highlight as a two-tone (dark plus white) outline. Add an AX5 frame.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: '1x fit, double-tap to 2x, pinch to 4x.' The header and bottom panel auto-hide on the first zoom or tap and return on a single tap.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 2.5.1 (A): pinch-only 4x needs a single-pointer alternative (the map +/- example). Under VoiceOver or TalkBack a single tap moves focus rather than activating, so auto-hidden chrome, including 'Delete this photo', becomes unreachable. Apple HIG says to offer onscreen alternatives to gestures.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add zoom buttons, or make double-tap cycle 1x, 2x, 4x. Never auto-hide chrome while a screen reader, Switch Control or Full Keyboard Access is running, and keep the chrome in the accessibility tree with its own 'Show controls' action.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Each thumbnail has 'its own small delete control and a "Retake" affordance on long-press/hover'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Hover and long-press-only actions are hidden and fail gesture-alternative guidance (Apple HIG; WCAG 2.5.1 intent; 1.4.13 for hover content). Small delete controls on 56px thumbnails fall below 44pt/48dp.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Show Retake and Delete as visible labelled controls (for example in a selected-thumbnail action row) with 44pt/48dp targets. Expose them as custom actions on each thumbnail, and give each progress ring a text value.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Cells are shaded on a 4-step ramp (primary.100/200/300/500) for posts-in-30-days buckets, with a legend. The map is the primary navigation and has no list alternative.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Adjacent ramp steps are 1.16, 1.26 and 1.66:1, and primary.100 against white is 1.15:1. The bucket is conveyed only by lightness, which fails WCAG 1.4.11 and 1.4.1. The map needs drag and pinch alternatives (2.5.1, 2.5.7).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Print the bucket label in each cell ('0', '1–5', '6–15', '16+'), or add a pattern or density-dot texture. Add +/- and pan buttons and a 'List cells' view that shows cell name, bucket and lock state. Give the sparkline a text summary.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The fact-count ring has 36pt with 3px stroke. Known segments are primary.600, and unknown segments are a 'border.strong hairline outline'. Segment order is fixed clockwise, with no labels. The unnamed state uses a silhouette in text.muted, and the ring is the tap target.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: border.strong on white is 1.47:1, so 'nothing known' segments are invisible to low-vision users (WCAG 1.4.11). Which categories are known exists nowhere else as text. A text.muted silhouette is 2.54:1. A 36pt target is below 44pt/48dp.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw empty segments as outlines of at least 3:1. Give the ring a spoken label listing the known and missing categories. Make the whole right side at least 44pt/48dp. Use text.secondary for the unnamed silhouette. Keep mood-by-pose, which is good for colour-blind users, since the mood line is already text.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Each shared track carries 'the sender's mark FILLED, the recipient's mark RINGED and labelled "You"'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: x-provenance-sheet makes filled against hollow the product-wide provenance encoding ('no exceptions'). For colour-blind and low-vision users shape is the only channel, so a ringed 'You' reads as 'unconfirmed', and a sender's unconfirmed radon reading has no way to show both meanings (WCAG 1.4.1, Apple's greyscale test).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Identify sender and you by label and placement (for example a pointer above the track labelled with the sender's first name and one below labelled 'You'), with the same neutral marker form. Show provenance with the standard mark beside each value's text. The merged same-band case reads 'Both: …' in words.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The air-alert threshold is a three-segment control: 'Sensitive groups (101+)' / 'Unhealthy (151+)' / 'Very unhealthy (201+)'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Segmented controls don't wrap. At AX sizes or 200% these labels truncate, and Apple's Larger Text criteria reject unreadable truncation. NN/g's seniors research reports trouble with compact controls on touch.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use three radio rows, each with its full label and a one-line meaning, at all sizes or at least at AX sizes. Keep helper text under each master switch as specified.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The date chip uses 'info tokens above 14 days, warning tokens at 14 or fewer'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Warning text on warningBg is 3.07:1 and info on infoBg is 3.84:1, both below 4.5:1 for chip-size text (WCAG 1.4.3). Urgency by hue alone is covered only because the day count is printed.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the tint change, but set chip text in text.primary and put the semantic hue on the calendar glyph and chip border (3:1 or more). Keep '9 days' always printed.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The paired equal-weight actions are labelled 'That's my day' and 'Not my schedule'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG Writing: 'it's almost always best to use a verb' on buttons. GOV.UK: button text describes the action. The current labels are statements whose effect (confirming the rule, or opening the Date sheet) is only implied. For screen-reader users reading buttons out of context, the purpose is unclear. This is a moderate conflict, since answer-style labels are defensible.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the equal weight. Either change the visible labels to verb phrases ('Yes, Tuesday is right' / 'Change pickup day'), or keep the current wording and give verb-led accessibility labels ('Confirm Tuesday pickup' / 'Change pickup day, opens date sheet').

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Tile selection is a '2px border.focus ring plus a primary.50 fill', with no checkmark. The name field 'takes focus automatically once a species is picked'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Using the focus colour and ring for selection makes focused and selected look the same for keyboard and switch users (WCAG 2.4.7). primary.50 against white adds almost no contrast. Moving focus when a choice is made is a change of context under WCAG 3.2.2, and it disorients screen-reader users as the keyboard covers the tiles.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use a selection cue distinct from focus that isn't a completion tick (for example a filled radio dot plus a bold label, exposed as the 'selected' trait) and keep the focus ring offset. Don't move focus automatically. Place the field directly below and let the user tap it, or move focus only when no screen reader is running.

numbers: Text contrast is at least 4.5:1. Large text is at least 3:1, where large means 24px regular or 18.66px (14pt) bold (WCAG 1.4.3). Android: 4.5:1 below 18sp, or below 14sp bold.
Meaningful graphics, UI component borders and state indicators are at least 3:1 against adjacent colours (WCAG 1.4.11).

Computed on white: text.primary 17.7 (not computed here, but well above AA), text.strong #374151 10.31, text.secondary #6B7280 4.83, text.muted #9CA3AF 2.54 (fail), primary.DEFAULT/600 #0284c7 4.10 (fail for text), primary.700 #0369a1 5.93, primary.800 7.56, primary.500 2.77, primary.200 1.33, border.default 1.24, border.strong 1.47, surface.raised 1.05, surface.sunken 1.10.

Computed semantic ratios: warning #D97706 3.19 on white and 3.07 on warningBg. success #059669 3.77, and 3.60 on successBg. info on infoBg 3.84. error on errorBg 4.41. White on primary.DEFAULT (web filled button) 4.10 (fail). White on primary.700 5.93.
Computed dark mode (base #0F172A): text.secondary #94A3B8 6.96, focus #38BDF8 8.33, primary.DEFAULT 4.36 (fail for text), primary.700 3.01. border.default #1F2937 against raised #1E293B 1.00.

EPA AQI standard RGB: Green 0,228,0 · Yellow 255,255,0 · Orange 255,126,0 · Red 255,0,0 · Purple 143,63,151 · Maroon 126,0,35. ColorVision Assist RGB: Green 158,255,145 · Yellow 255,201,5 · Orange 255,130,5 · Red 240,34,0 · Purple 137,9,151 · Maroon 100,0,21 (EPA-403/B-26-003, May 2026).
AQI categories: 0–50 Good, 51–100 Moderate, 101–150 Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, 151–200 Unhealthy, 201–300 Very Unhealthy, 301+ Hazardous (values above 500 are still Hazardous).

Computed AQI contrast: standard yellow 1.07:1 on white, green 1.74:1. Adjacent green/yellow 1.62, orange/red 1.57, purple/maroon 1.74. ColorVision Assist adjacent pairs 1.26 to 1.71. Maroon on dark base 1.62 (ColorVision Assist maroon 1.32). White text on EPA orange 2.55.

Touch targets: iOS 44×44pt default (28×28pt minimum). Android 48×48dp (about 9mm) with 8dp spacing. WCAG 2.5.8 AA 24×24 CSS px, or 24px-diameter non-overlapping circles. WCAG 2.5.5 AAA 44×44. NN/g at least 1×1cm; fingertips 1.6–2cm, thumb contact about 2.5cm.
Apple padding: about 12pt around controls with a bezel, about 24pt around controls without one.

iOS text: default body 17pt, custom-type minimum 11pt, captions 12pt and 11pt. Dynamic Type body: AX1 28pt, AX2 33pt, AX3 40pt, AX4 47pt, AX5 53pt (62pt leading). AX3 is above 200%, and AX5 body is above 300%.
Widgets: text at least 11pt, Dynamic Type Large to AX5, 16pt standard margins (11pt tight), update animation up to 2 seconds.
Android 14+: font scale up to 200% on a nonlinear curve. Use sp for text size and lineHeight, never sp for padding.

Web: text resizable to 200% (1.4.4). Reflow at 320 CSS px width, equal to 1280px at 400% zoom, or 256 CSS px height (1.4.10). Text-spacing overrides: line-height 1.5×, paragraph spacing 2×, letter spacing 0.12×, word spacing 0.16× (1.4.12).
Focus appearance (AAA 2.4.13): indicator area at least a 2 CSS px perimeter, with 3:1 change between focused and unfocused states.

Timing (2.2.1): a user must be able to turn off a limit, adjust it to at least 10× the default, or extend it after a 20-second warning. The only exemptions are real-time, essential and over-20-hour limits.
Colour vision deficiency: about 1 in 12 men (NEI), most often red-green.
Reading level: grades 6–8 for general audiences, 10–12 for experts, never above 12 (NN/g).
NN/g seniors research: 123 participants aged 65–89, six countries, 87 guidelines. Web usability ability declines about 0.8% per year between ages 25 and 60.
Systematic review of age-friendly mobile design: 132 studies (2014–2025), with no numeric thresholds agreed (Aging Clinical and Experimental Research, Aug 2025).
NN/g date input: calendar pickers suit dates within about 1 year. For dates further out (Pantopus needs about 24 months), typed entry is faster.
Chartability: 50 heuristics, with a 14-test short list that takes 20–40 minutes.

Pantopus-specific geometry: 14 day cells across 361pt of content width are about 25.8pt each, which passes WCAG 24px but fails 44pt/48dp. The widget strip at about 120pt / 14 is about 8.6pt per cell, below the 11pt text minimum. The keeper ring at 36pt is below 44pt.

Proposed minimum drawn size for a provenance mark that must be told apart from the others: about 12pt/12dp with a stroke of at least 1.5px. This is a design judgement; I found no authoritative standard.

topic: claude-design-prompting: how to prompt Claude Design (claude.ai/design) and other AI UI generators so 59 separate prompts produce high-fidelity, consistent multi-screen output for Pantopus

principles.principle: Load the design system through Claude Design's own design-system feature, and do it before sending any of the 59 prompts. Do not rely on a prompt line telling the model to 'open' other projects by share link.
principles.evidence: From the official Anthropic docs. The launch post (Apr 17 2026, research preview, Opus 4.7) says Claude builds a design system 'by reading your codebase and design files', teams can 'maintain more than one', and 'Every project after that uses your colors, typography, and components automatically.' The setup article says that once the 'Published' toggle is on, 'any projects created from the Claude Design homescreen while in your organization will use your design system instead of the default'. You change the system later with Open > Remix. The same article says to 'Include real examples, not just specs. A finished landing page ... tells Claude more about your brand's feel than a color palette alone.' The product page says 'Admins can lock a team to a single approved design system.' When asked directly, the Get-started article had no text about opening or referencing another Claude Design project by share link or as a 'linked project' (answer: NOT PRESENT). Linking a codebase is documented ('Link a code repository so Claude understands your existing components...'; '/design-sync' in Claude Code). An Anthropic designer (Ryan Mather, Apr 17 2026) gave this as tip 1: 'Set up your design system and your core screens. An hour of setup and refinement here is worth it.'
principles.implication: Step 0 of the pack: build one design system called 'Pantopus'. Feed it the token source files, the two existing projects exported as HTML, and screenshots of the core existing screens (Today, Place, Nearby, Mail, a sheet, a settings list). Then publish it and set it as the default. Test it with 2 or 3 throwaway prompts. Create every surface project from the homescreen so it inherits the system. In house-style-v1, replace 'open these two projects' with 'This project uses the published Pantopus design system. Attached are screenshots of the host screen(s).' Keep the share links as a human reference only. Whether Claude Design can read another project from its URL is unverified.
principles.strength: strong for the mechanism (official docs); moderate for 'share-link opening is unreliable' (the docs are silent on it, not negative)

principles.principle: Replace mood adjectives with concrete visual specs, and name the typeface. Claude models have a persistent default house style, and vague or negative style words move the output to another fixed default rather than to your brand.
principles.evidence: Anthropic's Opus 4.8 prompting guide describes 'a consistent default house style: warm cream/off-white backgrounds (~#F4F1EA), serif display type (Georgia, Fraunces, Playfair), italic word-accents, and a terracotta/amber accent'. It says this 'will feel off for dashboards ... fintech, healthcare, or enterprise apps' and that 'This default is persistent. Generic instructions ... tend to shift the model to a different fixed palette.' The fix it gives: 'Specify a concrete alternative. The model follows explicit specs precisely' (radius, palette hexes, type character, section structure). Anthropic's frontend-design skill lists the same cluster ('Warm cream + serif + terracotta') and a 'SaaS card kit' cluster ('identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything') as tells of AI-generated design. Claude Design launched on Opus 4.7. I could not verify which model it runs on today.
principles.implication: In house-style-v1, 'DESIGN DIRECTION: clean, trustworthy, warm' is the only style guidance that isn't a token, and 'warm' is the word most likely to trigger the cream, serif and terracotta default. Rewrite it as specs: 'Backgrounds are surface.app / surface.base only, never cream or tinted paper. One sans-serif family (name the one the codebase ships) at the listed scale. No serif display type, no italic accents. Warmth comes from copy voice and from primary.50 tints on selected states, not from background colour.' Also add the corner radius, card elevation and spacing unit the codebase uses (none of these are in house-style-v1 today).
principles.strength: strong (official model guidance), with the caveat that Claude Design's current model is unverified

principles.principle: Put the whole specification in one message, but ask for a bounded batch of frames per turn: the dense default and the layout-changing states first, then the remaining states, then platform variants, then dark mode.
principles.evidence: On scope: Figma's Make guide quotes a designer, 'The smaller the scope, the more detailed the LLM can be' (Figma blog, Jun 10 2025). Figma help says 'Focus on layout first, then add functionality through follow-up prompts.' Google's Stitch prompt guide says to work 'screen by screen' with 'one or two adjustments per prompt', and warns that prompts over 5,000 characters cause Stitch to 'omit some components'. IFScale (Jaroslawicz et al., Jul 2025) found 'even the best frontier models only achieve 68% accuracy at the max density of 500 instructions', with a 'bias towards earlier instructions'. Design2Code (Si et al.) found models 'mostly lag in recalling visual elements ... and generating correct layout designs'. On up-front specs: Anthropic says Opus 5 'performs best when given the complete task specification up front', and for Opus 4.8 recommends putting 'the task, intent, and relevant constraints upfront in the first human turn', because underspecified prompts spread over several turns reduce efficiency and sometimes performance. The two findings fit together: specify everything once, then deliver in batches.
principles.implication: The v1 pack asks for 594 frames, and up to 1,188 if every frame is drawn light and dark. 12 prompts ask for 12 to 19 frames each. Keep each prompt as one complete brief, and end it with a numbered BATCH PLAN. Batch 1 (this turn): the dense default on the primary platform plus the 2 or 3 states that change layout, at most about 6 frames. Batch 2 ('continue'): the remaining states on the primary platform. Batch 3: platform variants. Batch 4: dark twins of 2 or 3 representative frames. After each batch, check that every string and state listed for that batch is present before sending 'continue'. The 5,000-character Stitch limit applies to Stitch only. Treat it as a warning sign for any tool, not as a Claude Design rule.
principles.strength: moderate (converging vendor guidance and benchmarks, but no Claude Design-specific frame limit is published)

principles.principle: Write one canonical fixture world into the preamble and have every prompt refer to it by name. Separate generations only agree on content if they are given the same content.
principles.evidence: Anthropic says Opus 4.8 'does not silently generalize an instruction from one item to another', so every screen draws exactly the data it is given. NN/g (Sponheim & Brown, Apr 2024) found ChatGPT-4 produced 'three drastically different designs' from identical prompts, so any variation in the input adds to drift that already exists. Internal audit of prompts-v1: at least 10 different street addresses. Three different 'today' dates: Mon 19 Oct 2026 (Today tab, pickup card, air band, calendar strip), Mon 21 Sep 2026 (widget, widget-tap landing) and Wed 16 Sep 2026 (place file, compare reveal). HOA dues of $265, $285 and $385. Pickup on Tuesday with Waste Connections in one prompt and Thursday with City of Camas in another, both in Camas 98607. A near-duplicate address pair: 2416 NE Ingle Rd (keeper strip) and 2418 NE Ingle Rd (briefing opt-in).
principles.implication: Add a FIXTURES block to house-style-v1 that defines: HOME A (the claimed T3 household: one address, the owner and co-resident names, move-in date, pickup weekday and hauler, HOA amount and date, three bills with amounts, one pending invite); PLACE B (a T1 saved place); FRIEND C (the compare sender); one fixed 'today' date and time; one AQI reading and one weather line. Each prompt then says 'Use HOME A as of TODAY' and lists only the deltas its own states need. Surfaces that summarise one another must share fixtures so their artboards can sit side by side without contradiction: widget → widget-tap landing → Today tab → calendar strip → place file year band.
principles.strength: moderate (general principle from the vendor docs; the drift itself is measured directly in v1)

principles.principle: Give exact, real strings for every visible element, and use reserved or clearly fictional identifiers for personal data.
principles.evidence: Claude Design's Get-started article: 'Be specific about what you're building, who it's for, and what matters most.' Vercel's v0 guide (Dec 15 2025) found that specifying the actual product surface gave fully working features 'vs. placeholder-only versions'. NN/g (2024) observed a tool varying output mainly by 'placeholder text pulled from the prompt'. A community reverse-engineered Claude Design system prompt (unverified) instructs 'no filler — every element earns its place'. RFC 2606 reserves example.com, example.net and example.org for documentation.
principles.implication: Keep v1's exact-strings discipline, which is its strongest feature. Add one preamble rule: 'Every string on an artboard comes from this prompt or from FIXTURES. If a layout needs a string that isn't given, write it in Pantopus voice and list it on the surface's Notes artboard.' Change jules.okafor@gmail.com, priya.raman@gmail.com, rjmoore@proton.me and d.reyes@fastmail.com to @example.com addresses. Share cards and screenshots travel, and a real-domain address can belong to a real person.
principles.strength: strong for reserved domains (IETF standard); moderate for real content over placeholders

principles.principle: Attach pictures of what already exists, especially the host screen for every extension prompt. Pictures and structured frames steer a generator more reliably than prose.
principles.evidence: NN/g (Wang & Brown, Oct 24 2025) tested Bolt, Claude, Figma Make, v0, Stitch, Lovable and Replit and found designs improved significantly when Figma links or mockups were included ('An image is worth a thousand words'). Without visual specs the output defaulted to 'a similar, generic look'. Claude Design supports this directly: 'Upload screenshots of existing designs, competitor products, wireframes' and there is a web capture tool to 'grab elements directly from your website so prototypes look like the real product'. Figma says to attach frames rather than images because 'Frames contain structured design data'. Anthropic's general guide calls examples 'one of the most reliable ways to steer Claude's output', 3 to 5 of them.
principles.implication: Every EXTEND_EXISTING prompt currently says 'open it, keep everything', but only 5 of the 59 mention attaching anything. Add an ATTACH line to each: the host screen's current screenshot or web capture (iOS, Android and web), plus the component specimen sheet (see the next principle). For web surfaces, use the web capture tool on the running app.
principles.strength: strong (replicated NN/g finding plus vendor docs)

principles.principle: Design each shared honesty component once, first, as a specimen sheet. Put it into the design system, then refer to it by name in every later prompt.
principles.evidence: The house style already requires this ('Design that treatment once and reuse it') but never shows the treatment. Figma's guidelines.md advice: guidelines should cover component variants with 'Purpose and visual style', 'Usage scenarios' and specific constraints, and 'More context isn't always better. It can confuse the LLM.' v0 passes components to the model through a registry, 'a distribution specification designed to pass context from your design system to AI Models'. v0 also warns the model is 'trained on the default implementations of the shadcn/ui components and may struggle with any customizations', so custom components need to be shown, not just named. Claude Design updates a system through Remix. Internal audit: the 'hollow mark' / 'filled-with-tick' vocabulary appears in only 13 or 14 of the 59 prompts, and the scope caption appears in 5 wordings ('Only you will see this.', 'Only you see this.', 'Only you can see this.', 'Only you can see these.', 'Only you').
principles.implication: Generate x-provenance-sheet first (its frame 9 is already 'the mark specimen sheet'). Extend that sheet to include: the filled, hollow and ticked provenance marks; the unconfirmed row treatment; the two scope chips with ONE canonical string each (for example 'Saved place · Only you' and 'Your household'); the source caption ('FEMA flood zone'); the silence receipt row; the stale/offline 'as of' row; the locked-action row; and one scale-strip track. Remix it into the Pantopus design system, then generate hosts (Today, Place file), then cards, then sheets, then widgets and OG. Each later prompt says 'use the Provenance mark, Scope chip, and Silence receipt components from the design system' and restates only the exact string.
principles.strength: moderate (vendor guidance plus directly measured drift in v1)

principles.principle: State scope explicitly for every pack-wide rule. Current Claude models follow instructions literally and do not carry a rule from one item to the next.
principles.evidence: Anthropic, Opus 4.8: 'interprets prompts literally and explicitly ... It does not silently generalize an instruction from one item to another ... If you need Claude to apply an instruction broadly, state the scope explicitly.' In v1, house-style-v1 says 'DRAW BOTH LIGHT AND DARK', but 46 of 59 prompts never mention dark, every 'frames: N' count excludes dark twins, and f8-og-compare-card rightly overrides with 'LIGHT palette only'. So the generator gets two conflicting counts. Figma says multi-file guidance should be audited 'to identify conflicting information'.
principles.implication: End each prompt with an explicit artboard manifest, for example 'ARTBOARDS (14): 01–10 ios/light; 11 web-1440/light; 12 web-390/light; 13 android/light; 14 ios/dark = copy of 06'. Take the blanket dark rule out of the preamble and give dark twins per surface. Draw full dark sets only where dark mode carries meaning: widgets (including tinted mode), the provenance specimen, and the scale strips.

principles.principle: Take platform dimensions from the platform's own documentation, write them into the prompt, and say which devices and breakpoints are in scope.
principles.evidence: Claude Design: 'Mention whether your design needs to work on mobile, tablet, and desktop, or just one of those.' Apple HIG widget table: on a 393×852 pt screen, small is 158×158, medium 338×158 and large 338×354. The 170×170 / 364×170 / 364×382 sizes belong to 430×932 and 428×926 screens. HIG: 'use the standard margin width for widgets — 16 points for most widgets'; 11 pt 'can work well' for tighter groupings. In accented rendering the system 'tints primary and accented content white'. Android: portrait cell size is roughly 73n−16 dp × 118m−16 dp on a typical handset grid (table: 5×2 = 349×220 dp, 1×1 = 57×102 dp).
principles.implication: Fix the widget family to 393×852 sizes (158 / 338×158 / 338×354 pt) with 16 pt margins. Derive the Android sizes from the Android formula (2×2 ≈ 130×220 dp, 4×2 ≈ 276×220 dp, 4×4 ≈ 276×455 dp on the documented grid) or label them 'launcher-dependent, drawn at X'. Keep the tinted-mode frames: HIG confirms the marks become one or two flat colours, so filled, hollow and tick must differ by shape alone.

principles.principle: Give each rule its reason and say what to do. Keep prohibitions for the few true invariants, and pair each one with the thing to do instead.
principles.evidence: Anthropic's general guide: 'Providing context or motivation behind your instructions ... can help Claude better understand your goals' ('Claude is smart enough to generalize from the explanation'). Also 'Tell Claude what to do instead of what not to do.' Opus 4.8: 'Positive examples ... tend to be more effective than negative examples or instructions that tell the model what not to do.' Anthropic also advises dialing back aggressive language ('CRITICAL: You MUST') because newer models over-trigger on it. NN/g's CARE framework (Moran, May 2024) likewise pairs Rules with Examples of what you do or don't want. v1 has 'WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY' sections (good) and about 464 'do not' / 'never' phrasings across the pack.
principles.implication: Keep a short INVARIANTS block (four tabs, no fifth tab or FAB, no grades or percentages on risk, scope stated on every address) in the preamble only. In each prompt, rewrite DO NOT lines as INSTEAD pairs, for example 'Missing facts render as a one-line ask with a CTA in text.primary (not a red X or warning colour).' Remove all-caps emphasis except for the invariants.
principles.strength: strong (official guidance); the effect size for image generation specifically is unmeasured

principles.principle: Order each prompt as reference material first and the specific request last, with consistent section tags, and settle the clarifying-question round in advance.
principles.evidence: Anthropic: 'Place your long documents and inputs near the top of your prompt, above your query, instructions, and examples. This improves performance across all models.' Also: XML tags reduce misinterpretation, and 'Use consistent, descriptive tag names across your prompts.' Lost in the Middle (Liu et al., TACL 2023): performance 'is often highest when relevant information occurs at the beginning or end of the input context'. Opus 5: 'check in only when different readings of the request would lead to materially different work.' A community reverse-engineered Claude Design system prompt (unverified) says: 'ask clarifying questions before building — one consolidated round, then execute autonomously.' v1 headings drift: 'PLATFORMS/VIEWPORTS', 'PLATFORMS + VIEWPORTS', 'PLATFORM:', 'STATES —', 'STATES TO DRAW (...)', 'FRAMES:'.
principles.implication: Use one fixed skeleton for all 59 prompts, in this order: <house_style> <fixtures> <invariants> (pasted once per project) → <surface> (id, disposition, where it lives, job) → <content> → <visualization_decision> → <states> → <instead_of> → <artboards> (the manifest, last). Add to the preamble: 'Product decisions here are final. Ask a question only if two readings would produce materially different screens; otherwise proceed and record assumptions on a Notes artboard.'
principles.strength: moderate (official guidance plus peer-reviewed position effects; the clarifying-question behaviour is from an unverified source)

principles.principle: Iterate with targeted, element-level feedback. Use comments and sliders for visual tweaks, chat for structural changes, and ask for 2 or 3 options only where the visual form is genuinely open.
principles.evidence: Claude Design lets you 'Comment inline on specific elements, edit text directly, or use adjustment knobs', with 'Custom sliders (made by Claude)' for spacing, colour and layout. Its docs say: 'Be specific in your feedback', ''This doesn't look right' is hard to act on', 'Ask Claude to show you 2–3 options', and 'Save what we have and try a completely different approach'. Known limits: 'Claude Design doesn't have version history yet', 'Inline comments occasionally don't appear on the page', and multi-person editing 'may not work reliably'. v0 uses prompts for structural changes and Design Mode for visual ones. Stitch: 'Name specific elements explicitly' ('primary button on sign-up form'). Opus 4.8: 'propose 4 distinct visual directions ... then implement only that direction' breaks default styling. Mather (Anthropic) tip 3: use the Comment tool for detailed edits.
principles.implication: Ask for options only on the new visual forms: the year band and count ring (x-place-file), the four-layer scale strip, the keeper strip and naming, the widget's per-size forms, and the compare reveal. Tell the model to put options side by side on one artboard, then lock the chosen one into the design system. For extension surfaces, ask for no options and one faithful result. Because there is no version history, export HTML/PDF after each accepted batch into the repo (for example docs/design/exports/<surface-id>/). A May 2026 Hacker News thread reported losing project access after downgrading, which is another reason to keep local exports.
principles.strength: strong for the documented features; moderate for the options policy

principles.principle: Check every generated artboard against a written acceptance checklist, including contrast. Generated UI often lacks hierarchy and contrast even when the layout is correct.
principles.evidence: NN/g (2025): outputs lacked 'visual hierarchy or grouping among related elements' and showed 'poor color contrast'. Also, high-level prompts led to the wrong pattern ('profile page' built as a social profile). WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (AA): text needs at least 4.5:1, large text (18 pt, or 14 pt bold) at least 3:1. SC 2.5.8 (AA): targets at least 24×24 CSS px. Claude Design can be asked for accessibility reviews (Get-started). Contrast of Pantopus tokens, computed with the WCAG formula: text.muted #9CA3AF on base #FFFFFF is 2.54:1, on sunken #F3F4F6 2.31:1. text.secondary #6B7280 is 4.83:1 on base but 4.39:1 on sunken. primary #0284c7 on white is 4.10:1. success #059669 is 3.77:1, warning #D97706 3.19:1, home #16A34A 3.30:1. Dark text.secondary #94A3B8 on #0F172A is 6.96:1.
principles.implication: Add token usage rules to house-style-v1: text.muted is for disabled text and decoration only, never for content someone must read. Readable secondary text uses text.secondary on base, raised or app surfaces (4.51–4.83:1), not on sunken. primary, success, warning and home may colour icons and marks (above 3:1 non-text) but not body-size text. For primary buttons, check that white label text at 16 px passes (4.10:1 fails for normal text; use primary.700 #0369a1, which is 5.93:1 on white). Every batch is reviewed against: tokens only, contrast, 24 px minimum targets (44 pt iOS / 48 dp Android per platform practice), scope chip present, provenance mark present, all fixture strings present.
principles.strength: strong (WCAG standard; ratios computed directly from the house tokens)

patterns.name: System-first setup (publish once, inherit everywhere)
patterns.exemplars: Claude Design: a published design system is used automatically by every project created from the homescreen, updated through Remix, and admins can lock a team to one system. v0: a shadcn-based registry passes design-system context to the model. Figma Make: attach library components and a guidelines.md. Uizard: brand kits keep generated UIs aligned.
patterns.howToApply: Before prompt 1, build and publish the 'Pantopus' system from the token files, the two existing projects (exported HTML) and core-screen screenshots. Test it with 2 or 3 throwaway prompts ('design the Mail tab list'). Only then start the pack. Every surface gets its own project created from the homescreen.
patterns.pitfalls: Import quality depends on how complete the sources are (Claude Design docs). v0 warns customised components confuse a model trained on defaults. A design system with no example screens under-specifies the look ('Include real examples, not just specs').

patterns.name: Specimen sheet before surfaces
patterns.exemplars: Figma guidelines.md spells out component variants, purpose and constraints. Claude Design's Remix step folds new components back into the system. Anthropic's prompting guide recommends 3–5 examples.
patterns.howToApply: First generation: x-provenance-sheet with an extended specimen artboard (provenance marks, unconfirmed row, the two scope chips with one canonical string each, source caption, silence receipt, stale 'as of' row, locked-action row, one scale-strip track, light and dark, tinted-mode desaturation check). Accept it, Remix it into the system, and name those components in every later prompt.
patterns.pitfalls: If the specimen is only described and never drawn, every surface reinvents it. If it is drawn in a surface project but never added to the system, later projects will not see it.

patterns.name: Canonical fixture world
patterns.exemplars: Figma Make can generate mock data or accept CSV uploads so prototypes use consistent, realistic data. v0's guide shows that specifying the actual product surface removes placeholder output.
patterns.howToApply: A FIXTURES block in the preamble: HOME A (T3, claimed, the household, move-in date, pickup weekday and hauler, HOA, three bills, a pending invite at example.com), PLACE B (T1 saved), FRIEND C (compare sender), a fixed TODAY with date and time, one AQI reading and one weather line, and one year of dated rules. Prompts refer to these by name and state only deltas. Widget, widget landing, Today, calendar strip and place-file year band must all show HOME A on the same TODAY.
patterns.pitfalls: Changing the fixture mid-pack breaks earlier artboards, so version the block and freeze it. Real-looking addresses and real-domain emails can point at real people; use example.com and street numbers you have checked are fictional.

patterns.name: Full brief, batched delivery
patterns.exemplars: Anthropic Opus 5/4.8: give the complete spec up front. Figma: 'smaller the scope, the more detailed'. Stitch: screen by screen, one or two adjustments per prompt. Claude Design: 'Start simple, then layer in complexity' (from a summary of the Get-started article; not confirmed verbatim).
patterns.howToApply: Each prompt ends with an ARTBOARDS manifest grouped into batches of at most about 6. Send the prompt, which produces batch 1. Check it. Then send 'Continue with batch 2 exactly as specified', and so on. Dark twins come last and are limited to representative frames.
patterns.pitfalls: Batching without a manifest means the model forgets what was left. Rewriting the spec in later turns leaves conflicting versions in context. The Stitch 5,000-character component-drop limit is Stitch-specific.

patterns.name: Host screenshot attached to every extension
patterns.exemplars: NN/g 2025: outputs matched far better when Figma links or mockups were included. Claude Design: screenshot uploads and a web capture tool. Figma Make: attach frames because they carry structured data.
patterns.howToApply: Every EXTEND_EXISTING and NEW_CARD_IN_EXISTING prompt gets an ATTACH line: the current host on each platform, plus the specimen sheet. The instruction reads 'Reproduce the attached host exactly; change only: …'.
patterns.pitfalls: Screenshots of outdated builds carry old bugs forward. Capture from master. Image-heavy attachments can confuse some tools (Figma help).

patterns.name: Addressable artboards plus a Notes artboard
patterns.exemplars: Stitch: name elements precisely ('primary button on sign-up form'). Figma: 'The cleaner your design input, the better your output' (layer naming). Claude Design: inline comments on specific elements, 'Be specific in your feedback'. Mather (Anthropic): spend manual effort on icons and naming.
patterns.howToApply: Title every artboard '<surface-id> · <platform> · <NN-state> · <light|dark>' (for example 'f1-today-tab · ios · 06-quiet-day · light'), and use those exact titles in follow-ups and comments. The last artboard, 'Notes', lists assumptions, any invented strings, and which states were omitted and why.
patterns.pitfalls: I could not verify whether Claude Design has native named artboards. Third-party accounts describe it as HTML/JS. Put the title as a visible label above each frame so it survives HTML, PDF and PPTX export either way.

patterns.name: Options only where the form is open
patterns.exemplars: Claude Design: 'Ask Claude to show you 2–3 options' and 'quickly create a wide range of directions'. Opus 4.8: propose distinct directions, the user picks one, build only that. NN/g: AI is best for 'ideation, concept exploration'.
patterns.howToApply: Request 2 or 3 side-by-side options only for new visual forms (the year band and count ring, the scale strip, keeper strip and naming, widget per-size forms, the compare reveal). Pick one, then add it to the system. Extensions get exactly one result that is faithful to the host.
