patterns.pitfalls: Options on extension surfaces invite style drift away from the existing system. Options generated late cannot be reconciled with earlier accepted screens.

patterns.name: Export after acceptance and hand off
patterns.exemplars: Claude Design: exports to HTML, PDF, PPTX and .zip, sends to Canva, and packages 'a handoff bundle that you can pass to Claude Code'; '/design-sync' keeps Code and Design aligned. No version history yet.
patterns.howToApply: After each accepted batch, export HTML and PDF into the repo (docs/design/exports/<surface-id>/) and record the project URL in the surface index. Hand off to Claude Code per surface, not per pack.
patterns.pitfalls: No version history, so an iteration that goes wrong can overwrite accepted work. A May 2026 HN report describes losing project access after a plan downgrade (an Anthropic staffer said download would be made possible). Keep local copies.

antipatterns: Mood-only direction ('clean, trustworthy, warm') with no typeface, radius or background rule. Anthropic documents a persistent warm-cream, serif and terracotta default, and generic style words move it to another fixed palette instead of to your brand.

Telling the model to 'open' other projects by share URL as the only way it gets the design system. This is not documented in Claude Design's help. The documented route is a published design system plus attachments.

One prompt asking for 15–19 frames, doubled by a blanket 'draw both light and dark'. Scope and instruction-density research (Figma, Stitch, IFScale) predicts dropped states and components, and v1 reaches 594 frames (1,188 with dark).

Different addresses, dates and amounts in prompts whose screens summarise each other (widget vs Today vs place file). Literal models draw exactly what they are given, so the set can never be shown side by side.

Several wordings of the same honesty string ('Only you will see this.' / 'Only you see this.' / 'Only you can see this.'). The house rule asks for one treatment designed once, and a literal model will reproduce every variant.
Real-domain emails (gmail.com, proton.me, fastmail.com) and possibly real street addresses in fixtures. RFC 2606 reserves example.com for this, and share cards and screenshots circulate.
Type sizes outside the scale inside a surface prompt (31/37, 42/48, 15.5/23). This breaks the house rule against inventing a type scale and teaches the generator that the scale is optional.
Using text.muted (#9CA3AF, 2.54:1 on white, 2.31:1 on sunken) for readable content. It fails WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1), and generators will copy the token choice exactly.
Ending prompts with long DO NOT lists that have no 'instead'. Anthropic's guidance is to say what to do and to give the reason, and to keep emphatic prohibitions for true invariants.
'Open it, keep everything' with no screenshot attached. NN/g found visual references were what made AI output match real designs, and without them tools fall back to 'a similar, generic look'.

Adding self-verification instructions ('double-check every frame') to prompts for current Opus-class models. Anthropic says Opus 5 already verifies and such instructions cause over-verification. Use a human acceptance checklist between batches instead.
Asking for multiple options on extension surfaces. It invites visual drift away from the existing system. Keep options for genuinely new forms.
Using vague visual feedback during iteration ('doesn't look right'). Claude Design's own docs say this is hard to act on. Use element-level comments or exact values ('tighten spacing to 8px').
Accepting a batch without exporting it. Claude Design has no version history yet, and a user report shows projects can become inaccessible after a plan change.

Relying on unverified internals, such as the community 'reverse-engineered' Claude Design system prompt, as fact. Use it only as a weak hint (for example, that it may ask one round of clarifying questions).

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'Before designing, open these two projects [claude.ai/design/p/... share links] and use them as the source of truth for every token, component and layout convention.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Claude Design documents design systems as org-level objects built from codebases, design files and uploads. When published, every project created from the homescreen uses them automatically. Opening another project by share link is not in the Get-started article (asked directly: NOT PRESENT). Anthropic's Ryan Mather: set up the design system and core screens first.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Publish a 'Pantopus' design system built from the token files, the two projects' exported HTML and core-screen screenshots. Create each surface project from the homescreen. Change the preamble line to 'This project uses the published Pantopus design system; screenshots of the host are attached.' Keep the links for humans only.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'DESIGN DIRECTION: clean, trustworthy, warm.' The type scale is given but no font family, corner radius, elevation or spacing unit is named.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Anthropic (Opus 4.8 guide): the model's persistent default is warm cream (#F4F1EA), serif display type, italic accents and terracotta. Generic style instructions shift it to another fixed palette. 'Specify a concrete alternative. The model follows explicit specs precisely.'
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Replace 'warm' with concrete rules: the named sans family from the codebase, the radius and elevation values, the spacing unit, 'no serif, no italic accents, no cream or tinted-paper backgrounds; warmth comes from copy voice and primary.50 selected states'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: A blanket 'DRAW BOTH LIGHT AND DARK', while 46 of 59 prompts' state lists and every 'frames: N' count leave out dark twins, and f8-og-compare-card specifies light only.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Anthropic: current models follow instructions literally, do not carry an instruction from one item to the next, and need the scope stated explicitly. Figma: audit guidance for conflicting information.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Remove the blanket line. Each prompt ends with an explicit ARTBOARDS manifest that names which frames get dark twins (default: the dense frame plus one state-coloured frame; full dark sets only for widgets, the provenance specimen and the scale strips).

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'iOS widget family drawn on a 393×852 home screen — systemSmall 170×170pt, systemMedium 364×170pt, systemLarge 364×382pt' and 'Android ... 2×2 ≈ 150×150dp, 4×2 ≈ 330×150dp, 4×4 ≈ 330×330dp'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG table: 393×852 gives small 158×158, medium 338×158, large 338×354. 170/364×170/364×382 is the 430×932 and 428×926 row. Standard widget margin is 16 pt. Android: portrait cell size is roughly 73n−16 × 118m−16 dp (5×2 = 349×220 dp), which does not match 150×150 for 2×2.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use 158 / 338×158 / 338×354 pt with 16 pt margins on the 393×852 frame. Derive the Android sizes from the documented formula or state the assumed launcher grid. Carry the same sizes into f7-widget-gallery and f7-widget-howto-sheet previews.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: One prompt asks for 15 frames (12 iOS states plus 3 platform frames), and the preamble implies light and dark, up to 30 artboards in one generation. The same pattern appears in f3b-invitation-decision (19), f7-today-widget (19), f3-invite-banner (16), f3b-verify-address-sheet (15) and f3b-owner-attestation (15).
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Figma: 'The smaller the scope, the more detailed the LLM can be.' Stitch: one or two adjustments per prompt, and long prompts omit components. IFScale: adherence falls as instruction density rises, with a bias toward earlier instructions. Design2Code: models miss visual elements. Anthropic also says to give the complete spec up front.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the full brief in one message but deliver in batches of at most about 6 artboards (the dense default and layout-changing states first, then the other states, then platforms, then dark), checking each batch against the manifest.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Fixtures: 1420 NE Garfield St, rendered 'as of Monday 21 September 2026'. f1-today-tab (including its 'arrived from the widget' frame), f4-today-pickup-card, f1-today-air-band and f5-today-calendar-strip use 2418 NW Lacamas Dr on Monday 19 October 2026. x-place-file uses 2418 NW Sierra St on Sep 16 2026.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Literal instruction following means each screen draws only the data it is given (Anthropic), and generators already vary between runs (NN/g). Screens that summarise one another can only be checked side by side if they share fixtures.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Put one FIXTURES block (HOME A on one TODAY) in the preamble and use it in the widget, widget-tap landing, Today, pickup card, air band, calendar strip, date sheet and place file. Also resolve HOA dues ($265 / $285 / $385), the pickup weekday and hauler (Tuesday / Waste Connections vs Thursday / City of Camas), and 2416 vs 2418 NE Ingle Rd (f11-keeper-strip vs f4-briefing-optin-card).

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The house style says the unconfirmed treatment should be designed once and reused, but never defines it. The filled / hollow / filled-with-tick vocabulary appears in only 13–14 of 59 prompts. The scope caption appears in five wordings across prompts ('Only you will see this.', 'Only you see this.', 'Only you can see this.', 'Only you can see these.', 'Only you').
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Consistent components across generations come from passing the component itself as context (v0 registry, Figma guidelines and frames, Claude Design system Remix), not from re-describing it in each prompt. Literal models reproduce each wording they are given.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Generate x-provenance-sheet first, with an extended specimen artboard that fixes the marks, the unconfirmed row and ONE string per scope chip or caption. Remix it into the design system. Every later prompt names the component and uses the canonical string.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'H1 at 31/37/700 on mobile and 42/48/700 at 1440 ... Lede at 15.5/23/400 ... Contrast line at label or caption weight (13/18 or 12/16), text.muted'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The house style fixes h1 at 30/36/700 and forbids inventing a type scale. WCAG 1.4.3 needs 4.5:1 for normal text, and text.muted #9CA3AF on white measures 2.54:1.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use h1 (30/36) on mobile and state explicitly whether a larger display size exists in the design system (if it doesn't, use h1). Use body 16/24 for the lede. Set the contrast line in text.secondary (4.83:1 on white) and keep the weight-only emphasis.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The 'needs verification' column is drawn as 'lock glyph rows in the muted text token on the sunken surface'. f3b-locked-action-row likewise uses 'muted text on the sunken surface' for the reason line.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: text.muted on sunken #F3F4F6 is 2.31:1, and even text.secondary on sunken is 4.39:1. Both fail WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1). These rows carry the consent-relevant limits the prompt says must be read. NN/g reports poor contrast as a common failure in AI-generated UI.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw the locked rows in text.secondary on surface.base or surface.raised (4.83 / 4.63:1), keeping the lock glyph and the same row height, so the column stays calm but readable. Add a token-usage rule to the preamble: text.muted is never used for content someone must read.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Fixture emails use real consumer domains (jules.okafor@gmail.com, priya.raman@gmail.com, rjmoore@proton.me, d.reyes@fastmail.com), which also appear in f3-members-roster, f1-email-verify-handoff and x-place-file.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: RFC 2606 reserves example.com, example.net and example.org for documentation and examples.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Replace them with @example.com addresses in the FIXTURES block.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Extension prompts (this one and the other EXTEND_EXISTING surfaces) say 'this already exists ... open it, keep everything, and change only what is listed', but only 5 of 59 prompts mention attaching anything.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g 2025: output matched real designs far better when Figma links or mockups were supplied, and otherwise defaulted to a generic look. Claude Design supports screenshot uploads and web capture. Figma recommends attaching frames.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add an ATTACH line to every extension prompt: the current host screenshots on each platform (web via web capture) plus the specimen sheet. Reword to 'Reproduce the attached host exactly; change only: …'.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Each prompt closes with a 'DO NOT' list (about 464 'do not' / 'never' phrasings across the pack), several without a stated alternative.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Anthropic: tell Claude what to do instead of what not to do, and give the reason. Positive instructions and examples beat negative ones. Emphatic prohibitions can over-trigger.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep a short INVARIANTS block in the preamble. In each prompt, rewrite the DO NOT lines as 'Instead of X, draw Y because Z', keeping the existing WHY sections, which already match the guidance.

numbers: Claude Design launched Apr 17 2026 as an Anthropic Labs research preview on Opus 4.7, for Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans. Its current model is unverified.
Claude Design documented limits: no version history; inline comments occasionally don't appear; multi-person editing is 'basic'; usage counts against normal plan limits.

Claude Design documented export and handoff: PPTX, PDF, HTML (and .zip), Canva and other partner apps, a Claude Code handoff bundle, and /design and /design-sync in Claude Code. Figma export was not found on the product page or in the Get-started article.
Claude Design's own advice: ask for 2–3 options; state whether the design must work on mobile, tablet and/or desktop.
Anthropic prompting guide: 3–5 examples for best results; put long reference material at the top and the request at the end.
v1 pack size: 59 prompts, 594 frames (1,188 if every frame is drawn light and dark). 12 prompts have 12 or more frames; the maximum is 19 (f7-today-widget, f3b-invitation-decision).
Suggested batch size: at most about 6 artboards per generation turn (a working rule synthesised from the Figma and Stitch guidance and IFScale, not a published Claude Design limit).
Per-send length in v1: house style 3,371 characters plus a prompt of 3,189–7,054 characters, about 6.5k–10.4k characters. Stitch drops components above 5,000 characters (Stitch-specific).
IFScale: the best frontier models reach 68% accuracy at 500 simultaneous instructions, with a bias toward earlier instructions.
Apple widgets on a 393×852 pt screen: small 158×158, medium 338×158, large 338×354 pt. On 430×932 and 428×926: 170×170, 364×170, 364×382. Standard margin 16 pt, tight 11 pt.
Android widgets: portrait cell size is roughly (73n − 16) dp × (118m − 16) dp; 1×1 = 57×102 dp, 5×2 = 349×220 dp, 5×4 = 349×455 dp.
WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3 (AA): 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for large text (≥18 pt, or ≥14 pt bold). SC 2.5.8 (AA): targets at least 24×24 CSS px.

Pantopus token contrast (computed): text.muted #9CA3AF on #FFFFFF 2.54:1, on #F3F4F6 2.31:1; text.secondary #6B7280 on #FFFFFF 4.83:1, on #F9FAFB 4.63:1, on #F6F7F9 4.51:1, on #F3F4F6 4.39:1; primary #0284c7 on white 4.10:1; primary.700 #0369a1 on white 5.93:1; success #059669 3.77:1; warning #D97706 3.19:1; home #16A34A 3.30:1; dark text.secondary #94A3B8 on #0F172A 6.96:1.

Fixture drift in v1: at least 10 different street addresses; 3 'today' dates (16 Sep, 21 Sep, 19 Oct 2026); HOA dues of $265, $285 and $385; pickup on Tuesday (Waste Connections) vs Thursday (City of Camas); 2416 vs 2418 NE Ingle Rd; 5 wordings of the 'Only you' scope caption.
Only 13 of 59 v1 prompts mention dark mode; only 5 mention attaching screenshots or other files; the provenance-mark vocabulary appears in 13–14 prompts.

topic: Competitive and adjacent product teardown for an address-first home app. Covers Nextdoor, Citizen, Ring/Neighbors, Zillow, Redfin, Homebot, HomeZada, Hippo Home, Thumbtack, Google Home, Recycle Coach, WasteConnect, a ReCollect city app, Rocket Money, Life360 and Finch, checked against Apple HIG, App Store Review Guidelines, Android developer guidance, NN/g, Baymard and Pew. Method and limits: web search was unavailable because the shared budget was used up, so every source below was fetched directly. App Store review evidence comes from Apple's public review feed, one page of up to 50 of the most recent reviews per app, sorted into themes by a summarizer. Treat those counts as directional, not representative. Four things could not be checked. Reddit and Google Play could not be fetched. ACM papers returned 403 and Airship's opt-in benchmarks are behind a form. Centriq did not appear in a US App Store search (Sep 2026) and nothing was verifiable about Porch. Apple Home has no public review feed. No claims are made about any of these.

principles.principle: Ask for notification permission only in context, after the user has seen value, and show exactly which notification they are agreeing to.
principles.evidence: Android's POST_NOTIFICATIONS guidance says to let users get familiar with the app first. The prompt should come from a meaningful user action, or wait until the 3rd or 4th launch. The ask should make clear what the notifications are for; its example is an email app saying whether it notifies for every email or only some. Apple HIG Privacy: 'Avoid requesting permission at launch unless the data or resource is required for your app to function' and 'wait to request permission until people actually use an app feature that requires access.' NN/g (Kendrick, 2018): don't ask immediately, and 'Tell people what notifications will be about.' NN/g (Rosala, 2019): 'Context-related permission requests are less likely to cause surprise.'
principles.implication: The only triggers for the OS prompt are a tap on Yes in the Today briefing card, the first 'That's my day', or accepting household activity. It never fires at cold launch. The thing being agreed to is drawn as the literal pickup notification, never as a list of benefits. Every Today card, including pickup, air and the 14-day strip, must work in full with notifications denied, so declining costs nothing.

principles.principle: iOS and Android need different pre-permission screens. On iOS, a custom screen shown before the system alert has exactly one button (Continue or Next) and no cancel, so the decision to decline belongs on the in-context card. On Android, the rationale screen must include a 'no thanks'.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Privacy, verbatim: 'Include only one button and make it clear that it opens the system alert.' It says to title that button 'Continue' or 'Next', and warns that a button resembling 'Allow' in meaning and weight manipulates people. It also says not to add other actions, such as a way to leave without seeing the system alert, 'like offering an option to close or cancel.' Android's permission docs say the educational UI should 'include a "cancel" or "no thanks" button that lets the user continue using your app without granting the permission.' On Android, if the user taps Deny more than once, the system dialog never appears again; apps targeting 12L or lower get only one chance before a reinstall.
principles.implication: On iOS, the Today card's Yes / Not now is the real decision. Yes goes straight to the system alert, or to a primer whose only control is 'Continue' under the preview tray card. On Android, the rationale sheet keeps 'Not now'. Declining twice on Android is treated as permanent, so from then on show only the 'Open settings' state and move the widget row up.

principles.principle: Keep push titles glanceable, and put the 'unconfirmed' caveat where truncation cannot remove it: early in a short title, never as a long suffix.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Notifications: 'Prefer brief titles that people can read at a glance', use title-style capitalization with no ending punctuation, and 'don't truncate your message — the system does this automatically when necessary.' Android's build-notification doc: 'By default, the notification's text content is truncated to fit one line'; longer text needs an expandable BigTextStyle. Neither platform publishes an exact character limit, so the budget has to be tested on real devices.
principles.implication: Write pickup and reminder titles like 'Recycling Tomorrow · Unconfirmed' (about 30 characters) and start the body with the source: 'City of Camas schedule. Bins out tonight.' Check the tray at 393pt (iOS) and 412dp (Android) in collapsed form. A caveat placed after 40+ characters of title is lost the same way a body tail is.

principles.principle: Never put a full street address on the lock screen. Use the user's own place label or the street name, and provide a generic hidden-preview text.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Notifications: 'Avoid including sensitive, personal, or confidential information in a notification'; also provide generic text such as 'Reminder' for when previews are hidden. App Store Review Guideline 4.5.4: push 'should not be used to send sensitive personal or confidential information.' Android supports VISIBILITY_PRIVATE plus setPublicVersion() for a redacted lock-screen version. Pew (2023, n=5,101): 73% of Americans feel they have little or no control over company data collection.
principles.implication: In push bodies use 'Lacamas Dr' or the saved label ('Mom's house'), never '2418 NW Lacamas Dr'. Hidden-preview text is 'Pickup reminder' or 'Air quality alert'. Android pushes get a public version with no place label. The widget already does this right ('Garfield St · Camas'); push must match.

principles.principle: Send one notification per real-world event, group bursts, and set the interruption level to the event's true urgency.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Notifications: 'Avoid sending multiple notifications for the same thing'; doing so fills Notification Center and 'people may turn off all notifications from your app.' Apple HIG, Managing Notifications: 'Build trust by accurately representing the urgency of each notification'; use Time Sensitive only for notifications 'relevant in the moment'; 'Never use the Time Sensitive interruption level to send a marketing notification.' NN/g (2018): combine five or more simultaneous alerts into one message, and choose quality over quantity. In the sampled Ring reviews, 8 of 50 complained about notification volume, including getting two notifications for every alert. In the sampled Nextdoor reviews, users kept getting emails after unsubscribing.
principles.implication: Pickup gets exactly one push: the evening briefing. Date and bill reminders use a separate channel. Household activity is passive and grouped: 'Sam paid 3 bills' is one push, not three. An AQI or NOAA threshold crossing may be Time Sensitive; pickup is Active; Founding slots and referral rewards are never pushed at elevated urgency and never pushed without explicit opt-in.

principles.principle: Never silently change a user's notification settings or visibility scope. When settings are migrated or merged, carry every 'off' value forward and say so.
principles.evidence: In three pages of sampled Nextdoor reviews, users said app updates changed their notification settings, re-added neighborhoods about two hours away without consent, and defaulted new email types to on. NN/g (2018) notes users rarely customize defaults, so the default is effectively the decision.
principles.implication: When the notifications page absorbs the per-home toggles, show a one-time line: 'We moved your home reminder settings here. Nothing you turned off was turned on.' A permission or role migration that widens what a member sees is announced on the roster. The Nearby radius never grows without a tap.

principles.principle: Use the address the person types, not the phone's GPS, and never require precise or always-on location.
principles.evidence: App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(iv): 'if a user declines to share Location, offer the ability to manually enter an address.' In the sampled Citizen reviews (page 2), 7 of 50 complained the app is unusable without precise location. Wikipedia records controversy over a 2019 Citizen update that required continuous tracking. The Markup (2021): Life360 sold precise location from 33M users to about a dozen data brokers, earning $16M in 2020 (nearly 20% of revenue); one user said they had no idea the data would be passed around.
principles.implication: No Pantopus surface triggers a location permission. The add-place sheet and /start rely only on typed input. The privacy line on those inputs can say that this is the address you typed and that Pantopus does not track your phone. This is a real advantage over Citizen and Life360 and should be visible, not buried.

principles.principle: Address lookup is the most common failure in apps keyed to an address. Always offer a manual-entry fallback, tolerate typos, and never falsely say an address isn't served.
principles.evidence: In the sampled WasteConnect reviews, address lookup failures accounted for about 15 of the 23 one-star reviews, including users told the company doesn't pick up at an address it does serve. Recycle Coach's sample had 3 complaints that it rejected valid addresses; Zillow reviewers reported their home not being recognized. Baymard: 69% of test participants tried to type the address manually when autocomplete failed and were 'often at a loss' without the usual fields; 9% of manually typed addresses contained typos. Baymard recommends ordering matches by proximity and interpreting misspellings generously.
principles.implication: When geocoding fails, the add-place sheet shows 'Can't find it? Enter it line by line' (street, city, ZIP) in the same detent. Suggestions are ranked by closeness to the user or the pilot area. Outside the pilot area, save the address and say which layers exist there, rather than refusing. When the recipient's lookup fails on the compare screens, the sender's column stays on screen, as v1 already specifies.

principles.principle: Wrong or stale schedule data is what destroys trust in pickup apps, while the reminder itself is what people praise. Make correction an acknowledged loop, and show holiday shifts explicitly.
principles.evidence: Recycle Coach (4.78 stars, 25,233 ratings) sampled reviews: 27 praise the reminders; 6 complain about wrong or missing dates, including notifications that don't adjust for holidays and a report that nobody fixes errors. A ReCollect-built city app (Miramar, 2.63 stars, 30 ratings) draws complaints about reminders not firing and an app not updated in years. WasteConnect (4.71 stars, 9,359 ratings) sampled reviews praise the weekly reminders.
principles.implication: After 'This isn't right', the provenance sheet keeps showing where the report stands ('Reported 3 Oct · we're checking'), not just a thank-you. A household confirmation always overrides the city rule. A holiday shift appears as its own row and cell ('Pickup moves to Friday this week') and replaces the normal pickup text in the push and the widget.

principles.principle: Any estimate needs a published accuracy statement and an owner correction path. Estimates without both anger owners.
principles.evidence: Zillow says Zestimates are off by up to about 7% for most off-market homes and almost 2% for listed homes (per Wikipedia, 2026). Zillow Offers lost $420M in Q3 2021 before it was shut down. Redfin publishes a median error of 1.87% on-market and 7.28% off-market, lets owners edit home facts, and lets them post an 'Owner Estimate' using their own comparable homes. In sampled reviews, Zillow users describe their home shown as an empty lot and wrong bathroom counts, and Homebot users say the app's value doesn't match the email. NN/g (2016) lists upfront disclosure and correct, current content among its four trust factors.
principles.implication: Pantopus shows public-record values only, each with its authority, such as the county assessed value, and never a modeled 'home value'. Every fact leads to the provenance sheet with a confidence sentence and 'This isn't right'. The bill trend line disappears rather than faking a comparison.

principles.principle: Location precision hidden in the API is still shared. What a neighbour can reconstruct from the data matters more than what the UI draws.
principles.evidence: Gizmodo (Dec 2019): Ring Neighbors posts carried coordinates to up to six decimal places. Across about 65,800 posts they mapped up to 20,000 cameras, often within 4 to 6 feet of a home, while Ring said posts did not reveal exact addresses. An MIT researcher's database held 440,000 cameras. Separately, Ring paid $5.8M in a 2023 FTC settlement, including an employee viewing videos of at least 81 women, and ended police 'Request for Assistance' in January 2024. That aggregation across many posts recovers homes is documented; that random jitter re-rolled per post averages out is reasoning here, not a fetched source.
principles.implication: Ship the F9 coordinate-leak fix before any pilot user posts. The privacy mirror should promise only what the server actually returns. Treat 'your public posts: 7' as a risk as well as a count: several posts jittered around one point can be averaged, so prefer a stable coarse cell. Compare tokens and OG cards carry no coordinates at all.

principles.principle: State who can see something ('Only you' or 'your household') on the same surface and at the moment of input, before the record exists.
principles.evidence: Pew (2023): 67% understand little or nothing about what companies do with their data (up from 59%); only about 1 in 5 are confident companies will handle it responsibly; 56% often click 'agree' without reading privacy policies. Apple HIG: people are 'less likely to be comfortable sharing data with your app if they don't understand exactly how you plan to use it.' Wikipedia, citing a 2014 Georgia Tech study, reports that Nextdoor's address verification builds trust but raises concern about disclosing location. Life360's users did not know their location was being sold.
principles.implication: Put the scope sentence directly under the button that creates the record: save, date, keeper, snap, compare. Never hide it in settings. When a place is claimed, the scope change is shown row by row and can be declined. Plain one-sentence statements replace any link to a policy.

principles.principle: Safety content from neighbours or AI creates fear and misidentification. Label content Pantopus wrote, keep briefings factual about the address, and don't make the social layer the reason to come back.
principles.evidence: Wikipedia on Citizen: first launched as 'Vigilante' in 2016 and removed from the App Store within 48 hours. In May 2021 it pushed a photo of a man wrongly suspected in the Palisades fire to 860,000 LA users, with a $30,000 reward. Sampled Citizen reviews: a morning briefing that opened on a casualty count, and complaints that AI-written alerts get details wrong. Wikipedia on Nextdoor: reported racial profiling; the 2016 redesign of the crime-post form was claimed to cut it by 75% (2017). Sampled Nextdoor reviews: police-incident alerts labelled 'your neighborhood' from miles away, and irrelevant AI trending posts. Ring's Search Party (Oct 2025) was on by default, and after backlash to its Super Bowl LX ad Ring ended the Flock partnership (13 Feb 2026).
principles.implication: Curator posts carry the chip and the 'Why am I seeing this?' explanation. Briefings and seasonal headlines are about the address and its sources, never about crime or people. No push ever names or shows a person outside the household. Hero copy leads with public records, not with neighbours.

principles.principle: Putting public-record safety facts behind a paywall or upsell reads as extortion. Keep every reading and reminder free, and keep any scarcity claim honest.
principles.evidence: Sampled reviews: Citizen, 15 of 50 on page 2 were about the paywall, including anger that sex-offender information needs a subscription. Rocket Money (4.5 stars, 391K ratings), 15 about the paywall plus anger at a 30% fee on savings. HomeZada (2.86 stars, 44 ratings), 9 about the paywall. Ring, complaints about price rises. Thumbtack, professionals complaining about pay-per-lead charges.
principles.implication: The Founding tier, referral tiers and Block Founder rank never gate a scale strip, an air alert, a pickup reminder or a civic deadline. The Founding meter hides itself when the lookup fails. Today has no upsell interstitials. The Earn entry stays hidden until money can actually be withdrawn.

principles.principle: Give value before asking for data. Home-management apps that require setup before any payoff get abandoned.
principles.evidence: Sampled reviews: HomeZada users call setup slow and as tedious as a spreadsheet. A Hippo Home user entered all their information and 'got nowhere.' Thumbtack users were asked many unrelated questions before seeing results. NN/g (Kendrick, 2020): skip onboarding when possible, don't use deck-of-cards tutorials, and prefer contextual tips at the moment of need. Apple HIG Onboarding: provide reasonable defaults so people can start using the app immediately.
principles.implication: Today shows the address's reading before asking anything. Asks are capped at three: pickup day, one date, household. Missing rows in the place file are optional invitations. Add-place is one field. Mover rows and the household block can be dismissed and brought back.

principles.principle: A widget earns its place with one primary use case and content that changes. It should deep-link to the exact detail, let the system render relative dates, preview the user's own content where the platform allows, and, on Android, offer an in-app pin request.
principles.evidence: Apple HIG Widgets: 'Prefer dynamic information that changes throughout the day'; 'Deep link to details and actions that directly relate to the widget's content'; 'Use system functionality to refresh dates and times'; placeholders should be semi-opaque shapes standing in for content; gallery descriptions should 'Begin a description with an action verb'. Android widget quality guide: Tier 1 previews include user content or the system theme; the description helps users understand the widget's value; minimum touch target 48x48; a Tier 3 failure is a widget that doesn't update after a related action in the app; use the system corner radius. Android (Glance docs): 'With Android 8.0 (API level 26) and higher, you can let users pin your widgets to their home screen within your app' through a pin request dialog, if the launcher supports it.
principles.implication: 'That's my day' rewrites the widget snapshot immediately. The gallery description starts with a verb. On Android, the how-to sheet leads with a pin request button when the launcher supports it. Widget taps land on the exact card that produced the fact.

principles.principle: When inviting household members, name what each role can see and do before the invite is sent.
principles.evidence: Google Home offers Admin and Member roles. Admins can add and remove people and delete the home. Members have two separate toggles, Activity (device history, kept up to 60 days) and Settings; without them a member gets basic controls only. Sampled Rocket Money praise includes being able to share the budget with a spouse.
principles.implication: The invite composer's review list reuses the grant and lock columns from the invitation decision screen, so the sender sees what the invitee will see: calendar, bills, who lives here. Bill rows show who paid so two people don't pay the same bill.

principles.principle: A companion creature works when it encourages without guilt, can be personalized, and is never used as a channel for promotions or notifications the user can't act on.
principles.evidence: Finch: Self-Care Pet has 4.95 stars from 752,405 ratings. In the sampled reviews, 12 praise the pet for motivation without pressure and 5 enjoy customizing it. The complaints are about month-long movie promotions and notifications users can't interact with.
principles.implication: The keeper sends no push of its own and carries no promotions. Its mood comes only from records and has an 'unavailable' state. Rename, Change species and Remove are always available. The keeper and the fact count never become an app-icon badge.

principles.principle: Make status freshness and partial failure explicit. A generic 'something went wrong' or a device silently shown offline is the top complaint about home-control apps.
principles.evidence: In the sampled Google Home reviews, 22 of 50 were about reliability, including every device suddenly showing offline behind an 'Oops, something went wrong' message; 8 were about hard-to-find settings. In the sampled Ring reviews, 18 were about reliability. Apple HIG Widgets: 'Keep your widget up to date.'
principles.implication: Every data card names its age ('Observed 6:00 AM · AirNow — 9 hours ago') and the provider that failed ('We couldn't reach AirNow just now'), while the rest of the screen still renders. Stale is drawn differently from empty.

patterns.name: Night-before collection reminder as the core habit
patterns.exemplars: Recycle Coach (4.78 stars, 25K ratings) and WasteConnect (4.71 stars, 9.3K): in sampled reviews, users praise weekly reminders so they don't forget the bins, and say they check the app to see what to expect. Their 1-star reviews are about wrong dates, holidays not handled and addresses not found, not about the reminder itself.
patterns.howToApply: Keep the pickup push as the single weekly trigger. Pair it with a holiday-shift row, a household confirmation that overrides the city rule, and a correction loop that visibly acknowledges reports.
patterns.pitfalls: A reminder that fires on an unhandled holiday shift costs more trust than no reminder at all. Stale municipal data (as in the ReCollect Miramar app) makes the reminder a liability.

patterns.name: Published accuracy plus owner correction
patterns.exemplars: Redfin Estimate publishes a median error of 1.87% on-market and 7.28% off-market, lets owners edit home facts, and lets them post an Owner Estimate with their own comparables. Zillow publishes roughly 7% off-market error.
patterns.howToApply: The provenance sheet's confidence sentence plays the role of the accuracy statement. 'This isn't right' and household confirmation play the role of owner correction. Show public-record values with their authority, not a modeled value.
patterns.pitfalls: Publishing accuracy does not stop owner anger when a single house is badly off (Zillow reviews). The correction path must be reachable from the fact itself.

patterns.name: Named permissions at invite time
patterns.exemplars: Google Home: pick Admin or Member when inviting by email; Members get separate Activity and Settings toggles.
patterns.howToApply: Show the Member grant list (calendar, bills, tasks, who lives here) in the invite composer's review list and on the invitee's decision screen, using the same rows.
patterns.pitfalls: Toggles that exist on only one side (sender or invitee) create 'why can't I see bills?' confusion.

patterns.name: One list of recurring obligations
patterns.exemplars: Rocket Money: sampled reviews praise automatic detection of every recurring charge and sharing with a spouse. The complaints are about predicted bill dates that need checking every week.
patterns.howToApply: The place file's Dates and Money rows and the 14-day strip form one list of obligations, with a provenance mark on every row. Machine-read amounts are confirmed before they count.
patterns.pitfalls: Predicted dates shown as facts force the weekly re-checking that Rocket Money users complain about. Keep the hollow mark until a person confirms.

patterns.name: Soft ask in context, then the OS prompt
patterns.exemplars: Android's documented flow: user action, then an in-context rationale with a 'no thanks', then the system dialog. Apple HIG: the current context should explain the request; any pre-alert screen has a single 'Continue'.
patterns.howToApply: The Today opt-in card and the pickup card are the context and hold the real Yes / Not now. iOS goes straight to the system alert, or through a one-button primer. The Android rationale keeps 'Not now'.
patterns.pitfalls: Asking twice (card, then a second Yes/Not now primer) adds friction. On iOS, a second choice on the pre-alert screen conflicts with the HIG.

patterns.name: Trial (provisional) notifications on iOS
patterns.exemplars: Apple UserNotifications provisional authorization: notifications arrive quietly in Notification Center only, with Keep and Turn Off buttons, so people can judge real notifications before granting full permission.
patterns.howToApply: An option to evaluate for household activity rows (low urgency), so the one full-permission prompt is kept for the pickup push, which must be noticed.
patterns.pitfalls: Provisional notifications never appear on the lock screen or as banners, so they are wrong for the night-before pickup push, whose value depends on being seen.

patterns.name: Actionable notification buttons
patterns.exemplars: Apple HIG: 'Prefer actions that let people perform common, time-saving tasks that eliminate the need to open your app' and 'Avoid providing an action that merely opens your app.' Android addAction() can run the work in the background.
patterns.howToApply: The unconfirmed pickup push can offer 'That's My Day' as a notification action that confirms the rule and rewrites the widget snapshot. Bill reminders can offer 'Mark Paid' only after an explicit confirmation step in the app.
patterns.pitfalls: Destructive or money-related actions from the tray without review. The HIG says to prefer nondestructive actions.

patterns.name: In-app widget pin request (Android)
patterns.exemplars: Android 8.0+ lets apps show a system pin dialog if the launcher supports it (Glance: requestPinGlanceAppWidget).
patterns.howToApply: Place-file row 'Put today on your home screen': on supporting Android launchers, show a primary 'Add to home screen' that opens the system dialog, with the three gesture steps as fallback. iOS keeps the gesture teaching.
patterns.pitfalls: Some launchers don't support pinning, so check support first and fall back. The success callback doesn't fire on denial or on unsupported launchers.

patterns.name: Typed address instead of device location
patterns.exemplars: App Store Guideline 5.1.1(iv) names manual address entry as the alternative to location access. Citizen's forced precise location is a recurring 1-star theme.
patterns.howToApply: All Pantopus entry points take a typed address and ask for no location permission. Say this near the field.
patterns.pitfalls: Typed input moves the failure to geocoding, so a manual fallback is mandatory (Baymard).

patterns.name: Lock-screen-safe notifications and widgets
patterns.exemplars: Android VISIBILITY_PRIVATE plus setPublicVersion; Apple HIG generic hidden-preview text ('Reminder').
patterns.howToApply: A public version for every Pantopus push. Place labels at street-name level (as the widget already does: 'Garfield St · Camas'). Generic text for hidden previews.
patterns.pitfalls: For people with several saved places, the label must still say which place without giving the house number. Use the user's own label.

patterns.name: Friction in the form as a safety feature
patterns.exemplars: Nextdoor's 2016 redesign of the crime and safety form required descriptors other than race; the company claimed a 75% reduction in profiling (2017), though BuzzFeed found it incompletely implemented.
patterns.howToApply: Wherever Pantopus lets a person post about a place (Nearby composer), the location picker shows what neighbours will see ('Nearby · Camas, WA'). Comparison flows allow only your own address, never a third one.
patterns.pitfalls: Friction that is only partly implemented (as BuzzFeed found) gives false reassurance.

patterns.name: Guilt-free companion
patterns.exemplars: Finch (4.95 stars, 752K ratings): the pet motivates without pressure, and customizing it delights users. Complaints concern promotions and notifications users can't act on.
patterns.howToApply: The keeper reflects records, never pushes, and never carries promotions. Rename, Change species and Remove are always available.
patterns.pitfalls: Turning the keeper into a retention nag, or showing a cheerful mood when the underlying check failed.

antipatterns: Asking for notification permission at cold launch or before a place exists. Apple HIG Privacy and Android guidance both say to wait for a feature-driven moment, and NN/g says the same.
A pre-alert screen on iOS with a second choice ('Not now', close or cancel) beside the button that opens the system prompt. Apple HIG says to include only one button, titled Continue or Next.

A full street address or house number in a push, lock-screen preview, widget or share card. This conflicts with Apple HIG and App Store 4.5.4 on sensitive information in notifications, and Gizmodo showed hidden precision on Ring Neighbors located homes.
Caveats as a long suffix on a push title or at the end of the body. Both are truncated (HIG; Android truncates text to one line by default).

Two notifications for one event: an evening-briefing pickup push plus a calendar reminder push for the same pickup. HIG: 'Avoid sending multiple notifications for the same thing'. Ring reviewers complain about getting two notifications per alert.
Silently re-enabling notifications or widening scope (radius, neighborhoods, email types) after an update or migration. This is a recurring theme in Nextdoor reviews.
Requiring precise or always-on location. Citizen reviews complain about it, and App Store 5.1.1(iv) asks for a manual-address alternative.
Putting safety or public-record facts behind a paywall or upsell. Citizen's paywall, including sex-offender data, is its top 1-star theme in the sampled reviews.
Unlabeled machine-written or curated alerts, and trending content pushed as 'your neighborhood'. Seen in Citizen reviews (AI errors) and Nextdoor reviews.
Notifications that identify or show a person who might be a suspect. Citizen pushed a wrongly identified man to 860,000 users in 2021.
A modeled home value presented as fact, or without a correction path. Zillow puts off-market error at about 7%, and owners complain about wrong home facts.
A dead-end 'address not found' or a false 'we don't serve this address'. This is the WasteConnect 1-star pattern; Baymard found 69% of people fall back to manual entry.
Setup questionnaires before any payoff. Thumbtack, HomeZada and Hippo reviews complain about this, and NN/g advises skipping onboarding.

Marketing or scarcity messages (Founding slots, referral rewards) sent at Time Sensitive urgency or without explicit opt-in. HIG forbids Time Sensitive marketing, and App Store 4.5.4 requires opt-in for promotional pushes.
Using the app-icon badge for anything other than unread notifications, such as a keeper mood or a count of facts on file. The HIG reserves badges for unread counts.

Push copy that tells the user to do a task inside the app (for example, appending 'Set your pickup day to make it yours'). The HIG warns against this; use a notification action or the in-app card instead.
Generic 'Oops, something went wrong' errors, or devices shown as offline with no reason. This is the top Google Home complaint in the sample.
A button promising to add the widget for the user on iOS, where no such API was found. On Android the capability does exist, so leaving it out there is also a mistake.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The primer offers 'Yes' and 'Not now' side by side at equal weight on both iOS and Android. It opens after the user has already tapped Yes on the Today briefing card.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG Privacy: a custom screen before a system permission alert should 'Include only one button and make it clear that it opens the system alert', titled 'Continue' or 'Next'. It should offer no way to leave without seeing the alert, such as close or cancel. Android's guidance is the opposite: its rationale UI should include a 'no thanks' button.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Split by platform. On iOS, the in-context card holds the only Yes / Not now. Yes then opens the system alert directly, or a primer with just the tray preview and one 'Continue' button (no 'Not now'). On Android, keep 'Not now'. Keep the 'Open Settings' state for the already-denied case.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The example notification title is 'Recycling and garbage tomorrow - City of Camas schedule, not yet confirmed' (about 75 characters), with the caveat as a title suffix 'because a truncated tray line must not eat the honesty'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG: prefer brief titles readable at a glance; the system truncates automatically. Android truncates notification text to one line by default. A caveat placed after roughly 40 characters of title is truncated just like a body tail.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the caveat in the title, but in a short title that ends by about character 30: 'Recycling Tomorrow · Unconfirmed' (title case, no ending punctuation). Start the body with the source: 'City of Camas schedule. Bins out tonight.' Draw the collapsed tray at 393pt and 412dp to prove the caveat survives.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Push title 'Recycling and garbage tomorrow — not yet confirmed'; push body 'Bins out tonight. 2418 NW Lacamas Dr.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG: avoid sensitive or personal information in notifications and provide generic text for hidden previews. App Store 4.5.4: push should not carry sensitive personal information. Android supports a redacted public version. The long title also truncates the caveat.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Title: 'Recycling Tomorrow · Unconfirmed'. Body: 'City of Camas schedule. Bins out tonight · Lacamas Dr' (or the user's own label). Hidden-preview text: 'Pickup reminder'. Draw an Android public-version frame as well.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Push tray card: 'Air is unhealthy for sensitive groups at 2418 NW Lacamas Dr'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Same HIG and App Store 4.5.4 guidance on personal information in notifications. HIG also says Time Sensitive is only for notifications relevant in the moment, and urgency must be represented accurately.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use 'Air Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups · Lacamas Dr' (or the saved label), with the AQI value and the source in the body. Specify that only a real threshold crossing may use the Time Sensitive level. The in-app landing keeps the full address and the 'Saved place · Only you' chip.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: It draws a separate calendar_date reminder push, 'Garbage + recycling is tomorrow (not yet confirmed)', as one of five notification types, while F4 already delivers the same pickup through the evening briefing. The caveat is a parenthetical at the end of the title.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple HIG: 'Avoid sending multiple notifications for the same thing'; repeats lead people to turn off all notifications. Ring reviewers complain about two notifications per alert. The design doc's F5 reminder pass covers only the new date kinds (lease, insurance, warranty, HOA, tax appeal), not pickup.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Replace the pickup example with a real F5 date reminder, such as 'Lease Notice Deadline in 30 Days'. State that pickup arrives only through the evening briefing. Move any caveat to the front of a short title. Also require grouping at the push level, not only in the in-app list.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: 'No public API can place a widget for the user.' Do not add 'Add it for me', 'Install widget' or 'Take me there', because 'no API can do it'. This applies to both iOS and Android.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android documents in-app widget pinning from Android 8.0 (API 26). The app can ask the launcher to show a pin dialog; the success callback fires only if the launcher supports pinning and the user accepts. The fetched doc is the Glance page (requestPinGlanceAppWidget). The framework method for the RemoteViews widget, AppWidgetManager.requestPinAppWidget, was not fetched and needs checking. No equivalent iOS API was found.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: On Android, when the launcher supports pinning, show a primary 'Add to home screen' under the live preview that opens the system pin dialog. Keep the three gesture steps as the fallback for unsupported launchers and for iOS. Add frames for 'pin dialog shown' and 'launcher doesn't support pinning'. Update the surface-index job line too.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Build a dedicated preview composition with baked sample content, never the live layout bound to real state. Description: 'Pickup, air and your next date — no notification needed.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android widget quality guide, Tier 1: 'Preview includes user content and/or applies a system theme'. Apple HIG: 'Begin a description with an action verb' and avoid unnecessary phrases.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the baked sample as the fallback for users with no data. Where the platform supports it, render the picker preview from the user's real snapshot, never an empty state. Reword the description to start with a verb: 'See tomorrow's pickup, today's air and your next date at your address.'

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Geocode failure shows only 'We couldn't find that address.' in place of the suggestions, with no second step. An address outside the pilot area gets 'We only cover Clark County, Washington right now.'
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Baymard: always keep manual address fields available; 69% of participants tried manual entry when autocomplete failed and were often at a loss without the fields. In sampled WasteConnect reviews, most 1-star reviews are about address lookup, including being told an address isn't served when it is. The design doc also decides the pilot is 'available nationwide, observed locally', which contradicts a Clark-County-only refusal.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add 'Can't find it? Enter it line by line' (street, city, ZIP) inside the same detent as the recovery for a failed geocode. Replace the Clark County refusal: save the address and state which layers exist there. Rank suggestions by proximity and tolerate typos.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The caption says 'Your post lands somewhere inside this circle. It is re-rolled every time you post.' presented as the protection, next to 'Your public posts: 7'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Gizmodo (2019) mapped up to 20,000 Ring camera locations by aggregating about 65,800 Neighbors posts whose coordinates were hidden from the UI. Aggregation across posts is the documented threat. The claim that per-post random jitter centred on one point shrinks under averaging (roughly the radius divided by the square root of the post count) is reasoning here, not a fetched source.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Have a privacy engineer confirm how the jitter is actually generated before this copy ships. Prefer a stable coarse cell (one fixed offset or a snapped centroid per place) over a fresh random offset per post. Change the caption to describe what cannot be recovered even across many posts, and don't present re-rolling as a protection.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Native lede: 'Your flood risk, today's air, your home's value, and who your verified neighbors are — free, no account.' Web lede ends with 'the neighbors who've proven they're real'. Both sit directly above the contrast line saying Pantopus is not the neighbours' app.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Modeled home values have about 7% median error off-market (Zillow per Wikipedia; Redfin 7.28%), and owner complaints about them are common (Zillow and Homebot reviews). The in-app instrument deliberately shows only four sourced public-record layers and an assessor value. Neighbor-sourced content is where the fear and moderation complaints concentrate (18 of 50 sampled Nextdoor reviews; the Citizen incidents).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Replace 'your home's value' with a sourced public-record fact, such as 'your county assessed value', or drop it. Lead both ledes with public-record layers and move verified neighbours out of the first clause, so the lede no longer contradicts the contrast line under it.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Per-home notification toggles are 'DELETED, not rewired' into the new page. No state shows what happened to values users had set before. The AQI threshold control defaults to 'Unhealthy (151+)'.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Nextdoor reviews repeatedly complain that updates change notification settings and widen scope without consent. NN/g notes users rarely customize defaults, so the migrated default becomes the setting. Apple HIG asks for honest urgency. The design doc says alert_checker fires at AQI ≥ 101, so a default of 151 would show a setting that doesn't match what the server sends, unless the backend adds a per-user threshold.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add a one-time 'migrated' state: 'We moved your home reminder settings here. Nothing you turned off was turned on.' Carry every 'off' value forward. Make the threshold's default match what the server actually enforces, or mark the control as depending on backend support for per-user thresholds.

numbers: iOS pre-permission screen: exactly 1 button, titled 'Continue' or 'Next'; no close or cancel (Apple HIG Privacy).

Android: after the user taps Deny more than once, the system notification permission dialog never appears again; apps targeting 12L or lower get one refusal before a reinstall is needed (Android docs).
Android: defer the notification prompt to a meaningful user action, or to about the 3rd or 4th app launch (Android notification-permission docs).

Android notification text is truncated to 1 line by default; use BigTextStyle for more. Aim for push titles of about 30 characters so an 'Unconfirmed' caveat stays visible. No exact limit is published, so test at 393pt (iOS) and 412dp (Android).
Apple Time Sensitive interruption level: only for notifications 'relevant in the moment', never for marketing; Critical requires an entitlement (HIG Managing Notifications).
NN/g (2018, citing 2016 data): about 56 notifications per day per phone user; combine 5 or more simultaneous alerts into one.
Widgets: minimum touch target 48x48dp (Android widget quality guide); animated update transitions up to 2 seconds (Apple HIG Widgets); in-app widget pin request available from Android 8.0 (API 26).
Baymard address lookup: 69% of participants tried manual entry when autocomplete failed; 9% of manually typed addresses contained typos; 55% of e-commerce sites lack autocomplete.

Pew 2023 (n=5,101): 73% feel little or no control over company data; 67% understand little or nothing about companies' data use (up from 59%); about 1 in 5 are confident companies handle data responsibly; 56% often agree to privacy policies without reading them.
Home valuation error, median: Redfin 1.87% on-market, 7.28% off-market; Zillow about 2% listed and about 7% off-market (per Wikipedia, 2026).
Ring Neighbors leak (Gizmodo, Dec 2019): coordinates up to 6 decimal places; about 65,800 posts; up to 20,000 cameras mapped, often within 4 to 6 feet of a home; MIT database of 440,000 cameras.
Ring: $5.8M FTC settlement (May 2023); police Request for Assistance ended Jan 2024; Search Party launched Oct 2025, on by default; Flock partnership cancelled 13 Feb 2026.
Life360 (The Markup, 2021): 33M users; location-data revenue $16M in 2020, nearly 20% of revenue.

Citizen: launched as 'Vigilante' in 2016 and pulled within 48 hours; May 2021 misidentification pushed to 860,000 users with a $30,000 reward; sampled page-2 reviews: 15 of 50 about the paywall, 7 of 50 about forced precise location.
Nextdoor: 4.7 stars from 2.1M ratings; claimed 75% reduction in racial profiling after the 2016 form redesign (claim made 2017).

App Store ratings as fetched (Sep 2026): Recycle Coach 4.78 (25,233); WasteConnect 4.71 (9,359); ReCollect-built Miramar app 2.63 (30); HomeZada 2.86 (44); Homebot 3.74 (125); Rocket Money 4.5 (391K); Life360 4.8 (3.1M); Thumbtack 4.89 (467,788); Finch 4.95 (752,405); Citizen 4.7 (517K); Zillow 4.80 (7.2M); Redfin 4.80 (1.6M).
Google Home: household Member role has separate Activity and Settings toggles; activity history is kept up to 60 days (thermostat history up to 2 years).

topic: share-compare-civic: shareable cards, the compare flow, referrals, honest scarcity and civic deadlines

principles.principle: Put the message in the unfurl's text metadata, not in the image. Keep type in the image few in number and large.
principles.evidence: Apple TN3156 (Create rich previews for Messages) says to avoid text in preview images because images appear at different sizes by context and device, which can make text unreadable. It asks for images at least 900 px wide; images under 150 px wide may be ignored or shown as icons. Icons should be at least 108x108. Link previews do not follow meta redirects or run JavaScript, so metadata must be on the linked page itself. Titles should be short and specific. The Open Graph spec says that if a page specifies og:image it should also specify og:image:alt, which is a description of the image and not a caption. WCAG 1.4.5 asks for real text instead of images of text so users can adjust how text is presented.
principles.implication: The compare card frame spec should cover the whole unfurl, not only the PNG. og:title carries the question ("What's on record at Maya's place. Yours?"). og:description carries the sources and the contrast line. og:image:alt reads out the four readings. Inside the 1200x630 image, keep only the layer names, the band names, the filled/hollow marks, the sender line and "Yours?". Cap height should be at least ~40 px at 1200 wide so text is still ~13 px when rendered 400 wide. Headline text in the image should be at most ~60 characters, or dropped. Draw the Messages bubble with the title line under the image, because that text line is what reliably stays readable.

principles.principle: Author the card at 1200x630 (1.91:1), declare its size, and treat each image URL as immutable.
principles.evidence: Meta's sharing guidance recommends 1200x630 and keeping close to 1.91:1 to avoid cropping. It gives 600x315 as the minimum for large link images and an 8 MB maximum. Declaring og:image:width and og:image:height lets the crawler render the image immediately without downloading it first. A changed image needs a new URL because crawlers cache it. Apple caps the linked page at 1 MB and associated resources at 10 MB in total. Slack's classic unfurl reads Open Graph and X Card metadata and renders a 'micro-approximation'. I could not fetch X's summary_large_image spec (the docs returned HTTP 402), so any '2:1' or WhatsApp size or weight figure is unverified.
principles.implication: The OG route emits og:image:width=1200, og:image:height=630 and og:image:alt. The token-specific image URL can be cached, which matches the design doc's max-age=3600. Any redesign of the generic card needs a versioned URL. Put the essentials in the central band so a 2:1 or near-square crop does not cut the sender line or "Yours?" (hedge, not a verified spec). Add frames for a light iMessage thread and a narrow Slack message (~360 px wide) next to the existing dark-thread frame.

principles.principle: A share artifact spreads when it shows a result without exposing the private thing. The privacy has to be built into the artifact itself, because platform controls do not travel with shared content.
principles.evidence: Wordle's share is an emoji grid that shows performance without revealing the answer. 1.2 million results were shared on Twitter between Jan 1 and 13, 2022, and players grew from 90 (Nov 1, 2021) to over 300,000 (Jan 2, 2022). Strava hides the first and last 200 m of activity maps by default, but its help page says Map Visibility controls are not shared to other services. Strava's aggregate heatmap still exposed military bases (2018) and leaders' security details (Le Monde, 2024–2025). Spotify Wrapped, a story format since 2019, has been criticised as packaged surveillance: a lullaby-heavy Wrapped can reveal a young child in the home.
principles.implication: Keep the token address-free by construction (v1 already does). Also audit re-identification: first name plus a small city plus a rare reading (e.g. Zone AE) can narrow a location, so the sheet preview must render exactly the token's contents and nothing more. Once shared, a stateless token cannot be revoked, so the privacy line should also say who can see it and for how long ("Anyone with the link can see this card until {exp}"). Never add a map, pin, street fragment or house image, even blurred.

principles.principle: Show consent before anything goes out in the user's name, and one consent covers exactly one message. No automated follow-ups and no address-book import.
principles.evidence: The FTC staff report (Sept 2022) lists 'Friend Spam, Social Pyramid Schemes, and Address Book Leeching' and 'Nagging' as dark patterns. In Perkins v. LinkedIn, the court found users had consented to invitations but not to the two reminder emails LinkedIn sent on their behalf; LinkedIn settled for $13M in 2015. Nextdoor's mailed invitation letters credited to local residents drew complaints from people named without permission, or who thought they were only asking for more information.
principles.implication: Postcard invites need a front/back preview showing exactly how the sender is named, placed above 'Send postcard invite'. The compare sheet keeps the preview → privacy line → toggle → action order. No surface offers 'remind them', contact import or bulk invites. The allowance counter is the only nudge, and it sits on the sender's own screen.

principles.principle: Use the platform share sheet and give it rich metadata. Treat a dismissed share as neutral, and never call share after an async wait.
principles.evidence: Android guidance: 'Don't display your app's own list of share targets or create your own Sharesheet variations.' Add a preview with EXTRA_TITLE and a thumbnail via ClipData. The chooser callback reports the chosen target only. Apple HIG says to use the Share button to present an activity view, and activityViewControllerLinkMetadata supplies the title, icon and image for the sheet's preview header. MDN says navigator.share needs transient activation ('must be triggered off a UI event like a button click'). It rejects with AbortError both when the user cancels and when no share targets are available, and it is not Baseline across browsers.
principles.implication: On web, mint the token when the sheet opens and again when the name toggle changes, so the Share tap calls navigator.share synchronously. A stateless, unsent token is not a publication, so pre-minting does not make consent retroactive. Treat AbortError as 'back to ready, with Copy link still visible', never as an error. Browsers without Web Share get Copy. On iOS, supply LPLinkMetadata so the sheet header shows the card title and image instead of a bare URL. On Android, draw the system Sharesheet with a title such as 'Compare your place with mine', and no app-drawn chooser.

principles.principle: Compare two readings by overlaying them on one shared scale, and keep the attribute order fixed across every compare surface. Highlight what differs instead of reordering.
principles.evidence: Gleicher et al. (2011) show that all comparison designs are built from juxtaposition, superposition and explicit encoding. Ondov et al. (2018, crowdsourced perceptual experiments) found overlaid layouts beat standard juxtaposed small multiples for spotting value changes; mirror-symmetric and animated layouts also helped. NN/g calls inconsistent attributes 'the biggest problem with most comparison tables'. It cites Best Buy's 'Highlight Differences' toggle, which keeps rows aligned, and recommends limiting a mobile comparison to 2 items.
principles.implication: The reveal keeps the single shared track with both marks (v1 is right about this), at 390 px and at desktop. Rows stay in the same Flood · Wildfire · Air · Radon order the user just saw in the arrival header, OG card and scale strips. A differing row gets emphasis, such as a 'Differs' tag or strong weight, plus an optional summary line above ("1 of 4 layers differs: Flood"). At ≥768 px, don't split the marks into two separate tracks; use the second column for the recipient's own aha.

principles.principle: Compare like with like. A frozen reading must carry its own date and must not be labelled 'today' or compared with a live one.
principles.evidence: NN/g: inconsistent or missing attributes make a comparison table useless. Pantopus's own honesty rules require sources, and the design doc notes that 'Air is time-varying and says "today"'. The compare token is frozen at mint time (the arrival header shows "Dana's card, as of Sep 12, 2026"), so its AQI is not today's air.
principles.implication: In any token-rendered context (OG card, arrival header, reveal), label the sender's air row "Air on Sep 12 · AirNow", not "Air today". Alternatively, drop air from the compare instrument and keep the three static layers. Don't put a Sep-12 AQI and a Sep-16 AQI on one track without both dates.

principles.principle: Comparisons with others set off social-norm reactions. Choose the evaluative layer on purpose: for place hazards, offer an action from the authority, not approval or disapproval.
principles.evidence: Schultz et al. (2007, field experiment): showing average neighborhood energy use produced savings or a boomerang effect depending on each household's baseline, and adding an injunctive (approval/disapproval) cue removed the boomerang. How a comparison is framed changes the response.
principles.implication: Hazards are not behaviour, so no approval glyphs (smileys, ticks, 'better'). When the recipient's reading is the more serious one, pair it with a neutral next step from the authority, e.g. "What Zone AE means · FEMA" or "Free test kits · WA Dept of Health", so the difference leads somewhere other than anxiety. v1's ban on winner/versus/arrows stays.

principles.principle: Show scarcity or urgency only when it is true, checked right now, and ends when it says it ends. Show a date, not a ticking clock.
principles.evidence: The FTC staff report lists 'Baseless Countdown Timer' (a clock that disappears or resets when it times out), 'False Limited Time Message', 'False Low Stock Message', 'False High Demand' and 'False Activity Messages'. Mathur et al. (2019) crawled ~53K product pages on ~11K sites and found 1,818 dark-pattern instances, including 393 countdown timers on 361 sites (many offers stayed valid after expiry) and 632 low-stock messages on 581 sites. The CMA (April 2022, §4.7) says true scarcity claims can help people avoid missing out and overcome procrastination, while false ones such as 'countdown clocks that reset' put undue pressure on consumers. The CMA fined Viagogo over artificial-scarcity practices (reported by deceptive.design). Clubhouse's invite scarcity pushed codes to $400 on eBay, then weekly users fell 21% in three weeks.
principles.implication: Keep the slot meter only after a successful lookup (v1 already fails closed). Show the window end as a date in neutral tokens: no hh:mm, no pulsing, no warning tint on a badge. After it closes, the line disappears, and a new window for the same cell needs a stated reason. Say what the slot is (a badge; no money, no fee change) and what the user keeps if they miss it ("You can still claim this address"). Keep warning tokens for real civic and bill deadlines.

principles.principle: A referral reward is honest when it states the rule, the cap and the stage each invitee has reached, and when the recipient can see that the sender benefits.
principles.evidence: Dropbox states '500 MB per referral and can earn up to 16 GB' (Basic) or 1 GB up to 32 GB (paid). The friend gets 500 MB. Four conditions make a referral count, and progress shows four stages: Invitation sent / Waiting for install / Waiting for email verification / Completed. Ryu & Feick (2007, J. Marketing, four experiments): rewards raise referral likelihood most for weak ties and weaker brands; for strong ties with stronger brands, giving the receiver at least some reward works better. Tuk et al. (2009): a reward lowers the perceived sincerity of the referrer, and disclosing the motive mitigates this. FTC endorsement guidance expects compensation behind a recommendation to be disclosed. Massachusetts regulators accused Robinhood of gamification (Dec 2020); it paid $7.5M and agreed to overhaul its engagement practices (Feb 2024).
principles.implication: State the rewards card's tiers as the server's actual formula, with the cap spelled out ("Each neighbor who joins: +1 postcard invite every week, up to +3"). Replace the lone '3 joined · 11 invited' with per-invitee stages that match what counts (Invited → Joined → Address verified). The /join landing tells the recipient that the sender benefits and what the recipient gets (their own place reading). No confetti, lottery or mystery rewards. A locked tier states only its requirement.

principles.principle: Give civic deadlines per state and per method, in the official wording ('received by'), with the state as the source. Never collapse them into one 'registration closes' date.
principles.evidence: Washington Secretary of State: 'Online and mail registrations must be received 8 days before Election Day' (Oct 26 for the Nov 3, 2026 general), and you can 'Register to vote in person during business hours and any time before 8:00 p.m. on Election Day.' Vote.org shows each state's deadlines split into In Person, By Mail ('postmarked' vs 'received by') and Online, with the note 'It's best to double check with your state.' The EAC tells voters to verify summaries through linked state and local sources.
principles.implication: Any single-line civic headline names the method: "Online or mail voter registration for Nov 3 must arrive by Oct 26 in Washington." (80 characters, which fits the 90-character token). Every row that says 'voter registration deadline Oct 26' should say 'online/mail'. The in-person path (until 8 p.m. Nov 3) always appears as the second line or row. From Oct 27 to 8 p.m. Nov 3, the headline switches to the in-person path instead of disappearing. The source is 'Washington Secretary of State'.

principles.principle: Never state or imply someone's registration status. Send the check to the official state lookup, and keep 'I did this' a labelled, personal self-report.
principles.evidence: Vote.org's registration tool lists an 'Am I registered to vote in [State]?' link to each state's official lookup (for Washington, VoteWA). In 2008, the Voter Participation Center's automated calls in North Carolina gave confusing information that may have led voters to believe they were not registered, and the Attorney General ordered a $100,000 fine. Its 2024 'Voting Report Card' mailers, which showed names, addresses and voting records, were called 'invasive, intimidating, and threatening', and Maryland's AG sent a cease-and-desist. The design doc also says: 'Never claim to know whether the user is registered.'
principles.implication: The civic block's 'Check or update' is an outbound, external-glyph link to VoteWA. The Date sheet is a separate 'Remind me' action. The 'I did this' tick reads "You marked this done", belongs to the person who tapped it, and is never shown to the household as a fact about the address. No copy such as 'You're registered', 'You may not be registered' or 'Your household is registered'.

principles.principle: Help people make a concrete plan (how and when) rather than only encouraging them.
principles.evidence: Nickerson & Rogers (2010, Psychological Science) ran a field experiment in the 2008 US presidential election with 287,228 people. Helping people form a voting plan raised turnout by 4.1 percentage points, while standard encouragement and self-prediction had no significant effect. The gain was 9.1 points in single-eligible-voter households and zero in multi-voter households. The context was phone calls, so applying this to an app is an inference.
principles.implication: In the voter-registration kind of the Date sheet, add an optional one-tap plan: 'How will you do it? Online · By mail · In person', optionally with 'When?'. The reminder then targets that method's deadline (Oct 26 for online or mail, and earlier for mail to allow transit; Nov 3 by 8 p.m. in person). 'I did this' stays available as a separate self-report.

principles.principle: Write deadlines unambiguously: weekday + date, exact official time only when the authority states one, 'on or before' or 'received by', and never 'midnight'.
principles.evidence: The GOV.UK style guide writes dates like '4 June 2017' and times like '5:30pm', warns that 'midnight' causes day confusion (use 11:59pm), and says to use 'on or before' for deadlines. The WA SOS page gives no clock time for the online/mail deadline, only 'received 8 days before', but does give 8:00 p.m. for in-person registration on Election Day.
principles.implication: Write 'Received by Mon, Oct 26' with no invented clock time, and 'In person until 8:00 p.m. Tue, Nov 3 (Pacific)', adding the timezone when the device is outside Pacific time. Day counts ('40 days left', '18 days') are calendar days in the state's timezone. On the day itself, write 'Today' rather than '0 days'.

principles.principle: Quiet share controls still need full touch targets, announced status and readable contrast, including in the OG image.
principles.evidence: WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (≥18pt regular or ≥14pt bold, roughly 24 px and 18.5 px), and it covers images of text too. WCAG 4.1.3 requires status messages (such as confirmations) to be exposed with role=status or a live region. WCAG 2.5.8 sets a 24x24 CSS px minimum. Apple asks for a 44x44 pt hit region and says to 'Use style — not size' to mark the preferred option and to keep one or two prominent buttons per view. Google recommends 48x48 dp targets with 8 dp spacing. Computed with the house tokens: text.muted #9CA3AF on #FFFFFF is 2.54:1 (fails), text.secondary #6B7280 is 4.83:1 (passes), and warning #D97706 on warning-bg #FFFBEB is 3.07:1 (fails for small text).
principles.implication: The two tertiary text buttons get 44 pt / 48 dp hit areas with at least 8 dp between them, even without borders. 'Link copied' is a role=status message. Caption-size text never uses text.muted on white. Warning chips use text.strong or text.primary for their label, with the warning color only on the glyph or border. OG card body text meets 4.5:1.
