principles.principle: Name a competitor only in a truthful, plain-text contrast, with no borrowed branding.
principles.evidence: The FTC's 1979 Statement of Policy on comparative advertising encourages naming competitors, provided the comparison is truthful and non-deceptive, and judges it case by case like any other claim.
principles.implication: The contrast line stays one sentence of caption type (v1 is right about this). 'Nextdoor' is never set in their logo, colours or wordmark, including on the OG card. The sentence is a description, with no claims about Nextdoor's accuracy or safety.

patterns.name: Result-without-the-secret share artifact
patterns.exemplars: Wordle's emoji grid shares the outcome without spoiling the answer (1.2M shares Jan 1–13, 2022). Strava hides the first and last 200 m of activity maps by default. Spotify Wrapped's story cards share taste, not listening logs, though it is still criticised for what it implies.
patterns.howToApply: The compare card is the grid: four band names and a city, nothing that locates a house. Build the privacy into the token, because nothing on the Pantopus side can follow the image once it is posted.
patterns.pitfalls: Rare readings plus a first name plus a small town can still identify someone. A frozen reading labelled 'today' is a small lie that spreads with the card.

patterns.name: Unfurl-first metadata: title as the hook, image as the proof
patterns.exemplars: Apple TN3156: short, specific og:title, og:site_name for branding, no text in images. Meta: 1200x630 with declared width and height. OGP: og:image:alt always.
patterns.howToApply: Specify og:title ("What's on record at Maya's place. Yours?"), og:description (sources and contrast line) and og:image:alt as part of the OG frame set. Render them in the mock iMessage and Slack frames.
patterns.pitfalls: Metadata injected by client JavaScript is invisible to link previewers.

patterns.name: Arrival page that shows the friend's side and leaves an input-shaped gap
patterns.exemplars: No verified public teardown found. The pattern follows from NN/g's two-item mobile comparison guidance and the v1 arrival spec.
patterns.howToApply: Keep the sender strip collapsed above an autofocused field on phones, in the same fixed layer order the reveal will use. Never block typing on token verification.
patterns.pitfalls: Stacking the sender card pushes the field below the fold. Re-sorting rows between arrival and reveal breaks object constancy.

patterns.name: Superposed shared-scale comparison
patterns.exemplars: Ondov et al. 2018: overlaid layouts beat juxtaposed small multiples for spotting deltas. Best Buy's 'Highlight Differences' toggle (cited by NN/g) keeps rows aligned and flags differences.
patterns.howToApply: One track per authority, two marks (sender filled, 'You' ringed), a merged mark when both fall in the same band, a fixed row order, and emphasis on differing rows.
patterns.pitfalls: Sorting by mark distance creates an implicit cross-layer metric. Two facing scorecards invite a winner.

patterns.name: System share sheet with rich preview and a copy fallback
patterns.exemplars: Android Sharesheet with EXTRA_TITLE and a ClipData thumbnail. iOS UIActivityViewController with LPLinkMetadata in the header. Web navigator.share called inside the click handler.
patterns.howToApply: Pre-mint the link so the tap shares at once. Treat AbortError as neutral and leave Copy link visible. On iOS and Android, supply the card title and image to the system header.
patterns.pitfalls: An async mint between tap and share can lose transient activation. On Android there is no cancel callback, so don't design a 'cancelled' state there.

patterns.name: Staged, capped, two-sided referral ledger
patterns.exemplars: Dropbox shows the per-referral amount and lifetime cap, gives the friend a reward too, and shows each invitee's stage (Invitation sent → Waiting for install → Waiting for email verification → Completed).
patterns.howToApply: The rewards card lists invitees by stage (Invited / Joined / Address verified), states the weekly bonus rule with its cap, and puts the reward the user already has first. The /join landing says what the recipient gets and that the sender benefits.
patterns.pitfalls: Tier copy that disagrees with the server formula, rewards the user already holds shown as locked, confetti or lottery mechanics.

patterns.name: Truthful dated window
patterns.exemplars: CMA §4.7: accurate scarcity helps overcome procrastination. The FTC lists resetting timers as baseless. v1's founding meter already shows a date and fails closed.
patterns.howToApply: Five-segment meter plus a closing date, shown only after a successful lookup. It disappears at close and never restarts silently. The copy says what the slot is and that claiming still works without it.
patterns.pitfalls: Warning-tinted countdown pills for a badge, live hh:mm timers, an empty meter that reads as 'all open'.

patterns.name: Per-method deadline table with an official-lookup hand-off
patterns.exemplars: Vote.org's state table splits In Person, By Mail (postmarked vs received) and Online, and links 'Am I registered to vote in [State]?' to each state's official lookup. The WA SOS calendar gives both the online/mail and in-person rules.
patterns.howToApply: Two rows per state ('Online or by mail — received by Mon Oct 26'; 'In person at Clark County Elections — until 8:00 p.m. Tue Nov 3'), the WA Secretary of State as source, an outbound 'Check or update at VoteWA', and a separate 'Remind me'.
patterns.pitfalls: One 'registration closes' date. Hiding the card after the mail deadline while in-person registration is still open. Buttons labelled 'Check' that open an internal sheet.

patterns.name: Plan-making prompt with a labelled self-report
patterns.exemplars: Nickerson & Rogers 2010: asking how and when someone will vote raised turnout 4.1 points, while plain encouragement did nothing measurable.
patterns.howToApply: In the voter kind: an optional method picker (Online / Mail / In person) that picks which deadline the reminder fires on, plus a personal 'I did this' tick labelled as the user's own report.
patterns.pitfalls: Implying registration status. Sharing one person's tick as a household fact.

antipatterns: A single 'Voter registration closes Oct 26' headline in Washington: wrong, because only online and mail registration closes then; in-person registration runs until 8 p.m. on Nov 3 (WA SOS).
Hiding the civic card or showing 'No upcoming election' once the mail deadline passes: that removes the one remaining path to register at the moment a late mover needs it most.
Any copy that states or hints at registration status ('You're registered', 'You may need to register'): the product cannot know this, and misleading status calls led to a $100,000 fine in NC in 2008.
A 'Check' button that opens an internal sheet instead of the official state lookup (VoteWA): the label promises verification the product cannot do.
Dense captions, long headlines or full sentences baked into the OG PNG: Apple says to avoid text in preview images because they render at unpredictable sizes.
An OG image with no og:image:alt, or metadata that only JavaScript produces: link previewers do not run JS, and OGP asks for alt whenever og:image is set.

Calling navigator.share after awaiting a network mint: this risks losing transient activation. Also, styling AbortError as a failure is wrong, since it also fires when the user simply closes the sheet.
App-drawn share-target lists or a custom 'Material 3 chooser' on Android: Google explicitly says not to build your own Sharesheet variations.
Re-sorting compare rows by 'distance between marks': this creates a cross-layer ranking across four incommensurable authorities and moves rows the user just saw.

Versus badges, winner labels, arrows, smiley or frowny approval cues on a place comparison: evaluative framing changes how people respond to social comparisons (Schultz 2007), and here it would judge a home.
Labelling a frozen token's AQI as 'Air today': the token was minted days earlier.
hh:mm:ss countdowns, pulsing timers, windows that silently restart, or warning-tinted urgency on a badge: FTC 'Baseless Countdown Timer', CMA 'countdown clocks that reset'.
'Only N left' or 'N neighbors viewing' lines rendered without a successful live lookup: FTC 'False Low Stock' and 'False Activity Messages'. An empty 5-segment meter reads as all open.

Contact-book import, automatic reminder emails or texts to invitees, or postcards naming the sender without a per-send preview: Perkins v. LinkedIn ($13M, consent did not cover reminders) and complaints about Nextdoor's resident-credited letters.
Confetti, lottery or mystery-box referral rewards: gamification was central to the Massachusetts action against Robinhood ($7.5M, 2024).
Referral tier copy that disagrees with the server formula, or a locked tier paying something the user already has: this breaks the 'what a referral actually pays' promise.
Hiding from the recipient that the sender earns something: Tuk et al. 2009 show undisclosed rewards hurt perceived sincerity, and disclosure mitigates it.
Blurred, fogged or lock-iconed maps as a referral carrot: in a sparse pilot this turns 'nothing here yet' into 'withheld'.
Caption or contrast-line text in text.muted (#9CA3AF) on white (2.54:1) and small warning-coloured chip labels (#D97706 on #FFFBEB, 3.07:1): both fail WCAG 1.4.3.
Using a competitor's logo, colours or wordmark in the contrast line or OG footer: truthful comparative claims are fine, borrowed branding is not needed and invites confusion.
Stating unverified platform specs (X 2:1, WhatsApp 300 KB, fixed OG safe-area percentages) as fact in prompts: I could not verify them in this research pass.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Headline "Voter registration for November 3 closes October 26 in Washington." This string is also reused verbatim by f8-compare-sheet, f8-compare-arrival-header and f8-og-compare-card.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WA Secretary of State: online and mail registrations must be received 8 days before Election Day (Oct 26), and in-person registration is open until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day (Nov 3, 2026). Registration does not close on Oct 26. Vote.org and the EAC both present deadlines per method and send users to the state.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Replace it with a method-specific line within the 90-character token limit, e.g. "Online or mail voter registration for Nov 3 must arrive by Oct 26 in Washington." (80 chars). The detail line reads "In person: until 8 p.m. Nov 3 at your county elections office." Update the same string on the compare sheet preview, arrival header and OG card.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: "The deadline already passed → the seasonal card is suppressed entirely and the ranked aha renders instead"; "Do not ever render a deadline that has passed."
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Once the Oct 26 online/mail deadline passes, WA still allows in-person registration until 8:00 p.m. Nov 3. For a recent mover, that is the most urgent civic fact of the year.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Add a second phase from Oct 27 to 8:00 p.m. Pacific on Nov 3: "You can still register in person for Nov 3 — until 8 p.m. on Election Day." Source: WA Secretary of State. Suppress the card only after the in-person deadline. The rule 'never render a passed deadline' still holds, applied per method.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Civic block header "Washington · Register by Mon Oct 26, 2026 · 40 days left". Primary "Check or update" opens the Date sheet in seeded mode. The 'deadline passed' frame collapses to "No upcoming election".
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The header states one registration deadline where WA has two (online/mail received by Oct 26; in person until 8 p.m. Nov 3). Checking registration is done through the state's official lookup (Vote.org links each state's lookup; WA's is VoteWA), not an internal sheet. After Oct 26 there is still an election and still a way to register.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Header: "Washington · Online/mail: received by Mon Oct 26 · In person: until 8 p.m. Tue Nov 3". Make the primary an outbound "Check or update at VoteWA" with an external-link glyph, and add a secondary "Remind me" that opens the Date sheet. Redraw the 'deadline passed' frame as the in-person-only state until Nov 3, then as the election banner.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Put four rows each with value plus authority caption, a headline up to ~140 characters, a full-width contrast-sentence footer, and 'All type must survive the 400px thumbnail crop' into the PNG itself.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Apple TN3156 says to avoid text in preview images because they appear at varying sizes and text becomes unreadable. OGP says to specify og:image:alt. WCAG contrast applies to images of text. At 400 px wide a 24 px caption becomes ~8 px. The design doc and f8-seasonal-aha cap the token headline at 90 characters, not 140.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep only layer names, band names, the filled/hollow marks, the sender line and "Yours?" in the image, at ≥40 px cap height. Replace the per-row authority captions with one short "FEMA · USFS · AirNow · EPA" line (≥28 px) so sources survive. Move the contrast sentence into og:description and the question into og:title ("What's on record at Maya's place. Yours?"), and add og:image:alt. Use 90 characters (or none) for the in-image headline. Add a frame showing the iMessage bubble with its title line.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: "Rows are ordered by the distance between the two marks, descending ... never a fixed order."
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: NN/g: consistent attributes are the core of a usable comparison, and differences are highlighted in place (Best Buy's toggle). The arrival header and OG card show the same four layers in a fixed order, so re-sorting on reveal moves rows the user just read. Distance between marks on four incommensurable scales is itself a cross-layer ranking, which f8-og-compare-card forbids ('nothing sums, averages or ranks across them').
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Use the fixed Flood · Wildfire · Air · Radon order on every compare surface. Mark rows whose bands differ with a text tag ('Differs') and stronger weight, and optionally add a one-line summary above the table ("1 of 4 layers differs: Flood"). Keep the merged-mark treatment for matching bands.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Sender row "Air today 'AQI 42 — Good' (AirNow)" under a freshness caption "Dana's card, as of Sep 12, 2026". f8-og-compare-card likewise prints "Air today" and "AirNow, today", and f8-compare-reveal places Dana's frozen AQI on the same track as the recipient's live AQI.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Comparisons need like-for-like attributes (NN/g). A reading frozen at mint time is not 'today'. The product's own honesty rules and the design doc tie 'today' to a live air reading.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Wherever a token supplies the data, label the row "Air on Sep 12 · AirNow" and show the recipient's row as "Air today" with its own date. Alternatively, exclude air from the compare instrument and keep the three static layers. Never draw two different-day AQI marks on one track without both dates.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The Share/Copy tap triggers minting (state 3: button disabled with spinner), then the OS share sheet opens. 'Share cancelled' returns to idle. The privacy line says only "This card shows readings and your city, never your address."
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: MDN: navigator.share must be triggered from a UI event (transient activation), so an awaited network mint before share risks NotAllowedError. AbortError is returned both for user cancel and when no targets are available. A stateless signed token exposes nothing until someone shares it, and it cannot be revoked afterward. Strava shows privacy controls do not follow shared content.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Mint when the sheet opens and again (debounced) when the name toggle changes. Show the minting spinner on the URL row, and enable Share only when the link exists, so the tap calls share synchronously. In the cancelled/AbortError state, keep a visible 'Copy link' fallback. Extend the privacy line: "Anyone with the link can see this card until {exp date}."

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Android frame 8: "Material 3 bottom-sheet chooser presented". Android frame 9: an app-authored "No apps to share with." state.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Android developer guidance: 'Don't display your app's own list of share targets or create your own Sharesheet variations.' Use Intent.createChooser with EXTRA_TITLE and a ClipData thumbnail. The chooser callback reports only the chosen target. On iOS, LPLinkMetadata populates the share sheet's preview header.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Draw the system Android Sharesheet (not an app-drawn M3 sheet) with a title such as "Compare your place with mine" and the card thumbnail in its preview. Treat the no-target case as a system condition and show the fallback 'Copy link' inline. On iOS, draw the system sheet header populated from LPLinkMetadata (card title and image), not a bare URL.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: The contrast line is set at caption/label size (12–13 px), with clause one "Nextdoor is what your neighbors say." at 400 weight in text.muted.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for text under ~24 px regular. text.muted #9CA3AF on #FFFFFF is 2.54:1 (and 2.43:1 on raised #F9FAFB), so it fails.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Set clause one in text.secondary (#6B7280, 4.83:1 on white) and clause two in text.strong at 500–600, so the contrast still comes from weight. Check the dark-mode pair as well.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Date chip "Oct 26 · 9 days" drawn in warning tokens at 14 days or fewer.
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: WCAG 1.4.3: warning #D97706 on warning-bg #FFFBEB is 3.07:1 (3.19:1 on white), which fails for chip-size text.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Keep the warning bg and border or glyph, and set the chip label in text.strong or text.primary. Apply the same fix to the warning-tinted pill in f9-block-founders-panel.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: With "3 joined", the hero reads "4 postcard invites this week — 3 base + 1 earned". Tier 1 is "1 neighbor joins → An extra postcard invite this week". Tier 4 is "Block Builder — the badge, and 6 postcard invites a week permanently".
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The design doc's formula is a weekly allowance of 3 + min(converted referrals, 3), so 3 joined means 6 invites every week, and the bonus is per referral and recurring, not a one-off 'this week'. That makes tier 4's '6 a week permanently' something the user already has at 3 referrals. f9-block-founders-panel for the same state reads '4 of 6 left · +1 earned'. Honest referral programs such as Dropbox state the per-referral amount and cap exactly, and FTC guidance treats misstatements about rewards as deception.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Show the formula as tier 1: "Each neighbor who joins: +1 postcard invite every week (up to +3)". Fixture with 3 joined: "6 postcard invites this week · 3 base + 3 earned". Give tier 4 a reward the user does not already have, or remove it until one exists. Align the Block Founders counter copy to "+3 earned from referrals".

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: "The SCOPE changes only the footer sentence and nothing else", so on a claimed home the voter-registration 'I did this' self-report sits under "Everyone in this household will see this."
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: Voter registration belongs to each individual. A household-visible tick would read as a fact about everyone at the address. Voting-record exposure drew strong backlash (the 2024 'Voting Report Card' mailers were called invasive, and Maryland's AG issued a cease-and-desist). The design doc bars claiming to know registration status. Nickerson & Rogers show that a self-made plan (how and when) is what moves behaviour.
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Make voter registration a person-scoped kind. The seeded deadline can be household-visible, but the 'I did this' tick and any plan stay 'Only you' and read "You marked this done". Add an optional method picker (Online / Mail / In person) that selects which per-method deadline the reminder uses.

contradictionsWithV1.v1Decision: Tier shown as "a warning-tinted countdown pill reading 'closes in 6 days'". f9-founding-meter-preview decides the opposite for the same window: "a date, not a live countdown number".
contradictionsWithV1.researchSays: The CMA (2022, §4.7) and the FTC report accept true deadlines but flag urgency devices that pressure people. Warning semantics suggest a risk where there is only a badge, and at chip size the warning text fails contrast (3.07:1).
contradictionsWithV1.recommendation: Show the window end as a date ("closes Tue, Sep 22") in neutral tokens, matching the preview meter, and keep warning tokens for civic and bill deadlines. If a relative count is kept, pair it with the date and keep it out of warning colour.

numbers: OG image: 1200x630 (1.91:1) recommended; 600x315 minimum for large link images; 200x200 absolute minimum; 8 MB max (Meta). Always declare og:image:width and og:image:height.

Apple Messages previews: image at least 900 px wide; images under 150 px wide may be ignored or shown as icons; icons at least 108x108 square; linked page at most 1 MB; associated resources at most 10 MB total; no JS execution and no meta-redirect following.
og:image:alt: required whenever og:image is set (OGP). It describes the image and is not a caption.

In-image type for the OG card: aim for ≥40 px cap height at 1200 wide (≈13 px when shown 400 wide). Source line ≥28 px. Headline ≤90 characters (design doc token limit), ideally ≤60 in the image. These are derived targets, not a platform spec.

Unverified this pass (do not state as fact): X summary_large_image aspect/size (docs returned HTTP 402), WhatsApp image weight limits, any 'safe-area' percentage for OG crops, Instagram Story safe zones, Duolingo/Apple Music Replay/Zillow share specifics.
WCAG 1.4.3: 4.5:1 normal text; 3:1 large text (≥18pt/≈24 px regular or ≥14pt/≈18.5 px bold).

House-token contrast (computed): text.muted #9CA3AF on #FFFFFF = 2.54:1 (fail); on #F9FAFB = 2.43:1 (fail); text.secondary #6B7280 on #FFFFFF = 4.83:1 (pass); on #F3F4F6 = 4.39:1 (fail for small text); text.strong #374151 on white = 10.31:1; warning #D97706 on #FFFBEB = 3.07:1, on white = 3.19:1 (fail for small text); dark text.secondary #94A3B8 on #0F172A = 6.96:1.
Touch targets: 44x44 pt (Apple); 48x48 dp with 8 dp spacing (Google); 24x24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.5.8 AA). Keep prominent buttons to one or two per view (Apple).

Washington, Nov 3, 2026 general election: online and mail registrations must be received 8 days before (Mon Oct 26, 2026); in person during business hours and until 8:00 p.m. on Election Day (Tue Nov 3, 2026). No clock time is published for the Oct 26 online/mail cutoff, so don't invent one.
Day counts from today (Wed Sep 16, 2026): Oct 26 is 40 days out; Sep 21, 2026 is a Monday; Sep 22 is a Tuesday; Nov 27, 2026 is a Friday.
Method-specific headline example: "Online or mail voter registration for Nov 3 must arrive by Oct 26 in Washington." is 80 characters (fits the 90-character token).

Nickerson & Rogers 2010: n = 287,228; voting-plan script +4.1 percentage points turnout; +9.1 points in single-eligible-voter households; no effect in multi-voter households; plain encouragement and self-prediction had no significant effect.

Mathur et al. 2019: ~53K product pages on ~11K sites; 1,818 dark-pattern instances; 183 sites with deceptive ones; 393 countdown timers on 361 sites; 632 low-stock messages on 581 sites; 47 high-demand messages; 313 activity notifications.
Dropbox referrals: +500 MB per referral up to 16 GB (Basic), +1 GB up to 32 GB (paid); referee +500 MB; four visible stages.
Perkins v. LinkedIn: $13M settlement (2015) over two reminder emails sent without consent.
Robinhood: Massachusetts gamification complaint Dec 2020; $7.5M resolution Feb 2024 with an engagement-practice overhaul.
Wordle: 1.2M results shared on Twitter Jan 1–13, 2022; players grew from 90 (Nov 1, 2021) to 300,000+ (Jan 2, 2022).
Strava Map Visibility: first/last 200 m hidden by default; the hide radius can be extended (up to 1 mile per the help page); controls do not carry to other services.
Clubhouse: invite codes resold for up to $400; weekly users fell 21% over three weeks in Feb–Mar 2021; 10M on the waitlist when invites were dropped in July 2021.
NN/g comparison tables: at most ~5 items (3–5 static, 3–4 dynamic); limit to 2 items on mobile.
Founding meter: always exactly 5 segments; 21-day window. Render nothing on a failed lookup (v1, consistent with the FTC/CMA rule against unsubstantiated scarcity claims).
